reports.headline: Most of the release ingestion path is already correct and needs no code: `buildhub.VERSION_PATS["release"]` is anchored and excludes 0 of 32 real release versions while rejecting `155.0b9`/`140.8.0esr`/`155.0a1`; ESR is its own Buildhub channel and its own Socorro label, so release needs no `aurora`-style alias; buildid == hg pushdate in 26 of 26 release builds and 25 of 25 build revisions are members of a `releases/mozilla-release` push, so `Build.put_data`'s `if rev in revs_c` guard is satisfied; `CHANNEL_TYPE` on the prod DB already contains `release`, so there is no migration; and steady-state release ingestion is ~30x CHEAPER than beta (152 `changesets` rows over 14 windows / 77 days = 2/day, vs beta's 45-122 per 2-day window). Three things are broken. (1) Prod still holds 7,267 orphaned `release` nodes and a `release` `lastdate` row stamped 2026-07-06, so the first tick after switch-on is a 56-day, 30.4 MB, 20,096-changeset `json-pushes` fetch peaking at 215 MB RSS — measured to reach 441 MB (a 512 MB dyno) at a 183-day gap, and the gap grows one day per day. (2) `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention cascade-deletes `builds` rows faster than release ships (median cadence 7.02 d, max gap 20.9 d), so replaying the real `dc.get_builds` gives a short (<3 build-day) selection window on 19.1% of run-days and a one-build-day window — zero selections — on 0.2%. (3) The merge suppression is the right decision on release but its stated reason is false there: 4.9-10.2% of a beta→release merge push's members are hashes that exist on mozilla-beta and NOT on mozilla-central, and those grafts are exactly the cycle's approved uplifts — which is why the merge-day release build (46,715 reports / 36,050 installs for 154.0) ends up with literally 0 on-stack candidates.

gaps.title: Switch-on tick replays a 56-day pushlog because prod's orphaned `release` clocks were never reset — and the fetch grows toward an OOM
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The first `update('release')` job pulls 56 days of `releases/mozilla-release` with `full=1` — 30.4 MB, 20,096 changesets, 324 pushes, three cycle merges — parses it in one RQ work-horse and inserts ~20k `nodes` rows in one transaction. Today it survives (measured peak RSS 215.0 MB vs an 80.7 MB baseline). Every day release stays off, the gap grows one day; at a 183-day gap the same code path peaks at 441.1 MB inside a 512 MB dyno, which is an OOM plus a lost job. `put_filelog` has no clamp of any kind, so this is a live hazard for nightly/beta after any long stall too.
gaps.evidence: Read-only prod SQL (`heroku pg:psql`): `nodes` holds 7,267 rows for channel=release spanning 2026-06-07 18:10:51 .. 2026-07-06 12:00:35; `lastdate` release row = mindate 2026-06-07 18:10:51 / maxdate 2026-07-06 12:36:38; `changesets` holds 20,320 release rows (19,527 analyzed=t on merge=f nodes, 793 analyzed=f on merge=t). BOTH clocks `put_filelog` reads say 2026-07-06, so deleting only the nodes does not help. Measured fetch growth (spike/_release_recon/ing_16_memory.py, ing_17_growth.py): 30d = 20.1 MB / 13,041 chgsets / peak 165.7 MB; 56d (today's gap) = 30.4 MB / 20,096 / 215.0 MB / 7.5-9.1 s; 90d = 48.0 MB / 27,389 / 291.8 MB; 183d = 81.1 MB / 48,965 / **441.1 MB**. Baseline process RSS 80.7 MB. Queue `default_timeout=6000` (worker.py:57) so time is not the binding constraint; memory is.
gaps.proposed_fix: Clamp the start in `put_filelog`: `start_date = max(start_date, end_date - relativedelta(days=config.get_ndays_of_data()))` — one line, fixes every channel, and is exactly the window `Node.clean` retains anyway so nothing useful is lost. Separately, as a pre-deploy step, DELETE the orphaned release rows (`nodes` where channel='release' cascades the 20,320 `changesets`) AND the `release` row in `lastdate`; deleting one without the other still yields the 56-day fetch.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I expected today's 56-day fetch to OOM the 512 MB worker and it does NOT — measured peak 215.0 MB. I also checked whether the fetch would time out: `net.get`'s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is (10, 60) as a gap-between-bytes limit and the whole 30.4 MB arrives in 7.5-9.1 s, and RQ's `default_timeout` is 6000 s, so neither bites. The claim survives only as a growth claim, which is why the numbers at 90d and 183d are given.

gaps.title: `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention cascade-deletes release `builds` rows faster than release ships: 19.1% of run-days get a short selection window, 0.2% get zero selections
gaps.where: crashclouseau/models.py:302-309 (Node.clean), crashclouseau/models.py:581 (builds.nodeid ondelete=CASCADE), crashclouseau/models.py:654-711 (Build.get_last_versions), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:45, crashclouseau/config.py:81-82 (get_ndays_of_data)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `Node.clean` deletes nodes with `pushdate <= now - max_ndays(30)`, and `builds.nodeid` is ON DELETE CASCADE, so the `builds` table can only ever hold release builds pushed in the last 30 days. Release ships every 7.02 days (median) with gaps to 20.9 days, and a 3-build window spans a median 13.78 and up to 31.24 days — longer than the retention. `Build.get_last_versions(n=3)` then returns 2 rows on 18.9% of run-days and 1 row on 0.2%. With `shift = 1` (datacollector.py:305) a 2-day series leaves only the newest build-day evaluable (the middle build-day is never tested), and a 1-day series leaves index 0 only, which `evaluate_days` declines as `untestable_prefix` — a whole run-day of zero selections with no error, the same failure class plan #18 removed from the major-version break, reached from the retention side.
gaps.evidence: REPLAYED through the real code (spike/_release_recon/ing_21_replay.py): seeded a sqlite DB with the 83 real Buildhub release builds (2025-01-13..2026-08-26, pushdate == buildid, verified 26/26 on hg), emulated Node.clean + cascade at each instant, then called `datacollector.get_builds('Firefox','release',day)` for 549 run-days 2025-03-01..2026-08-31. Result: build ROWS returned {1: 1, 2: 83, 3: 465}; distinct build-DAYS = 3 on 444 (80.9%), = 2 on 104 (18.9%), = 1 on 1 (0.2%, 2026-01-05, a single build from 2025-12-17). Short (<3 build-days) on 105/549 = 19.1%. Independent hand simulation (ing_08) gave the identical 19.1%/0.2%. Retention sweep (ing_09): 30d -> 80.9% full windows, 35d -> 90.2%, 40d -> 94.7%, 45d -> 96.0%, 50d/60d/90d -> 96.2% (saturated; the residual 3.8% is respins, irreducible). Cadence (ing_07, 45 gaps since 2025-10-01): median 7.02 d, mean 7.27, max 20.89; over the full 83-build history max gap 20 d, 0 gaps > 30 d (so the window is never empty).
gaps.proposed_fix: Make retention per-channel, the shape `get_threshold`/`get_spike` already use: `config.get_retention_ndays(product, channel)` reading `retention_ndays.Firefox.release = 45`, with `Node.clean` (and only `Node.clean`) using it. 45 buys 96.0% full windows and 50+ buys nothing. Do NOT raise the global `max_ndays`: prod holds 6,316 nightly and 9,184 beta nodes at 30 days, and a 45-day global grows both ~50% for no benefit (beta's 2-day cadence never comes near the bound). Also raise `buildhub_lookback_ndays` in lock-step or it becomes the new binding constraint.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I first assumed a short window was a switch-off. It is not: with `shift=1` a 2-row window still tests the newest build-day against the previous one, so 18.9% of run-days lose the MIDDLE build-day's test, not the whole run. Only the 1-row day (0.2%) is a true switch-off. I also checked whether the beta `buildhub_lookback_ndays` fix already covers this — it does not: the lookback is 30 and the retention is 30, and `Node.clean` runs FIRST inside `update()` (put_filelog -> Changeset.add -> Node.clean, update.py:277-280), so the oldest build Buildhub offers is exactly the one whose node was just deleted and `put_data` skips it.

gaps.title: The merge-day release build — the new major version every user receives — gets ZERO on-stack candidates, and the merge suppression's stated justification is false on release
gaps.where: crashclouseau/pushlog.py:39-68 (suppresses_merge_extraction), crashclouseau/pushlog.py:88-166 (collect), crashclouseau/update.py:67-81 (put_report mindate), crashclouseau/models.py:502-524 (Changeset.find, channel-filtered at :516)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `suppresses_merge_extraction('release')` is True, so a beta->release cycle merge yields its members with `files=[]`, no `changesets` rows and no `patch.parse`. For the merge-day build that leaves the on-stack candidate set EMPTY: measured 0, 0 and 2 `changesets` rows for the 155.0, 154.0 and 153.0 windows. Unlike beta, that build is not a no-user build that `find_no_user_days` discards — it is the shipping release (154.0: 46,715 reports / 36,050 installs in the last 7 days). So release triage is structurally off-stack-only on the one build that matters. The docstring's reason for suppressing ("its members are a whole development cycle of work that already has `changesets` rows under nightly") is FALSE on release, and `Changeset.find` is channel-filtered anyway so an m-c row could never have helped a release crash.
gaps.evidence: Node-hash overlap (spike/_release_recon/ing_06_merge_overlap.py) against m-c and mozilla-beta pushlog universes built monthly 2026-03..08 (central 39,462 / beta 44,270 hashes): release push 6069 @2026-08-26 (155.0, 5,391 members) = 95.1% on m-c, 99.9% on beta, **263 (4.9%) beta-only**, 3 on neither; push 5982 @2026-08-12 (154.0, 7,448) = 92.8% / 100.0% / **533 (7.2%)** / 3; push 5809 @2026-07-15 (153.0, 6,888) = 89.7% / 100.0% / **705 (10.2%)** / 3. The 3-on-neither per push are the merge commit, the version bump and "Update configs after merge day operations a=release" — and that last one IS the build revision in 3 of 5 cycles (152.0/154.0/155.0 inside the merge push; 151.0/153.0 in 1-changeset pushes 21-28 min later; ing_10). On-stack cost of NOT suppressing, measured with the repo's own `pushlog()` (ing_11): the 155.0 merge window yields 2,051 changesets with an interesting file -> 10,515 `changesets` rows, i.e. 2,051 serial `patch.parse` at the tree's measured 3.45-6.51 s = 2.0-3.7 h of the shared queue. Prod already paid a version of this once: 20,320 stale release `changesets` rows, 19,527 analyzed.
gaps.proposed_fix: Keep the suppression (the cost measurement justifies it) but (a) rewrite the docstring's release half to the measured truth — the members are redundant with the BETA pushlog, not the nightly one, and 4.9-10.2% of them exist on no other branch we ingest; and (b) extract the bounded beta-only-graft subset instead of nothing: 263-705 changesets per merge, which ARE the cycle's `a=`-approved uplifts, at 15-76 min of serial queue once every 14-35 days. Detect them as `hash not in the m-c pushlog` or, cheaper and offline, `via_merge and node has a `nodes` row on channel='beta'`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to kill this by showing the merge members are reachable some other way. They are not: `Changeset.find` filters `Node.channel == channel` (models.py:516), so a release crash can only score against release `changesets` rows. I also checked whether the merge-day build is simply dropped as a no-user build the way beta's is — it is not: `find_no_user_days` uses `min_build_installs=15` and 154.0 shows 36,050 installs. Finally I checked whether the merge is excluded from the window by `mindate`: it is not, because for the merge-day build itself `get_pushdate_before` returns the PREVIOUS cycle's last dot-release, so the window contains the whole merge (measured 7,464 and 5,405 nodes).

gaps.title: `put_report`'s no-previous-build fallback NARROWS the candidate window on release, inverting its own documented invariant
gaps.where: crashclouseau/update.py:67-81 (specifically the `mindate = buildid - relativedelta(days=config.get_ndays())` at :79), crashclouseau/config.py:64-68
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: When `Build.get_pushdate_before` returns None the code falls back to `buildid - get_ndays()` = 3 days, with the comment "a wider window is a worse window, not a broken one". On beta (2-day cadence) 3 days IS wider. On release the median gap between builds is 7.02 days and 36 of 45 gaps (80.0%) exceed 3 days, so the fallback silently TRUNCATES the candidate window to as little as 14% of the true one (a 20.9-day gap scored over 3 days) and drops real candidates. The scorer then reports "nothing on-stack" for a crash whose regressor is in the window it declined to read, and the only trace is one WARNING line.
gaps.evidence: Cadence measured from Buildhub (spike/_release_recon/ing_07_window.py, 45 consecutive gaps since 2025-10-01): median 7.02 d, mean 7.27, max 20.89; gaps <= 3 days are 0.1, 0.4, 2.0, 2.1, 2.1, 2.2, 2.2, 2.8, 2.8 = 9 of 45, so 36 of 45 = 80.0% exceed the fallback. Ordinary release windows really do carry candidates the fallback would miss (ing_11): 5-84 nodes and 0-69 `changesets` rows per window, e.g. the 153.0.1 window carried 12 interesting-file changesets / 69 rows over a 12-day gap.
gaps.proposed_fix: Make the fallback a per-channel floor rather than `get_ndays()`, or better: derive it from data already in hand — `Build.get_two_last` gives the previous build when the pushdate query cannot, and failing that use the channel's observed cadence (release: 21 days covers 45/45 measured gaps). At minimum invert the direction: on a channel whose cadence exceeds `get_ndays()`, widen rather than narrow, and say so in the log line.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show it is unreachable. The selector cannot reach it (a picked build-day sits at window index >= 1, so an older row exists by construction), which is what the `get_pushdate_before` docstring says. But the two OTHER paths it names — `redo.reset()` and an un-analysed backlog outliving the pruning — become MORE likely on release precisely because of gap #2: the retention prunes release `builds` rows on 19.1% of run-days, so the oldest surviving build row has no predecessor by construction. The two gaps compose; neither is dead.

gaps.title: `Build.put_data` skips a build with no `nodes` row silently — no log line at the exact point where release loses builds
gaps.where: crashclouseau/models.py:594-618 (the `if rev in revs_c:` at :608), crashclouseau/update.py:206-225 (update_builds)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: This branch is the mechanism of gap #2 and it emits nothing. `update_builds` logs only "Update builds: started/finished", so a release build that Buildhub offered and we declined to insert (because `Node.clean` had just deleted its node one line earlier in the same `update()` call) leaves no trace at all. The operator sees a 2-row selection window and has no way to learn why. This is the four-silent-no-ops shape the tree has already been bitten by.
gaps.evidence: Read: `put_data` (models.py:594-618) contains no `logger` call of any kind; the guard `if rev in revs_c` has no else. `update_builds` (update.py:216, 225) logs only the two bookends. The ordering that makes it fire is read in `update()` (update.py:277 `put_filelog` -> models.py:308 `Node.clean` at `now - 30d`, then :280 `update_builds` asking Buildhub from `LastDate.maxdate - 30d`, which `LastDate.update` has just set to `now` — so the oldest build requested is exactly the one whose node was just pruned).
gaps.proposed_fix: Add one `logger.info("no nodes row for %s (%s/%s/%s): builds row not created", rev, bid, prod, chan)` in the else of :608. It costs nothing on nightly (its build revisions are always in-window) and it is the difference between diagnosing gap #2 in one log grep and rebuilding the arithmetic by hand.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the skip is logged anywhere upstream or downstream: `get_new_signatures` does log `"No buildids for {}-{}"` (datacollector.py:247) but only when the window is COMPLETELY empty, and `put_crashes` logs `"No buildid in db for ..."` (update.py:271) only for buildids returned by a query we scoped to the bids we already have — neither can fire for a build we never inserted.

gaps.title: `VERSION_PATS.get(channel, "*")` matches ZERO Buildhub documents — the next channel added silently gets no builds
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing for release itself (`release` is a listed key and its pattern is correct). But the fallback is not "match anything" — an Elasticsearch `regexp` of `*` is a repeat with no atom and matches nothing. So `buildhub.get(min, 'esr', ...)` returns `{}`, `update_builds`' `if data:` is False, no builds are inserted, and the only symptom is one "No buildids for Firefox-esr" per 20-minute tick. Given the release work will invite "and esr next", this is the trap that is one config edit away.
gaps.evidence: Measured (spike/_release_recon/ing_19_star.py): on target.channel=release, no regexp -> 32 distinct versions, regexp `*` -> **0**, regexp `.*` -> 32; on target.channel=esr, no regexp -> 29, `*` -> **0**, `.*` -> 29. `buildhub.get(20260601000000, 'esr', prods='firefox')` returns `{}` even though Buildhub holds 199 firefox esr documents for 2026 (ing_01).
gaps.proposed_fix: Change the default at all three sites to `".*"`, or make the missing key loud (`VERSION_PATS[channel]` and let it KeyError at the one place a new channel is added). Add the two-line regression test to `tests/test_buildhub.py`, which today tests nightly only.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the `*` default is dead code because every channel is keyed: `VERSION_PATS` has exactly nightly/beta/release, and `config.get_channels()` is the same three, so today it IS unreachable. It stops being unreachable the moment anyone adds a channel to `config/global.json` — which is the mechanism `_ensure_enum_values`/`CHANNEL_TYPE` assume people will use.

gaps.title: No test in the tree exercises release ingestion, and the one release assertion asserts the foot-gun rather than the path
gaps.where: tests/test_buildhub.py:1-79 (nightly-only, live network), tests/test_shipped_channels.py:117-157, tests/test_beta_merge_push.py, tests/test_beta_windows.py
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Every fixture in the merge/window suites is `channel="beta"`; nothing asserts `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction("release") is True` (the only references are mocks, tests/test_trend_window.py:324), nothing asserts `VERSION_PATS["release"]` selects anything, and `tests/test_buildhub.py` reaches the live network for nightly 2018 fixtures only. So the release half of the merge rule, the release version pattern and the release build window can all regress green. Flipping `INGEST_CHANNELS` to include release passes the suite today either way.
gaps.evidence: `grep -rn suppresses_merge_extraction tests/` returns exactly one file (test_trend_window.py:314-324) and it mocks the function. `grep -n 'VERSION_PATS\|release' tests/test_buildhub.py` returns nothing. `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:117` (`test_ingest_channels_must_always_be_set_explicitly`) asserts the empty-value default enqueues `["nightly","beta","release"]` — i.e. it pins the trap, not the behaviour. Ran `tests.test_buildhub tests.test_update tests.test_beta_windows tests.test_beta_merge_push tests.test_shipped_channels`: 49 tests, OK, 11 skipped (Postgres-gated).
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a `tests/test_release_ingest.py` in the shape of test_beta_windows: pin (a) `VERSION_PATS["release"]` against `155.0`/`155.0.1`/`155.0b9`/`140.8.0esr`/`155.0a1` offline via a compiled equivalent, (b) `suppresses_merge_extraction("release") is True` and `collect(..., channel="release")` dropping files on a merge push while keeping the nodes, (c) `Build.get_last_versions(n=3)` over a seeded 7-day-cadence build list with the 30-day retention applied, asserting the short-window count that gap #2's fix is supposed to change.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the beta tests happen to cover release by parameterisation — they do not; `tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:121` iterates `("nightly","release","esr","aurora","esr140")` but only to assert `get_search_channel` does NOT widen them, which is a negative assertion about Socorro labels, not about ingestion.

kills.idea: Release needs a bigger `buildhub_lookback_ndays` on switch-on, the way beta did (71% of switch-on moments under-filled the window at 3 days)
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. `update()` calls `put_filelog` first, which sets `LastDate.maxdate = now` (models.py:83-95), and `update_builds` then subtracts the already-widened 30 days — so the first Buildhub fetch is `now - 30d`, which for today's data returns 154.0 (2026-08-12), 154.0.1 (08-24) and 155.0 (08-26): a full 3-row window on tick one, all three revisions node-backed because 2026-08-12 survives the same call's `Node.clean` cutoff of 2026-08-01. Release's median cadence is 7.02 days and the largest gap in 83 builds of history is 20 days, so a 30-day window is never empty. The binding constraint is the RETENTION, not the lookback.

kills.idea: `target.channel=release` includes ESR builds, so `VERSION_PATS["release"]` must exclude `140.8.0esr`
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD twice over. Buildhub's firefox channel buckets for 2026 are nightly 3,002 / beta 751 / aurora 546 / release 205 / esr 199 / nightly-maple 69 — esr is its OWN channel and 32 of 32 versions on channel=release are `N.0` or `N.0.M`. Separately the regexp IS anchored, so it rejects all 29 esr versions when pointed at them. Nothing to fix.

kills.idea: `target.channel=release` carries RC/candidate builds that would pollute the 3-build window
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. The RC and the shipped release are ONE Buildhub document listed under two channels: for 155.0/154.0/154.0.1/153.0.1/151.0 the build.id sets and source.revisions on channel=release and channel=beta are identical. There is exactly one build.id per (version, respin) on the release channel.

kills.idea: Release needs a Socorro channel alias the way beta needs `aurora` (esr, esr140, esr115...)
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. Every one of the 26 Buildhub release buildids facets to exactly `[('release', n)]`. The `esr`/`esr140`/`esr115`/`esr128` labels (121,107 + 247 + 181 + 28 reports since 2026-08-24) belong to ESR builds with their own buildids, and the junk labels (`default` 3,297, `Bosch` 1,084, `no`, `r`, `pig`) belong to unofficial builds. `utils.get_search_channel("release")` returning the bare string is correct and needs no change.

kills.idea: `CHANNEL_TYPE` needs a Postgres migration / an `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` entry for `release`
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD on the prod DB: `SELECT enumlabel FROM pg_enum JOIN pg_type ...` returns nightly, beta, release. `config/global.json` has listed all three since before the DB was created, so `create_all()` built the enum with every value. `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` stays `{"VERDICT_TYPE": ("lead",)}` — which matters, because `_ensure_enum_values` can never ALTER on this DB anyway (see the known `postgres-enum-and-pinned-source-dead` finding).

kills.idea: `builds.version VARCHAR(10)` will truncate or error on a release version string
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. Longest `target.version` in Buildhub history per channel: release `134.0.1` (7 chars), beta `148.0b12` (8), nightly `152.0a1` (7). No release version has ever exceeded 7 characters.

kills.idea: Adding release as a third channel re-breaks `analyze_reports`/`analyze_patches` (the `len(queue) <= 1` silent no-op)
kills.why_dead: DEAD IN TREE. `update._chain_is_running` (update.py:157-177) now counts only jobs whose `func_name` matches the chain function, and its own docstring names "three channels" as the case the old depth check broke on. Release adds a third `update` job per 20-minute tick and cannot suppress the chain.

kills.idea: The extra serial patch-parsing load from release will starve nightly and beta on the shared queue
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. 152 `changesets` rows over 14 release build windows spanning 77 days = 1.97 patch.parse/day, against beta's 45-122 per ~2-day window (~25-60/day). Merge windows add 0-2 rows because the suppression is already on for any channel != nightly. Release ingestion is ~30x cheaper than beta, not more expensive.

kills.idea: The switch-on pushlog fetch will OOM the 512 MB worker dyno today
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD AT TODAY'S GAP: the 56-day / 30.4 MB / 20,096-changeset fetch peaks at 215.0 MB against an 80.7 MB baseline, and the RQ queue timeout is 6000 s. It becomes an OOM at ~180 days (441.1 MB measured at 183d), which is why the fix is a clamp on the window rather than more memory.

kills.idea: A respin collapses two revisions into one buildid, so `buildhub.get`'s `size: 1` revisions sub-aggregation silently picks the wrong one
kills.why_dead: MEASURED DEAD. 0 of 35 release build.ids have more than one distinct `source.revision`; a respin is a NEW build.id (20260727110312 vs 20260727124451). The size-1 sub-agg loses nothing on release. What a respin actually does is add a second `builds` row with 0 reports / 0 installs — a no-user build the existing `min_build_installs=15` gate already handles.

kills.idea: `Build.get_last_versions`' removed major-version break needs a release-specific replacement so 155.0 is not compared with 154.0.4
kills.why_dead: DEAD by the same argument the beta docstring gives, and the release data does not change it: the builds before the first release of a cycle ARE the previous cycle's dot releases, and "is this build crashier than the ones before it" is exactly the question. What IS release-specific is that the merge-day build's whole cycle of new code lands at once, so the from-zero branch fires broadly — but that is a selector/threshold decision (`floor`, `installs`, `min_build_installs`), not a window one, and re-adding a break would restore the 9.4%-of-run-days silent switch-off plan #18 just removed.

open_questions: Per-channel retention, or accept the short windows? Option A: add `retention_ndays.Firefox.release = 45` and use it only in `Node.clean` (96.0% full windows vs 80.9%, +1 merge's worth of nodes retained, ~14k release nodes peak). Option B: leave `max_ndays = 30` global and accept a short selection window on 19.1% of release run-days plus one zero-selection day per ~18 months. RECOMMEND A — it is a config-shaped change with a measured saturation point (50+ buys nothing) and it does not touch nightly/beta retention.

What should a crash on the merge-day release build be scored against? Option A: nothing on-stack (today's behaviour: 0, 0 and 2 candidates measured for 155.0/154.0/153.0) and rely on the off-stack path. Option B: extract the beta-only graft subset of the merge — 263-705 changesets per merge, which are exactly the cycle's `a=`-approved uplifts, at 15-76 min of serial queue once every 14-35 days. RECOMMEND B: it is bounded, it is the semantically right candidate set for a release regression, and it is 1/3 to 1/8 the cost of unsuppressing the whole merge.

Clamp `put_filelog`'s start window, or hand-clean the orphaned release rows before switch-on? RECOMMEND BOTH, clamp first: `start_date = max(start_date, end_date - relativedelta(days=config.get_ndays_of_data()))` is one line, is exactly the window `Node.clean` retains, and protects nightly/beta from the same hazard after any stall. The one-off DELETE of the 7,267 release `nodes` / 20,320 `changesets` / the `release` `lastdate` row is still worth doing, because both clocks currently read 2026-07-06 and deleting only the nodes changes nothing.

Does `Build.get_pushdate_before`'s fallback stay a 3-day narrowing on release, or become a per-channel widening? RECOMMEND per-channel: 21 days covers 45 of 45 measured release build gaps, and the current 3 days is narrower than 80.0% of them — the opposite of what its own comment claims to guarantee.
cross_dimension: OFF-STACK: `agent.orchestrator._offstack_window`'s `revs` mode uses `Build.get_two_last`, so on a merge-day release build the enumerated window is the whole cycle. Measured with `pushlog_for_revs`-equivalent bounds (154.0.1 -> 155.0): 5,405 changesets, 2,051 of them touching an interesting file, fetched LIVE per run at 8.0 MB / 3.4 s, against beta's 45-122. `_offstack_candidates` drops only `merge`-flagged nodes (21-34 of 5,391), NOT `via_merge` members, then ranks 5,384 candidates by desc-token overlap and recency and caps to `max_candidates`. That is a 40x blow-up of the candidate pool on precisely the build that has no on-stack signal.

SELECTOR/THRESHOLDS: the newest release build is dark for days. 155.0 (shipped 2026-08-26) shows 2 reports / 2 installations five days later — a staged rollout — while 154.0.1 (08-24) already has 52,358 / 38,694 and 154.0 (08-12) 46,715 / 36,050. The `installs` threshold is 50 and the spike `floor` is 50, so the newest release build-day is structurally unevaluable for its first week or two; the productive window index on release is therefore not beta's index 1.

SELECTOR/THRESHOLDS: the release respin creates a genuine zero build-day, but only sometimes. 20260727110312 and 20260506041011 share a calendar day with their surviving pair (so `base[day]` merges them), but 20260513195118 is THREE days before 20260516144017 and has 0 reports / 0 installs — a true no-user build-day sitting between two real ones, i.e. the from-zero baseline trap `get_no_user_build_floor` exists for. `min_build_installs` is already configured at 15 for release, which handles it; worth pinning with the measured 0/0.

SELECTOR/THRESHOLDS: on release the merge-day build brings a whole development cycle of new code at once (5,391-7,448 changesets), and unlike beta that build is NOT a no-user build (36,050 installs). Every signature new in the major version therefore spikes from zero against the previous major's dot releases on the same day. Somebody should measure the size of that burst against `floor`=50 / `installs`=50 before release filing is armed.

PROD HYGIENE / OPS: turning a channel OFF in `INGEST_CHANNELS` orphans its rows permanently — `Node.clean` is reached only from `put_filelog`, which only runs for ingested channels. Prod is carrying 7,267 release `nodes` and 20,320 release `changesets` rows from a ~2026-07-06 ingestion that nothing will ever prune, and the 19,527 analyzed ones prove a release switch-on WITHOUT the merge suppression already cost ~5,000 patch parses once. A channel-agnostic retention sweep (or a `Node.clean` pass over every value of `CHANNEL_TYPE`) would fix the class.

AGENT COST: `Changeset.to_analyze()`'s no-channel variant (models.py:377-391) is channel-agnostic, so the serial patch chain will parse the same node hash once per channel row. With release on, the 263-705 beta-only grafts per merge would have `nodes` rows on BOTH beta and release; `get_scores(channel=)` is already fixed for the double-scoring half, but the duplicate fetch cost is not.

reports.headline: Release is CHEAP on average and ruinous in bursts, and its value is close to zero as configured. Replaying the real selector (`utils.evaluate_days` + `datacollector.find_no_user_days` + the shipped config) over 133 run-days of real release data gives 329 distinct (signature, buildid) pairs = 2.47/run-day, comparable to beta's 2.31-3.5 and 1/50th of nightly's — but 89% come through the `ratio` branch, which on release is not a spike detector at all: it fires when the evaluated build-day simply has a bigger INSTALL BASE than the single preceding build-day (median base ratio 2.71 on run-days with >=5 selections vs 0.40 on run-days with none), producing four bursts of 90-110 pairs whose loudest members sit at count/baseline = 3.00-3.20 exactly (`OOM | small` 14,314 vs 4,741). Those 294 ratio-branch pairs have a median signature age of 1,306 days and ZERO are on a signature younger than 30 days; the stale-signature gate fires on 199/203 signatures (98.0%) and clamps probable(70) to medium(50), below `autofile.min_confidence`, so release filing is structurally blocked before any release-specific decision. Two config numbers are right and were unmeasured (`installs 50` = ~390 real machines under Socorro's 10% release throttle, population-proportionate; `min_build_installs 15`, safe range [2, 833]); one is provably dead (`floor 50` can never bind because `count >= installs` by construction); one is badly wrong in the expensive direction (`protos 20` in a channel whose per-pair proto cardinality is median 11-21 / max 3,930, giving 58 UUIDs/day and $1,510-6,342 in a single burst week). As configured, release buys 2 genuinely-new signatures in 4.5 months for 27-53% of nightly's dossier spend.

gaps.title: `spike.ratio.Firefox.release = 3` is an install-base-ratio detector, not a spike detector: 89% of release volume, 0% of its novelty, in bursts of 90-110 pairs
gaps.where: crashclouseau/utils.py:199-219 (`is_spike` second branch), crashclouseau/utils.py:299-347 (`evaluate_days`), config/global.json:66-72 (`spike.ratio.Firefox.release`), crashclouseau/config.py:377-388
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Switching release on ships four multi-day selection bursts per 4.5 months, each 90-110 new pairs, each triggered purely by a short-lived build sitting in front of a long-lived one. At the shipped `protos` cap that is ~2,745 UUIDs and $1,510-6,342 in ONE week (1.8-3.5x nightly's entire weekly dossier volume), and config.py:751 confirms the per-crash cost cap 'warns; it does not abort mid-run', so nothing stops it. All 294 ratio-branch pairs sit on signatures with a median age of 1,306 days and none younger than 30 days.
gaps.evidence: Replay with the production functions, 133 run-days 2026-04-20..08-30 (spike/_release_recon/sel_13_replay.py, reproduced independently by sel_21_counterfactual.py MODE=prod to the pair -- 329/2.47/max 35 both ways): 329 pairs, 294 (89.4%) via floor/ratio, 35 (10.6%) via from-zero. Bursts: 2026-05-25..31 = 106 new pairs (window 151.0.2/151.0.1/151.0, index-1 install base 151.0.1=71,392 lifetime installs against baseline 151.0=21,845, a 4-day build -> 3.27x); 2026-06-23 = 35 (152.0.1=83,575 vs 152.0=29,264 -> 2.86x); 2026-06-30..07-05 = 93 (152.0.3=70,734 vs 152.0.2=25,584, a 3-day build -> 2.76x); 2026-07-22..26 = 12 (153.0 vs 152.0.6, a 2-day build). sel_20_burst.py: run-days with >=5 new selections have median evaluated/baseline install-base ratio 2.71 (n=15), run-days with 0 have 0.40 (n=70). The 20 loudest pairs a rate normalisation removes all sit at count/baseline 3.00-3.20. Novelty split (sel_22_novelty.py + SignatureFirstDate, answered 203/203): ratio branch median age 1,306 d, 8 of 292 <=90 d, 0 <=30 d; from-zero branch median 448 d, 12 of 35 <=90 d, 4 <=30 d.
gaps.proposed_fix: Two measured options, both at threshold 50 over the same 133 run-days. (a) One-line: `spike.ratio.Firefox.release` 3 -> 5 -- 329 -> 117 pairs, 2.47 -> 0.88/day, worst run 35 -> 11, named boilerplate 57.4% -> 46.2%, from-zero share 10.6% -> 29.9%. (b) Rate-normalise the second branch: compare count / install_base(build-day) instead of raw count, where install_base is the max per-signature install cardinality `find_no_user_days` already computes for free -- 118 pairs, 0.89/day, worst run 7, boilerplate 44.9%, from-zero 29.7%. Prefer (a) unless the flatter worst case matters: at matched volume the two are indistinguishable on boilerplate, which falsifies my initial claim that (b) is strictly better. Do NOT touch nightly/beta's ratio -- this measurement says nothing about them.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show the rate normalisation was strictly better than raising the ratio and FAILED: at n=117 vs n=118 their boilerplate shares are 46.2% and 44.9%, within noise, and both keep `mozilla::ErrorLoadingSheet` (baseline 4 -> 372) and drop the same `OOM | small` class. I also checked whether the bursts were an emulator artefact by reimplementing the selector twice (once calling utils.evaluate_days directly, once open-coded) -- both give 329 pairs / 2.47 per day / max 35 NEW on the same run-days. I checked whether the burst pairs were merely small: the loudest is `OOM | small` at 14,314 crashes from 10,940 installs.

gaps.title: `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release = 20` is 4x beta's measured value in a channel with 4-7x beta's proto cardinality, and the cap does not bound the LLM-run count at all
gaps.where: config/global.json:41-47 (`thresholds.protos.Firefox.release`), crashclouseau/config.py:315-344, crashclouseau/datacollector.py:407 and 475 (`get_proto_small`/`get_proto_big` read it), crashclouseau/models.py:1455-1462 (`UUID.add` dedups on (signatureid, protohash, buildid))
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: At the shipped cap, release's 2.47 pairs/day become 58.4 UUIDs/day -> 32-45 dossiers/day -> $32-135/day (~$960-4,050/month), i.e. 27-53% of nightly's recorded 85-120 dossiers/day, on a channel where 98% of selections cannot produce a filing. In a burst week it is ~2,745 UUIDs / $1,510-6,342. Worse, the cap is applied PER TICK and update_all runs every 20 minutes, while UUID.add dedups only on (signature, protohash, buildid) -- so a pair accumulates the UNION of its per-tick top-N proto sets, not N.
gaps.evidence: sel_18_protos.py on the 27 pairs of the 2026-07-26..08-30 replay: distinct protos per pair median 11, mean 50.7, max 250; 11 of 27 exceed the cap of 20; sum kept at cap 20 = 332 runs from 27 selections (12.3/pair). sel_23_cost.py on a 35-pair sample of the 05-25..31 burst: median 21, mean 324.9, max 3,930, 18/35 capped. Cap sweep on the 27-pair set: cap 1 -> 27 runs, 3 -> 81, 5 -> 123, 10 -> 207, 20 -> 332, 50 -> 660. sel_19_protodrift.py, union of the DAILY top-20 sets over the days each pair stayed selected: js::GCData<T>::get 35, nsBlockFrame::RemoveFrame 43, js::StringFlags::isAtom 37, shutdownhang | RtlWaitOnAddress 25 -- 1.25-2.15x the cap (mean 1.75) at daily granularity, and prod ticks 72x/day. At cap 5 the same unions are 6/7/11/6 = 1.2-2.2x. Compare plan #18 2.3: beta median 3.0 protos/pair, p90 14, max 22 -> cap set to 5; nightly mean 1.07, max 6, cap 50 never binds.
gaps.proposed_fix: Set `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release` to 3-5 (beta's measured range), not 20. Measured funnel: cap 5 -> 17.8 UUIDs/day, 10-14 dossiers/day, $10-41/day; cap 3 -> 10.3 UUIDs/day, 6-8 dossiers/day, $6-24/day (beta's tuned level). Separately, and channel-agnostic: the per-tick cap should be a per-(signature, buildid) LIFETIME cap -- count existing UUID rows for the pair before inserting -- otherwise every channel's cost estimate (including plan #18's beta figures, taken from a single run) is understated by ~1.2-2.2x.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether UUID.add's dedup already prevents the accumulation: it dedups on (signatureid, protohash, buildid), so re-inserting the SAME proto is a no-op but a proto newly entering the count-ordered top-N is a new row. I then measured the drift rather than assuming it, and the union exceeded the cap on 4 of 4 pairs tested. I also checked orchestrator._proto_already_triaged / proto_already_analyzed: it dedups across BUILDS by (sigid, protohash), so it does not suppress a new protohash on the same build.

gaps.title: The stale-signature gate fires on 98.0% of release selections and blocks filing, and 89% of release volume carries no novelty at all
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Release triage runs and spends, and essentially nothing can be filed: _STALE_SIGNATURE_CLAMP maps probable(70) -> medium(50), below autofile.min_confidence 70, so a clamped lead is a filing blocker rather than a downweight (the mechanism plan #18 2.4 measured on beta at 88%). If release is switched on expecting bugs it will produce dossiers and no bugs, and the reason will not be a release-specific decision anyone made.
gaps.evidence: sel_22_novelty.py: 203 distinct signatures selected, sigage.first_seen_ever (SignatureFirstDate) answered 203/203. All-time age at selection: median 1,288 d, p25 568, p75 2,510, max 6,802; 2/202 (1.0%) <=7 d, 4 (2.0%) <=30 d, 17 (8.4%) <=90 d, 43 (21.3%) <=365 d. On the gate's OWN clock (sigage.signature_history(channel='release') windowed first_seen): median 678 d, only 4/203 (2.0%) <=7 d, so min_age_days=7 fires on 199/203 = 98.0% (beta 88%, nightly control 71%). 198 of 203 signatures also crash on other channels (median 1,225 other-channel reports over 364 d). Exactly TWO of the 329 pairs sit on a signature first seen on the selected build: mozilla::dom::FontFaceSetImpl::Add (150.0) and '<name omitted> | Mutex::Unlock' (152.0.2) -- two in 4.5 months.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not treat this as a threshold to tune. Either (a) accept release as a TRIAGE-ONLY channel (AGENT_CHANNELS includes release, autofile.channels.release.enabled=false) and judge it on dossier quality rather than filings, or (b) restrict release selection to the from-zero branch plus a hard novelty gate (age <= 90 d on first_seen_ever), which would keep 17 of 203 signatures and 12 of the 35 from-zero pairs and make release's cost negligible. Whichever is chosen, write the expected filing rate into the plan BEFORE arming, because the honest number is near zero.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the gate would actually reach release by reading _apply_signature_age_gate: it needs seed['signature_first_seen_buildid'] and a candidate pushdate, and off nightly it resolves the pushdate via sigage.pushdate_for_node -- which for release returns the channel's own push date (measured: equals the buildid to the second in 22/22 release builds), i.e. recent. So landed_after is large for any signature older than the current cycle, which is 98% of them. The one thing I could not verify without running the pipeline is which first-seen the seed writes, so I report both clocks (98.0% windowed, 99.0% all-time).

gaps.title: `spike.floor.Firefox.release = 50` is provably inert for selection -- dead config that reads like a protection
gaps.where: config/global.json:52-58 (`spike.floor.Firefox.release`), crashclouseau/utils.py:216-219, crashclouseau/utils.py:324-345 (`evaluate_days`: `spiked` is tested before the install check), crashclouseau/config.py:348-388 (`_SPIKE_DEFAULTS['floor'] = 5`)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Anyone tuning release will reach for `floor` first, because plan #18 11 names it as one of the two unmeasured numbers. Changing it between 1 and 50 changes NOTHING about what gets selected, so a tuning pass on it looks harmless while the real driver (`ratio`) is untouched. Its only live effect is on models.Selection write volume, which is the opposite of what the name suggests.
gaps.evidence: Structural: evaluate_days only picks a build-day if some bid on it has installs >= threshold (50), and a build-day's count is the sum of its bids' report counts, each >= that bid's install cardinality -- so count >= 50 is implied by installs >= 50 and any floor <= 50 can never be the binding test. Measured (sel_21_counterfactual.py MODE=prod FLOOR=..., 133 run-days): floor 1, 3, 10, 20 and 50 all give exactly 329 pairs / 2.47 per day / max 35 NEW / 35 from-zero. It first binds at 100 (198 pairs) and 200 (129). Contrast beta, where floor 10 sits ABOVE installs 6 and therefore can bind -- that asymmetry is why the release value is dead and beta's is not.
gaps.proposed_fix: Leave the value at 50 but document in config.get_spike's docstring (and the release plan) that on release floor <= installs makes the second is_spike branch's absolute test inert, so `ratio` is the only knob. If a floor is wanted on release it must be > 50 to exist at all, and the measured curve is 100 -> 198 pairs, 200 -> 129, 500 -> 83 -- a blunt volume dial that removes small ratio spikes and small from-zero spikes indiscriminately, which is why `ratio` is the better lever.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to find a case where count < installs so the floor could bite: it cannot happen, since cardinality_install_time is a cardinality over the same report set the count comes from (and datacollector.py:274 coerces 0 to 1). The measured reports/installs ratio on the 329 selections is 1.000 at minimum (median 1.036), so count == installs is the tightest case and count is never lower. I also checked the other two places floor is read in evaluate_days (the UNTESTABLE_PREFIX record at line 320 and the maturity test at line 333): maturity is off on release (get_maturity_bar returns (None, 1)), so only the logging path remains.

gaps.title: `models.Selection` writes a median of 3,679 rows per run on release (max 9,830) = ~265,000 upserts/day, 93% of them saying only "fewer than 50 machines"
gaps.where: crashclouseau/models.py:1093-1141 (`record_many`/`_upsert`), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:353-357 (the `outcome != NOT_SPIKING or count >= floor` filter), crashclouseau/update.py:243-251, bin/schedule.py:55-57 (20-minute tick)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Every 20-minute tick adds ~3,700 upserts against a unique index on top of nightly's ~2,600 (the figure models.py:1117 records for a live nightly run), and the worst release run is 9,830. That is ~265,000 upserts/day for release alone, in a single-worker clock dyno whose tick already does Buildhub, the sigtrend backfill, the selector and the proto queries. It fails by making the tick slow, which on this app looks like an ingestion stall rather than a write-volume problem.
gaps.evidence: sel_25_floorlog.py over the 133 run-days, counting exactly what datacollector passes to record_many (dropped_day_records plus outcome != NOT_SPIKING or count >= floor): floor 50 -> median 3,679 rows/run, max 9,830 (x72 = 264,888/day). Composition from the replay's outcome counter: below_install_threshold 497,252 over 133 runs = 3,738/run, untestable_prefix 155/run, selected 11/run, recorded not_spiking ~112/run -- so ~93% are below_install_threshold, i.e. the from-zero branch firing on a signature with under 50 machines. So floor is the only bound on the log and 50 already sits on the flat part of that curve; lowering it is the failure mode.
gaps.proposed_fix: Gate below_install_threshold rows the same way not_spiking rows are gated -- record them only when count >= floor (or when installs are within some fraction of the threshold) -- so the log keeps the near-misses it exists for and drops the ~3,600 rows/run that say "a signature appeared on a new build with a handful of machines". Also assert in the release plan that spike.floor.Firefox.release must never be lowered below 50 while release is on, because that is the only thing keeping the log at 3.7k instead of 13.2k rows a tick.

So this is a WRITE-rate cost, not a storage cost, and I downgraded it from blocker accordingly. I also confirmed _CHUNK = 1000 keeps each statement at 15,000 bind parameters, well under Postgres's 65,535, so it does not fail outright at 9,830 rows.

gaps.title: `facets_limit = 10000` truncates the per-signature facet on release and manufactures 2.1% of its selections as phantom from-zero
gaps.where: config/global.json:8 (`facets_limit`), crashclouseau/config.py:52-53, crashclouseau/datacollector.py:279 (`_facets_size: limit`), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:262-268 (a signature absent from a build's facet keeps `count = 0` from `base`)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Socorro's terms facets are COUNT-ordered, so a release build with more than 10,000 distinct signatures silently loses its quietest ones. A signature truncated out of the BASELINE build reads as count 0 there, and is_spike's from-zero branch is gated by neither floor nor ratio -- so the selector pays for a 'new' signature that was already crashing on the previous build. Release is the only channel that gets anywhere near the limit.
gaps.evidence: sel_09_perbuild.py: 7 of 35 release builds return exactly 10,000 signature facets over their lifetime (148.0, 148.0.2, 149.0, 149.0.2, 150.0.1, 150.0.3, 152.0.6); sel_08_sigcard.py gives _cardinality.signature of 5,393-9,014 per release build over a 19-21 day window against beta 439. In the replay's own fetches, 23 of 399 (n=3 window) and 65 of 665 (n=5 window) queries hit the limit, and 16 of 133 run-days carry at least one truncated build. sel_25_floorlog.py: 7 distinct selected pairs (20.0% of the 35 from-zero pairs, 2.1% of all 329) have their zero baseline on a truncated build and are missing from that build's facet list -- e.g. mozilla::dom::FontFaceSetImpl::Add, 'shutdownhang | ntdll.dll | mozilla::OffTheBooksMutex::Unlock' and SerializeJSONProperty on 150.0 with 149.0 truncated.
gaps.proposed_fix: Raise facets_limit for the per-signature aggregation (a release build's true cardinality is 5.4k-10k+, so 20000 covers it with margin) OR, cheaper and safer, make the from-zero branch require that the baseline build's facet was NOT truncated -- get_new_signatures already knows len(json['facets']['signature']) per build and could mark the day 'unknown baseline' rather than zero. Note facets_limit is shared with get_proto_small, so scope the change to the signature aggregation.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My first count said 50 phantom instances (15% of selections), which was wrong -- it counted per-run-day SELECTED records rather than distinct pairs. Recounted as distinct pairs it is 7, so I report 2.1% not 15%. I also checked the direction: a truncated signature is by construction a LOW-count one on that build, so its true baseline is small but nonzero -- the effect is a real false from-zero, not a false negative. And I confirmed nightly/beta cannot hit this: the largest beta build facet measured was 439.

gaps.title: 36.1% of release run-days have an UNSHIPPED build occupying the exempt newest window slot -- including 5-6 contiguous days per cycle, exactly when a new cycle's code first reaches release users
gaps.where: crashclouseau/models.py:654-708 (`get_last_versions`, buildid-ordered, no users test), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:45-56 (`get_builds` non-nightly branch), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:154-180 (`find_no_user_days` exempts the newest day unconditionally)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: A release build enters the selection window the moment Buildhub knows it, which for a MAJOR is 6-7 days before it reaches any user (staged rollout). It then occupies the newest of three window slots, find_no_user_days cannot drop it (the newest day is exempt by design), and the only selecting index moves onto a build too fresh to clear 3 x max(before). Measured live: 2026-08-25 selected 9 pairs with window [154.0.1, 154.0, 153.0.4]; 155.0 (built 2026-08-26, still 2 reports on 2026-08-31) entered the window on 08-26 and 08-26..08-30 selected ZERO. Same shape at every major: 05-13..05-18, 06-10..06-15, 07-15..07-20, 08-12..08-17.
gaps.evidence: sel_11_lag.py (per-build daily install histogram from the build DAY): dot releases reach 100 installs/day at lag 1 (18 of 18); MAJORS take 3-6 days -- 149.0.2 lag 4, 150.0 6, 151.0 3, 152.0 6, 153.0 6, 154.0 6, and 155.0 (20260826195058) is still at 0-1 installs/day five days after its buildid. sel_30_dropwindow.py counting run-days whose newest build-day carries < 15 installs: 48 of 133 = 36.1%, and those days produced 40 of 329 selections (0.83/day vs 2.47 overall -- a 66% suppression). Contiguous major stretches of 5-6 days appear once per 4-week cycle. This is the release analogue of the beta get_last_versions blackout plan #18 item 7 fixed (12 of 127 beta run-days = 9.4%), but it is inherent rather than a bug.
gaps.proposed_fix: Report it as a known degradation and do NOT fix it the obvious way. I measured the obvious fix -- take the newest 3 builds whose install base >= min_build_installs out of the newest 5 -- and it recovers only +28% (329 -> 420 pairs, zero-days 70 -> 59) while RAISING the worst run 35 -> 42 and recovering only 2 of the 5 lost days in the 08-26..30 case. If the blackout matters, the cheaper honest answer is to note in the plan that the first 6 days of a major release are not covered and rely on beta for that window.
gaps.falsification_attempt: This started as my leading structural finding and I demoted it after measuring the fix. I expected dropping the unshipped build to restore the 9 selections/day 08-25 had; it restored 2. I also checked whether the unshipped build does harm as a BASELINE (the thing find_no_user_days exists for) and it does not: it sits at index 2 where nothing follows it, so it is never a baseline, and its own selection is impossible (n >= 3x a fully-ramped build). The only cost is the wasted slot.

gaps.title: `thresholds.installs.Firefox.release = 50` is right, but it means ~390 real machines and nothing in the repo says so
gaps.where: config/global.json:26-32, crashclouseau/config.py:315-344 (the `get_threshold` docstring covers only the `protos` beta measurement), crashclouseau/datacollector.py:306
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks -- but the number is 50 in a channel where Socorro accepts 10% of reports, so it is not comparable to beta's 6 or nightly's 1 as written, and the next person to tune it will read it as 8x beta rather than 65x. The from-zero branch is ungated by floor/ratio, so `installs` is the ONLY thing standing between release and a runaway: at installs = 1 (which is get_threshold's own default when a key is missing, config.py:343) the replay produces 91,014 pairs, 684/day, and 5,997 NEW in a single run.
gaps.evidence: Sampling: antenna MOZILLA_RULES `is_firefox_desktop` = ProductName==Firefox AND ReleaseChannel==release -> (10, ACCEPT, REJECT) (mozilla-services/antenna main, throttler.py:507-515), corroborated by Socorro docs. Converting to machines (sel_16 plus the geometric fit): the 329 selections have observed reports/installs median 1.036 (p25 1.013, p75 1.102); fitting a shifted-geometric true crash count under p=0.1 to that ratio gives 7.80 true machines per observed install, so 50 observed ~ 390 real machines (beta's 6 = 6, nightly's 1 = 1). Population-normalised: release's true crashing installs/day ~ 139,230 (17,850 observed x 7.8) vs beta 1,097 and nightly 463, so release's threshold is 0.51x as strict as beta's and 1.30x as strict as nightly's -- proportionate. Sweep (133 run-days): 1 -> 91,014 pairs / 684 per day / 5,997 max; 5 -> 1,233 / 9.27 / 94; 10 -> 527 / 3.96 / 45; 20 -> 408 / 3.07 / 39; 50 -> 329 / 2.47 / 35; 100 -> 166 / 1.25 / 21; 500 -> 50 / 0.38 / 10.
gaps.proposed_fix: Keep 50. Add the two facts to get_threshold's docstring: that on release the value is read through Socorro's 10% throttle so 50 observed installs is ~390 machines, and that it is the ONLY gate on the from-zero branch, with the measured cliff at 1 (91,014 pairs) versus 5 (1,233). Add a config test that thresholds.installs.Firefox.release >= 20, because get_threshold's missing-key default is 1 and that value is a 5,997-selection single run.
gaps.falsification_attempt: The 7.80x factor is a fit, not a direct measurement, so I bounded it independently: since observed reports = 0.1 x true reports and observed installs are between 1 and (reports) in number, the real machines behind 50 observed installs lie in [50, 500], and the measured reports/install of 1.036 puts it near the top. I also tried to falsify the 10% rate itself -- see the kills; my one clean prediction (exempt process types over-represented ~10x on release vs beta) came out at 2.43x and is confounded by client-side auto-submission, so I do NOT claim to have measured 10% independently.

gaps.title: Both channel env vars default release ON when empty, and none of the release thresholds has an env override
gaps.where: crashclouseau/update.py:307 (`os.getenv("INGEST_CHANNELS", "").split() or config.get_channels()`), crashclouseau/config.py:436-440 (`get_agent_channels`), crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:4103-4105 (empty list = no filter), crashclouseau/config.py:315-344 and 377-388 (no env reader), config/global.json:2-11
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Clearing INGEST_CHANNELS turns release INGESTION on (config `channels` already lists release), which plan #18 11(d) states. Less obviously, setting AGENT_CHANNELS="" -- the intuitive way to express 'no channels' -- evaluates to [], and the orchestrator's guard is `if channel is not None and channels and channel not in channels`, so an empty list means NO FILTER and release TRIAGE turns on at ~$1-3 a crash. Meanwhile every number in this report lives only in config/global.json, so correcting `protos` or `ratio` after release is armed requires a DEPLOY, and a deploy kills in-flight ~20-minute runs at ~$3 each (bin/predeploy.py:8).
gaps.evidence: Read in tree at the cited lines; get_agent_channels' own docstring says "An explicitly EMPTY value means 'no filter' (every channel)". config.get_channels() returns [nightly, beta, release] from config/global.json:3-11 (it must, because it also defines the CHANNEL_TYPE enum). Grep of config.py for env readers finds _env_bool/getenv on POPULATION_STATS, AGENT_CHANNELS, AGENT_SWEEP, AUTOFILE_BUGS, AUTOFILE_NEEDINFO, SHOW_ABSTAIN, OFFSTACK_*, SECOND_OPINION_ENABLED, SIGNATURE_AGE_ENABLED, BIT_FLIP_GATE_ENABLED, BAD_MACHINE_GATE_ENABLED -- and none on `thresholds` or `spike`. tests/test_beta_selection.py:801 test_release_is_on_the_off_nightly_side pins shift == 1 for release, so any shift change must update it.
gaps.proposed_fix: Before any release rollout: (1) set INGEST_CHANNELS and AGENT_CHANNELS EXPLICITLY on the dyno rather than relying on config, and add a rollout note that AGENT_CHANNELS="" means every channel; (2) give the two numbers most likely to need correcting in flight an env override -- RELEASE_PROTOS_CAP and RELEASE_SPIKE_RATIO read by get_threshold/get_spike -- so a burst can be throttled without a deploy; (3) add config tests pinning thresholds.installs.Firefox.release >= 20 and thresholds.protos.Firefox.release <= 5.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I traced the empty-list semantics to the actual consumer rather than trusting the docstring: orchestrator.py:4104's `and channels` short-circuits, so [] skips the check entirely, and orchestrator.py:4171's max(1, len(channels or ())) in the sweep confirms the empty case is treated as 'all'. I did not check prod config (that needs a Heroku session); the prod facts given (INGEST_CHANNELS="nightly beta", AGENT_CHANNELS="nightly beta") mean release is currently off by explicit value, which is the safe state.
