Over 245 non-newest build-day observations the respin-only days sit at install base 1 (9/9) and the quietest LEGITIMATE non-newest build-day at 833 -- safe range [2, 833]. It drops 9/9 respins, falsely drops 0/236 legitimate days, and it actually fires in the replay (dead=1 on 9 of 133 run-days, 2026-05-16..05-24, on the 151.0 respin 20260513195118). Do not touch it. spike/_release_recon/sel_27_nouser.py

kills.idea: Give release an alias set in utils.get_search_channel, the way beta needs ['beta','aurora'].
kills.why_dead: Measured: the only other label carrying release buildids is release_channel=default at 0.3-6.2% of reports, and it comes from 2-12 machines (6,567 reports from 4 installs on 153.0.3; 1,398 from 2 on 154.0) -- distro-rebuild or CI loops, which antenna accepts at 100% while throttling real release traffic to 10%, so aliasing it in would import unthrottled single-machine floods into the install counts the whole selector is keyed on. esr on a release buildid is 4-5 reports, version-tagged X.Y.Zesr, and esr's own builds have their own buildids. get_search_channel must stay 'release'. spike/_release_recon/sel_15_alias.py

kills.idea: Give the install threshold a per-process-type or per-throttle-class correction, because antenna exempts gpu/rdd/socket/utility/plugin and PHC and commented crashes from the 10% sample while ShutDownKill is throttled to 1%.
kills.why_dead: The rules are real but they never touch release selection. Across all 27 selections of the 07-26..08-30 replay, exempt-process reports are 0 of 22,784 (0.00%) -- every selection is parent/content -- and ipc_channel_error=ShutDownKill on release over 30 days is ONE report (nightly 1,197). The class composition difference between channels is client-side auto-submission, not throttling: nightly's TRUE exempt-process share is 34.2% against beta's 0.75%. A flat 10% is the correct model for everything release selection ever sees. spike/_release_recon/sel_04_procshare.py, sel_17_selclass.py

kills.idea: Rate-normalising the ratio branch is strictly better than simply raising spike.ratio from 3 to 5.
kills.why_dead: At matched volume they are indistinguishable on quality: 117 pairs / 46.2% named boilerplate for ratio 5 versus 118 pairs / 44.9% for the rate-normalised version, over the same 133 run-days. The rate version's only measured advantage is a flatter worst run (7 vs 11 new pairs). The one-line config change is therefore a legitimate substitute for the code change, and I withdraw the claim that the normalisation is required. spike/_release_recon/sel_21_counterfactual.py

kills.idea: Fix the unshipped-newest-build window slot by making window membership conditional on the build having users (take the newest 3 builds with install base >= min_build_installs out of the newest 5).
kills.why_dead: Measured, and it does not buy what it looks like it should. Over 133 run-days it takes 329 -> 420 pairs (+28%) and zero-selection run-days 70 -> 59, but it RAISES the worst run 35 -> 42, and on the specific 5-day 155.0 blackout (2026-08-26..30) it recovers 2 selections, not the 9/day 08-25 had -- because the next-newest live build is itself too fresh to clear 3 x max(before). It also drags in a max_ndays change (29% of 5-build release windows exceed 30 days, at which Node.clean plus ON DELETE CASCADE deletes the build rows). Report the 36.1% degradation; do not build this. spike/_release_recon/sel_30_dropwindow.py

kills.idea: Node.clean's 30-day prune will silently shrink the release selection window the way it can on beta after a merge.
kills.why_dead: Not at n=3. The widest 3-build release window in the whole Buildhub history spans exactly 30 buildid-days (148.0 -> 149.0) and 0 of 33 exceed 30, and a release build's Node.pushdate equals its buildid to the second in 22 of 22 builds measured, so the prune clock is not shifted earlier the way beta's merge pushdate is. It only becomes a hazard if the window is widened to 5 builds (9 of 31 = 29% over 30 days). spike/_release_recon/sel_24_misc.py, sel_29_pushdate.py

kills.idea: Release is unaffordable on volume grounds, so the first job is to cut the number of selected pairs.
kills.why_dead: The pair count is already small -- 2.47/run-day against beta's 2.31-3.5 and nightly's 102.6-144.6 -- and 52.6% of run-days select nothing. The cost is entirely in thresholds.protos.Firefox.release = 20 times the per-tick re-capping (13.5 protos kept per pair x a measured 1.75 daily union = 58.4 UUIDs/day) and in the four bursts. Cutting protos to 3-5 gets release to beta's spend without touching selection at all. spike/_release_recon/sel_26_funnel.py

open_questions: What is release FOR? Pick one: (a) triage-only, no filing (AGENT_CHANNELS includes release, autofile.channels.release.enabled=false), judged on dossier quality; (b) filing armed, accepting that the stale-signature gate blocks 98.0% of selections so the expected rate is ~0-1 bug/quarter; (c) not switched on. I recommend (a) at protos=3 for one cycle (~6-8 dossiers/day, $6-24/day), because that is the only way to learn whether a release dossier is worth anything, and it is reversible via AGENT_CHANNELS without a deploy.

spike.ratio.Firefox.release: 3 -> 5 (one config line, 329 -> 117 pairs, worst run 35 -> 11), or rate-normalise is_spike's second branch by the build-day install base (118 pairs, worst run 7, but a code change to a function nightly and beta also call)? I recommend the config line, because the two are measured equivalent on boilerplate share and the config change cannot regress the two live channels.

thresholds.protos.Firefox.release: 3 or 5? Measured 2.25 vs 3.42 selections-worth of LLM runs per day before the ~1.5x per-tick union factor, i.e. ~10.3 vs ~17.8 UUIDs/day. I recommend 5 for parity with beta's measured value, and 3 if the release dossier yield comes in below nightly's 0.55-0.77.

Do we fix the per-tick proto cap so it bounds a pair's LIFETIME run count, or accept the measured 1.2-2.2x overrun? This is channel-agnostic and means plan #18's beta cost figures are understated too. I recommend fixing it before release is armed, because release is the channel where the overrun is priced in thousands of dollars per burst week.

Do we accept that the first 6 days of every major release are uncovered (48 of 133 run-days degraded, 5-6 contiguous days per cycle when a whole cycle's code first reaches release users), or spend on a window-membership change? I recommend accepting it and documenting it: the measured fix recovers only +28% and worsens the worst run.
cross_dimension: CANDIDATE WINDOW: a release build's Node.pushdate equals its buildid to the second in 22 of 22 builds measured (sigage.pushdate_for_node falls back to the channel repo; m-c 404s on every release revision) -- so on release the pushlog clock is the SHIP-IT moment, not the beta-style merge date. Build.get_pushdate_before therefore gives a dot release a ~5-12 day uplift window but gives a MAJOR release the entire cycle merge push. pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction returns True for release (channel != nightly), so the merge push's members get Node rows with no files, exactly as designed for beta. Worth confirming the release repo mapping actually points at releases/mozilla-release.

COST: the proto cap is applied PER TICK and update_all runs every 20 minutes, while UUID.add dedups only on (signature, protohash, buildid) -- so a pair accumulates the UNION of its per-tick top-N proto sets. Measured at DAILY granularity on 4 release pairs the union is 1.25-2.15x the cap (25/35/37/43 against a cap of 20). Channel-agnostic, so plan #18's beta cost estimate (protos-per-pair from a single run) and nightly's are understated by the same factor. Someone should measure the 20-minute-cadence version on prod data.

COST/SAFETY: config.py:751 states the per-crash cost cap 'warns; it does not abort mid-run' and plan #18 section 11 leaves that out of scope. Release's measured burst is ~2,745 UUIDs / $1,510-6,342 in one week, so release is the first channel where the missing abort is a real exposure rather than a documentation gap. A per-tick or per-day selection cap would be a cheaper backstop than making the cap abort.

FILING: models.py:676-681 records that RC/dot-release builds on target.channel=beta report release_channel=release in Socorro. I confirmed the mirror image: version 155.0 on release appears on SIX buildids, only one of which (20260826195058) is in Buildhub's release channel; the rest are RC builds with beta-era buildids and are invisible to us because Build.get_id finds no row. Anything that searches BMO or Socorro by release VERSION rather than by our buildid needs to know that.

POPULATION: release has the LOWEST reports-per-installation of the four channels (1.20/day vs esr 1.52, beta 1.36, nightly 1.99), the fingerprint of the 10% throttle. Any population or hardware-noise statistic that compares a release rate against a nightly or beta rate is comparing a 10% sample against a census -- including sigage.hardware_noise's all-channel denominators and population.for_crash's concentration share.

UI/SECURITY: crashstack.html and reports.html would start showing release rows the moment INGEST_CHANNELS includes release. The memory-safety finding (mccr8, bug 2065051) is that our site serves the same analysis ANONYMOUSLY while a sec-restricted bug does not -- and release crashes reach ~8x more machines per observed install than the raw numbers suggest, so the poison-address detector and the per-product sec-group routing need to be verified as DEPLOYED before release ingestion, not after.

reports.headline: On release the two windows do not scale, they invert. Measured through the repo's own `pushlog`/`Changeset.find` code over all 26 inter-build windows since 2026-04: a DOT-release window is 5-116 changesets (median 46, median 4 candidate-bearing) and a MAJOR-release window is 5,405-7,464 changesets of which 0-2 are candidate-bearing, because 5,391-7,448 of them are cycle-merge members whose files `pushlog.collect` deliberately drops on any non-nightly channel. Per real crash that is 0 on-stack candidates on 57 of 58 crash x build pairs (28/28 on 154.0, 29/30 on 154.0.1) against nightly's "zero on 29%", so release would run ~98-100% off-stack — and on a major build the off-stack path fetches 8.0-17.1 MB per run and hands the agent 150 candidates of which 150/150 are `via_merge`, 150/150 are `pref_flip`, and all share ONE pushdate, so `is_suspected_regression` is False for every candidate it can pick and the signature-overlap ranking decides nothing. The deeper question has a number: of 207 crash-signature regression bugs fixed in fx148-155 with a `regressed_by`, only 5 (2.4%, ~0.6/cycle) have a regressor that ever landed on releases/mozilla-release outside a cycle merge; for the other 97.6% it is nightly-cycle work, median 43.6 days old at ship, of which `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention still holds 16.1% on ship day and 0% a week later. Release on-stack is not an unmeasured-threshold problem: it is a window that structurally cannot contain the answer.

gaps.title: A MAJOR release build's on-stack candidate set is structurally EMPTY - and that build carries the whole release population
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `suppresses_merge_extraction(channel)` is `channel != "nightly"`, so on release a cycle-merge push yields its members with `files: []` -> no `changesets` rows -> `Changeset.find` (which joins Changeset->Node->File) can return nothing from them. The merge push sits INSIDE the major build's own window (its pushdate IS the build's pushdate and `Node.pushdate <= maxdate` is inclusive), so every crash on 150.0/151.0/152.0/153.0/154.0/155.0 scores 0 candidates and falls through to the off-stack path. With OFFSTACK_ENABLED=1 that is 100% of a release major build's runs on the most expensive path, with no line-proximity signal at all.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/windows_06_full.py ran `pushlog.pushlog(mindate, maxdate, channel="release")` with production defaults for all 6 majors since 2026-04: changesets 6164/7079/6997/6907/7464/5405 (median 6952), candidate-bearing 0/1/0/2/0/0, `changesets` rows 0/1/0/2/0/0, via_merge 6118/7063/6985/6888/7448/5391. Per real crash on 154.0 (28 Socorro reports through `inspector.inspect_stacktrace`, windows_13_major.py): min 0, median 0, max 0 - zero on 28 of 28. Unlike beta's merge-day b1 (0-7 installs) this build is the shipped one: 6,563 reports / 5,031 distinct install_time in 3 days, 18 days after ship (windows_24_buildage.py). buildid == node pushdate on release in 35/35 builds (windows_02_probe.py), so the merge is always exactly at the upper bound.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not reuse beta's answer. Either (a) for a release crash whose window contains a cycle merge, build the candidate set from the MERGE MEMBERS' node hashes and query them across channels - `Changeset.find` filters `Node.channel == channel`, and 95.6% of the per-crash candidates already exist on mozilla-central under the same hash with parsed diffs - which needs the retention fix below; or (b) set `drop_merge_files=False` for the release cycle merge only, paying 2,905 `patch.parse` per cycle (~3.1 h of the shared serial queue at the measured 3.8 s/fetch); or (c) declare release off-stack-only and write it down. Leaving it as-is is silent, not degraded.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Three attempts to make the window non-empty. (1) Removing the interesting-file filter takes the major windows from 0 to 12/16/16/19/19/46 candidate-bearing (release-branch config commits), not to thousands, because `collect` empties `files` BEFORE any filter runs. (2) Checked whether the crash gets attributed to a later build instead: no - the major build is in `get_last_versions(n=3)` for ~3 dot releases and is ingested (5,031 installs). (3) Checked whether the repo's own pin test contradicts me: tests/test_beta_windows.py:141-146 states its merge-member fixture is 'deliberately not what pushlog.collect emits today', so it does not.

gaps.title: Only 2.4% of release crash regressions have a regressor the deployed release window can contain
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The pipeline's premise (`_record_window_membership`, orchestrator.py:2448) is 'the regressor is somewhere in this build's pushlog window'. On release that is false for 97.6% of the crash regressions that actually get fixed: the regressor reached mozilla-release only as one of ~7,000 merge members. Shipping release on-stack buys ~0.6-0.9 nameable crash regressions per cycle, against nightly's ~3 filings/day.
gaps.evidence: hg as ground truth (windows_22_definitive.py): R = 678 distinct bugs with a non-merge-member changeset on releases/mozilla-release 2026-01..08, built with `pushlog.pushlog` per window filtering `merge` and `via_merge` (majors contribute only 12-46 non-member changesets each). Population = the 217 distinct BMO bugs with cf_crash_signature set + regressed_by set + cf_status_firefox148..155 fixed/verified (windows_08_bmo.py); 207 carry a regressed_by. 5 (2.4%) name a regressor in R: 2006998, 2023331, 2036484, 2049845, 2056166 - and windows_21_regressors.py locates each regressor inside a SPECIFIC dot window (e.g. bug 2036484's regressor 2021892 landed 3 changesets in 150.0->150.0.1). Independent instrument: bugs whose regressed_by names a bug with `approval-mozilla-release+` = 6-32 per version, 0-4 with a crash signature, 7 distinct over 8 versions (windows_10_uplift.py).
gaps.proposed_fix: Put this number in the release plan's scope section instead of 'thresholds are unmeasured'. If release is wanted, the on-stack path must reach the merge window or be dropped; if not, scope release to off-stack-only and expect ~0.6 nameable on-stack regressions per cycle from the dot windows.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Two instruments from different sources (BMO approval flags vs hg pushlog descriptions) agree to within 5 vs 7 bugs over 8 cycles. My first hg run gave a spuriously large R (10,908 bugs) because 2 of 6 majors (151.0, 153.0) push their build revision ~21 minutes AFTER the merge, so a `maxdate - 1s` cut did not exclude those merges; re-running with the production `via_merge` predicate gave 678. I also verified json-pushes' enddate handling directly (windows_23_bound.py: enddate=build+0s -> 7464 changesets, build-1s -> 16) rather than reasoning about the +/-1s inside `pushlog()`.

gaps.title: The off-stack 150-candidate cap collapses to `_looks_pref_flip` on a merge window; the only content-based signal is never consulted
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `_key` is a TIER function: (prior_sig, non-backout, pref_flip, sig<->desc overlap, recency). On a release merge window the (non-backout AND pref_flip) tier is 294 changesets against `max_candidates` 150, so the cap is filled entirely from it and every non-pref-flip changeset is unreachable - including those with the highest signature-token overlap. Recency is also a no-op: all 7,448 members share ONE pushdate. The agent's list is 'the first 150 pref-flip changesets of the cycle'.
gaps.evidence: windows_19_prefsat.py + windows_20_rank.py + windows_25_viamerge.py on the real 153.0.4->154.0 window through `orchestrator._offstack_candidates`: 7,430 non-merge changesets, 361 pref_flip (4.9%), 294 non-backout, cap 150 -> kept 150/150 pref_flip, 150/150 via_merge, 1 distinct pushdate. For signature `mozilla::net::HttpBaseChannel::~HttpBaseChannel` the window holds 233 changesets at overlap 2, 19 at 3, 2 at 4; the kept 150 holds 144 at overlap 0 and 6 at 1, and both overlap-4 changesets are dropped. Controls where the pipeline runs today: nightly 3-day window 819 non-merge / 53 pref_flip, beta in-cycle 61 / 6, release dot 83 / 8 - the cap never binds.
gaps.proposed_fix: Make `pref_flip` a tiebreak below the signature<->description overlap, or gate the tier on `len(tier) < max_candidates`. The saturation threshold is window size > cap/0.049 ~= 3,060 changesets: no nightly or beta in-cycle window reaches it, every release merge window does.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether the 16 non-merge-member changesets could sneak in (they cannot: 150/150 kept are via_merge), whether `prior_sig` re-orders it (no prior bugs are passed for a new signature and it is the same tier structure), and whether the collapse already exists on the ingested channels (measured no: 53 and 6 pref_flips against a 150 cap). Also ran 5 different real 154.0 signatures: all 5 gave 150 kept, 150 pref_flip.

gaps.title: `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention cannot hold a release build's honest candidate set - 83.9% of it is already deleted on ship day
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The cheap fix - answer a release crash from the nightly rows we already have, since 95.6% of a merge window's per-crash candidates share a hash with mozilla-central and both repos serve byte-identical raw-rev - is defeated by pruning: `Node.clean` deletes nodes with `pushdate <= date - max_ndays(30)` per channel, and the code a release build ships is older than that by construction.
gaps.evidence: windows_11_age.py + windows_14_dot_and_retention.py. m-c push age of merge members at ship: 150.0 median 33.9 max 45.4 (65.1% >30 d); 152.0 median 36.9 max 51.1 (75.5%); 154.0 median 42.4 max 58.2 (82.6%); 155.0 median 26.9 max 37.1 (33.3%). Beta-graft members (4.9-7.2% of a merge push) are young: median 6.3-11.9 d, 0% >30 d. Restricted to the 2,905 candidate-bearing members of the 154.0 merge window: 2,677 have an m-c push date (92.2%), median age 43.6 d; inside max_ndays=30 at ship+0d 467 (16.1%), at ship+7/14/28d 0 (0.0%).
gaps.proposed_fix: If the merge-member node-set query is adopted, raise nightly retention to ~90 days (max observed cycle age 58.2 d + the ~30 d a major build stays current) and stop filtering `Node.channel == channel` for that one query - deduping by hash, because `get_scores`' docstring documents why the channel filter exists (one hash, two channel rows, two Score rows per frame). The retention cost is small: mozilla-central pushed 39,130 changesets in 180 days (217/day), so 60 extra days is ~13k `nodes` rows and zero extra `patch.parse`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether the beta channel could supply the missing rows instead: only 263-574 members per merge (4.9-7.2%) are beta-only grafts, so beta covers the young tail and not the 93-95% that matters. Checked whether a shorter cycle rescues it: 155.0 (a 14-day beta cycle) still has median 26.9 d and 33.3% over 30 days.

gaps.title: Even the coherent DOT-release window does not intersect crash stacks: 0 candidates on 29 of 30 crashes
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The ride-along-uplift window is real and high-signal in principle (median 46 changesets, median 4 candidate-bearing) but it is narrow on the axis that decides scoring - distinct source files, median 7. So even on a dot release the pipeline is off-stack in practice, and the on-stack scorer contributes almost nothing on release as a whole.
gaps.evidence: windows_06_full.py over the 20 dot windows: changesets min 5 median 46 p75 83 max 116; candidate-bearing min 0 median 4 p75 10 max 49; `changesets` rows median 7.5 max 129; distinct files min 0 median 7 p75 16 max 104. Per real crash on 154.0.1 (30 Socorro reports, windows_14_dot_and_retention.py; window = 83 changesets / 8 candidate-bearing / 19 files): median 0, max 1, zero on 29 of 30 (97%). Plan #18 measured beta in-cycle at 'zero on 90% of stack x window pairs' and nightly at 'zero on 29%'.
gaps.proposed_fix: Record this as the expected release behaviour rather than discovering it in prod: a release canary should assert an off-stack rate near 100%, and the release cost model must be priced at the off-stack per-run cost, not at nightly's mix.
gaps.falsification_attempt: The 154.0.1 window is one of the larger dot windows (83 changesets, 285 h gap), so it is not a pessimistic pick; the richest dot window measured (150.0->150.0.1: 108 changesets / 49 candidate-bearing / 94 files) is 5x more file-rich and would raise the hit rate, which is why I report 97% as measured on one build, not as the release-wide rate.

gaps.title: The +1 second at update.py:60-82 is load-bearing on release for the DOT builds and useless for the MAJOR one - and nothing pins the difference
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The comment explains the boundary as a beta fact. On release the same mechanism has a different conclusion in each direction and no test to break: for every build AFTER a major, `mindate` = previous build pushdate + 1s lands strictly above all ~7,000 merge members (6/6 cycles), so the merge is excluded; for the MAJOR build itself the merge is at `maxdate`, which is inclusive, so no boundary can help. And since `drop_merge_files` already empties those members' file lists on release, the +1s is the second line of defence, not the first.
gaps.evidence: windows_03_merge.py / windows_04_rev.py: the major build's own revision is a MEMBER of the cycle merge push in 4 of 6 majors (152.0 rev 931e624c6f53 in push 5578 of 6,985 members; 154.0 9ce1ee6baeb9 in push 5982 of 7,448; 155.0 21a096119103 in push 6069 of 5,391; 150.0 1a6c5c6f11fc in push 5151 of 6,118 - all 'No Bug - Update configs after merge day operations a=release'), and in the other two (151.0, 153.0) the build revision is pushed minutes AFTER the merge, so the merge is still inside the major's window and still below the next build's mindate. buildid == node pushdate in 35/35 release builds, so the boundary is exact. Window sizes: 152.0->152.0.1 = 41 changesets; without the +1s it would be 41 + 6,985.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add tests/test_release_windows.py as the release analogue of tests/test_beta_windows.py, pinning the OPPOSITE conclusion: a dot build sees only the uplifts; the major build sees the merge at its inclusive upper bound and `Changeset.find` returns NOTHING because the members have no rows; `is_merge_push` fires on all 8 release cycle merges measured (5,405-7,464 changesets, 14-22 merge-flagged) so the file-drop cannot silently stop applying.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Tested whether the file-drop makes the +1s fully redundant: it does for `Changeset.find` today, but not if `is_merge_push` ever fails to fire (it needs a `len(parents) > 1` changeset in the push) - measured firing on 8 of 8 release merges, so both mechanisms are live and independent, exactly as the beta test file argues.

gaps.title: Off-stack window cost on a major release build: 8.0-17.1 MB and +54 MB RSS per run, on a 512 MB dyno
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `_offstack_candidates` fetches the window LIVE per analysis (`json-pushes?full=1`), and on a major release build that is the whole cycle merge. Measured 7,464 changesets in 5.3 s with a +54 MB resident step for the parse alone; bodies are 8.0/10.1/10.7/11.9/17.1 MB across the 6 majors. The worker dyno is 512 MB with a known OOM history, and ingestion pays the same body once per merge through `put_filelog`.
gaps.evidence: windows_18_offstack.py (resource.getrusage around `pushlog_for_revs`: 95 -> 149 MB) and windows_06_full.py's per-window byte/second columns (the on-stack and off-stack paths request the same body, median 10.4 MB each; 3.48-5.38 s). Dot windows are 0.0-0.1 MB and 1.2-2.4 s.
gaps.proposed_fix: For a window whose pushes are merge pushes, do not fetch `full=1`: the same push list without `full` is 655 KB instead of 11.9 MB (measured in windows_03_merge.py), and the ranker only needs desc+files for the 150 it keeps. Add a member-count guard, or bound the window before the fetch.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether the rising-signature widening makes it worse: it produces the same window (see kills). Checked whether the cost already exists on beta: yes for the merge-day b1, but that build ships to 0-7 installs and is never selected, so it is unreachable there and reachable on every release major build.

gaps.title: The agent's documented escape hatch to mozilla-central 404s for a release crash (pre-existing on beta)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: history.py's docstring says 'pass nightly to query mozilla-central (where regressors usually land first) even for a beta/release crash'. In pinned (off-stack) mode `_pin` rewrites the default node to `ctx.build_rev`, a release-branch-only revision, so `file_history`/`blame` with channel="nightly" resolve a node that does not exist on mozilla-central and return 'fetch failed'. Release runs are ~100% off-stack, hence ~100% pinned, so the one documented way to look where the regressor actually landed is closed by default on the channel that needs it most.
gaps.evidence: windows_16_pin.py: json-rev of 4 release build revisions (9ce1ee6baeb9, 21a096119103, 8b532c2140db, 6526f112c78a) returns 200 on releases/mozilla-release and 404 on mozilla-central and mozilla-beta, 4/4. windows_17_betapin.py: the same holds for 8 of 8 recent beta build revisions, so this is pre-existing rather than release-specific - release just makes it load-bearing.
gaps.proposed_fix: When `channel` is overridden away from the crash's own channel, drop the pin or translate it: the honest as-of revision on mozilla-central for a release crash is the merge base, i.e. the merge push's first parent, available free from the same json-rev the pin came from. Cheap alternative: fall back to `tip` with an explicit warning line rather than returning 'fetch failed'.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether the agent can recover unaided: only by passing an explicit node that exists on m-c, and the only such nodes it is handed are the off-stack candidate hashes (92.8-95.1% of merge members do exist on m-c) - recovery depending on the model guessing the trick is not a mechanism.

gaps.title: Every off-stack candidate on a major release build is via_merge, so every filing from that build is the hedged 'NOT a suspected cause' shape
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `is_suspected_regression` returns False whenever `candidate_arrived_by_merge` is set, and report_bug.py:1540-1551 then prints 'Starting point - NOT a suspected cause ... thousands of changesets at a single push date'. On a major release build that is unconditional: 150 of 150 offered candidates are via_merge. So release majors can only ever produce filings that correctly say the pipeline has no recency evidence, about a changeset chosen by a pref-flip heuristic out of 7,448.

kills.idea: Port the 24 h rising-signature off-stack widening (_RISE_WINDOW_HOURS, orchestrator.py:308) to release, or re-fit it there
kills.why_dead: Measured inert. _offstack_window(rising=True) sets start = buildid - 24 h then moves it back to get_pushdate_before whenever that is earlier - and on release the previous build is earlier in 24 of 26 measured windows (majors 47.75-293.4 h, dots median 165.8 h; only 9.92 h and 1.69 h fall below 24 h, both same-day respins). The widened window therefore equals the deployed window in 24/26 cases and the trend statistic buys zero extra changesets on release. Data: spike/_release_recon/w06_full.json gap_h column.

kills.idea: The interesting-file filter (utils.is_interesting_file) is what hides the major release build's candidates - admit .js/.mjs/.yaml and the window fills up
kills.why_dead: Wrong by two orders of magnitude. Re-running the same 6 major windows with file_filter=lambda f: True takes candidate-bearing from 0/1/0/2/0/0 to 46/16/12/19/16/14 - the release-branch config and repo-update commits, not the cycle's work - because pushlog.collect sets files = [] for merge members BEFORE any filter is consulted. The filter is irrelevant here; the file-drop is the whole mechanism.

kills.idea: Reuse beta's item-8 rule (drop a build-day with no users) to keep the merge window out of the selector on release
kills.why_dead: Inverted on release. On beta the merge-day build was a distinct near-empty build (0-7 installs) the selector never picked. On release the merge-day build IS the shipped major: buildid == the merge pushdate in 35/35 builds, and 20260812182057 (154.0) reported 6,563 crashes from 5,031 distinct installations in three days, 18 days after ship. There is no low-user build to drop.

kills.idea: Add a size threshold on merge pushes so release keeps extracting normal pushes and skips the big ones
kills.why_dead: Unnecessary, and plan #18 already killed the general form. is_merge_push fires on 8 of 8 release cycle merges measured (14-22 merge-flagged changesets among 5,405-7,464 members), and the separation from ordinary release pushes is total: 20 dot windows span 5-116 changesets. A threshold would add a per-branch constant for a predicate that already works.

kills.idea: Fix the release on-stack window by fetching the merge push without full=1 to save bytes
kills.why_dead: Solves the wrong half. The 655 KB vs 11.9 MB saving is real (windows_03_merge.py vs windows_06_full.py) and worth taking on the OFF-STACK fetch, but it cannot help the on-stack path: with no file lists there is nothing for Changeset.add to make changesets rows from, which is exactly the state that already yields 0 candidates.

kills.idea: Treat the beta-vs-release difference as 'release windows are just bigger, so widen the thresholds'
kills.why_dead: The distributions do not overlap and the direction reverses. Release windows are BIMODAL: 5-116 changesets (20 dot windows) or 5,405-7,464 (6 major windows), with nothing in between, and the big mode belongs to the build with all the users rather than to a build with none. No single window-size threshold describes release, which is why this has to be a per-window-kind decision, not a tuned number.

open_questions: Ship release on-stack at all? Measured: the deployed window can contain the regressor for 2.4% of release crash regressions (5 of 207, ~0.6/cycle) and produces 0 candidates on 57 of 58 crash x build pairs. Choose (a) release off-stack-only, planned and priced as ~100% off-stack; (b) admit the cycle merge as a first-class release window (needs the cross-channel node-set query + ~90-day nightly retention, or 2,905 patch.parse ~= 3.1 h of serial queue per cycle); (c) do not ship release. RECOMMENDATION: (a) for a first canary, and (b) only if the major-build class is wanted, because (b) is the only version that can ever name a nightly-cycle regressor.

If the merge window IS admitted, what may a filed bug claim? Every candidate is via_merge, so is_suspected_regression is False for all of them and the bug says 'Starting point - NOT a suspected cause'. Choose: file with that prose, or suppress filing on a build whose window is a cycle merge and surface it on crashstack.html only. RECOMMENDATION: suppress filing from the major build for the first cycle and read the dossiers.

Fix the off-stack ranking tier order, or raise max_candidates? Measured: tier(non-backout AND pref_flip) = 294 vs cap 150 on a release merge window, and the two best token-overlap changesets are dropped. Choose: move pref_flip below the signature<->description overlap, gate the tier on len(tier) < cap, or raise the cap to ~350. RECOMMENDATION: move pref_flip below overlap - raising the cap trebles the agent's candidate prose for a window where 4.9% of changesets are pref-flips by accident.

Does max_ndays become per-channel? A release fix needs ~90 days of NIGHTLY nodes (max observed cycle age 58.2 d plus the ~30 d a major build stays current) while nightly's own window needs 30. Choose one global 90 or per-channel retention. RECOMMENDATION: per-channel - Node.clean is already called per channel, and a global 90 changes nightly's pruning for no reason.

Does the release plan get its own tests/test_release_windows.py? The beta file pins the OPPOSITE conclusion for the same mechanism. RECOMMENDATION: yes, pinning three release-specific facts: buildid == node pushdate (35/35), the merge sits at the major build's inclusive upper bound, and Changeset.find returns nothing there.
cross_dimension: SELECTION/POPULATION: build 20260826195058 (155.0, shipped 2026-08-26) had exactly 2 crash reports in SuperSearch on 2026-08-31, while 154.0.1 had 52,388 and 154.0 46,694. A release major appears in Buildhub and in `builds` days-to-weeks before it has crash data (staged rollout), so get_last_versions(n=3) will hold a build-day with no reports at the top of the window - the mirror image of beta's merge-day problem, and item 8's 'only if it is not the newest' rule is what protects it. Someone should measure the release rollout curve before trusting the newest build row.

SELECTION: Buildhub's release channel carries RESPINS - two build rows for the same version with different revisions (150.0.2 at 20260506041011 and 20260506140522, 9.92 h apart; 151.0 at 20260513195118 and 20260516144017, 66.8 h apart; 153.0.1 at 20260727110312 and 20260727124451, 1.69 h apart). uix_builds is (buildid, product, channel) so both land, and a 3-deep selection window can be two rows of the same version hours apart. VERSION_PATS["release"] admits all of them.

INGESTION: release crash frames use the git URI form and inspector.git2hg (lando) resolves them correctly - 40 of 40 sampled reports on 154.0/154.0.1/155.0 had frame nodes equal to the Buildhub build revision (8b532c2140db 48x, 9ce1ee6baeb9, 21a096119103), so inspect_stacktrace's node-mismatch bail-out does not fire on release. Side fact: json-rev for 8b532c2140db is 2.4 MB (a repo-update commit touching 12 files), so per-changeset hg reads on release can be far larger than on nightly.

COST/OPS: Node.clean deletes a release cycle merge's ~7,000 nodes at one instant 30 days after the merge, and builds.nodeid is ON DELETE CASCADE, so the MAJOR build's `builds` row disappears then. In the cycles measured every dot release ships before that (152.0.6 is the latest at 33 days and its predecessor row is 152.0.5), so no window actually jumps - but Build.get_id returning None sends put_crashes down its `errors` branch for that buildid, and 16.8% of release installations reporting crashes are already on builds older than 30 days.

UI: html.py:626 renders pushlog_for_buildid_url, which for a major release build is a pushloghtml?fromchange=...&tochange=... link spanning 5,405-7,464 changesets. Nothing fetches it server-side, but it is a link that will not render; worth degrading to the merge push's own page.

LLM: searchfox.repo_for_channel maps release -> Repo.RELEASE -> tree firefox-release. I did not verify that tree is indexed - the beta note at searchfox.py:176-180 verified firefox-beta explicitly and there is no equivalent line for release.

reports.headline: The LLM half is in better shape for release than plan #18 §11 implies: `compiled_out._CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]`, `_CHANNEL_OFF_HOLLOW["release"]`, `roles._BUILD_NAME`, `triage._CHANNEL_LABEL`, `searchfox._CHANNEL_REPO["release"]` and the per-channel `_system_prompt` cache all exist, and I verified each against mozilla-release's OWN source at tip AND at a real 154.0.1 build rev — every macro answer is right, and firefox-release is genuinely indexed (rev `d065a04b`, version 155.0) and measurably CLOSER to the build than firefox-main on 6 of 8 crash-relevant files. What is missing is measurement, not wiring: `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` has no release arm, so on the channel with the highest and most STABLE hardware-noise rate (bit-flip 8.91%, broken-CPU 5.79%, n=3,759,071 reports; 9.18/8.47/9.06% across three sub-windows) the prompt prints a bare "50% carry a bit-flip annotation" with no denominator — and one sentence in `_cpu_spread_line` (triage.py:588-590) prints a nightly-sample claim ("9 of the 26 at 100%, against 118 of the 200 overall") unconditionally, immediately after telling the model that sample does not exist for this channel. That sentence is a live BETA bug today. The measured landing-date shift is release = central + 14.7 to 49.9 days (median ~28-31), and `sigage.ORIGIN_CHANNEL` is a single hop to nightly, so the 2 of 18 merge members that are beta uplifts (central has never heard of them; beta answers 18/18) fall back to the release merge date — 23.4 days late, straight into `_bug_for_this_regression`'s 30-day venue window. Cost is decided by `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release = 20`, which nobody measured: at the same draw beta's cap-5 yields 3.7 LLM runs per selection and release's cap-20 yields 8.2. Separately, verifying the release arm uncovered a live beta defect: the `is_early_beta_or_earlier = is_nightly` alias only landed in the 155 cycle, and at every earlier rev `build/defines.sh` carries `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER=1` for ~39% of the beta cycle — so the beta partition is wrong in both directions on an early-beta build, while release is immune at all 10 revs I sampled.

gaps.title: `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` has no release arm, so the hardware-noise paragraph on release prints a share with no denominator — on the channel where the denominator is biggest and most stable
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `population_bit_flip_rate("release")`/`population_broken_cpu_rate("release")` return None (release is deliberately absent), so `_hardware_noise_lines` renders "Of its 120 reports, 50% carry a Socorro bit-flip annotation; and 20% come from a known-defective Intel Raptor Lake CPU" with NO population figure, immediately followed by "the higher these are, the likelier it is that this signature is a failing-hardware artefact ... any mechanism you can construct for it will be fiction that fits". The docstring at sigage.py:492 says it itself: "a bare 50% is unreadable: a model cannot know whether that is alarming". Release is exactly where this bites — its population flip rate is 3.6x nightly's shipped constant, so an ORDINARY release signature reads as alarming to a model with no baseline. `POPULATION_LABEL` also has no release key, so `population_label("release")` returns the bare "Firefox" (harmless only because it is read solely inside the branch a rate exists for).
gaps.evidence: Measured with `hardware_noise`'s exact query shape (Firefox, `get_search_channel(channel)`, 364-day window, facets `possible_bit_flips_max_confidence` + `cpu_info`, `_facets_size` 200) — spike/_release_recon/llm_10_pop_rates.py: release n=3,759,071, flip 334,970 = 8.91%, Raptor Lake 217,525 = 5.79%. The instrument reproduces the shipped beta constants (6.72%/5.85% against the recorded 6.75%/5.82%), so it is the same instrument. Stability, spike/_release_recon/llm_11_pop_stability.py: release flip 9.18% (2026-03..06, n=1,843,049) / 8.47% (06..08, n=1,314,841) / 9.06% (08, n=601,190); Raptor Lake 5.06/6.75/5.90%. Release is the most stable of the three channels — nightly's flip rate over the same sub-windows runs 2.32 / 5.61 / 14.99%. `top_cpu_share`: measured the way nightly's 0.32 was (signatures with >=5 reports in a 14-day window, sampled, then `sigage.hardware_noise` per signature) — spike/_release_recon/llm_13_topcpu_full.py: 2,612 release signatures qualified, 200 sampled, 196 measured; min 0.04, p25 0.09, MEDIAN 0.138, p75 0.25, max 1.00, and 2 of 196 (1%) sit on exactly one model against nightly's 26 of 200 (13%).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show release's rate is not a constant (which would force `None`). Month-by-month it moves 8.47-9.18%, a ±4% relative band — versus nightly, whose same-instrument flip rate moved 2.32% -> 14.99% inside the window and no longer reproduces its own shipped 0.025. So the release arm is BETTER founded than the nightly one it would sit next to. I also checked that 10% sampling cannot distort it: numerator and denominator are sampled identically, so the ratio is unaffected.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"release": {"bit_flip": 0.089, "broken_cpu": 0.058, "top_cpu_share": 0.138}` to `_POPULATION_RATES` and `"release": "Firefox-release"` to `POPULATION_LABEL`, with the denominators in the comment (n=3,759,071 reports 2026-08-31, and 196 of 2,612 signatures for the median). Shipping the median REQUIRES the next finding first: the "13% of them (26 of 200 sampled 2026-08-21)" literal at triage.py:573 is nightly's and would print beside a release median.

gaps.title: `_cpu_spread_line`'s closing sentence prints a nightly-sample claim on EVERY channel, contradicting the "not measured" sentence two clauses earlier — live on beta today
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The `background` half is correctly per-channel (None -> "how concentrated a typical signature on this channel is has NOT been measured ... treat the number above as unbenchmarked"), but the sentence AFTER it is unconditional: "concentration is not support for a bug either, since in that same sample the most concentrated signatures carry a known Firefox bug LESS often than the rest (9 of the 26 at 100%, against 118 of the 200 overall)". On release and on beta the prompt therefore says the sample does not exist for this channel and then quotes it. On release the quoted figure is wrong by 13x: 2 of 196 sit at 100%, not 26 of 200. And the moment a release `top_cpu_share` median ships, the OTHER nightly literal at :573 ("13% of them (26 of 200 sampled 2026-08-21)") starts printing next to a release median too.
gaps.evidence: Rendered the real function per channel with a fixed noise dict (spike/_release_recon/llm_14_render.py): the beta and release outputs both contain "has NOT been measured (the 32% figure this note quotes elsewhere is Firefox-nightly's)" and, 40 words later, "(9 of the 26 at 100%, against 118 of the 200 overall)". Release's own value of that statistic, measured the same way as nightly's (spike/_release_recon/llm_13_topcpu_full.py, n=196 of 2,612 qualifying signatures): 2 at 100% (1%), median 0.138 vs nightly's 0.32.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the sentence is guarded anywhere upstream — it is not: the `return (...)` at triage.py:581-591 concatenates it after `{background}` with no channel test, and `_cpu_spread_line`'s only channel-dependent input is `median`. I also checked whether the claim might be channel-invariant (a bug-rate ratio rather than a share); it is not, because both its numerator (26 at 100%) and denominator (200) are the nightly draw, and release's draw gives 2 and 196.
gaps.proposed_fix: Move the "9 of the 26 / 118 of the 200" clause inside the `median is not None` branch and render its two counts from the same per-channel table as the median (nightly 26/200 and 9/26; release 2/196, or drop the bug-collision half for release and keep only "one processor model is ORDINARY"). Per the rule at sigage.py:391 an unmeasured comparison is DROPPED, not borrowed — and this one is currently printed at zero cost to the drop.

gaps.title: `second_opinion._SYSTEM` is channel-blind: it never names the tree its searchfox tools read and gets no revision-drift paragraph
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `SearchfoxCtx(client=..., channel=channel)` at second_opinion.py:129 correctly points the blind reviewer's searchfox at `mozilla-release`, but `_SYSTEM` is a module constant passed verbatim (`system_prompt=_SYSTEM`) and its only statement about trees is "mcp__source__raw_file reads source AS OF the crash build — leak-free, searchfox is tip-only" (line 62). It never says WHICH tip, and it never gets `triage._drift_paragraph`. So the second opinion — which refutes 74% of leads and decides the fold — reads firefox-release at 155.0 while judging a 154.0.1 build, is told nothing about the branch, and has no instruction that a line delta is expected drift. Plan #18 item 13 fixed the ctx here and item 16 fixed `system.md` and `roles.py`; nobody fixed `_SYSTEM`, so this is already wrong for every beta run in prod.
gaps.evidence: `grep -n "repo\|drift\|tip\|_system_prompt\|mozilla-" crashclouseau/agent/second_opinion.py` returns only the docstring, line 62's "tip-only", and the `Reporter` lines — no repo token, no substitution, no call to `triage._system_prompt`. `build_options` (second_opinion.py:149) passes `system_prompt=_SYSTEM` unmodified. Measured drift the SO is blind to (spike/_release_recon/llm_24_sfdrift.py): at the release 154.0.1 build rev vs firefox-release, `dom/base/nsINode.cpp` is 4,724 lines in the build and 4,875 in the tree with a max matching-block shift of 151 lines; `js/src/gc/GC.cpp` 6,097 vs 6,151, shift 54.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the SO's tight allowlist keeps it away from searchfox (it does not — `roles.searchfox_tool_ids()` is the first entry of `allowed`), and whether the shared `triage._crash_facts` might carry the tree (it does not; the only channel token the SO prints is `"Channel: {}"` at second_opinion.py:90).
gaps.proposed_fix: Make `_SYSTEM` a function of the channel exactly as `roles._compiled_out_text` and `triage._system_prompt` already are: substitute the tree name into line 62 and append `triage._drift_paragraph(repo, channel)` for a non-nightly crash. Keep the nightly rendering byte-identical so the SO's existing behaviour and cost do not move.

gaps.title: `sigage.ORIGIN_CHANNEL` is one hop, but a release changeset is two: the beta-uplift class falls back to the release merge date, up to 23.4 days late
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `landing_pair` asks mozilla-central and falls back to the crash's own repo. On release the chain is central -> beta -> release, so a change UPLIFTED to beta (an hg graft with a fresh hash) is unknown to central and known only to beta; `landing_pair` then returns the RELEASE merge date. Five consumers read that number and all five want "when did this code first exist": the seed's `candidate_pushdates`, `triage._user_prompt`'s `landed=`/`arrived-with-the-cycle-merge=` label (triage.py:1436-1445), `_apply_signature_age_gate`, `_offstack_candidates`' recency tiebreak, and `bugzilla_apply._candidate_landed` -> `_bug_for_this_regression`'s `comment_max_bug_age_days` = 30 window. A clock up to 49.9 days late errs toward accepting an OLD bug as this crash's venue — the direction the file-only-new-bugs rule forbids — and on release the max is comfortably past 30 where on beta it was marginal (34.8).
gaps.evidence: Two real mozilla-release cycle merges, members resolved on all three repos via `sigage.json_rev` (spike/_release_recon/llm_16_shift.py, llm_30_merge2.py). Push 6069 (2026-08-26T19:50:58, 5,391 changesets, 5,370 non-merge), 10 sampled: all 10 report the release merge date; release-vs-central shift min 14.7 / median 26.6 / max 36.0 days; central knew 9/10, beta 10/10; the one central did not know (`4bf71cade253`) is a beta uplift beta dates at 2026-08-25 (1.3 d before the merge). Push 5982 (2026-08-12T18:20:57, 7,448 changesets), 8 sampled: release-vs-central min 26.9 / median 30.9 / max 49.9 days; release-vs-beta 23.0-23.4 days; central knew 7/8, beta 8/8; `b628ee0441f4` again central-unknown, beta-known. Combined: central 16/18 (88.9%), beta 18/18 (100%). Release merge cadence measured 27.93 then 14.06 days (spike/_release_recon/llm_17_classify.py).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show the whole thing is moot because release candidates are all grafts: spike/_release_recon/llm_19_uplift_shift.py resolved 14 release CODE pushes (the ride-along window) and central knew 0/14, beta knew 0/14 — for those the release push date IS the landing date and `landing_pair` is already right. So the gap is confined to the MERGE population, which is where 5,391-7,448 of the candidates live, and there the beta hop is worth exactly 2/18 of the members and 23.4 days on the one that needs it.
gaps.proposed_fix: Turn `ORIGIN_CHANNEL` into a per-channel ordered chain (`nightly` for beta; `nightly` then `beta` for release) and stop at the first repo that knows the node. Cost is one extra `json-rev` only on the 11% central misses; better still, follow `build_related_bugs_note`'s own KNOWN GAP note and hand `_candidate_landed` the pushdate the run already computed instead of re-asking hg. Store both dates on the candidate so the prompt can say "landed on central <date>, reached beta <date>, shipped to release <date>".

gaps.title: Two role prompts and one schema default still hand the model `"repo":"mozilla-central"` on a non-nightly run
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `triage._system_prompt` substitutes `"repo": "mozilla-central"` in system.md, but `make_role` only swaps the `_COMPILED_OUT` block — so the handoff JSON EXAMPLE in the call-graph-explorer and data-flow-tracer prompts still tells the two roles that produce every `SearchfoxCitation` to record `mozilla-central`, while `SearchfoxCtx.repo` is `mozilla-release` and every permalink they copy is `searchfox.org/firefox-release/...`. `StructLayoutCitation.repo` defaults to `"mozilla-central"` on top of that. The filed bug then cites firefox-release permalinks tagged as trunk, and nothing downstream can tell which tree was read.
gaps.evidence: `roles.build_roles(None, channel="release")` -> call-graph-explorer prompt contains `mozilla-central` x1, data-flow-tracer x1 (unchanged from the nightly rendering); `triage._system_prompt("release")` contains `mozilla-release` x5 as expected. `schema.StructLayoutCitation.model_fields["repo"].default == "mozilla-central"`. Measured by importing both modules and counting occurrences per channel.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the deterministic consumer is protected: `orchestrator._resolve_struct_layout` calls `client.field_layout(cit.type_name, repo=repo)` with the crash's own tree (orchestrator.py:3023, with a comment saying exactly why), so the GATE is safe and only the recorded provenance is wrong. That downgrades this from a gate defect to a citation-provenance defect — still wrong in a bug we file.
gaps.proposed_fix: Render both `_ROLES` prompt examples from the resolved repo in `make_role` (same targeted-replace trick already used for `_COMPILED_OUT`), and make `StructLayoutCitation.repo` default to `""` with the resolver filling it, or default it from `compiled_out.build_channel()` via `searchfox.repo_for_channel`.

gaps.title: The "new to this channel" block tells a release run its cycle merge comes from mozilla-central; it comes from mozilla-beta
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `_channel_age_lines` renders "...which for a change that rode this cycle's merge from mozilla-central is the nightly debut" and `_NEW_TO_CHANNEL_GUIDANCE` renders "a change uplifted onto this branch, or a change that came in with the merge from mozilla-central and only now ships here". Both are true for beta and wrong for release: a release build's cycle merge is beta -> release, and the change crossed TWO merges. This is the one block on release that says "treat the window below as TRUSTWORTHY", so it is precisely where the model is told where to look — and it points `mcp__history__file_history channel=nightly` at trunk when the immediate parent (and the only repo that dates a beta uplift) is mozilla-beta.
gaps.evidence: Rendered directly: with `channel="release"`, `signature_first_seen_channel=20260820000000`, `signature_first_seen_ever=20200101000000`, `buildid=20260824154132`, `_signature_age_lines` emits "...but it is NEW ON RELEASE: its first release report is build 20260820000000 (2026-08-20), 5 days before the build ... which for a change that rode this cycle's merge from mozilla-central is the nightly debut" plus the guidance naming mozilla-central again. Measured provenance: the 2026-08-26 mozilla-release merge push's own description is "No Bug - Update configs after merge day operations a=release" and its members carry beta pushdates for 18/18 sampled and central pushdates for 16/18, with release-vs-beta 13.2-23.4 days and release-vs-central 14.7-49.9 days (spike/_release_recon/llm_16_shift.py, llm_30_merge2.py). How often the block fires on release: 1 of 60 sampled signatures (1.7%) — spike/_release_recon/llm_26_ages.py.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the block is simply unreachable on release, which would make this cosmetic: it fires on 1 of 60 sampled signatures (1.7%), lower than beta's 4% but not zero, and it is the ONLY branch on release that does not print `_OLD_SIGNATURE_GUIDANCE` — so the 1.7% is the entire population this channel can name a regressor for.
gaps.proposed_fix: Parameterise the parent repo per channel (beta -> mozilla-central, release -> mozilla-beta) and say both hops on release: "the figure above is its debut ANYWHERE, which for a change that rode the merges from mozilla-central into mozilla-beta and then into this branch is the nightly debut, one to two cycles before release ever built it (measured 15-50 days)". Point the history affordance at mozilla-beta first for a release crash.

gaps.title: `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release = 20` is an unmeasured cost multiplier: 8.2 LLM runs per selection against beta's measured 3.7
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The proto cap is the dominant cost term off nightly — that is the plan's own measured finding for beta, which moved 20 -> 5 for it. Release still sits at 20, a value nothing measured. Every selected (signature, build) pair fans out to up to 20 paid runs; at the observed per-run price band that is $20-60 per selection for the busy pairs.
gaps.evidence: Random sample of 20 signatures with >=5 reports on release build 20260824154132 (spike/_release_recon/llm_23_protos_random.py, `_facets=proto_signature`, size 200): protos/pair median 6, p75 13, max 178 (facet-capped); the configured cap 20 lets 165 runs through for 20 selections = 8.2 per selection. Same draw on beta 155.0b5: median 5, p75 14, max 200, cap 5 -> 74 runs / 20 selections = 3.7. Same draw on nightly 20260826205548 (16 qualifying signatures): median 4.5, p75 7, max 17, cap 50 -> 5.6. Top-8-loudest draw for the tail (llm_21_protos.py): release protos/pair median 128, three signatures at the 200-term facet ceiling.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My first draw was the 8 LOUDEST signatures, which gave release a median of 128 and would have justified a much lower cap; I redrew uniformly from the 634 signatures with >=5 reports on the same build and the median fell to 6, so the '4x worse than beta' story is an artefact of the draw. The honest statement is that release and beta have nearly the SAME proto distribution and only the CAP differs by 4x. I also note my draw over-represents busy signatures relative to nightly's real selections (67% of which are single-crash from-zero fires with 1 proto by construction), so the nightly row here is not comparable to the config docstring's 1.07.
gaps.proposed_fix: Set `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release` to 5 for parity with beta until a release dossier yield exists, and record in `config.get_threshold`'s docstring the measurement above with its draw and denominator (20 of 634 signatures on build 20260824154132). If cost is the binding constraint, 3 gives ~2.5 runs/selection at the same draw.

gaps.title: `tests/test_prompt_budget.py` has nightly and beta rows but no release rows, and `_log_prompt_budget` does not log the channel
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The budget test is the only instrument in the repo that can see prompt growth (its own docstring: the v109 +1,914-byte growth was found weeks later by rebuilding 500 prompts offline). Its beta rows exist for a stated reason — "without a beta fixture a beta-only sentence adds ZERO bytes to the four numbers above and the ledger stays green". The same hole opens for release: a release-only sentence is invisible. And `_log_prompt_budget` logs `system=%d user=%d (crash facts=%d)` with no channel, so with three or four channels live the log line can no longer distinguish "release prompts are bigger" from "we grew the prompt".
gaps.evidence: Measured the release values so they can be pinned: `len(triage._system_prompt("release"))` = 17,676 (nightly 17,115, beta 17,655, aurora 17,659); on the test file's own plain-deref fixture, crash facts 219 and user prompt 988 for release (identical to nightly — the channel is a switch, not a paragraph, exactly as the beta row asserts); on a release two-age fixture, crash facts 1,654 and user prompt 2,423 against beta's pinned 1,342 and 2,108. grep of the test file shows rows for `system.md, beta`, `crash facts, plain deref (beta)`, `user prompt, plain deref (beta)`, `crash facts, beta with two signature ages`, `user prompt, beta with two signature ages` and none for release.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the beta rows already cover release by proxy — they do not: the release two-age numbers are +312/+315 bytes over beta's, because the age figures themselves are an order of magnitude larger on release (median age_ever 1,473 days vs beta's cycle-offset ages), so a beta tolerance of 200/300 would not hold a release regression.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add five release rows with the measured values above and a `_release(crash, ages=False)` fixture mirroring `_beta`. Add `channel=%s` to the `_log_prompt_budget` log line — one format argument, and it makes the per-channel ledger groupable in production.

gaps.title: `compiled_out._CHANNEL_MACROS` is keyed on the channel LABEL while the semantics live in the BUILD's source rev — release survives that, beta does not
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing on release — this is the falsification result, and it is the positive half of the finding. But the same table is wrong for BETA, which is triaged in prod today: the `is_early_beta_or_earlier = is_nightly` alias the beta arm was justified from only landed in the 155 cycle. At every earlier rev `is_early_beta_or_earlier` is True when `build/defines.sh` sets a non-empty `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER` and `app_version_display` contains 'a' or 'b', and `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED` is gated on `moz_debug | milestone.is_early_beta_or_earlier` with NO `moz_dev_edition` term. So on an early-beta build both macros are ON while `_CHANNEL_MACROS["beta"]` lists them as "genuinely ABSENT from this build, and it is free to say so": the prompt grants a false veto, `is_build_flag_ground` lets the claim BIND and abstain a good lead, and `_CHANNEL_OFF_HOLLOW["beta"]` lets `hollow_symbols` deterministically suppress a verdict behind a macro that is actually defined — with no LLM in the loop.
gaps.evidence: Read from each branch's own source at real build revs via `hgedge.raw_file` (spike/_release_recon/llm_01_configure.py, llm_08_pinned_configure.py, llm_09_ebe.py, llm_32_ebe_beta.py). mozilla-release tip (milestone 155.0): `is_nightly = None`, `is_release_or_beta = True` (init.configure:1113-1121), `set_define("NIGHTLY_BUILD", milestone.is_nightly)` :1166, `set_define("RELEASE_OR_BETA", ...)` :1168, `is_early_beta_or_earlier=is_nightly` :1140, `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED when=moz_debug | milestone.is_nightly | moz_dev_edition` (moz.configure:169-178), `debug_defines` returns `["NDEBUG", "TRIMMED"]` :191, `MOZ_ESR` from `app_version_display.endswith("esr")` :1141 = off. At the 154.0.1 build rev `8b532c2140db` the OLD form: `is_early_beta_or_earlier` from `build/defines.sh` + an 'a'/'b' in version_display (:1122-1137), `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED when=moz_debug | milestone.is_early_beta_or_earlier` (:146-155). Ten release revs sampled 152.0.5 -> 155.0: alias False at nine, True at 155.0, and version_display never contains 'a'/'b', so both macros are OFF at every one. Beta: alias False at 153.0b7/b8/b9, True at 156.0b1. `build/defines.sh` filelog on mozilla-beta shows two changes per cycle — `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER=1` at "Promote main to beta" (154 cycle 2026-07-20, 153 cycle 2026-06-15) and `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER=` at "Update configs after merge day" (2026-07-31 at 154.0b6, 2026-06-26 at 153.0b6) — i.e. ON for ~11 of the 27.9-day cycle = 39%. `_compiled_out_text("release")` renders correctly (2,064 bytes; `channel_on` = MOZILLA_OFFICIAL/NDEBUG/RELEASE_OR_BETA, `channel_off` = DEBUG/EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER/MOZ_ASSERT_ENABLED/MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED/NIGHTLY_BUILD, no 9-11% clause).
gaps.falsification_attempt: This finding IS the falsification attempt: I set out to prove `_CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]` wrong by reading the release branch's own source rather than central's, and read it at TWO revs a cycle apart because the release branch is always behind. Release survived both. The beta half fell out of the same probe, and I then verified it end to end rather than inferring it — I found the actual `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER=1` string at two "Promote main to beta" revs and the empty value at the two "Update configs" revs that follow, on both the 153 and 154 cycles.
gaps.proposed_fix: For release: ship as-is, and add a comment recording that the partition was verified at both the pre-alias (`8b532c2140db`, 154.0.1) and post-alias (tip, 155.0) forms and why release is immune to the difference (`app_version_display` never contains 'a'/'b'). For beta: key `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER`/`MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED` on the BUILD REV's own `build/defines.sh` + version_display rather than on the channel label — `_configure_text` already reads at `pin_rev`, so the reader exists; it is the static table beside it that is channel-keyed. Do NOT relax the beta arm globally: at post-155 revs the current values are right.

gaps.title: The searchfox tool descriptions enumerate nightly and beta only, and point release at the wrong intermediate tree
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `calls_from`'s `repo` description reads "default: THIS CRASH'S OWN repo -- mozilla-central for a nightly crash, mozilla-beta for a beta/DevEdition one" — an enumeration that does not contain the release case, so a release run's model is left to guess what its default is. The other six tools say "pass mozilla-central to look at trunk even for a beta crash", hard-coding beta. For release the useful intermediate is mozilla-BETA (it is the immediate parent and the only repo that dates a beta uplift: 18/18 merge members resolve there against central's 16/18), and the tool text never mentions it.
gaps.evidence: Read the seven `Field(description=...)` strings directly. `tools/history.py`'s module docstring (:16-17) already gets this right — "pass `nightly` to query mozilla-central ... even for a beta/release crash" — so the affordance the beta plan named as the model to copy names release and the searchfox one does not. Cross-repo knowledge measured in spike/_release_recon/llm_16_shift.py and llm_30_merge2.py: central 16/18, beta 18/18 on release merge members; central 0/14, beta 0/14 on release ride-along pushes.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I confirmed the DEFAULT is correct regardless of the text — `SearchfoxCtx.repo` resolves through `repo_for_channel` (searchfox_cg.py:63-65) and `repo_or` applies it to all seven tools — so this is a description defect, not a behaviour defect. That is why it is quality and not correctness.
gaps.proposed_fix: Render the enumeration from `searchfox._CHANNEL_REPO` instead of restating it, or at minimum add "mozilla-release for a release crash" and change the six "even for a beta crash" strings to "even for a beta/release crash; for a release crash mozilla-beta is the intermediate branch where an uplift's own landing lives".

gaps.title: The skeptic's pref clause forbids a `fail` that is free on release, the same free kill the beta work restored for `#ifdef NIGHTLY_BUILD`
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Limit (3) says "A path reachable only when a `StaticPrefList.yaml` pref is on is `unverifiable`, NEVER `fail`: the YAML default is not what shipped (16 prefs ship the opposite value from firefox.js; 82 more default to a nightly-on build template)". On release a pref whose YAML default IS that nightly-on build template is genuinely off, so "this path needs pref X, which is nightly-only" is exactly as true and as free as the `#ifdef NIGHTLY_BUILD` conclusion the beta work went to trouble to unlock — and the clause forbids it. The direction is safe (it only refuses a suppression), so this costs correct noise-kills, not correctness.
gaps.evidence: Rendered `_compiled_out_text("release")`: the clause is present verbatim, with the words "a nightly-on build template" in a prompt whose preceding sentence says "This crash is on release, NOT nightly: code behind `#ifdef NIGHTLY_BUILD` ... is genuinely ABSENT from this build ... that is `fail`". The two sentences give opposite instructions about the same milestone predicate depending on whether it is spelled as a macro or as a pref default.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked the size of the population before claiming it matters: `searchfox-cli -R mozilla-release -q NIGHTLY_BUILD --cpp` returns 368 hits against EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER 20, RELEASE_OR_BETA 77 and MOZ_ESR 5, so NIGHTLY_BUILD is 78% of the channel-gate surface in C++ — but I did NOT measure the pref-template population on release, so the size of this particular win is unknown and I am reporting it as a quality item rather than a threshold to move.
gaps.proposed_fix: Split limit (3) per channel: keep the blanket "NEVER fail" for the 16 firefox.js-overridden prefs on every channel, and off nightly add "a pref whose `StaticPrefList.yaml` default is the nightly-on build template IS off in this build — cite the YAML line and the channel and that is `fail`". Measure the firing rate on a release back-test before trusting it, per the same rule item 14 set for beta.

gaps.title: Nothing in any prompt tells the model that release is 10%-sampled, or that the crash reached shipped users
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Answering question 7 directly: I found NO prompt anywhere that asserts the crash is on a pre-release channel — `system.md` never contains the word "nightly", and the only channel statement is `Channel: {channel}` at triage.py:1324 plus the (correct) per-channel compiled-out and drift blocks. The gap is the other direction: nothing states the stakes. `mcp__socorro__crash_stats` prints "crash-stats for [@ sig] (product Firefox, channel release, last 30d): N crashes" where N is a 10%-sampled count, unlabelled; and `_first_seen_line` prints "N of this signature's M reports are on other channels", mixing a sampled release numerator with unsampled nightly/beta/esr ones, which overstates off-channel presence and pushes toward "a recent changeset can at most have EXPOSED it".
gaps.evidence: `grep -rn -i "sampl" crashclouseau/agent/prompts/*.md crashclouseau/agent/roles.py crashclouseau/agent/second_opinion.py crashclouseau/agent/tools/*.py` returns only `ProgramD3D::getSamplerMapping` in a backtick example — no sampling statement reaches any prompt. `grep -rn -i "pre-release\|opt in\|early adopter"` returns nothing. The 10% figure is stated three times in the repo (sigage.py:120, sigage.py:398, sigtrend.py:129) and never in a prompt. Off-channel share measured over 40 release signatures with >=5 reports on build 20260824154132 (spike/_release_recon/llm_28_offchannel.py): median 0.278, max 0.976, and `other_channel_floor`=20 clears on 38 of 40 so `first_seen` is the all-channel value 95% of the time. Socorro's channel facet for one week shows `release` 144,236 and `esr` 116,608 as disjoint tokens, i.e. the off-channel mass on a release signature is largely ESR, which is not sampled the same way.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to measure the sampling rate rather than cite it: a release processed crash carries `throttleable` but no rate field (spike/_release_recon/llm_27_throttle.py), so I could not derive 10% from the data and I am relying on the repo's own three statements. I also checked that the RATES the hardware paragraph prints are immune (numerator and denominator are sampled identically, so 8.91% is unaffected) — only absolute COUNTS and cross-channel ratios are distorted.
gaps.proposed_fix: Two additions, both measured or citable: (a) in `tools/socorro.crash_stats`, when the channel is release, append "(release reports are Socorro-sampled, so the true count is roughly 10x this)" to the totals line and to the off-channel clause; (b) decide explicitly whether the user-population stakes belong in the prompt at all — see the open question. Do NOT borrow a nightly install figure for it.

Merge push 5982 (2026-08-12T18:20:57, 7,448 changesets), 8 sampled: release-vs-central min 26.9 / median 30.9 / max 49.9; release-vs-beta 23.0-23.4; central 7/8, beta 8/8. Combined central 16/18, beta 18/18. Release merge cadence 27.93 then 14.06 days; merges at 2026-07-15, 08-12, 08-26 carrying 6,888 / 7,448 / 5,391 changesets.

measurements.claim: `_CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]` is correct, verified against mozilla-release's own source at ten build revs spanning the `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER` alias change
measurements.method: `hgedge.raw_file` on `build/moz.configure/init.configure`, `moz.configure`, `config/milestone.txt`, `browser/config/version_display.txt` and `build/defines.sh` at mozilla-release tip and at every buildhub release revision from 152.0.5 to 155.0 (git2hg-resolved where needed)
measurements.numbers: tip (155.0): NIGHTLY_BUILD off, RELEASE_OR_BETA on, EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER = is_nightly = off, MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED `when=moz_debug|is_nightly|moz_dev_edition` = off, NDEBUG on, MOZ_ESR off. open_questions: Ship the measured release `top_cpu_share` median 0.138 (n=196 of 2,612 qualifying signatures), or leave it `None`? RECOMMENDATION: ship it, but only together with the fix that makes the "13% of them (26 of 200 sampled 2026-08-21)" and "9 of the 26 at 100%, against 118 of the 200 overall" literals per-channel — release measures 2 of 196 (1%), so shipping the median alone would put a 13x-wrong nightly count beside a correct release one.

`thresholds.protos.Firefox.release`: keep 20 (measured 8.2 LLM runs per selection), match beta at 5 (3.7), or take 3 (~2.5)? RECOMMENDATION: 5, for parity with the one channel where the fan-out was measured against real selections, until a release dossier yield exists; the release and beta proto distributions are nearly identical at the same draw (median 6 vs 5), so there is no evidence for a looser cap.

Should `landing_pair` take a per-channel ORDERED origin chain (release: central, then beta, then own) at the cost of one extra `json-rev` on the 11% of merge members central misses — or should the filer be handed the pushdate the run already computed, per `build_related_bugs_note`'s own KNOWN GAP note? RECOMMENDATION: do both, chain first: `_bug_for_this_regression`'s 30-day window is exposed to a clock up to 49.9 days late on release, and the fallback direction (accept an older bug as venue) is the one the file-only-new-bugs rule forbids.

Should any prompt state the release user-population stakes — that this build shipped to hundreds of millions rather than to opt-in testers? RECOMMENDATION: only if the sentence carries a measured number the pipeline already holds (the `stats` row's installation count for this signature+build), and NEVER a borrowed nightly figure. If no number is available, add nothing: I found no prompt that currently asserts the opposite, so silence is the honest default.

Does the beta `EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER` defect (ON for ~39% of every pre-155 beta cycle, while `_CHANNEL_MACROS["beta"]` calls it "genuinely absent, free to say so") get fixed as part of the release work, or as a separate beta correctness patch? cross_dimension: SELECTOR: buildhub lists a release 155.0 build stamped at exactly the mozilla-release merge push timestamp (2026-08-26T19:50:58, rev `21a096119103`) — the same merge-day zero-baseline shape plan #18 item 8 fixed for beta, where the counterfactual was 35 signatures / 142 runs -> 3 / 15. Whoever owns the selector should confirm item 8's `dropped_no_users` floor fires on release before ingestion is turned on.

INGESTION: `datacollector.get_changeset` (datacollector.py:566-608) now returns None on EVERY channel. Its Socorro filter is `topmost_filenames: '@"hg:hg.mozilla.org/".*:[0-9a-f]+'` and its regexp is `^.*:([0-9a-f]+)$`, but post-git-migration every term is `git:github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox:<path>:<git sha>` — verified None for release builds 20260824154132, 20260812182057, 20260825051950, and the facet has the same `git:` shape on nightly and beta. INGESTION/WINDOWS: an ordinary release window is the smallest and highest-signal in the project — 154.0 -> 154.0.1 (12 days) is 83 nodes with 8 touching an interesting file, and only 31 of 351 mozilla-release pushes over two months are code pushes (8.8%). On merge day the same window is 5,405 nodes / 2,051 interesting / 5,391 `via_merge`. `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction("release")` already returns True, so the beta merge rule covers release for free.

Same shape as beta (0 of 1,009 in-cycle beta changesets exist on m-c), so it is a pre-existing cost, not release's, but it is now 100% of the non-merge release candidate supply.

MEASUREMENT HYGIENE: the shipped `POPULATION_BIT_FLIP_RATE = 0.025` no longer reproduces.
