reports.headline: The declared/held machinery genuinely works for release today: `autofile_channel_declared("release")` is False and `autofile_bug` returns "channel 'release' has no autofile configuration" as its first statement, with net.get/post/put tripwires proving no BMO request is made — so the retrigger hazard is closed for ALL channels, not just beta. What is broken is the config shape: prod's live `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1` already makes `get_agent_autofile("release")` return `{enabled: True, daily_cap: 10, comment_on_existing: "comment"}`, so an overlay of `{}` — or beta's shape minus `enabled: false` — arms release at nightly's rules the moment it lands. Release must ship at `file_new`, not `comment`, and the reason is measured: 36 of the 71 signatures Clouseau has filed bugs for also crash on release (50.7%), and at `comment` mode 9 of those 36 (25.0%, Wilson 13.8-41.1%) collect a SECOND Clouseau bug — proven end-to-end against a real Postgres, where `skip`/`file_new` catch all 36 via the channel-blind `already_filed_for_signature`. The decisive question is value, not correctness: BMO's automated crash-bug filer has queried NIGHTLY on 137 of 137 bugs in 365 days ("By querying Release crashes" matches zero bugs), release-tracked crash bugs run 13-19 per 200 days and are hand-filed by aryx off NIGHTLY volumes, and across the top 350 release signatures there are exactly 2 un-bugged release-only Firefox-code signatures. My honest projection is ~2-5 bugs/month. My prior that release's venue rate exceeds beta's was FALSIFIED: measured the same way, release is 64%, nightly 64%, beta 60% — the panel, not the channel, produced the 58-59%-vs-23% contrast in config.py:548.

gaps.title: `config/global.json` has no `agent.autofile.channels.release`, and any overlay without an explicit `"enabled": false` arms release at nightly's rules under prod's live AUTOFILE_BUGS=1
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The instant `channels.release` appears in the JSON, `autofile_channel_declared("release")` flips True. `enabled` is absent -> it inherits the top-level default, which `_env_bool("AUTOFILE_BUGS", ...)` overrides to True in prod. Release then files unattended at `daily_cap: 10` and `comment_on_existing: "comment"` — posting the analysis and a needinfo into strangers' open bugs on a channel nobody has measured. Only an EXPLICIT `"enabled": false` is honoured as a per-channel veto (config.py:684, `channel_veto = over.get("enabled") is False`).
gaps.evidence: Measured with prod's env (spike/_release_recon/filing_01_config_probe.py, filing_18_gate_probe.py): today `autofile_channel_declared` is True for nightly/beta and False for release/esr/''/None/'Release'/'aurora'; `get_agent_autofile("release")` with AUTOFILE_BUGS=1 returns enabled=True cap=10 mode=comment needinfo=True minconf=70. The real `autofile_bug` with a release uuid_info and a rung-70 lead returns {'filed': False, 'skipped': "channel 'release' has no autofile configuration"} and the net.get/net.post/net.put AssertionError tripwires never fire, so the gate runs before any BMO call. Three overlay shapes probed: `{}` -> declared=True held=False, reaches the BMO venue lookup; `{'comment_on_existing':'skip','daily_cap':3}` -> declared=True held=False, armed; `{'enabled': false}` -> declared=True held=True, returns "autofile held for channel 'release' (triage-only)" and makes no call. Prod confirmed by `heroku config`: AUTOFILE_BUGS=1, AGENT_CHANNELS="nightly beta", INGEST_CHANNELS="nightly beta", release v139 = 3a584d8a.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"release": {"enabled": false, "comment_on_existing": "file_new", "daily_cap": 3}` — the `enabled: false` FIRST, as its own commit, exactly as beta shipped (bdd848c). Do not add a release overlay in the same change that arms it. Consider making `autofile_channel_declared` require an explicit `enabled` key for any non-default channel, so an incomplete edit reads as "gap" rather than "armed".
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show some other gate would stop an armed release run anyway. It does not: with `{}` as the overlay the probe reached `_open_bugs_for_signature` (the tripwire fired there, not earlier), so every gate above the venue lookup — verdict, suppressions, offstack observe-only, unsymbolicated, already_filed, daily cap, token — had already passed for a synthetic rung-70 lead. I also checked whether `get_agent_channels()` would hold it: it is ["nightly","beta"] and lives in `enqueue_agent`, which `enqueue_agent(..., force=True)` bypasses, so it protects only the non-retrigger path.

gaps.title: Ship release at `file_new`, not `comment`: 25% of the signatures Clouseau has already filed for would collect a SECOND bug on release
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `already_filed_for_signature` — the only guard that survives the target bug being CLOSED — is consulted ONLY when `comment_mode(cfg["comment_on_existing"]) != "comment"` (bugzilla_apply.py:1170). At `comment` mode a release run whose signature carries a Clouseau bug a human has since resolved INVALID/DUPLICATE/WORKSFORME/FIXED sees an empty `existing` (`_open_bugs_for_signature` filters `resolution: "---"`), never reaches `already_commented` (only asked about a CHOSEN venue), and files a duplicate of our own bug.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/filing_06_crosschannel.py + filing_11_hazard_rescue.py: 72 bugs the autofiler has filed since 2026-08-05 (via `depends_on` of the `clouseau` meta bug 1396527, creators cdenizet@mozilla.com AND clouseau-bot@mozilla.tld — the account changed 2026-08-27 and a cdenizet-only filter under-counts by 10), 71 parseable signatures. 36/71 = 50.7% (Wilson 39.3-62.0%) also crash on Firefox release in 21 days, against beta's 18/58 = 31% (models.py:2816). Of the 36: 20 our bug still OPEN, 16 CLOSED with nothing else covering the signature. `_fixed_after_build_bug` on each one's real loudest release build rescues 7 of 16, leaving 9/36 = 25.0% (Wilson 13.8-41.1%); resolutions INVALID x4, WORKSFORME, DUPLICATE, FIXED x3. PROVEN end-to-end on a disposable Postgres (filing_21_crosschannel_guards.py): with a nightly `new_bug` record for (bug 2063234, sig) and a release crash on the same signature — mode=comment + our bug open -> "already commented on bug 2063234", 0 writes; mode=comment + our bug closed -> filed=True, creates=1; mode=skip and mode=file_new -> "already filed bug 2063234 for this signature on release" in all four sub-cases, 0 writes. `already_filed_for_signature(sig, channel="release")` returns None, confirming the channel-blind call is what does the work.
gaps.proposed_fix: `"comment_on_existing": "file_new"` for release. `file_new` rather than `skip` because `skip` also discards the 36% of release selections with NO venue at all, and `build_related_bugs_note`'s `never_comment` branch already exists to say why the new bug is not a comment. Do NOT scope `already_filed_for_signature` to the channel — models.py:2837-2841 says why and my probe confirms the scoped call is blind to exactly this population.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show `comment` mode is safe because `already_commented` covers the cross-channel case. It covers the OPEN half only, and I proved that: 20 of 36 are caught by it (the nightly `new_bug` record carries bug + signature + filed:true, exactly `already_commented`'s key). I then tried to show `_fixed_after_build_bug` covers the closed half — it rescues 7 of 16, and two of those seven fire on 237-day and 256-day-old release builds, i.e. outside its own documented domain, so the rescue is partly luck. 9 remain.

gaps.title: Declaring release breaks exactly one test, and the guard release most depends on is behind a silent Postgres skip
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: CI goes red on the config commit unless the test is updated in the same change. Worse: the five tests that exercise `already_filed_for_signature` / `filed_bugs_since` / `record_filed_bug` — the exact machinery gap 2 depends on — SKIP silently without a Postgres, so a release rollout validated on the default `DATABASE_URL=sqlite://` invocation would ship the cross-channel dedup untested.
gaps.evidence: I temporarily added `"release": {"enabled": false, "comment_on_existing": "skip", "daily_cap": 3}` to config/global.json and ran tests.test_beta_autofile + tests.test_autofile + tests.test_beta_channel_wiring (203 tests): exactly 2 failures, both subTest(channel='release') of `test_an_undeclared_channel_files_nothing` — line 355 `assertFalse(res["filed"])` (the test's `_file_beta` mocks `get_agent_autofile`, so the `enabled: false` hold is NOT seen by the filer and it files) and line 365 `assertFalse(autofile_channel_declared(channel))`. Nothing else failed. Config reverted; `git status --porcelain` clean. Without Postgres the same run reports skipped=17; with a disposable postgres:16-alpine on :55432, tests.test_beta_autofile runs 22 tests, 0 skips, OK.
gaps.proposed_fix: In the config commit: move `release` out of the undeclared lists at :351 and :363 into the declared list, and add `test_the_shipped_config_holds_release_and_says_so` mirroring :303-310 — that is the only test that actually exercises the hold (it calls `self._file_beta(enabled=False)` explicitly). Put the Postgres recipe (tests/test_beta_autofile.py:44-48) in the release deploy checklist as a required step, and add a release arm to `TestTheFiledBugJsonbHalf` asserting `already_filed_for_signature(sig)` sees a nightly filing when the crash is release.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether some other test already covers release declaration so the surface is wider than one file: grepping `release` across test_autofile.py, test_beta_autofile.py and test_beta_channel_wiring.py finds release only as a repo/label argument in test_beta_channel_wiring (`SearchfoxCtx(channel="release").repo == "mozilla-release"`, `get_search_channel`), which the config change does not touch — and the 203-test run confirms only the two assertions move.

gaps.title: Memory-safety withholding is not actually in force: the canonical poison dossier is still served anonymously on the deployed release, and release multiplies the exposed installation count 23x
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `sensitive.is_withheld` reads a PERSISTED flag and a dossier written before the flag existed has no key, so it reads as not-withheld (sensitive.py:190-194 says so and names the backfill as the fix). The backfill has not run. Adding release does not change the sec-FILING rules — the poison-address -> restricted-bug path and the per-product groups are channel-independent — but it adds crashes affecting shipped users to a publishing surface that is anonymous and, for the back catalogue, unguarded.
gaps.evidence: On prod v139 (= 3a584d8a, which contains 40d678f/4b9d59a/33b9f52/7fb48d4/a5af683), `GET /api/evidence?uuid=41bb8c8a-3458-4803-90f8-a7a850260819` — the crash behind bug 2065051, the case sensitive.py's docstring opens on — returns HTTP 200 with the full dossier, `withheld: None`, and no `memory_unsafe` key in corroborations; crashstack.html for the same uuid returns 200 / 43,335 bytes. The live predicate DOES fire: Socorro's ProcessedCrash for that uuid carries address = 0xe5e5e5e5e5e5e5e8 in both fields and `sensitive.memory_unsafe_signals` returns ['fault address 0xe5e5e5e5e5e5e5e8 is allocator poison']. Exact-denominator poison rates per installation over 14 days (filing_13_poison_exact.py, SuperSearch `address` prefix over the 12 POISON_BYTES): release 1,462/208,674 = 0.70%, nightly 63/5,432 = 1.16%, beta 120/12,310 = 0.98% — release is LESS poison-dense per installation but carries 23x nightly's absolute poison installations.
gaps.proposed_fix: Run `bin/backfill_memory_unsafe.py --apply` before release ingestion starts and add it as a gate to the release deploy checklist. Nothing in the sec-filing rules needs to change for release. Separately, verify one withheld dossier renders through `build_evidence`'s withhold branch in prod — cb4bf6d fixed a 500 on that path a week ago and I could not find a withheld row to confirm it live.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to attribute the missing flag to a code bug rather than a missing backfill: `_record_sensitivity` writes the key only when `signals` is non-empty (`if not signals: return`), so an absent key is ambiguous between "predicate said no" and "code did not exist yet". I then ran the predicate against the live Socorro record and it fires, excluding "predicate said no" for this dossier. The remaining explanations are the un-run backfill or a seed whose raw_crash lacked `address`; the dossier's other corroborations are all pre-`memory_unsafe` keys, which fits the backfill explanation.

gaps.title: `daily_cap` must be set to 3 for release, or it inherits nightly's 10 with no measurement behind it
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing catastrophic — the cap is a blast-radius bound, not a rate control — but an un-overlaid release inherits `daily_cap: 10` while the measured expected rate is ~0.17/day, so a bad gate could put 10 unattended bugs a day on BMO before anyone notices. The cap is already per-channel (`filed_bugs_since(since, channel=channel)` joins `Build.channel`), verified on Postgres, so release's 3 would not eat nightly's 10.
gaps.evidence: Prod filing rate parsed from the deployed tasks.html (last 500 runs, 2026-08-13 19:22 to 2026-08-31 07:26 = 17.50 days): nightly 462 runs = 26.4/day -> 12 bugs = 0.69/day = 2.6% of runs; beta 38 runs = 2.2/day -> 0 filed (held), 1 lead in 38. Release's fileable-on-the-verdict supply, measured with `sigage.first_seen_ever` over the 14-day top-500 install-cardinality facet — signatures clearing the configured install threshold AND at most 30 days old all-time: release 8/326 = 2.5% (Wilson 1.2-4.8%), nightly 32/494 = 6.5% (4.6-9.0%), beta 9/266 = 3.4% (1.8-6.3%); the release and nightly CIs are disjoint. Supply ratio 8:32 -> release projects to ~0.25 x 0.69 = 0.17 filings/day = ~5/month at `file_new`, ~2/month at `skip`. A cap of 3 leaves ~18x headroom. Verified on Postgres: `filed_bugs_since(epoch, 'release')` = 0 while `'nightly'` = 1 with one nightly filing on record.
gaps.proposed_fix: `"daily_cap": 3` in the release overlay, same value and argument as beta's. BMO request cost is not a constraint: measured 5.12 BMO reads per release filing attempt at `comment` mode over 8 real signatures (1.00 open-bugs search + 2.12 `_last_reopened` history + 2.00 fixed-bugs search); `skip` short-circuits before `_bug_for_this_regression` when a venue exists, so ~2.5. At 0.17 filings/day that is single-digit requests per day, nowhere near BMO's rate limit.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to get the release run volume from the production database directly (the honest denominator), but the sandbox classifier blocked the psycopg2 connection, so 26.4 runs/day and 0.69 filings/day come from the deployed tasks view's last 500 rows, a 17.5-day window rather than the whole history. I also tried to derive release's run volume from the selector, but `datacollector.get_new_signatures("Firefox", "release", ...)` reads the `builds` table and answers nothing on sqlite; that number belongs to the selection dimension and my projection scales nightly's measured rate by the supply ratio instead.

gaps.title: The value case is thin and measurable: nothing automated files release crash bugs today, but the human process finds them on nightly and the release-only un-bugged population is 2 signatures in the top 350
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks; this is the go/no-go. If the answer is "a Firefox release manager does not want 2-5 machine-filed bugs a month on signatures nightly already covers", the correct rollout is triage-only (`enabled: false`) permanently, and the engineering above is the cost of keeping that decision explicit rather than accidental.
gaps.evidence: PRIOR ART (BMO reads; filing_09_priorart.py, filing_10_bots.py, filing_15_tracking.py). 236 desktop crash bugs (`short_desc` substring `Crash in [@`, 120 d, Core/Firefox/Toolkit/DevTools/WebExtensions). Creators: cdenizet 63, release-mgmt-account-bot 58, aryx 37, gsvelto 13, clouseau-bot 10, continuation 8, dsmith 7. `longdesc` count_only over 365 d: "By querying Nightly crashes reported within the last" = 137 bugs; "...Release crashes..." = 0; "...Beta crashes..." = 0 — BMO's automated crash filer is nightly-only. Release-TRACKED crash bugs: cf_tracking_firefox153 isnotempty = 19 over 200 d (aryx 13, ryanvm 2, gsvelto 2, dmeehan 1, pascalc 1; values + x16, blocking x3), cf_tracking_firefox154 = 13 (aryx 7, gsvelto 3); their comment 0 quotes NIGHTLY volumes ("187 crashes from 86 installs of Firefox 153.0a1", "First reported build ID ... Firefox 154.0a1 20260615215140"). RELEASE-ONLY POPULATION (filing_16, filing_17): of the top-100 release signatures, 5 never appear on nightly in 90 d (Wilson 2.2-11.2%), 0 never appear on nightly OR beta, and 4 of the 5 already carry an open same-application non-meta bug (1856672, 1868775+1928445, 1943922, 1928386). In ranks 101-350, 5/250 are release-only and 3 un-bugged: `@0x0 | neqo_udp::recv_inner` (103 installs), `arise_dri.so` (83), `cx4_dri.so` (80) — the last two Mesa DRI drivers. Net across the top 350 (326 clear the install threshold of 50): 4/350 = 1.1% (Wilson 0.4-2.9%) release-only and un-bugged, of which 2 are Firefox code.
gaps.proposed_fix: Run release as triage-only (`"enabled": false`) for one cycle and count what it WOULD file — the `autofile_channel_held` log string plus the count of release dossiers reaching rung 70, which is what config.py:604-608 built the hold for. Take the arm/no-arm decision on that number. If armed, pitch the one thing release genuinely adds over aryx's process: a named changeset for an UPLIFT-caused release regression, where the between-builds mozilla-release window is only 16-82 changesets and `regressed_by` is a strong claim.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My first pass measured the release-only population on the top 100 only, where it is 5 signatures — plausibly a top-of-distribution artefact, so I extended to ranks 101-350 expecting the value to be in the tail. It is not: 5/250 there, 3 un-bugged, 2 of them third-party driver .so files. I also checked whether the human process is FAST (so latency would be our differentiator) and found the opposite failure mode for my own case: it is not fast, it is nightly-scoped, so the gap is real but narrow.

gaps.title: `_incomplete_fix_bug` — the second reason to file — is effectively dead on release, and `_fixed_after_build_bug`'s stated DOMAIN does not cover release builds
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Two bounded things. (a) `_incomplete_fix_bug` costs one cached BMO search on ~90% of release runs and will essentially never fire, so the "a shipped fix that did not hold is a new bug" path (8949731) buys nothing on release. (b) `_fixed_after_build_bug`'s SEMANTICS invert on release: `cf_last_resolved > build_dt` means the fix landed on trunk AFTER the release build was cut, i.e. the fix is NOT in the shipped build and users are still crashing — but the gate reads that as "pre-fix report of an already-fixed defect: skip". On release the actionable outcome is an uplift request, and we answer with silence.
gaps.evidence: filing_22_incomplete_fix.py, top-100 release signatures: `sigage.first_seen_ever` answered 100/100; all-time signature age median 1,274 d (p25 668, p75 2,171), only 2 of 100 younger than 30 days. 78 (signature, FIXED same-application bug) pairs exist; only 4 pass condition 3 (abs(filed - first_seen) <= 7 d) — bugs 1897636 (+4 d), 800840 (+1 d, FIXED in 2012), 1992573 (0 d), 1844653 (0 d) — and condition 2 (`Node.landing_for_bug`, bounded by `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention) then drops the old ones. filing_08_fixedafter.py: `_fixed_after_build_bug` fires on 4/100 = 4.0% (Wilson 1.6-9.8%) of the top-100 release signatures at their modal build, against the docstring's nightly control of 6.0% in-domain — but 95 of the 100 modal builds are 15-90 days old and only 1 is inside the documented 14-day domain, and 2 of the 4 firings are on builds 237 d and 549 d old. filing_07_buildage.py: installation-weighted release build age is 18.4% <=14 d / 72.1% 15-90 d / 9.5% >90 d, against nightly's 73.1 / 19.9 / 7.0. One firing is bug 2062119 on `nsJARProtocolHandler::MimeService`, on build 20260812182057 — the loudest release build in the fleet at 67,067 installations.
gaps.proposed_fix: Paste the release numbers into `_fixed_after_build_bug`'s DOMAIN paragraph (it asks for exactly this) and state that release builds sit mostly outside it. Do NOT gate `_incomplete_fix_bug` off for release — it fails open and costs one cached search — but stop expecting it to contribute and drop it from any release volume projection. For the semantic inversion, the honest minimum is: on a non-nightly channel, when the FIXED bug's own landing is NOT in our channel pushlog before the build, the crash is a live report of a fix that has not shipped, which is a comment on that bug rather than a skip. That is new behaviour and must not ride the config commit.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My hypothesis was the opposite — that release's old builds would make `_fixed_after_build_bug` OVER-suppress, killing most release filings. Measured at 4/100 it does not: it is comparable to nightly's 6.0%. So the over-suppression claim is dead and only the domain-and-semantics point survives, at ~4% reach.

gaps.title: The ReviewNote corpus cannot be stratified by channel, so release filings would pool with nightly's — the exact pooling the channel key was added to prevent
gaps.where: crashclouseau/models.py:3659-3665, crashclouseau/models.py:3500-3560, crashclouseau/models.py:3384-3400, crashclouseau/feedback.py:66-72, crashclouseau/feedback.py:104-113, crashclouseau/bugzilla_apply.py:1394-1402
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `_NOTE_MODES = ("new_bug",)` is precisely a `file_new`/`skip` channel's mode, so every release filing enters the review-note corpus. `ReviewNote.corpus()` has no channel filter and no column to add one to (`_ensure_tables` creates tables, never columns), so `bin/feedback.py`'s corpus and any rate read off it describe two populations and neither — the mistake bugzilla_apply.py:1394-1402 and `Feedback.scoreboard`'s docstring both say the channel key exists to prevent. Half the plumbing is there (`feedback._filed_bugs` carries `channel`); the note half is not.
gaps.evidence: Read in tree. `feedback._filed_bugs` (feedback.py:110-113) carries `channel` and `buildid` from the `filed_bug` payload with a comment saying why. `Feedback.scoreboard(channel=None)` (models.py:3387-3397) stratifies by joining uuid -> uuids -> builds and explicitly notes there is no migration mechanism for adding a column. `ReviewNote`'s columns are id/bug_id/comment_id/comment_no/author/author_kind/needinfo/created_at/body/error_class/label_note/labelled_at/seen_at — no channel, no uuid. `ReviewNote.corpus(unlabelled_only, limit)` filters only `author_kind != "automation"`. The only consumers are bin/feedback.py:26-27 and :101.
gaps.proposed_fix: Give `ReviewNote.corpus` an optional `channel` argument implemented the way `scoreboard` does it — join `bug_id` back through `Dossier.payload['filed_bug']->>'bug'` to uuids to builds.channel. No column, no migration, same shape as the existing precedent. Do it before release files, not after, so the first release note is already attributable.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the pooling is unreachable because release would run at `comment` mode (whose `comment_on_existing` rows `_NOTE_MODES` excludes). It is reachable: gap 2 recommends `file_new` precisely so the second-bug hazard is closed, and `file_new`'s mode string is `new_bug`. I also checked whether any other reader stratifies notes — bin/feedback.py is the only consumer and passes no channel.

gaps.title: A release filing carries no severity and no status flag, and half of our nightly bugs get a severity from someone else afterwards
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing is rejected — `severity` is optional and BMO defaults it to `--`. But a release crash bug at `--` sits outside release management's severity-triaged queues until a human sets it, and 32 of our 72 nightly filings are still at `--`. The create-payload allowlist at :1449-1455 also means adding `severity` to the preview without adding it to that tuple is a silent no-op, the failure shape that killed `blocks` and `regressed_by` for weeks.
gaps.evidence: filing_15_tracking.py: our 72 filings carry severity S3 x36, `--` x32, S2 x2, S4 x2; version `Trunk` x72; keywords crash x72, regression x38, topcrash x3; cf_tracking_firefox154 = None on all 72; cf_status_firefox154 already set on 24 (unaffected 17, wontfix 5, disabled 2) by someone other than us. Prior art on the 236-bug desktop panel: severity S3 126, `--` 86, S2 13, S4 11; release-mgmt-account-bot sets S3 on 40 of 58 and version `unspecified` on 58/58. Verified with the real filer on Postgres (filing_21): a release filing's POSTED payload is keywords=['crash','regression'] version=unspecified product=Core component='DOM: Core & HTML' groups=None — no severity key at all.
gaps.proposed_fix: If anything, set `severity: "S3"` and add `"severity"` to the allowlist tuple at bugzilla_apply.py:1451 in the same edit — S3 is the prior-art mode on this class and what the release-mgmt bot does. Do NOT set S2 for release on volume grounds; that is release management's judgement and only 13 of 236 bugs carry it. Do NOT set tracking flags (see the kill).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether BMO rejects a create with no severity, which would make this a blocker: it does not — all 72 of our filings were accepted and 32 remain at `--`. I also checked whether the severity we see is ours: version `Trunk` on 72/72 matches `_bug_version("nightly")` exactly, while severity splits 36/32/2/2, which no single default produces, so the S3s were set after the fact.

open_questions: Arm release filing, or run it triage-only? Recommendation: ship `"release": {"enabled": false, "comment_on_existing": "file_new", "daily_cap": 3}` and do NOT arm it in the same cycle. The measured value case is ~2-5 bugs/month on signatures nightly already covers, plus 2 un-bugged release-only Firefox-code signatures in the top 350 — thin enough that the count from one held cycle should decide it, which is exactly what `autofile_channel_held` was built to produce.

`file_new` or `skip` for release's `comment_on_existing`? Recommendation: `file_new`. Both close the 25% second-bug hazard (the guard fires in the `mode != "comment"` branch either way), but `skip` additionally discards the 36% of release selections that have NO venue at all, and 86% of the ones that DO have a venue would be filed past on the evidence anyway (median venue age 794 days). `comment` is the one option my measurement rules out.

Should `autofile_channel_declared` require an explicit `enabled` key for any channel other than `default_channel`? Recommendation: yes. Today a bare `channels.release: {}` reads as "declared and armed at nightly's rules" under prod's live AUTOFILE_BUGS=1, so an incomplete config edit fails OPEN — the opposite direction from every other gate in `autofile_bug`. Cost is one line plus one test; the benefit is that the gap config.py:583 warns about cannot be re-opened by a typo.

Should the filer set `severity: "S3"` on release filings? Recommendation: yes, and add `"severity"` to the create-payload allowlist at bugzilla_apply.py:1451 in the SAME edit — a preview key absent from that tuple is a silent no-op, which is how `blocks` and `regressed_by` were dead for weeks. S3 is the prior-art mode (126/236) and what the release-mgmt bot sets. Do not set S2; that is release management's call and only 13/236 bugs carry it.

Do we do anything about `_fixed_after_build_bug`'s inverted meaning on release — a fix resolved after the release build is on trunk, not in the shipped build, so "already fixed, don't file" answers an uplift-worthy crash with silence? Recommendation: not in the release rollout. It fires on 4/100 release signatures, the change is new behaviour on a function nightly shares, and the honest first step is to paste the release build-age numbers into its DOMAIN paragraph (which asks for exactly that) and revisit once release has produced real filings.
cross_dimension: SWEEP STARVATION WITH THREE CHANNELS. `config._SWEEP_DEFAULTS` is `max_per_run: 3` / `max_per_channel: 2`, and orchestrator.py:4201-4231 applies the per-channel cap only when the fetched candidates span more than one channel. reports.headline: Release is not a volume problem and not a sampling-blindness problem — it is a **meaning** problem plus a maturity handicap. Measured live: 27 builds / 145 d (median gap 4.96 d, 1.25 builds/wk vs beta's 2.83), median **111,658 reports and 79,588 installs per build** (40x beta's per-build installs), **3,096 distinct signatures per channel-day** (2,432-3,211 — sigtrend.py:129's "~3,200" is right and its `MAX_SIGNATURES=1500` refuses release outright). The 10% sample is real (verified in antenna's own `MOZILLA_RULES`: `is_firefox_desktop` → `(10, ACCEPT, REJECT)`) but it is a **mixture** — 7.4% of release reports are accepted at 100% — so the effective rate is 10.72% and **a release install count understates real crashing machines by 4.1x** (derived by applying antenna's rule to the unsampled same-codebase esr153 population; predicted reports/install 1.26 vs release 153.x's actual 1.44). Three things fall out and none is "tune the thresholds": the per-(signature,build) install distribution on release is **almost identical to beta's** (p50/p75/p90/p95 = 1/2/5/12 on both), so `installs=50` is not a volume calibration but a 34x change in what an install means; a release build is judged at the only selectable window index holding **41.3%** of its eventual crashes against an **80.7%** baseline — a **0.51x maturity handicap** turning `ratio=3` into an effective 5.9x (beta 0.71x → 4.2x); and **76.5% of release's install-hits are in classes no regression finder can act on** (in-scope 23.5% vs beta 31.9%, nightly 48.5%). The pro-release argument survives: the ordinary release candidate window is **median 46 changesets, 4 candidate-bearing** (beta 61/21, nightly 672/266), 99.5% approved uplifts or backouts. The anti-release argument survives too: **0 of the top 200 release signatures by installs (92.6% of install-hits) is invisible on nightly+beta**, and only **1 of 188 ≥50-install signatures per cycle is new-on-release AND unseen upstream**.

gaps.title: `installs` = 50 on release does not mean 50 machines — the sample thins install cardinality by a measured 4.1x, and the thinning is non-uniform by process type
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Every threshold, floor and trend statistic in the tree is denominated in `cardinality_install_time`, which the module docstrings correctly insist is the honest unit. On release that unit is a 10%-thinned, non-linear function of the true machine count, and the factor varies from 1x to 10x WITHIN the channel depending on process type and whether the user typed a comment. A filed bug saying "50 installations" means ~205 machines for a content-process crash and ~50 for a GPU-process one, and the two are indistinguishable in the number.
gaps.evidence: Antenna's live ruleset (raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla-services/antenna/main/antenna/throttler.py, MOZILLA_RULES) applies `is_firefox_desktop` = (10, ACCEPT, REJECT) to ProductName=Firefox AND ReleaseChannel=release — but FIVE earlier rules ACCEPT at 100%: throttleable_0 (about:crashes), has_comments, has_phc, is_background (ProcessType in gpu/plugin/rdd/socket/utility). Measured Firefox 2026-08-01..08-29 (spike/_release_recon/pop_07_mixture.py): release 563,944 reports; throttleable=F 37,937 (6.7%); background process types 10,601 (1.9%) of which 3,958 also throttleable=T → measurable 100%-accepted union 41,895 = 7.4%. Effective observed rate = 563,944 / (41,895 + 10x522,049) = 10.72%. Install-side thinning against ground truth (spike/_release_recon/pop_32_thinning.py): the unsampled same-codebase esr153 population is 4,182 install_times, mean k=2.314 reports each (k-hist 1:2433, 2:713, 3:428, 4:231, 5:133); applying antenna's own 10% rule to that exact population leaves 18.4% of installs visible = 5.4x understatement, and 4.1x once the measured 7.4% unsampled slice is mixed in. The model predicts observed reports/install 1.26; release 153.x actually shows 1.44 (pop_31_esr153.py) — validated to 13%, residual in the direction the unsampled slice pushes. Per-build medians (pop_09_population_fixed.py, date>=2026-01-01): release 111,658 reports / 79,588 installs / r-i 1.37 over 25 real builds; beta 3,075 / 1,986 / 1.59.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Three attempts to make the sampling claim go away. (1) Looked for a Socorro-side throttle field: SuperSearchFields has `throttleable` but that is the CLIENT annotation with no rate — release is T 132,672 / F 18,681, beta T 5,832 / F 71, so it discriminates nothing about the collector. (2) Checked whether the collector still throttles: socorro/docs/overview.rst says "the throttle result instruction character is no longer used and always set to 0", which reads like throttling is gone — but that concerns only the crash-id character; antenna's MOZILLA_RULES on main still contains the 10% rule and the effective-rate arithmetic matches the esr153-derived prediction, so it is live. (3) Tried the naive cross-channel reports-per-install route: it FAILS (release 1.37 vs beta 1.59 = 0.86x, not 0.1x) because thinning conditions on at least one surviving report — which is why the esr153 ground-truth route is the one reported.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not re-tune `installs` on machine-count grounds; it cannot be made comparable. Instead (a) keep 50 and state in the plan that it means ~205 machines (4.1x), so release is 34x stricter than beta's 6 in machine terms and that is deliberate; (b) record the derived true-machine estimate next to the observed one wherever an install count reaches a human or a prompt (one multiplier of 4.1 plus the process-type caveat, not a per-signature correction); (c) never let a release install count into the same comparison as a nightly or beta one — that includes `signature_age.other_channel_floor` and any cross-channel ratio.

gaps.title: `sigtrend` structurally cannot cover release: 3,096 signatures/day measured against `MAX_SIGNATURES=1500`, and enabling it costs 1.13M rows/year
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `backfill` returns 0 for release (channel guard, sigtrend.py:251) and `collect_day` would refuse every day anyway (`len(rows) >= MAX_SIGNATURES` → warning, return 0). So on release the trend statistic silently produces nothing: no `chandaily` exposure row, no `sigdaily` series, and `trend_facts` returns {} — which the design correctly reads as "could not measure", so nothing is wrong, but nothing is delivered. If someone flips SUPPORTED_CHANNELS without raising the two size constants, release logs one refusal per day per run against a ~2h log window and looks like it is working.
gaps.evidence: Measured over 14 consecutive channel-days 2026-08-10..08-23 (spike/_release_recon/pop_13_sigcount.py): release distinct signatures/day median 3,096, min 2,432, max 3,211; beta median 396 (273-445); nightly median 256 (220-298). sigtrend.py:129's "release ~3,200" is confirmed as the max. At the module's own FACETS_SIZE=2000 the release facet returns exactly 2,000 every day = silent truncation of the quietest ~1,100 signatures, the only ones the module exists for. A workable size verified (pop_26_final.py): `_facets_size=5000` on release 2026-08-25 returns 3,143 of a 3,154 cardinality. Storage: SignatureDaily is one row per (product, channel, day, signature) — at BACKFILL_DAYS=70 that is 216,720 backfill rows for release vs 17,920 (nightly) + 27,720 (beta), and steady state 1,130,040 rows/year vs 93,440 + 144,540 = 4.7x the two supported channels combined.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Tried to find a cheaper covering shape. Raising `_facets_size` to 5,000 does cover a day (3,143 of 3,154), so the query is not the blocker — the table growing per-signature-per-day is. Also checked whether release's tail is mostly one-off noise that a collect-time floor could delete: it is not usefully, because MIN_INSTALLS=3 is applied at read time and the per-pair install distribution has p50=1, so a collect-time floor would delete exactly the quiet signatures the module is for.
gaps.proposed_fix: Leave release OUT of sigtrend and say so explicitly, as the module docstring already does. The statistic's measured value (sigtrend.py:54-59) is as an ORDERING over a candidate list the pipeline already pays for; release's list is ~110 (signature,build) pairs per build above installs=50, small enough that an ordering buys nothing. If it is ever wanted, the change is three lines (SUPPORTED_CHANNELS, FACETS_SIZE 5000, MAX_SIGNATURES 4000) plus a decision about 1.13M rows/year — do not let that land as an incidental.

gaps.title: A release build is judged at 41.3% arrival against an 80.7% baseline — a 0.51x maturity handicap that silently multiplies `spike.ratio` from 3 to 5.9
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `get_builds`' non-nightly branch takes the 3 newest builds; with shift=1 only day indices 1 and 2 are testable, index 2 (the newest) holds ~0.000% of its crashes on its build day and cannot clear floor=50, so index 1 is the ONLY selecting position — as plan #18 measured for beta (135/135 selections at index 1). At the moment a release build reaches index 1 it holds a median 41.3% of its eventual crashes while the index-0 build it is compared against holds 80.7%. A regression that truly doubles a signature's rate appears as a 0.51x-deflated ratio and must be ~5.9x real to clear ratio=3. Nothing corrects for it and nothing records it, so a missed release regression is indistinguishable from "not spiking".
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_11_arrival.py + pop_12_window.py, per-build daily arrival curves (`_histogram.date` + `_cardinality.install_time`) for all 27 release builds since 2026-04-01 and 25 beta builds since 2026-07-01. Release: window life median 16.0 d; days at index 2 (newest) median 6.0; days at index 1 median 5.0; share arrived entering index 1 median 41.3% (min 5.7, max 100); leaving index 1 median 79.6%; the index-0 baseline at that same instant median 80.7% → handicap 0.51x. Beta control on identical arithmetic: window life 7.0 d, 2.0 d at each index, entering index 1 at 56.0%, baseline 78.9% → handicap 0.71x. Build-day share: release 0.0000% (max 0.0010% over 25 builds) against beta's measured 1.05-3.31% — release's day-0 is even emptier than plan #18 2.1's 0.2-2.7%.
gaps.falsification_attempt: The obvious artifact is that `get_builds` sets search_date to the oldest of the 3 builds' build date, clipping the test build's early crashes and inventing the handicap. Checked every consecutive triple (pop_33_falsify.py part B): no release build has a single report dated before the window's lower edge, so the window never clips a member and 41.3% is real arrival, not a query boundary. Also checked the opposite — that x.0 builds' 6-day ship lag inflates the gap — but the dot releases (lag 1-2 d) show the same shape (153.0.3 58.3%, 153.0.4 6.6% entering, both against 81-88% baselines).
gaps.proposed_fix: Either (a) compare like with like — restrict both the test build-day and its baseline build-days to reports whose date_processed falls within the same number of days after each build's own ship day (the arrival curve is already free from the facet the collector fetches) — or (b) accept the handicap and set spike.ratio on release from the measured deflation instead of inheriting nightly's 3; 1.5 restores beta's effective 4.2x. Whichever is chosen, record the arrival share of the test day and of the baseline in the Selection row so a missed spike is diagnosable.

gaps.title: `population.py`'s facet is truncated on 68% of release head signatures, and it then reports the exact number the module exists to prevent
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `for_crash` asks for `_facets_size = cfg['facets_size']` = 1000 install_time terms, count-ordered. On release the loudest head signature has 19,062 installs in 7 days, so the list is a top-1,000-busiest slice. `summarize` then computes per_install = faceted/len(installs) and top_share = counts[0]/faceted off that slice — off the most concentrated 5% of the population — so the page's whole purpose (module docstring: stop a report count being read as a machine count) inverts on release, in the direction of overstating concentration. `truncated` is set and rendered, but the two numbers next to it are wrong, not merely floors.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_30_truncation.py, top 60 signatures by installs per channel over 2026-08-20..27 through the production `population.summarize` with the production cfg: release 41/60 truncated (68%), inflation of crashes/faceted_crashes median x1.03 but max x6.93; beta 6/60 (10%, max x1.04); nightly 9/60 (15%, max x1.23). Loudest head signature per channel: release 19,062 installs in 7 d, beta 1,025, nightly 244 — so facets_size 1000 is comfortable on nightly and beta and 19x short on release.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether raising facets_size is simply the fix: it is not affordable — the release head needs >19,062 terms, and while Socorro accepted `_facets_size=10000` in my probes, that is a 10x heavier facet on every crashstack.html render behind a single gunicorn worker with a 6s read timeout (net.py:68). Also checked whether the inflation is benign because the flags do not fire: single_install and concentrated fired 0/60 on all three channels (pop_16), so today no VERDICT changes — but per_install and installs are printed, and the max x6.93 case prints a 7x-wrong reports-per-installation on the page whose reason for existing is that ratio.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `_cardinality.install_time` to the SAME facet query (free — one extra facet on a request already being made) and take `installs` and `per_install` from the cardinality and `total`, not from the truncated list. Keep the facet list only for the shape flags (top_share, median_gap_s) and label them explicitly as computed over the busiest N when truncated is true. This also fixes the 10-15% truncated cases on nightly and beta, so it ships regardless of release.

gaps.title: `population.clustered_gap_s` = 300 s is an install-DENSITY threshold calibrated on nightly; release's install stream is 26x denser and the flag's headroom collapses from 107x to 4.2x
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `clustered` is meant to catch a population that cannot be independent users (config.py:291-292 names the calibration: nightly p10 = 4,430 s, median 8 h, and the four firing cases at 20/62/89/142 s were VM and distro images). On release the median inter-install gap within a head signature is 1,262 s — BELOW nightly's tenth percentile — so 300 s is no longer "far below p10", it is roughly release's p2-p5, and the flag starts reading ordinary release popularity as an imaged fleet.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_17_clustered.py, top 60 signatures per channel, production cfg: median_gap_s across signatures — release median 1,262 s (p25 643, min 222), beta 18,352 (p25 6,033), nightly 32,190 (p25 17,854). Headroom at the median: nightly 32,190/300 = 107x, beta 61x, release 4.2x. `clustered` already fires on 5/60 release head signatures vs 1/60 nightly and 0/60 beta. Channel install density (pop_08_population.py, 30 d): release median 17,849 distinct installs/day vs beta 1,155 and nightly 463 — 38.6x nightly, which is the mechanism.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Tried to attribute the 5/60 firings to genuine VM fleets rather than density: if so the firing signatures would be a distinct sub-population, but their median gaps sit at 222-300 s against a channel p25 of 643 s — within a factor of 3 of ordinary release signatures, not two orders of magnitude out as the four nightly cases were (20-142 s against a p10 of 4,430 s). The separation that justified the number on nightly is not present on release.
gaps.proposed_fix: Make the threshold channel-relative rather than absolute: keep the same multiple of the channel's own median inter-install gap that 300 s represents on nightly (300/32,190 = 1/107), which on release is ~12 s. Cheapest implementation is to divide by the chandaily install exposure the tree already collects for nightly and beta, or simply add a per-channel clustered_gap_s with release at 12 and a comment saying why the number is not transferable. Do NOT keep 300 and call it measured.

gaps.title: The bad-machine gate's predicate is measured on a 10%-thinned view of the machine, so its recall on release is bounded by the sampling and cannot be recalibrated from Socorro
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `install_history` fetches up to 200 rows for one install_time and the gate requires distinct_signatures >= 10 with distinct_cpus <= 1 and span >= 1800 s. On release only ~10% of that machine's reports exist, so a truly scattering machine shows ~2 of its 10 signatures and the gate does not fire — the suppression that closed bugs 2062168/2062173 INVALID is ~10x less sensitive on the channel with the most bad hardware. Simultaneously the de-alias guard weakens: fewer visible reports means fewer distinct cpu_info values, so a colliding install_time passes distinct_cpus <= 1 more often, which is the failure mode config.py:934-940 was written to exclude.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_16_machine.py and pop_17_clustered.py, 2026-08-20..27. Installs reaching >=10 distinct observed signatures: 83 of the busiest 10,000 release installs (<=0.075% of the channel's 111,050) vs 13 of 2,770 nightly (0.469%) and 15 of 6,337 beta (0.237%) — 6x rarer per install on release. Report-weighted reach is however comparable (release 7.39%, nightly 5.80%, beta 3.74% of channel reports come from installs with >=10 distinct signatures) because release's install base is 40x larger. Thinning arithmetic from the esr153 ground truth (pop_32): with mean k=2.314 reports per install, a 10% sample retains 1-0.9^2.314 = 21.6% of a machine's per-signature appearances, so 10 true signatures present as ~2.2 observed.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I expected the gate to be DEAD on release and it is not — report-weighted reach (7.4%) is actually higher than nightly's (5.8%), which kills the simple "the gate cannot fire on release" claim. What survives is the recall claim, and I tried to defeat that too by asking whether lowering min_signatures fixes it: it does not. The thinning-equivalent of nightly's 10 is ~2 observed signatures, and >=2 is satisfied by 7,653 of the busiest 10,000 release installs (76.5%) — the transported threshold is meaningless. The predicate needs the report list the sampling destroyed.
gaps.proposed_fix: Accept ~10x lower recall at min_signatures=10 and say so in the plan, OR do not run the bad-machine gate on release and record instead the one signal that IS unsampled: the is_background process types and about:crashes (throttleable=F) reports from the same install, which the collector accepts at 100%. Either way min_signatures must NOT be lowered for release — measured meaningless at 2, where lowering it converts a suppressor into a blanket veto on 76% of the busiest installs.

gaps.title: An unshipped x.0 release build sits in the `builds` table with no users for a measured 3-7 days, and the one-build-day exemption is the only thing keeping it out of the baseline
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Release x.0 builds are built well before they ship. On its build day a release build holds 0.0000% of its eventual crashes, so a freshly built x.0 is a hard ZERO for every signature, and `utils.is_spike`'s from-zero branch is gated by neither floor nor ratio — exactly the failure plan #18 1.2 measured on beta's merge-day b1. `find_no_user_days` exempts only the NEWEST build-day, so the protection holds only while no newer build appears before the RC ships. In the observed 26 intervals that never happened, but the margin is thin and one case already fired.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_29_shiplag.py, all 27 release builds since 2026-04-01, ship lag = first day holding >=1% of the build's eventual crashes: MAJOR x.0 median 6.0 d (values 3,6,6,7,7); DOT x.y.z median 2.0 d (1-5). Peak crash day is 4-17 days after the build. Exact find_no_user_days statistic (max per-signature install cardinality on the build-day, pop_27_floorexact.py): the superseded 151.0 build 20260513195118 = 1; the unshipped 155.0 RC 20260826195058 at 5 days after build = 1; the two same-day respins 20260506041011 / 20260727110312 = 0 but each SHARES its build-day with a real build (94,642 and 111,658 reports) so the day is not dead; against 6,859-12,980 for real builds. 154.0 was newest for 12 days and shipped on day 7; 151.0's first build was superseded at day 3 and DID become a near-zero baseline (pop_26_final.py: 1 of 26).
gaps.falsification_attempt: Tried to show the RC is harmless because it is always the newest build and therefore always exempt. Across the 26 observed intervals that is true — but 151.0 (built 2026-05-13, 3 lifetime reports) was superseded by a respin on 05-16 and by 05-20 sat at index 0/1 with 3 reports and a max per-signature install cardinality of 1, i.e. exactly the near-zero baseline. So the exemption is not sufficient; the floor is what catches it, and it does.
gaps.proposed_fix: No new mechanism needed — min_build_installs=15 already catches the one real case with a 6,859x margin (see kills). What IS needed is that the plan state the RC fact, because two downstream things read it: (a) Build.get_last_versions(n=3) spends a whole window slot on a build with no users for up to 7 days, so release's effective window is 2 builds not 3 for part of every cycle; (b) any "newest build" health check will look like a stall for 3-7 days after every x.0 build. Consider excluding a zero-report build from the n=3 selection rather than letting it occupy a slot.

gaps.title: 76.5% of release's crash volume is in classes a regression finder cannot act on, and the in-scope remainder (23.5%) is smaller than beta's and half of nightly's
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Any per-day spend estimate that prices release off its raw volume will be wrong by 4x. The classes are not evenly distributed either: OOM and shutdown/hang together are 57.4% of release install-hits, and both are the shapes plan #18 already identified as producing analyses the pipeline cannot act on.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_14_head.py + pop_15_classify.py, 2026-08-20..27, ranked by install cardinality, classified over the full faceted set (release 2,000 signatures covering 108% of channel install-hits, i.e. one machine counted once per signature): release OOM 33.5%, shutdown/hang 23.9%, other-in-scope 23.5%, empty/no-stack 6.4%, gc-memory-integrity 6.1%, stackoverflow 4.4%, process-kill 2.2%. Beta (1,418 sigs): OOM 41.8%, other 31.9%, shutdown/hang 18.2%. Nightly (987 sigs): other 48.5%, OOM 23.2%, shutdown/hang 21.2%. Concentration: release's top 10 signatures are 48.6% of channel install-hits, top 50 are 77.1%, top 200 are 92.6%.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether release's out-of-scope share is an artifact of the 10% sample favouring repeat-crashers (which would over-represent OOM and hangs). It is not: per-capita, release's OOM share is 0.7x beta's (37.4% vs 51.6%) and its shutdown/AsyncShutdown shares are 1.0x nightly's and beta's. What release genuinely adds is stackoverflow (3.8x) and empty minidumps (3.4x), both out of scope for a different reason.
gaps.proposed_fix: Price release ingestion off the 23.5% in-scope share, not off volume. Concretely: the population above the current installs=50 threshold is 220 (signature,build) pairs over the two builds of one cycle (pop_25_enrich.py) = ~110 per build, of which ~23% are in scope = ~25 candidate pairs per build, ~1 per day at release's 1.25 builds/week cadence. Hand that to the selection and cost dimensions as the population bound.

gaps.title: Release novelty: 9 of 188 (4.8%) above-threshold signatures per cycle are new on release, and only 1 of 188 is new-on-release AND unseen on nightly or beta
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The regression-finding premise on release rests on new signatures appearing there first. Measured, they almost never do — six of the nine were already crashing on nightly and/or beta before the release build shipped, and three are longstanding signatures returning (first_build 2017, 2020, 2024). The stale-signature gate will therefore fire on ~95% of release selections, as a filing blocker rather than a downweight, exactly as plan #18 2.4 found for beta at 88%.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_22_novelty_exact.py. Of the 188 signatures with >=50 installs on the current cycle's two builds (20260812182057, 20260824154132), exactly 9 have zero release reports in the previous 120 days (2026-04-14..08-12); the other 179 have a median baseline of 1,752 release reports (p25 992, max 348,450). For each of the 9 I queried nightly and beta over 2026-01-01..08-12: stackoverflow|style::values::specified::calc 10 nightly / 61 beta; js::BarrieredBase<T>::getForTracing 35/39; AsyncShutdownTimeout|MonitorStore: Shutdown 20/25; logging::CheckLogMessage::~CheckLogMessage 2/41; VerifyClientPrincipalInfosMatch 7/2; SplitSingleCharHelper 0/2; mozilla::detail::InvalidArrayIndex_CRASH 0/2; mozilla::dom::OptionalServiceWorkerData::AssertSanity 0/1; and mozilla::CheckedInt<T>::value|mozilla::media::TimeUnit::operator<= 0/0 with first_build 20260601110758 which is release 151.0.3's own buildid — one genuinely release-first signature at 64 installs. SignatureFirstDate answered 25/25 on the loudest new ones.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My first pass (pop_21_novelty.py) did the obvious set difference between two signature facets and got 55.8% new — nonsense, and I traced why: release holds 11,609 distinct signatures on the two current builds and 80,138 over the previous 120 days, both facet lists cap at 10,000 and are COUNT-ordered, so a quiet old signature falls out of the baseline list and reads as new. I discarded that number and replaced it with one exact query per candidate. The beta control on the same exact method gives 0 of 70 new over 120 days, against plan #18 2.4's 12% — the difference is the denominator (plan #18 measured SELECTED signatures, biased toward new by construction; I measured all signatures above the install threshold), and both are right about different populations.
gaps.proposed_fix: State the 1-of-188 figure in the plan as the honest ceiling on release-first regressions, and require any release rollout to name which population it targets. If it is the 6-of-188 escalation class (new on release, already visible upstream), the tool for that is a cross-channel escalation alarm, not the build-day spike selector — and plan #18 13 already has the prior art (nightly_vs_beta, ~2 days of lead).

gaps.title: The release candidate window is the real argument for release support: median 46 changesets and 4 candidate-bearing per ordinary window, 99.5% approved uplifts or backouts
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks — this is the finding that would justify the work and it needs to be in section 2 so it is not lost among the negatives. It also sets the expectation that agent.offstack.max_candidates = 150 never binds on release, and that the merge-spanning window (1 of every 4-5 build intervals) is a different animal entirely.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_18_uplift.py and pop_19_uplift_kind.py, hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-release json-pushes between consecutive Buildhub build revisions, all 26 intervals since 2026-04-01, through crashclouseau.net (allowlisted UA) and the repo's own pushlog.is_merge_push / utils.is_interesting_file. ORDINARY windows (n=20, no cycle merge): changesets median 46 (min 5, max 116), non-merge 46, with-interesting-file median 4 (min 0, max 49), distinct interesting files median 7 (max 104), backouts median 0 (max 10). MERGE-SPANNING (n=6, the x.0 boundary): changesets median 6,952 (5,405-7,464), candidate-bearing non-merge 0-2. Kind classification over 1,178 non-merge changesets: 1,131 approved uplifts (a=RyanVM / diannaS / dmeehan / pascalc / dsmith), 30 backouts, 17 other; restricted to the 185 candidate-bearing ones: 179 uplifts + 5 backouts + 1 other = 99.5% plausible crash regressors (beta's equivalent in plan #18 2.5 is 93.2%). 15.7% of non-merge release changesets carry an interesting file. Comparison: beta median 61 changesets / 21 candidate-bearing; nightly median 672 / 266. Also: 5 of the 185 (2.7%) are blank-description security uplifts and 1 of those 5 bugs is still ABSENT from BMO (restricted) at read time.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked that the hg-to-git migration has not broken this path: json-rev for the newest release build revision (21a096119103) returns 200 on releases/mozilla-release, and all 26 json-pushes ranges resolved, so release revisions are still addressable by the hg client the tree uses. Also confirmed pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction('release') is True (any channel other than nightly), so the 6 merge windows will not be patch-extracted into ~7,000 redundant changesets rows.
gaps.proposed_fix: Put this table in section 2 of the release plan as the pro column, with two consequences stated: (a) agent.offstack.max_candidates = 150 is 3x above the ordinary release maximum of 49 and never binds in-cycle, same as plan #18 2.6 found for beta; (b) the x.0 build's window IS the cycle merge, so a signature first appearing on x.0 is a beta escape with a 6,952-changeset window, not a release-introduced regression — attach the release candidate window only to the DOT releases.

gaps.title: There is a release-only crash class and it is measurably worthless: 0 of the top 200 signatures is invisible upstream, and the 14% of the tail that is consists of third-party DLLs and distro rebuilds at <=21 installs
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: This is the argument that would justify release support on grounds nightly and beta cannot cover. Tested hard it does not hold at any volume the selector can reach, so the plan must not lean on it. The per-capita enrichment that DOES exist points at system add-ons, parser recursion and empty minidumps — none of which has an m-c regressor to name.
gaps.evidence: pop_23_release_only.py: of the top 200 release signatures by installs (92.6% of channel install-hits), 0 have zero nightly+beta reports over 2026-01-01..08-27. pop_24_tail_and_pop.py, random sample of 120 signatures ranked 200-2000: 17 (14.2%) are release-only, median 4 installs, max 21 — all below installs=50 — and the content is astmcwebextension3.dll, hpb6sy8739_x64gui.dll, aetcngss.dll, libc.so.6|libX11.so.6, libGL_INNO_MESA.so.1, plus boilerplate. Per-capita class enrichment (pop_26_final.py, signature installs / channel installs, 7 d): trainhop system-addon 39.4x (3.11% of release install-hits vs 0.08% beta / 0.04% nightly — AsyncShutdownTimeout|quit-application|newtabTrainhopAddon scheduleUpdate, 3,413 installs, the 6th-loudest release signature), stackoverflow 3.8x (4.74% vs 1.00/1.26), EMPTY minidump 3.4x (6.98% vs 2.07/1.48), AsyncShutdownTimeout 1.0x, shutdownhang 1.0x, OOM 0.7x (beta worse), IPCError-browser 0.4x (nightly worse). Structural population (pop_24): cpu_arch x86 release 10.3% vs beta 40.0% vs nightly 1.2%; signatures naming a non-Mozilla/non-Windows binary release 6.0% of signatures / 2.8% of install-hits vs nightly 14.1% / 11.7%.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Three attempts to rescue the claim. (1) Maybe 8 months upstream is too generous: re-ran the top 60 against a 30-day upstream window — still 0/60 release-only (pop_33_falsify.py), and the same script proves the query CAN return 0 (astmcwebextension3.dll returns 0 in both windows). (2) Maybe absence is the wrong test and per-capita enrichment the right one: ran it, and the enriched classes are trainhop / stackoverflow / empty-minidump, all unactionable, with OOM and IPC actually DE-enriched on release. (3) Maybe release has the old-hardware / 32-bit population nightly cannot see: measured false — x86 is a BETA phenomenon (40.0%) not a release one (10.3%), and third-party binaries in the signature are 4x more common on nightly than release.
gaps.proposed_fix: Delete the release-only argument from the plan's motivation, or restate it as what it is: a 14%-of-tail population of third-party-software and Linux-distro crashes at <=21 installs, below every threshold, with no Mozilla regressor. Keep the one measured exception visible so it is not re-litigated: AsyncShutdownTimeout|quit-application|newtabTrainhopAddon scheduleUpdate at 39.4x enrichment and 3.1% of the channel is genuinely release-only (system add-on trainhop updates do not ship to nightly or beta) — and it is a shutdown hang on an add-on update, still out of scope.

gaps.title: Release's per-(signature, build) install distribution is almost identical to beta's, so `installs` 50 vs 6 is not a volume calibration and cannot be defended as one
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Plan #18 11 says release's thresholds "exist and nothing about them is measured" — the implicit expectation is that release needs a much higher threshold because it is 40x bigger. Measured, it does not: the distribution the threshold cuts is the same shape as beta's, because the 10% sample and release's 12x-longer signature tail cancel the 40x population. So 50 is not scaled for release; it is an arbitrary point on a beta-shaped curve, and its only defensible justification is candidate supply.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_25_enrich.py, per-(signature, buildid) install cardinality over builds built inside the window. Release (2 builds, 20260812182057 + 20260824154132, 13,868 pairs): p50 1, p75 2, p90 5, p95 12, p99 93, max 11,471; installs>=50 fires on 220 pairs (1.59%), >=6 on 1,264 (9.11%). Beta (4 builds, 1,955 pairs): p50 1, p75 2, p90 5, p95 12, p99 48, max 365; >=50 on 15 (0.77%), >=6 on 176 (9.00%). The bodies are identical to the p95. Mechanism: release build 20260812182057 has 8,521 distinct signatures against beta 20260819090452's 439 — 35x the installs spread over 19x the signatures.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I expected release's distribution to be shifted right by roughly the 4.1x install-thinning factor relative to beta's true distribution, which would make 6 map to ~24, not 50. That is consistent with what I measured — the identical percentiles are the OBSERVED distributions with thinning already baked into release's. So the honest reading is that at installs=6 release and beta select the same 9% of pairs, but release's 6 means ~25 machines and beta's means 6; at 50 release selects 1.59% meaning ~205 machines. Neither number is wrong; the plan just must not claim either is calibrated.
gaps.proposed_fix: Keep installs=50 and justify it by candidate supply (220 pairs per cycle over two builds = ~110/build = ~1/day in scope), explicitly NOT by machine count, and record the 4.1x conversion next to it. Do the same for spike.floor=50: it is 5x beta's 10 on a distribution whose p99 is 93 vs beta's 48, so it is roughly the same percentile — say so rather than leaving it unexplained.

gaps.title: SuperSearch silently substitutes a 7-day window when `date` is omitted, and `_facets_size: 0` silently kills every facet — both fired during this recon
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Production is safe — every SuperSearch in the tree that needs a window passes one (search_date in datacollector, date in population/machine/sigtrend) — but any release measurement or offline replay that omits `date` silently reports a week instead of a lifetime, and on release the error is 15x. Plan #18 1.2's "Lifetime totals, all channels, no date bound" is the exact phrasing that triggers it.
gaps.evidence: spike/_release_recon/pop_09_population_fixed.py, same query twice on release build 20260810162159: date omitted gives 7,744 reports / 6,926 installs; date=">=2026-01-01" gives 112,611 / 81,843 — a 14.5x understatement. My own pop_08 produced a whole table of wrong "lifetime" numbers this way before I caught it. Separately, pop_10b_hist_probe.py: adding `_facets_size: 0` to a request with `_histogram.date` returns facets {} with errors [] — every facet vanishes with no error, and my first arrival-curve run reported 0 days for all 27 builds as a result.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Checked whether the 7-day default is a libmozdata artifact rather than Socorro's: the same omission through a plain net.get against the SuperSearch endpoint reproduces it, and _results_number=0 does not change it, so it is the service's default. Also confirmed the tree is not exposed — grep shows every SuperSearch call site in crashclouseau passes an explicit date or search_date.
gaps.proposed_fix: No production change needed. Put both traps in the plan's measurement-rules section (plan #18 12 is the right home) so the release recon's numbers can be re-derived: always pass `date`, never pass `_facets_size: 0`, and treat any "no date bound" figure in an existing document as suspect until re-measured.

gaps.title: Release has NO aurora-style channel alias — but Firefox 153 is also an ESR on the same codebase, and ESR is UNSAMPLED, which is a free high-resolution instrument for release code
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks — this closes the question the ask raised. What is worth adding is the positive: the same code that ships to release 153.x also ships to esr153 under a channel the collector accepts at 100%, so for any release signature there is a 0.3%-sized but unthinned view of the same defect.
gaps.evidence: Buildhub channel facet for source.product=firefox, build.id>=20260101 (pop_02_buildhub_raw.py): nightly 3002, beta 751, aurora 546, release 205, esr 199, nightly-maple 69 — ESR is its own target.channel, and all 29 esr target.versions carry an esr suffix which buildhub.VERSION_PATS['release'] = [0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? rejects (verified per version); all 32 release target.versions match it. Socorro release_channel for Firefox 2026-08 (pop_03, pop_04): release 595,774, esr 449,667, nightly 31,763, beta 26,254, default 17,104, aurora 15,928, plus junk (Bosch 1,565, no 1,025, esr140 976, esr115 811, r 24, release-localtest 4, norelease 1, releasexx 1) — ESR never appears as release. So get_search_channel('release') returning the bare label is correct and needs no change. The instrument: esr153 family (153.0esr / 153.1.0esr / 153.2.0esr) over 2026-08-01..08-29 is 9,683 reports / 4,204 installs / 1,116 signatures at reports-per-install 2.30, against release 153.x's 333,402 / 232,331 / 19,845 at 1.44 (pop_31_esr153.py) — 2.82% of observed 153 reports, ~0.29% of true 153 crashes, and it is what supplied the ground-truth k-distribution for the 4.1x thinning factor.
gaps.falsification_attempt: Tried to find a release alias by faceting release_channel with no filter and reading the whole tail — the only release-adjacent labels are release-localtest (4 reports), releasexx and norelease (1 each), i.e. noise, plus `default` (17,104) which is locally-built Firefox, not release. Also checked that ESR is not partially filed under release by faceting release's version: the top 25 are all bare x.y.z with no esr suffix.
gaps.proposed_fix: State in the plan that release needs no get_search_channel change and that the Buildhub regexp already excludes ESR — the aurora lesson does NOT transport, and nobody should spend time on it. Separately note esr153 as a measurement instrument: any release-signature question needing unthinned per-machine structure (the bad-machine gate, population's concentration flags) can be asked of esr153 instead, at 1/350th the volume and 100% of the reports.

measurements.claim: Release cadence: 27 builds over 145.2 days, median consecutive gap 4.96 d, 1.25 builds/week; 7 majors and 20 dot releases; 3 versions respun
measurements.method: buildhub.get(20260401000000, 'release', prods='firefox') through the repo's own client and its VERSION_PATS['release'] regexp; consecutive build-date gaps

Per-capita, release's OOM share is 0.7x beta's (37.4% of install-hits vs 51.6%), and cpu_arch=x86 is 10.3% on release against 40.0% on BETA and 1.2% on nightly — the 32-bit population that drives beta's OOM|large escalation is a beta/DevEdition phenomenon, not a release one. kills.idea: Release builds accumulate crashes too slowly, or arrive too late, for the selector to see a spike in time
kills.why_dead: Measured false in both directions. A release build gets a median 16.0 days of window life and 5.0 days at index 1 (the only selecting position), and it holds 41.3% of its eventual crashes when it arrives there and 79.6% when it leaves — plenty. The real defect is the opposite: the BASELINE it is compared against holds 80.7%, a 0.51x maturity handicap turning ratio=3 into 5.9x. Fixing the clock buys nothing; fixing the comparison does. spike/_release_recon/pop_12_window.py

kills.idea: There is a class of crash only release can see, and that is the reason to support release
kills.why_dead: Tested three ways and it fails at every volume the selector can reach. (1) Absence: 0 of the top 200 release signatures by installs (92.6% of channel install-hits) has zero nightly+beta reports over 8 months, and 0 of the top 60 over 30 days — with the query proven able to return 0 (astmcwebextension3.dll returns 0 in both windows). (2) The tail: 14.2% of a 120-signature sample from ranks 200-2000 IS release-only, but median 4 installs / max 21, all below the release threshold of 50, and the content is third-party DLLs (astmcwebextension3.dll, hpb6sy8739_x64gui.dll, aetcngss.dll) and Linux distro rebuilds (libc.so.6, libGL_INNO_MESA.so.1).
