kills.idea: Release needs handling for ipc_channel_error=ShutDownKill, which antenna throttles to 10% on top of the release 10%
kills.why_dead: Measured: 1 report in 28 days on release (2026-08-20..27 window: 1 of 151,356). The rule is real (antenna is_shutdownkill, (10, CONTINUE, REJECT)) and it does bite — on NIGHTLY, where ShutDownKill is 1,029 reports = 3.5% of the channel — but there is no release population to handle. spike/_release_recon/pop_06_throttle.py, pop_07_mixture.py

kills.idea: Raise population.facets_size so release's install_time facet is not truncated
kills.why_dead: Measured unaffordable and unnecessary. The loudest release head signature has 19,062 installs in 7 days, so covering it needs more than 19,000 terms — a 19x heavier facet on every crashstack.html render behind one gunicorn worker with a 6s read timeout (net.py:68). The same query already returns _cardinality.install_time for free, which gives the exact install count and the exact per_install with no facet at all. Fix the arithmetic, not the size. spike/_release_recon/pop_30_truncation.py

kills.idea: Estimate the release sampling factor by comparing reports-per-install across channels
kills.why_dead: Measured to be the wrong instrument, and it gives the wrong answer. Release reports-per-install is 1.37 and beta's 1.59 — 0.86x, nothing like 0.1x — because thinning conditions on at least one surviving report, so a machine with one true crash shows 1.0 whether sampled or not. The route that works is applying antenna's own rule to an unsampled same-codebase population (esr153, mean k 2.314), which predicts observed 1.26 against release 153.x's actual 1.44 and yields the 4.1x install-count understatement. spike/_release_recon/pop_32_thinning.py

open_questions: Is release ingestion wanted at all, given the population argument is 1-of-188 signatures per cycle new-on-release-and-unseen-upstream, 23.5% of volume in scope, and a 0.51x maturity handicap — against a candidate window of median 4 changesets? RECOMMENDATION: no to the build-day spike selector on release; yes to a cross-channel escalation alarm for the 6-of-188 class that reaches release already visible on nightly/beta, which is the population that actually exists and which plan #18 section 13's nightly_vs_beta prior art prices at ~2 days of lead.

Which correction for the maturity handicap: (a) restrict the test build-day and its baseline build-days to the same number of days-since-ship (free — the arrival curve comes from the facet already fetched), or (b) leave the handicap and set spike.ratio on release to 1.5 so the effective bar matches beta's 4.2x? RECOMMENDATION: (a) — it is the correct comparison and it also improves beta, whose handicap is 0.71x; (b) is a number fitted to one channel's arrival curve and will drift with the cadence.

Does sigtrend cover release (raise FACETS_SIZE to 5000 and MAX_SIGNATURES to 4000, verified to fit at 3,143 of 3,154, and pay 216,720 backfill rows plus 1.13M rows/year = 4.7x the two supported channels combined), or stay out? RECOMMENDATION: stay out, and say so in the plan rather than leaving the channel guard to answer it silently. The statistic's measured value is as an ORDERING over an existing candidate list, and release's list is ~110 (signature,build) pairs per build.

Is installs=50 kept as-is with the plan stating it means ~205 real machines (4.1x), or re-set to make the machine count comparable to beta's 6? RECOMMENDATION: keep 50 and justify it by candidate supply, not by machines. Making machine counts comparable would put release's threshold at ~2 observed installs, which fires on 9%+ of 13,868 pairs; and the two channels' observed distributions are identical through the p95, so no value makes the numbers mean the same thing.

How is the release population panel fixed: derive installs and per_install from _cardinality.install_time and label the shape flags as top-N (cheap, correct, and it also fixes the 10-15% truncated cases on nightly and beta), or suppress the panel on release? RECOMMENDATION: fix the arithmetic — the max observed misreport is 6.93x on the exact ratio the module exists to protect.

Does the bad-machine gate run on release at ~10x lower recall, or not run at all? RECOMMENDATION: run it unchanged and record that its recall on release is sampling-bounded. Do NOT lower min_signatures — measured meaningless at the thinning-equivalent value of 2, which 76.5% of the busiest 10,000 release installs satisfy.

Should the release candidate window be attached only to DOT releases, leaving x.0 builds unanalysed? The x.0 window IS the cycle merge (median 6,952 changesets, 0-2 candidate-bearing non-merge), so a signature first appearing on x.0 is a beta escape, not a release-introduced regression. RECOMMENDATION: yes — analyse dot releases only, which is 20 of 26 intervals and where the median-4-changeset window lives.
cross_dimension: SuperSearch substitutes a 7-DAY window when `date` is omitted. Same query on release build 20260810162159: no date gives 7,744 reports / 6,926 installs; date>=2026-01-01 gives 112,611 / 81,843 — a 14.5x understatement. Production is safe (every call site in the tree passes a window) but plan #18 section 1.2's "Lifetime totals, all channels, no date bound: 8/4, 13/6, 7/7, 17/4, 1/1" and "435-9,124 reports for all 54 other builds" are phrased exactly the way that triggers it — the merge-day-b1 conclusion is almost certainly still right (a build nobody ran has no reports in any window) but the 435-9,124 denominators should be re-measured before anyone reuses them. spike/_release_recon/pop_09_population_fixed.py

`_facets_size: 0` silently returns facets {} with errors [] — every facet vanishes, no error. My first arrival-curve run reported 0 days for all 27 builds because of it. Worth a line in the measurement-rules section next to the date trap. spike/_release_recon/pop_10b_hist_probe.py

user_comments and phc_kind are permissions_needed ['protected'] and a FILTER on them is silently ignored, not rejected: user_comments=!__null__ on release returned the full 563,944 total rather than 0 or an error. Same family as the RemoteType / SuperSearchUnredacted finding in memory, but the failure mode is worse — a protected FACET comes back absent (visible), a protected FILTER comes back as no filter at all (invisible). Anything in the tree or in a recon that filters on a protected field is measuring the unfiltered population.

antenna's has_old_buildid rule REJECTS any crash report whose buildid is more than 730 days old, before any channel rule runs. Anything reasoning about the long tail of old builds still crashing (release's builds table, sigage's all-time clock, the 2-year-old-build population on crashstack.html) is looking at a hard 730-day horizon imposed upstream, not at the real population.

antenna's is_shutdownkill rule throttles ipc_channel_error=ShutDownKill to 10% on ALL channels including nightly and beta — it sits above is_alpha_beta_esr and is_nightly in the ruleset. Nightly shows 1,029 ShutDownKill reports = 3.5% of the channel over 7 days, so that slice represents ~10,290 true crashes. Any nightly volume or rate statistic including ShutDownKill understates it by 10x. Source: raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla-services/antenna/main/antenna/throttler.py MOZILLA_RULES.

antenna's release 10% rule is keyed on ProductName == 'Firefox', so Firefox for Android (ProductName=Fenix) release is accepted at 100%. Relevant to plan #16's Fenix work: Fenix release is an unsampled channel and its install counts mean what they say, unlike desktop release's.

libmozdata.hgmozilla.Mercurial.get_repo_url('esr') returns https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-esr, which is not a repository — ESR repos are per-version (mozilla-esr115, mozilla-esr140, mozilla-esr153). Plan #18 section 11 scopes ESR out on the _ensure_enum_values grounds; this is a second, independent blocker for whoever picks it up.

Firefox 153 is ALSO an ESR (153.0esr / 153.1.0esr / 153.2.0esr, release_channel=esr, 9,683 reports / 4,204 installs in 28 days). It shares release 153.x's codebase at the branch point and it is UNSAMPLED. Two consequences outside my dimension: (a) the BMO signature-search venue problem gains an arm — a release-153 signature also carries esr153 reports and cf_crash_signature search has no channel filter either; (b) whoever owns the agent's crash facts has a free unthinned instrument for any release signature at 1/350th the volume.

3 of 27 release builds since 2026-04-01 are respins sharing a build DAY with the real build (20260506041011/20260506140522, 20260727110312/20260727124451) and 2 of those have literally 0 reports. datacollector.get_new_signatures collapses them into one build-day so the day is not dead — but Build.get_last_versions(n=3) counts BUILDS, so a respin pair spends two of the three window slots on one day, leaving the release series with 2 evaluable build-days instead of 3 and only index 1 testable. The selection dimension should replay that.

Buildhub's release list is missing 148.0.1, 149.0.1 and 153.0.2 — those version numbers exist in the sequence but were never shipped as desktop release builds. Anything inferring a dot-release sequence by incrementing the last component will be wrong roughly 1 cycle in 3.

reports.headline: The refusal at `sigtrend.py:133` is not arithmetic, it is a facet-page choice, and I bought it: the complete release per-signature facet closes at 3,218 terms for 0.59 s and 410 KB per day (91/91 days complete, `sum(facet counts) == total`), a 70-day cold backfill is 56 s, and the rollup costs a measured +105.7 MB in real Postgres 16 on a database at 204 MB of 10 GB. The ~3,200 figure is right (mean 2,984, weekday 3,247, max 3,686 over 91 days) and the 10% sampling is confirmed at source (`antenna/throttler.py` `is_firefox_desktop` -> `(10, ACCEPT, REJECT)`), but the docstring's reason is wrong: sigtrend only ever compares a signature to itself inside one channel, so a uniform sample cancels; what survives is that the release rate is class-dependent, 1% to 100% (ShutDownKill 1%, gpu/rdd/socket/utility/PHC/commented 100%), measured as a 15.8x gpu enrichment on release vs esr, and on 2 of the top 3 risers the throttle-class mix itself moved enough to manufacture up to 2.40x of a 3.94x "rise". Two things must not be ported: raising `FACETS_SIZE` alone still refuses release because `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` is a policy cap dressed up as a truncation guard, and the shipped 24 h build-axis window (`0aa2e02`) is a measured no-op on 24 of 26 release build pairs because a release build's pushdate equals its buildid and the median gap is 112 h. The real release attribution story is bimodal and it decides the value: 58.7% of release reports sit on a dot-release build with a 5-81 changeset window (better than nightly's 95), 41.3% sit on an x.0 merge-day build with a 5,405-7,462 changeset window that `max_candidates=150` samples at 2.0%.

gaps.title: The release refusal is a `_facets_size` choice, not a Socorro limit — the complete facet costs 0.59 s and the rollup costs 105.7 MB, both measured
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks — that is the problem. With release added to INGEST_CHANNELS/AGENT_CHANNELS and `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` untouched, `backfill` returns 0 forever, every release dossier carries `signature_trend: {}`, `is_rising` is permanently False, and the one prompt block built for an unattributable window (triage.py:1503, "NO CHANGESET IS REQUIRED FOR THIS ONE") can never fire on the 41.3% of release exposure that most needs it. The release channel gets the pipeline without the only statistic that can excuse an empty answer.
gaps.evidence: Measured live with production's own query shape (`spike/_release_recon/trend_03_release_universe.py`, 2026-06-01..08-30, 91 days): at `_facets_size=4000` every single day is COMPLETE (`sum(facet counts) == json["total"]`), mean 0.59 s (median 0.59, max 0.99), mean 409,711 bytes, 91 days in 54.1 s total. True distinct signatures/day: mean 2,984, median 3,112, p95 3,317, max 3,686, min 2,403; weekday means Mon 3,203 / Wed 3,247 / Sun 2,485. `_facets_size` accepted at 4000/5000/8000/10000 for this shape (3,218 terms, 445 KB, 0.52-1.67 s) — so `sigage.py:22`'s "`_facets_size=10000` is rejected outright (HTTP 400)" does not apply to `collect_day`'s shape. Raising it is free on the existing channels: nightly 2026-08-26 returns 276 terms and 37,777 bytes at 2000, 4000 and 10000 alike. DB cost measured in real Postgres 16 through the repo's own `SignatureDaily.record_day` (`spike/_release_recon/trend_11_pgsize.py`): nightly+beta 91 d = 55,465 rows / 21.8 MB total relation size; +release 91 d = 327,003 rows / 127.5 MB, i.e. release adds 271,538 rows (2,984/day) and 105.7 MB, of which 96 MB is the two composite indexes. Prod is `essential-1`, 204 MB / 10 GB (`heroku pg:info`), so this is 204 -> ~310 MB = 3.1% of the plan. Steady-state per run: 1 SuperSearch (0.59 s) + one full-day upsert (0.21 s measured, 4 chunks of <=1000 rows x 6 columns, far under the 65,535 bind ceiling) = 0.80 s; the clock runs `update_all` every 20 min (bin/schedule.py:55-57) so 72 x 0.80 s = 58 s/day. Cold start: 70 days (`BACKFILL_DAYS`) x 0.80 s = 56 s inside one `put_crashes` call.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried three ways to make release too expensive and failed at all three. (a) Is `_facets_size` capped? No — 10000 is accepted for this shape on three separate release days. (b) Does the 3,000-row upsert every 20 minutes hurt? 0.21 s measured against real Postgres (nightly 0.016 s); 15 s/day of writes. (c) Does the 70-day cold backfill blow the RQ job timeout? `worker.get_queue` sets `default_timeout=6000` (worker.py:57), not RQ's 180 s default, and the backfill is 56 s. I also checked the prune, which filters on `day` alone while both indexes lead with (product, channel): it IS a seq scan (EXPLAIN ANALYZE, `Rows Removed by Filter: 327003`) and it costs 19.5 ms — 14-44 ms through `SignatureDaily.prune()`. The hot read path uses `sigdaily_lookup_idx` at 0.45 ms.
gaps.proposed_fix: Four edits, all in `sigtrend.py` plus one test. (1) `FACETS_SIZE = 10000` (verified accepted; 4000 leaves only 8.5% headroom over the measured max of 3,686). (2) Replace `if len(rows) >= MAX_SIGNATURES` with the exact truncation test — `len(rows) >= FACETS_SIZE or sum(counts) != got["total"]` — and delete `MAX_SIGNATURES` (see the next gap). (3) `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS = ("nightly", "beta", "release")`. (4) Replace `tests/test_sigtrend.py:172` with a release test that asserts the query IS made and that a genuinely truncated response is still refused. Do NOT add per-channel thresholds (see kills).

gaps.title: `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` is documented as a truncation guard but is 75% of the facet page, so raising `FACETS_SIZE` alone still silently refuses release
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The obvious first attempt at buying release — bump `FACETS_SIZE` to 4000 and add release to `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` — writes zero rows on every single release day and logs one WARNING per day that reads like a Socorro problem. `collect_day` returns 0, `ChannelDaily.upsert` is never called, so `trend_facts` sees no exposure row and returns `{}` — indistinguishable from "the rollup is cold". The failure mode is a silent no-op behind a log line that names the wrong cause.
gaps.evidence: The comment at sigtrend.py:227-229 says "Refused rather than truncated", but 1500 < FACETS_SIZE = 2000, so the check fires 500 terms before truncation can begin. Truncation is exactly detectable and I measured the detector: on release 2026-08-26, `_facets_size=2000` -> 2000 terms / sum(counts)=21,598 vs total=22,816; `=3000` -> 3000 terms / 22,598 vs 22,816; `=4000` -> 3,218 terms / 22,816 == 22,816. So `len(sigs) >= facets_size` and `sum(counts) != total` both flag truncation exactly, and they agree on 100% of the 91 release + 206 nightly + 206 beta days I read (`facet_coverage_of_reports` == 1.0000 for every untruncated day). Verified end to end against production's own function with the writers mocked (`spike/_release_recon/trend_01_collect_day_cost.py`): `collect_day("Firefox", "release", 2026-08-26)` returned 0 after paying 0.38 s and 280 KB, logging "returned 2000 signatures (>= 1500): refusing to store a truncated day", `upsert_called: false`, `record_called: false`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I looked for a reason 1500 might be deliberately below 2000 — a Socorro quirk where the last terms of a full page are unreliable, or a day where the count is right but the cardinality sub-facet is missing. There is none: at `_facets_size=4000` the release facet's counts sum exactly to `total` and every term carries a `cardinality_install_time` value. I also checked git: `sigtrend.py` has exactly one commit (`a15cfd0`) and both constants have their original values, so 1500 was never a migrated-down number.
gaps.proposed_fix: Delete `MAX_SIGNATURES` and refuse on `len(rows) >= FACETS_SIZE or sum(r[0] for r in rows.values()) != got.get("total", 0)`. That is channel-agnostic, needs no magic number, and cannot be defeated by a future channel growing past a hand-set cap. Keep the WARNING but print the coverage fraction so the log says which of the two conditions fired.

gaps.title: The shipped 24 h build-axis attribution window is a measured no-op on release, and 41.3% of release exposure has a candidate window the cap samples at 2%
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing crashes; an expectation does. `0aa2e02` is the highest-value thing plan #19 shipped and it is worth exactly zero on release, so anyone budgeting the release project as "the trend work already landed, we just switch it on" is wrong about the half that matters. Worse, on the 41.3% of release exposure that sits on an x.0 merge-day build, the off-stack candidate list is 150 of 5,405-7,462 changesets — 2.0% of the window — so a named lead from that path is a lottery ticket, and the trend statistic is the only thing that could tell the model so.
gaps.evidence: `_offstack_window(rising=True)` sets `start = buildid - 24h` then pulls it back to `Build.get_pushdate_before(buildid)` whenever that is earlier (orchestrator.py:357-360), so the widening only bites when the previous build's pushdate is <24 h before this buildid. Measured off Buildhub + hg `json-rev` on `releases/mozilla-release` (`spike/_release_recon/trend_05*.py`): 27 release builds 2026-04-03..2026-08-26 (145 days, median gap 112 h, one build every 5.4 days); a build's revision pushdate equals its buildid to the second on 27 of 27; only 2 of 26 consecutive pairs are under 24 h apart (9.92 h for the second 150.0.2 build, 1.69 h for the second 153.0.1), so the widening changes nothing on 24 of 26 (92.3%). Where it does bite it is harmless and small: 7 -> 31 and 5 -> 40 changesets. The deployed windows, priced live: 154.0 (merge day) = 15 pushes / 7,462 changesets / 1 merge push; 155.0 = 15 pushes / 5,405 changesets / 1 merge push; the dot releases 153.0.3/153.0.4/154.0.1 = 45/35/71 pushes and 58/38/81 changesets. Exposure split (release_channel=release, product=Firefox, 2026-08-24..30, 144,236 reports, `version` facet, 97 versions, full coverage): x.0 versions 59,525 = 41.3%, x.y.z versions 84,711 = 58.7%. Attribution diffuseness measured directly (`trend_09`): for the top 20 risers, median share of window installs on the newest build = 36.9% on a run-day whose window straddles a ship (2026-08-30) and 11.4% on a quiet one (2026-08-20); median distinct buildids carrying the 7-day window = 3 and 12.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to find a release build cadence that makes 24 h useful. Two candidates: dot releases shipped hours apart (found 2, both rebuilds of the same version) and same-day multi-platform builds (none — release buildids are per-version, not per-platform, and Buildhub lists one revision per buildid). I also checked whether the widening could ever be NARROWER than the deployed bound on release and it cannot: the `prev < start` pull-back makes it a superset by construction, verified in `tests/test_trend_window.py` and by arithmetic on all 26 pairs. So the change is inert on release, not harmful.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not port, tune or extend `_RISE_WINDOW_HOURS` for release; leave it and record that it is inert. Instead spend the effort where the measurement points: make the merge-day case legible. Compute `len(window) / max_candidates` when the off-stack path enumerates, and when it exceeds ~10 (measured 50:1 on 154.0, 36:1 on 155.0, vs 2:1 on nightly's 24 h window) say so in the prompt and force the triage.py:1503 "no changeset is required" block on, whether or not `is_rising` fired. That block is worth more on release than on nightly and it currently depends on a statistic release does not have.

gaps.title: Release's Socorro sample is class-dependent from 1% to 100%, not a flat 10% — the docstring's reason for refusing release is wrong, and the real consequence is different
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Two separate things, and the module docstring names neither. (a) The stated reason — "its install counts are not comparable with the other two anyway" — is irrelevant: nothing in sigtrend or its three consumers ever compares install counts across channels, so if it were a flat sample it would cancel exactly. Refusing release for this reason refuses it for nothing. (b) The reason that IS real: the accept rate depends on the crash's own class, so `MIN_INSTALLS = 3` means ~3 true installs for a GPU-process signature, ~30-50 for a content-process one and ~300 for a ShutDownKill; and plan #19 item 2's cross-signature RANKER — the one part of the plan not yet shipped — would be ordering quantities sampled 100x apart.
gaps.evidence: Read live from the source of truth, `antenna/throttler.py` `MOZILLA_RULES` (fetched through `crashclouseau.net`): `Rule(rule_name="is_firefox_desktop", condition=ProductName=="Firefox" and ReleaseChannel=="release", result=(10, ACCEPT, REJECT))` — 10% nominal, confirmed. But the rule set is ORDERED and these all accept 100% ahead of it: `throttleable_0` (Throttleable=="0", about:crashes), `has_comments`, `has_phc` (PHCKind), `is_background` (ProcessType in {gpu, plugin, rdd, socket, utility}); and `is_shutdownkill` (ipc_channel_error=="ShutDownKill") is `(10, CONTINUE, REJECT)` which then falls through to `is_firefox_desktop`'s 10% = 1% effective. `is_alpha_beta_esr` and `is_nightly` are plain ACCEPT, so nightly/beta/aurora/esr are unsampled — which makes esr the right unthrottled reference for release, not nightly. Measured `process_type` shares (product=Firefox, 2026-08-24..30, `spike/_release_recon/trend_13_nonuniform_sampling.py`): gpu release 1.296% vs esr 0.082% = 15.8x, rdd 0.105% vs 0.003% = 35x, utility 0.035% vs 0.000%, content 46.303% vs 69.794% = 0.66x. Solving `observed = s/(s + r(1-s))` on the gpu share gives a non-background accept rate r = 6.2%, and the same arithmetic on the `throttleable` F-share (release 6.63% vs esr 1.09% over August) gives r = 6.22% — two independent routes agreeing, both bracketing the nominal 10%.
gaps.falsification_attempt: My first estimator was `throttleable` alone, and I killed it myself: applied with esr as reference it implies r = 0.1434 for nightly and r = 0.3799 for beta, which is impossible since both are plain ACCEPT. The release-wide F-share is also not stable in time (weekly over 91 days: 0.0297 to 0.1311), so a single-day reading of 9.58% that happened to solve to r = 0.102 was a coincidence and I discarded it. Nightly is likewise refuted as a reference (release/nightly gpu share ratio is 0.10x, because nightly's own composition is 40.1% rdd from nightly-specific bugs). Only esr survives as a reference, and only for the composition argument, not for a precise r.
gaps.proposed_fix: Fix the docstring to say the true thing: the sample cancels in a within-signature ratio and the residual risk is class-dependence, not cross-channel comparability. Then, if release is admitted, add one clause to `describe()` on release only — "... (Socorro accepts ~10% of release crash reports, so these are sampled counts)" — because `report_bug.py:695` puts that sentence in a Bugzilla comment where "N distinct installations" reads as a population claim. And record in `corroborations.py` that `signature_trend_score` must not be used as a cross-signature ranker on release without a per-class correction; today it is write-only, which is why this is not yet a live bug.

gaps.title: A signature's throttle-class mix can shift, and on 2 of the 3 loudest release risers it moved enough to manufacture most of the "rise"
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The one release-specific way `is_rising` produces a false positive on the head of the list — precisely the signatures a human will look at first. `EMPTY: no frame data available; EmptyMinidump` is the loudest riser on 2026-08-25 at 5,694 window installs and ratio 3.94, and up to 2.40x of that 3.94x is a collection artefact rather than a rate change. A bug comment saying "the crash rate for this signature has risen 3.9x" on that signature is wrong in a way a Socorro-literate reviewer can refute in one query.
gaps.evidence: `throttleable` F-share for the top 15 risers on release as of 2026-08-25, 7-day window (2026-08-19..25) vs 56-day baseline (2026-06-24..08-18), `spike/_release_recon/trend_08_throttle_bias.py`: `EMPTY: no frame data available; EmptyMinidump` 0.4762 -> 0.8471 (ratio 3.94, 15,490 -> 6,552 reports); `OOM | large | EMPTY: no frame data available; EmptyMinidump` 0.3592 -> 0.8645 (ratio 3.87); `IPCError-browser | GPUProcessKill` 0.8406 -> 0.9216 (ratio 7.33). Because F is accepted at 100% and T at r, observed count is proportional to `f + (1-f)r` in the TRUE F-share f; inverting the observed shares at r = 0.1 gives f 0.0833 -> 0.3565 and an observed-count multiplier of 2.40x with no change in the true rate, i.e. 61% of the first signature's measured 3.94x. The other 12 of 15 move by only a few points (e.g. `stackoverflow | cssparser::parser::Parser::skip_whitespace` 0.0074 -> 0.0097, `nsWrapperCache::GetWrapperMaybeDead` 0.0512 -> 0.0401).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether this is universal (it is not — 12 of 15 risers are stable, so it is a head-of-list problem) and whether it could be an artefact of the baseline being short for high-ratio risers (the three affected signatures have 15,490 / 2,213 / 3,161 baseline reports, so no). I could not falsify the direction: for any r < 1, a rise in the observed F-share must inflate the observed count, and the arithmetic only gets worse as r gets smaller (at the measured r = 0.062 the multiplier is 3.2x, not 2.4x).
gaps.proposed_fix: On release only, add `"throttleable": "T"` to `collect_day`'s params so the rollup measures one uniformly-sampled population. That costs nothing (same query, same 0.59 s), makes the sample rate constant by construction, and the ~9.6% of release reports it drops are the ones whose acceptance is user-driven rather than random. It must be a per-channel query knob, not a global one — on nightly/beta everything is accepted, so filtering there would silently delete 1% of a channel's denominator for no reason. Alternative if a per-channel param is unwanted: refuse a release rise whose `throttleable` F-share moved by more than ~0.1 between window and baseline (one extra query per riser, ~2 signatures/run-day at nightly's rate).

gaps.title: `backfill` refuses an unsupported channel silently — the exact shape of the four silent no-ops this repo has already been bitten by
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: If release goes into `INGEST_CHANNELS`/`AGENT_CHANNELS` and someone forgets `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS`, every release dossier gets `signature_trend: {}` forever. There is no log line, no counter, and no web surface (I grepped: the rollup reaches only the agent prompt via triage.py:631 and the bug comment via report_bug.py:676 — `templates/` never touches it). The only observable is the absence of `chandaily` rows for release, which reads identically to "the rollup is still warming up".
gaps.evidence: `sigtrend.py:251-252` is a bare `if channel not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS: return 0`, and `update.put_crashes` (update.py:239) discards the return value inside a try/except that logs only on exception. `trend_facts` then returns `{}` at sigtrend.py:307-308 because `ChannelDaily.series` is empty, and both consumers treat `{}` as "not measured" and emit nothing (triage.py:632-633, report_bug.py:691-693). Correct by design, invisible by accident.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether some other surface would notice: `bin/predeploy.py`, `api.py`, `templates/*.html` — none reads `chandaily`/`sigdaily`. `tests/test_corroboration_registry.py` only checks that declared keys are written somewhere, not per channel. So nothing catches it.
gaps.proposed_fix: One `logger.info("sigtrend does not cover %s-%s; no rate statistic will be computed", product, channel)` on the refusal, rate-limited to once per process per channel. Cheap, and it is the difference between a five-minute diagnosis and the five-day one `feedback.refresh` cost (bin/schedule.py:28-31).

gaps.title: `collect_all` iterates `config.get_channels()` — which already includes release — and has no callers at all
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing today: it is dead code, and the `backfill` guard makes it safe even if revived. But it is the exact trap the ask asks about — a function whose channel source is the config list rather than `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` — so the first person who wires a scheduled rollup job will wire it, and the day `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` and the truncation check disagree it will silently write truncated release days.
gaps.evidence: Grepped `collect_all` across the whole tree excluding `spike/`: it appears only at its own definition (sigtrend.py:383) and nowhere else — not in `bin/schedule.py` (which registers exactly four jobs: `update.update_all`, `orchestrator.reap_stale_agent_jobs`, `orchestrator.sweep_untriaged_crashes`, `feedback.refresh`), not in `bin/`, not in `Procfile`, not in tests. The only live path into the collector is `update.put_crashes` -> `sigtrend.backfill(product, channel)` at update.py:239, which is guarded. `collect_all` also duplicates the two `prune()` calls that `put_crashes` already makes (update.py:250-251).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I searched for indirect dispatch (`getattr`, string job names, RQ `func_name` strings) in case it is enqueued by name — nothing. `_chain_is_running` builds names from function objects only.
gaps.proposed_fix: Delete it, or change its default to `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` and add a caller. Deleting is better: `put_crashes` already does the work per (product, channel) on the 20-minute clock, so a second entry point is a second place for the channel list to be wrong.

gaps.title: `triage.py` blames facet truncation for the 80.7% "rate not measurable" share; the facet has never truncated on nightly or beta, and the real cause is `MIN_INSTALLS`
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: It makes truncation look like an inherent property of the design, and it will be quoted as a reason release "cannot" be covered — which is the opposite of true, since release truncates for one reason (facet page too small) that is fixable in one constant, while the 78-79% non-measurable share is a deliberate install floor that behaves identically on all three channels.
gaps.evidence: The docstring says "`sigdaily` is filled from a COUNT-ordered facet page, so it holds only the loud signatures". Measured over the study's own 206-day panel at the deployed `FACETS_SIZE = 2000` (unchanged since `a15cfd0`, the file's only commit): nightly distinct signatures/day min 0, median 259, p95 304, max 337; beta min 0, median 405, p95 468, max 511 — 3.9x and 5.9x under the page, and `sum(facet counts) == total` on every day I sampled (`facet_coverage_of_reports` 1.0000). The real cause is `MIN_INSTALLS = 3` at sigtrend.py:317-318: replaying production's own `trend_facts` over 23-28 run-days, facts/active = 22.0% nightly, 23.2% beta, 21.1% release, i.e. 78-79% of active signatures are not measurable on every channel including the unthrottled ones. Note also that beta's documented range ("290-450", sigtrend.py:122) understates its measured max of 511.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I considered that the 80.7% figure might have been measured against a prod `sigdaily` that was genuinely thin at the time (the feature had just landed, so `MIN_BASELINE_COVERAGE = 21` would reject) — that would make the number right for a third reason, still not truncation. Either way the stated mechanism is refuted: the facet page is 4-6x the observed need on both channels the rollup covers.
gaps.proposed_fix: Correct the sentence to name the install floor. While there, update sigtrend.py:121-122 and :129-131 with the measured ranges (nightly <=337, beta <=511, release 2,403-3,686 over 91 days) so the next person sizing `FACETS_SIZE` is not sizing against numbers that are already low.

Prune predicate: Seq Scan, Rows Removed by Filter 327,003, Execution Time 19.533 ms; through the model 14-44 ms (n=6). Series read: Index Scan on sigdaily_lookup_idx, 0.447 ms. Clock cadence 20 min (bin/schedule.py:55) -> 72 runs/day -> 58 s/day of release rollup work, 15 s/day of it writes.

measurements.claim: The 24 h build-axis window is inert on release: a release build's pushdate is its buildid, and only 2 of 26 build pairs are under 24 h apart
measurements.method: Buildhub release builds since 2026-04-01, each revision's pushdate from hg `json-rev` on `releases/mozilla-release`, then `json-pushes` priced for the deployed window (prev pushdate+1s .. buildid) and the widened one (min(buildid-24h, prev pushdate) .. buildid)
measurements.numbers: 27 builds 2026-04-03..2026-08-26 (145 days, one per 5.4 days, median gap 112 h). pushdate - buildid = 0.00 h on 27/27. Pairs under 24 h: 2 of 26 (9.92 h, 1.69 h) -> widening inert on 24/26 = 92.3%. Where it bites: 7 -> 31 and 5 -> 40 changesets. Deployed windows: 154.0 = 15 pushes / 7,462 changesets / 1 merge push; 155.0 = 15 / 5,405 / 1; 153.0.3 = 45 / 58 / 0; 153.0.4 = 35 / 38 / 0; 154.0.1 = 71 / 81 / 0.

Per-riser diffuseness: median newest-build share of window installs 36.9% (asof 2026-08-30) / 11.4% (asof 2026-08-20); median distinct buildids per 7-day window 3 / 12.

measurements.claim: The 10% release sample is real but class-dependent from 1% to 100%, and esr — not nightly — is the valid unthrottled reference
measurements.method: Read `antenna/throttler.py` `MOZILLA_RULES` from source, then tested the composition prediction with `process_type` and `ipc_channel_error` facets per channel, and solved observed = s/(s + r(1-s)) for r using esr's share as s
measurements.numbers: Source: `is_firefox_desktop` (ProductName==Firefox and ReleaseChannel==release) -> `(10, ACCEPT, REJECT)`; `is_nightly` and `is_alpha_beta_esr` (aurora/beta/esr) -> ACCEPT; ahead of them `throttleable_0`, `has_comments`, `has_phc`, `is_background` (gpu/plugin/rdd/socket/utility) -> ACCEPT 100%; `is_shutdownkill` -> `(10, CONTINUE, REJECT)` then 10% again = 1%. Empirical process_type shares (2026-08-24..30): gpu release 1.296% vs esr 0.082% (15.8x), rdd 0.105% vs 0.003% (35x), utility 0.035% vs 0.000%, content 46.303% vs 69.794% (0.66x). Implied non-background accept rate r = 6.2% from gpu, r = 6.22% from the August `throttleable` F-share (release 6.63% vs esr 1.09%). Nightly refuted as a reference (release/nightly gpu ratio 0.10x; nightly is 40.1% rdd from its own bugs).

kills.idea: Cover release with a narrower facet — top-N signatures only, or an installs-thresholded query
kills.why_dead: There is nothing to narrow. The COMPLETE release facet is 3,218 terms, 445 KB and 0.59 s (91/91 days complete at `_facets_size=4000`; 10000 is also accepted and returns byte-identical results). A narrower facet would be a workaround for a cost that does not exist, and it would reintroduce exactly the COUNT-ordered truncation the module exists to avoid — the quiet signatures are the ones the statistic is for.

kills.idea: Control release row growth by storing only signatures above an install floor at collect time
kills.why_dead: Measured, and it churns the answer. 69.9% of release daily rows have installs == 1 (nightly is 70.4% — not a release peculiarity), so an `installs >= 2` floor keeps 30.1% of rows. But replaying `is_rising` on the floored panel: asof 2026-08-20, 148 risers full vs 150 floored, with 69 lost and 71 gained; asof 2026-08-30, 131 vs 126 with 61 lost and 56 gained. Dropping a row lowers the 56-day BASELINE as well as the 7-day window, so it invents rises as fast as it deletes them. The 105.7 MB is affordable; this saving is not free.

kills.idea: Give release its own `MIN_INSTALLS` / `MIN_INTERESTING_RATIO` / `WORDING_MIN_INSTALLS`, because release is 5x louder
kills.why_dead: Dead as a prompt-dilution argument, which is the only thing the thresholds control today. Nothing consumes the universe-wide alarm count — the ranker from plan #19 item 2 is NOT shipped (`signature_trend_score` appears only in `corroborations.py`'s registry text and two docstrings; no caller cuts on it). What the thresholds actually decide is how often the sentence appears on a crash the pipeline analysed, and among the loudest signatures release fires on 16% of the top 25 and 13% of the top 100, against nightly's 8% and 15%. The composition is no worse either (37.0% boilerplate vs nightly's 42.4%, median ratio 5.1 vs 5.7). If someone still wants absolute parity with nightly's 24-32 alarms/day, the swept grid says ratio 3.0 / floor 30 gives 24 on release — but they should be able to name what reads that number first.

kills.idea: Release is 10% sampled, therefore its install counts are not comparable and the statistic cannot be computed
kills.why_dead: The premise is right and the conclusion does not follow. `trend_facts` compares a signature's 7-day window against its OWN 56-day baseline, with the SAME channel's exposure on both sides (sigtrend.py:320-321); there is no cross-channel comparison anywhere in the module or its three consumers, so a uniform sample cancels. Measured: facts are computable for 21.1% of active release signatures against 22.0% on unsampled nightly — the sample costs essentially nothing in coverage. The surviving objections are narrower and different: the rate is class-dependent (1% ShutDownKill to 100% background-process), and `describe()` prints a sampled absolute count into a Bugzilla comment. Residual I could not eliminate: install cardinality is sublinear in the sample rate (E[observed] = sum over installs of 1-(1-p)^k), so the cancellation is first-order rather than exact; at release's observed 1.22 reports/install the second-order distortion is small and its direction is conservative (it dampens rises driven by repeat crashers, which is what installs-not-reports wants).

kills.idea: Raise `FACETS_SIZE` and release is covered
kills.why_dead: `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` refuses it anyway, on every day, because it is a policy cap (75% of the 2000-term page) rather than the truncation guard its comment claims. Verified live: `collect_day("Firefox", "release", 2026-08-26)` returns 0 with `upsert_called: false`. Both constants have to move, or better, both should be replaced by the exact truncation test I measured (`len(rows) >= FACETS_SIZE or sum(counts) != total`, which agrees with reality on 91 release + 206 nightly + 206 beta days).

kills.idea: The 70-day cold release backfill will blow the RQ job timeout inside one `update` run
kills.why_dead: `worker.get_queue` sets `default_timeout=6000` (worker.py:57), overriding RQ 2.10's 180 s default, and the cold release backfill is 70 x 0.80 s = 56 s. `backfill` even has a `budget` parameter for this, and `put_crashes` correctly does not need to pass it.

kills.idea: The 90-day prune, which filters on `day` alone while both indexes lead with (product, channel), will seq-scan a 327k-row table 216 times a day
kills.why_dead: It does seq-scan — EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) confirms `Rows Removed by Filter: 327003` — and it costs 19.5 ms, 14-44 ms through `SignatureDaily.prune()`. At 3 channels x 72 runs that is under 10 s/day. No index needed.

kills.idea: Port or re-tune the shipped 24 h build-axis attribution window for release
kills.why_dead: Inert by measurement. A release build's revision pushdate equals its buildid to the second on 27 of 27 builds, and only 2 of 26 consecutive pairs are under 24 h apart, so `min(buildid-24h, prev_pushdate)` returns `prev_pushdate` on 92.3% of release builds and the widened window IS the deployed window. On the two rebuild pairs where it bites it goes 7 -> 31 and 5 -> 40 changesets — harmless, and nowhere near the problem. Release's attribution problem is the opposite of nightly's: too WIDE (5,405-7,462 changesets on 41.3% of exposure), not too narrow.

kills.idea: Release needs an `aurora`-style channel alias in `utils.get_search_channel`, probably esr
kills.why_dead: The `release_channel` facet over product=Firefox settles it: release 144,236 and esr 116,608 are disjoint terms, and antenna's rule set treats them as different channels (`is_alpha_beta_esr` accepts esr at 100%, `is_firefox_desktop` samples release at 10%) — so folding esr into release would mix a 100%-sampled population with a 10%-sampled one in the same denominator. `get_search_channel("release") == "release"` is correct as it stands. Separately, esr is 40.9% of the shipped population and has no channel in `config/global.json` at all — see cross_dimension.

open_questions: Admit release to `sigtrend.SUPPORTED_CHANNELS`, or leave it out and accept that every release dossier says "rate not measured"? RECOMMEND ADMIT: it is three constants and one test, it costs 0.59 s + 0.21 s per 20-minute run and a measured 105.7 MB on a 10 GB plan, and it is the only thing that can make the "NO CHANGESET IS REQUIRED FOR THIS ONE" prompt block (triage.py:1503) fire on the 41.3% of release exposure whose candidate window is a whole 5,405-7,462-changeset cycle sampled at 2% by `max_candidates`. The value case is not mine to certify, but `spike/trend/REPORT.md` section 11 already counts 22 of 92 human "existing signature" cases as release/esr rises.

Should the release rollup query `throttleable=T` only? RECOMMEND YES, per-channel. It makes the sample rate constant by construction at zero extra cost and removes the one measured false-positive mechanism on the head of the list (F-share 0.4762 -> 0.8471 on the loudest riser = up to 2.40x of a 3.94x "rise"). The cost is that the release denominator then means "the randomly-sampled population" rather than "everything Socorro accepted", which must be said in the docstring. It must NOT be applied to nightly/beta, where everything is accepted and the filter would silently delete ~1% of a channel's denominator.

Does `describe()` need a sampling clause when it goes into a Bugzilla comment on a release bug? RECOMMEND ONE CLAUSE ("Socorro accepts about 10% of release crash reports, so these are sampled counts"). The counter-argument I could not dismiss: a triager reading crash-stats sees the same sampled numbers, and :aryx's own motivating sentence was a raw Socorro count — so the sentence is consistent with what a human would write, and the clause is honesty rather than a correction.

On an x.0 release build, should the off-stack candidate path run at all? RECOMMEND NOT A GATE, but make the merge-day case legible: print the window/cap ratio (50:1 on 154.0, 36:1 on 155.0, vs 2:1 on nightly's widened window) and force the no-changeset-required prompt block on. A hard gate would be the first place release differs structurally from nightly and I have no measurement of what it would cost in recall.

Should `MAX_SIGNATURES` be raised, or replaced by the exact truncation test? RECOMMEND REPLACE. `len(rows) >= FACETS_SIZE or sum(counts) != total` needs no magic number, agrees with reality on all 503 channel-days I checked, and cannot be defeated by a future channel outgrowing a hand-set cap — which is exactly how release got refused in the first place.
cross_dimension: BUILD RESOLUTION: 6.8% of a week's release reports sit on buildids Buildhub has never heard of — 248 of 332 distinct buildids in 2026-08-24..30, the largest being 20260814105733 (1,796 reports), 20260811004252 (817), 20260825051950 (788). Buildhub lists only 129 release buildids since 2024-01-01. These look like distro/Flatpak/Snap rebuilds plus builds Buildhub missed; `update.put_build` -> `dc.get_changeset` and `models.Build.get_id` will not resolve them and `put_crashes` will log "No buildid in db" for each. It caps what any attribution layer can do on release, but it belongs to the build/ingestion dimension.

CHANNEL COVERAGE: `release_channel` on product=Firefox is release 144,236 (50.5%) and esr 116,608 (40.9%) for the same week — esr is 81% of release's own volume, is unsampled (antenna `is_alpha_beta_esr` -> ACCEPT), and has no entry in `config/global.json`'s `channels`. A release-only build of this project covers 55% of the shipped population and leaves the cheaper, unsampled, longer-lived half on the table. Whoever owns scope should decide release-vs-esr rather than inheriting it.

INGESTION WINDOW: `update.put_report`'s non-nightly `mindate` (update.py:67, `Build.get_pushdate_before(buildid) + 1 s`) gives 15 pushes / 7,462 changesets between 153.0.4 and 154.0, and 15 / 5,405 between 154.0.1 and 155.0, each containing exactly 1 merge push. The beta trick that makes this work (+1 s over the merge push's own pushdate, so the window becomes the cycle's uplifts) does NOT transfer: on release the merge push sits strictly BETWEEN the two build rows, not at the lower boundary. Dot-release windows are fine (38-81 changesets). Someone owns deciding whether the merge push should be excised by parent-count rather than by pushdate arithmetic.

PATCH EXTRACTION: `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction` returns True for any channel != nightly, so release inherits beta's merge-suppression — which is right (a release merge push's members already have `changesets` rows under nightly). But it means the 5,405-7,462 changesets of an x.0 window are enumerated and ranked without file lists on the ingestion path, while `pushlog_for_revs` keeps them on the off-stack read path. Worth a check by whoever owns the candidate window that the two paths agree on release.

FILING: `config/global.json`'s `agent.autofile.channels` has a `beta` key and no `release` key, so release would inherit the top-level settings (`min_confidence: 70`, `comment_on_existing: "comment"`, `daily_cap: 10`) with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1` live in prod. Given that 41.3% of release exposure has a 5,405+ changeset candidate window sampled at 2%, a release filing path that names a changeset needs its own hold, the way beta got one in `bdd848c`.

VALUE CASE (not mine to certify): `spike/trend/REPORT.md` section 3 says release would take human-bug coverage from 81.5% to 86.3% (+25 bugs) and section 11 taxonomises 22 of the 92 human "existing signature" cases as release/esr rises (9 build-aligned, 13 date-aligned) against 19+4 on nightly. Those are the numbers that decide whether any of this is worth doing; I only priced the doing.

reports.headline: The switches are in better shape than plan #18 §11 implies: 46 per-channel knobs exist, 15 already carry a measured release value (searchfox repo `mozilla-release` and its `firefox-release` tree both verified live; `compiled_out._CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]` verified against `releases/mozilla-release`'s own `init.configure`/`moz.configure`; the merge-extraction suppression, the `ORIGIN_CHANNEL` pushdate fallback, the prompt labels and `tasks.html`'s channel cell all generalise correctly), and the containment holds — `bugzilla_apply.autofile_bug:1059` fails closed on an undeclared channel and is the ONLY reader of that config, so an accidental release ingest cannot write to Bugzilla. 16 knobs are missing or unmeasured for release, and adding `release` to `agent.channels` fails exactly 6 tests, all in `tests/test_shipped_channels.py`, each naming a real prerequisite — that forcing function works. Three things are genuinely wrong. (1) `get_agent_calibration("release")` returns NIGHTLY's fitted table `{25:0.5, 50:0.5714, 70:0.7234, 85:0.7234}` because an ABSENT channel key falls back to the top-level fit, so a release bug would publish "72% worth investigating" from a fit on 90 Firefox-nightly rows — the exact rule the module forbids. (2) `AGENT_CHANNELS=""` (empty, not unset) means NO FILTER, i.e. release triaged at $1-3/crash, and DEPLOY.md warns about the identical `INGEST_CHANNELS` hazard but not this one. (3) prod already carries 7,267 stale `release` nodes and a `lastdate(release)` frozen at 2026-07-06 from a previous accidental ingest, so the first release tick pulls 56 days / 20,094 changesets / 30.4 MB of json-pushes at a 114.9 MB tracemalloc peak on the 512 MB `worker` dyno. The docs are the weakest link: plan #18 §12 listed the lines to fix and the beta work fixed only `DEPLOY.md:15-18`.

gaps.title: `agent.calibration.channels` has no release key, so a release bug would publish nightly's fitted p_worth to Bugzilla
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `report_bug._worth_phrase` puts "N% worth investigating" in the FILED BUG text and the crashstack badge shows it. With release triaged, every release verdict at rung 70 publishes 0.7234 — a number fit on 90 rows of `corpus_ship`, every one Firefox NIGHTLY, on a channel that is additionally 10% sampled. This is the identical defect that retired the 0.9714 positives-only table, and the module's own rule (config.py:1095) says "a number a Bugzilla reviewer reads cannot be fit on the wrong arm".
gaps.evidence: MEASURED with `spike/_release_recon/config_knob_table_full.py`: `config.get_agent_calibration("nightly")` -> `{25:0.5, 50:0.5714, 70:0.7234, 85:0.7234}`; `("beta")` -> `{}`; **`("release")` -> the same nightly table**. config.py:1100-1102 reads `over = (cal.get("channels") or {}).get(channel)` and only overrides `if over is not None` — so an ABSENT key inherits the top-level fit. config.py:1097-1099 states the asymmetry deliberately ("nightly must keep its table without naming itself") but says nothing about the third channel. The guard exists: `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:305-311` loops every `get_agent_channels()` channel != nightly and asserts it names itself in `calibration.channels`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show the guard makes this a non-issue. It does not, in one direction: I patched `agent.channels` to `["nightly","beta","release"]` and ran the registry tests — `test_beta_publishes_no_calibrated_probability (channel='release')` FAILS, so the test does stop a config-only rollout. But `AGENT_CHANNELS="nightly beta release"` is an env var that needs NO deploy and therefore never runs a test: I proved with `config_env_sequence.py` that that value makes `enqueue_agent(uuid, "release")` enqueue. So the guard covers the JSON path and not the env path, which is the documented canary path.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"release": {}` to `config/global.json` `agent.calibration.channels` BEFORE any `AGENT_CHANNELS` change, for beta's reason plus two stronger ones (no release arm of `corpus_ship`; release is 10%-sampled so even the volume terms differ). Then extend the config.py:1089-1099 comment to say what release gets and why, and extend `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:305-311`'s loop to also read `os.getenv("AGENT_CHANNELS")` so the env path is covered too.

gaps.title: `AGENT_CHANNELS=""` (empty, not unset) turns release triage ON at $1-3/crash, and no doc warns about it
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `heroku config:set AGENT_CHANNELS=` is the instinctive way to "clear" the money switch. It means "no channel filter", i.e. every channel including release, effective on the next tick with no deploy and no log line. DEPLOY.md:69-72 warns in bold about exactly this shape for `INGEST_CHANNELS` (which is FREE) and says nothing about it for `AGENT_CHANNELS` (which SPENDS). The asymmetry is the trap: `config:unset AGENT_CHANNELS` is SAFE (falls back to the JSON), `config:set AGENT_CHANNELS=` is not.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED with `spike/_release_recon/config_env_sequence.py`, exercising the real `orchestrator.enqueue_agent` gate. Does a RELEASE crash get triaged? `AGENT_CHANNELS` unset -> False; `"nightly"` -> False; `"nightly beta"` -> False; **`""` -> True**; `"nightly beta release"` -> True. The gate is `if channel is not None and channels and channel not in channels` (orchestrator.py:4104) — an empty list is falsy, so the whole condition is skipped. `INGEST_CHANNELS` semantics measured in the same run: unset / `""` / `"   "` all -> `['nightly','beta','release']` (update.py:307). Prod config read 2026-08-31: `INGEST_CHANNELS="nightly beta"`, `AGENT_CHANNELS="nightly beta"`, `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show it is contained by the filer. Filing IS contained: with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1` and channel release, `autofile_bug` returns `filed=False, skipped="channel 'release' has no autofile configuration"` (proven in the same script), and `bugzilla_apply.py:1049-1061` is the ONLY reader of `get_agent_autofile` in the tree (grepped). SPEND is not contained — `enqueue_agent` runs before any filing gate, and there is no per-run cost abort (`get_agent_offstack_cost_cap` is log-only, config.py:751-752).
gaps.proposed_fix: Extend DEPLOY.md's lever table (:76-80) with an explicit "empty string != unset" row for BOTH channel vars, and state the rollback verbs: to stop release triage use `heroku config:set AGENT_CHANNELS="nightly beta"`, never `config:unset` (once the JSON contains release) and never `config:set AGENT_CHANNELS=`. Optionally make `get_agent_channels` treat an explicitly-empty value as `["nightly"]` rather than "no filter" — but that changes documented semantics `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:104-110` pins, so the doc fix is the cheap one.

gaps.title: Prod's `lastdate(release)` is frozen at 2026-07-06 with 7,267 unpruned release nodes, so the first release tick is a 56-day / 30.4 MB catch-up on the 512 MB ingestion dyno
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `put_filelog("release")` starts from `Node.get_max_date("release")`. Prod's is 2026-07-06, so the first tick after `INGEST_CHANNELS` gains release issues ONE `json-pushes` request covering 56 days, inserts ~20,094 `nodes` rows in one `Changeset.add` transaction, then `Node.clean` immediately deletes everything past the 30-day retention. `Node.clean` is only reached from `Changeset.add`, i.e. only during that channel's own ingest, so a channel that stops being ingested keeps stale rows forever — which is why 7,267 release nodes from June are still there 56 days past retention.
gaps.evidence: READ-ONLY prod SELECTs (`spike/_release_recon/config_prod_reads.py`): `nodes` release = 7,267 rows, pushdate 2026-06-07..2026-07-06; `lastdate(release)` = mindate 2026-06-07 / maxdate 2026-07-06 12:36; `builds` release = 0 rows; `uuids`/`dossiers`/`selection`/`sigdaily`/`chandaily` release = 0. Replayed the catch-up with the repo's own `pushlog.pushlog()` (`config_stale_lastdate_cost.py`, `config_catchup_memory.py`): 8.4s, **20,094 changesets, 30.4 MB json body, tracemalloc peak 114.9 MB, process maxrss 81.1 -> 251.3 MB**, 13 `logger.error` lines. `heroku ps`: `worker` is Standard-1X (512 MB), ONE dyno, and it is the same dyno that runs the serial report- and patch-scoring chains.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I expected this to be the 3.3-4.5-hour queue burst `pushlog.collect`'s docstring measured for a beta merge, and it is NOT. 19,727 of the 20,094 changesets arrive `via_merge` (two release cycle merges: 7,448 nodes at 2026-08-12, 5,391 at 2026-08-26) and `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction("release")` is True, so their files are dropped: only **110 `changesets` rows / 34 nodes with an interesting file** survive = ~2 minutes of `patch.parse`. The historical cost was real — prod holds 20,320 `changesets` rows on release nodes of which **19,527 are `analyzed=True`**, i.e. 19,527 hg fetches at 3.45-6.51 s = 18.7-35.3 hours of the serial worker, paid in June-July before the merge suppression shipped in `4749e29`. So the fix already works and the remaining risk is the one-shot 251 MB RSS spike, not the queue.
gaps.proposed_fix: Two options, both cheap. (a) Accept it and say so in the rollout doc: the spike is 251 MB of 512 MB, one tick, self-healing. (b) Add a bounded first-fetch: in `put_filelog`, clamp `start_date` to `max(Node.get_max_date(channel), now - get_ndays_of_data())` — a start date older than the retention window is fetching rows `Node.clean` will delete in the same call. Also worth a line: the 793 release `changesets` rows still at `analyzed=False` are on `merge=True` nodes and are permanently excluded by `Changeset.to_analyze`'s `Node.merge.is_(False)` — they are inert, not a stuck chain (nightly has the same 338).

gaps.title: `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` has no release entry; the two rates are 0.0891 / 0.0579, and the suppression threshold is only 2.2x background on release against 8.0x on nightly
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `population_bit_flip_rate("release")` and `population_broken_cpu_rate("release")` return None, so `triage`'s hardware-noise lines print the signature's own share with no denominator beside it — the `hardware-noise-denominator` failure mode. Worse, `bit_flip.max_bit_flip_rate` is channel-blind at 0.2: that is 8.0x nightly's population, 3.0x beta's and only **2.2x release's**, so the same suppressor is materially more aggressive relative to background as you go down-channel, and nothing in the config says so.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED with `spike/_release_recon/config_release_population_rates.py`, reproducing `sigage.hardware_noise`'s exact shape (Firefox, `utils.get_search_channel(channel)`, 364 days, facets `possible_bit_flips_max_confidence` + `cpu_info`, sum/total): **release bit_flip 334,984/3,759,235 = 0.0891, broken_cpu 217,527/3,759,235 = 0.0579**. Instrument validation on the arm whose value is shipped: beta reads 0.0672 / 0.0585 against the shipped 0.0675 / 0.0582 — agreement to 3e-4. Multiples of the 0.2 gate: 0.2/0.025 = 8.0 (nightly), 0.2/0.0675 = 2.96 (beta), 0.2/0.0891 = 2.24 (release). `population_label("release")` returns "Firefox", not "Firefox-release".
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the missing entry silently borrows nightly's, which would be the dangerous shape. It does not: `sigage._population` (sigage.py:413-425) returns `{}` for a NAMED-but-unmeasured channel and only falls back to nightly for an ABSENT one, and `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:521-525` pins `None` for all three release rates. So the degradation is honest. I also checked whether the same-day nightly reading reproduces its shipped constant: it reads 0.0375 against 0.025 (n dropped 692,770 -> 533,914 as the 364-day window rolled 6 days), so nightly's shipped number is itself now 6 days stale — but that is a separate item and beta's exact reproduction is what validates my instrument.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"release": {"bit_flip": 0.0891, "broken_cpu": 0.0579, "top_cpu_share": None}` to `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` and `"release": "Firefox-release"` to `POPULATION_LABEL`, with the measurement and denominator (n=3,759,235, 364d, `get_search_channel`) in the comment as beta's has. Leave `top_cpu_share` None — nobody has drawn the 200-signature sample on release, and sigage.py:438-445 says None is the honest answer. Separately, record the 8.0x / 3.0x / 2.2x multiples next to `max_bit_flip_rate` so the next reader knows the gate's meaning is not channel-invariant, and re-measure nightly's own two constants while you are there.

gaps.title: `agent.autofile.channels` has no release entry, so release is UNDECLARED — the right state to ship, but `get_agent_autofile("release")["enabled"]` reads True with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks today, and that is the point worth writing down: `autofile_channel_declared("release")` is False and the filer refuses before any BMO request. But the dict's own `enabled` key is True in prod, so any SECOND reader of `get_agent_autofile(channel)["enabled"]` added later would arm release filing. Before release is triaged it needs a DECISION (an explicit `enabled: false` overlay), not the absence of one, because config.py:595-613 makes "held on purpose" the only state that leaves a log line — an undeclared channel's skip string is a gap, not a Phase-4-style measurement.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED (`config_knob_table_full.py`, `config_env_sequence.py`): with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`, `get_agent_autofile(...)["enabled"]` = nightly True / beta **False** (the explicit `channel_veto`, config.py:648) / **release True**; `autofile_channel_declared` = True / True / **False**; `autofile_channel_held` = False / **True** / False. `autofile_bug("u-1", {"channel":"release",...})` returns `filed=False, skipped="channel 'release' has no autofile configuration"` under both `AUTOFILE_BUGS=0` and `=1`. Also measured: `comment_on_existing` for release inherits the top-level `"comment"` and `daily_cap` inherits 10 — nightly's values, on a channel where 58-59% of beta signatures already carried an open bug.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I grepped for every reader that could bypass the declared gate: `get_agent_autofile` has exactly ONE caller outside config.py (`bugzilla_apply.py:1049`) and it calls `autofile_channel_declared` first (:1059). I also checked the retrigger bypass that motivated the beta gate: `enqueue_agent(..., force=True)` skips the channel filter (orchestrator.py:4102) but `autofile_bug` still refuses release. So the containment is real and single-sited — this is a prerequisite, not a live hole.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"release": {"enabled": false, "comment_on_existing": "skip", "daily_cap": <measured>}` to `agent.autofile.channels` in the SAME change that adds release to `agent.channels`, so release ships as "triaged, filing HELD" exactly as beta did. `tests/test_shipped_channels.py:215-236` already enforces "every triaged channel has a filing decision" and fails without it (verified). The `daily_cap` and `comment_on_existing` values are the filing agent's to measure.

gaps.title: `agent.sweep.max_per_channel` = 2 of `max_per_run` = 3: at three channels the comment's own justification stops holding and one backlogged channel gets zero slots per tick
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: config.py:486-489 justifies 2 as "2 of 3 leaves at least one slot for anything else that is waiting" — true with two channels, false with three: 2+1 = 3 = `max_per_run`, so in any tick where three channels each hold a contiguous backlog, exactly one channel is served zero times. Total sweep throughput also does not scale: it stays 3 per 6-hourly tick = 12/day shared across three channels instead of two, so per-channel drain rate falls by a third.
gaps.evidence: Simulated the exact cap arithmetic of orchestrator.py:4163-4244 (`spike/_release_recon/config_sweep_sim.py`, no network/DB): ONE tick, three channels with deep contiguous backlogs in id order -> enqueued `[(1,'release'),(2,'release'),(100,'nightly')]`, mark -> 2, **'beta' served 0**. Prod shape confirms the fetch limit is co-binding: `models.UUID.untriaged` applies one SQL `LIMIT max_per_run * len(channels)` = 9 ordered by `UUID.id`, so with two 6-deep backlogs the third channel's rows are never fetched at all. Prod agent capacity read from `heroku ps`: agentworker = **3 dynos, Standard-2X** (not 1 x 512 MB).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried `max_per_channel: 1` as the free fairness fix and MEASURED it worse: with only 2 channels present it caps the tick at 2 runs instead of 3 (a 33% throughput loss on the measured prod shape, which is a burst of 8 on ONE channel), and with 2 deep contiguous backlogs it still serves only 2 because the over-fetch window never reaches the third channel. I also checked whether this is permanent starvation: it is not — a 12+4+4 backlog drains fully within 12 ticks (3 days) under every `max_per_channel` in {1,2,3}. So this is per-tick latency, not loss. Downgraded from correctness to quality on that basis.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not change `max_per_channel`. Either (a) raise `max_per_run` to 4 (2+1+1) and price it — at ~$3/run that is +$12/day of sweep ceiling, and the sweep is bounded by real arrivals, not the cap; or (b) fetch per channel (`limit=max_per_run` per channel in `UUID.untriaged`) so the over-fetch window cannot exclude a channel. Either way, rewrite the config.py:484-490 comment: its stated guarantee is "at least two channels get a slot", not "each channel gets a slot", and that must be said before the third channel exists.

gaps.title: `sigtrend.SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` excludes release with a silent `return 0` — correct, but the trend statistic then vanishes on release with no trace
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `sigtrend.backfill` returns 0 immediately for release with no log line, so `chandaily`/`sigdaily` gain no release rows and `trend_facts`/`is_rising` can never speak about a release signature. The exclusion is deliberate and correctly argued (a day's per-signature facet must fit one COUNT-ordered page), but it is a hardcoded module constant with no config key and no env override, and `update.put_crashes:238-241` calls it inside a try/except — so "release has no trend statistic" is indistinguishable from "the collector is failing".
gaps.evidence: Read: sigtrend.py:133 `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS = ("nightly", "beta")`, sigtrend.py:251 `if channel not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS: return 0` (no log). `FACETS_SIZE = 2000`, `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` (sigtrend.py:123-124). MEASURED the premise (`config_facets_limit.py`): distinct Firefox signatures over a 3-day window — nightly 609, beta 744, **release 6,194**; over 14 days release hits exactly 10,000, i.e. truncated at `facets_limit`. So the ~3,200/day figure in the sigtrend.py:129 comment is the right order of magnitude and the exclusion is right: release is 4-8x over `FACETS_SIZE`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to find a cheaper release trend by asking whether the quiet tail is even needed. It is: the module exists to rank quiet rising signatures, and release's facet tail is entirely count-1 signatures (measured: ranks 5,000-10,000 all have count 1), so a truncated page loses exactly the population the statistic is for. No threshold rescues it — this exclusion should stand.
gaps.proposed_fix: Keep release out, but make the skip audible: log once per (product, channel) at INFO in `backfill` when the channel is unsupported, and state in the release rollout doc that release ships with no trend statistic and why (6,194 signatures/3d vs `FACETS_SIZE` 2000). If a trend on release is ever wanted it needs a paged or install-thresholded collector, not a bigger facet.

gaps.title: Every doc line plan #18 §12 flagged is still wrong, plus five more that a release rollout makes wrong — and DEPLOY.md still tells the reader Clouseau is read-only
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Anyone following DEPLOY.md to roll release out is told the app is a "nightly-only, observe-only canary" (:4) and to NOT set a Bugzilla token because "Clouseau is strictly read-only" (:40-42) — both false in prod, where `LIBMOZDATA_CFG_BUGZILLA_TOKEN` is set and `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`. `docs/architecture.md:100-101` states the `INGEST_CHANNELS` default is `nightly`; the code default is ALL configured channels, which is precisely the hazard that turns release on. README.md:9 sends a verifier to a different app.
gaps.evidence: `git blame`: DEPLOY.md:4 is `fa32269c` (2026-07-06) and `docs/architecture.md:97-108` is `c1f4b9aa` (2026-07-06) — UNTOUCHED by the beta series. The only line the beta work fixed is DEPLOY.md:15-18 (`27673c45`, 2026-08-26). Prod `heroku config` 2026-08-31 confirms the token and `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`. `heroku ps` shows agentworker = 3 x Standard-2X against DEPLOY.md:45's `agentworker=1`. README.md:9 URL verified a DIFFERENT app: `clouseau.moz.tools` answers 200 on /reports.html but **404 on /tasks.html, /selection.html and /api/selection**, all of which are 200 on `crash-clouseau-augmented-2d0335d53b8d.herokuapp.com`. Stale plan lines: §12 says `bin/schedule.py` "has exactly two jobs" — it has FOUR since `9db2de3` (timed_job, reap_orphans_job, sweep_untriaged_job, feedback_job); §12 says `archetypes.seed_quietly()` is only called from `bin/init.py` — `bin/release.py:22-30` now seeds it.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the diagram lines are merely imprecise rather than wrong. `docs/architecture.md:143` ("mindate = buildid - backward_lookup_ndays (nightly), else previous build's pushdate") is CORRECT and generalises to release, so the diagram is not uniformly stale — which makes the specific wrong lines (:23 `update_all(nightly)`, :33/:70 the NIGHTLY node and `skip · non-nightly`, :100-101, :106, :162) worth naming individually rather than rewriting the file.
gaps.proposed_fix: In the release diff: DEPLOY.md:4 -> "nightly + beta triaged, beta filing held"; delete the "do NOT set a Bugzilla token / strictly read-only" paragraph and replace it with the real prod state and the `AUTOFILE_BUGS` kill switch; fix :45 to `agentworker=3`; add a "Turning the release channel on" section mirroring :54-98 including the `AGENT_CHANNELS=""` warning; change :124/:127-133 to name the channel a reader should actually check. architecture.md: :23 -> `update_all($INGEST_CHANNELS)`, :33/:70 rename NIGHTLY -> AGENTCH and `skip · non-nightly` -> `skip · channel not in agent.channels`, :100-101 -> "default: ALL configured channels — nightly-only is a prod config var, not a default", :106 and :162 -> "agent channel". README.md:9 -> the augmented URL (or both, labelled). Mark plan #18 §11's release bullet superseded and correct §12's two stale claims.

gaps.title: There is no registry or test for the 15 behaviour-changing env vars; DEPLOY.md documents 3 of them
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: A release rollout is entirely an env-var operation, and the set of env vars that change behaviour is written down nowhere. `tests/test_corroboration_registry.py` is a registry test for CORROBORATION flags, not env flags — I grepped and there is no test in the tree that enumerates `_env_bool` names or asserts a documented set. So a rollback that flips the wrong lever, or a lever nobody knew existed (`AGENT_SWEEP` stops the one job that spends unattended), has no forcing function and no doc.
gaps.evidence: Grepped: 12 `_env_bool` readers (config.py:311 POPULATION_STATS, :500 AGENT_SWEEP, :650 AUTOFILE_BUGS, :653 AUTOFILE_NEEDINFO, :689 SHOW_ABSTAIN, :734/:736/:739 OFFSTACK_ENABLED/PINNED/OBSERVE_ONLY, :769 SECOND_OPINION_ENABLED, :828 SIGNATURE_AGE_ENABLED, :903 BIT_FLIP_GATE_ENABLED, :955 BAD_MACHINE_GATE_ENABLED) plus `AGENT_CHANNELS` (:436), `INGEST_CHANNELS` (update.py:307), `BUGZILLA_TOKEN`/`LIBMOZDATA_CFG_BUGZILLA_TOKEN` (:118) and `BUGZILLA_REST_URL` = 15 behaviour-changing levers, against 6 infra vars (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, QUEUES, SEARCHFOX_CLI, SOCORRO_TOKEN, API_WRITE_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). DEPLOY.md:76-80's table lists three. Prod `heroku config` shows 7 of the 15 set; the other 8 silently take code/JSON defaults — including `AGENT_SWEEP` (default on) and `AUTOFILE_NEEDINFO` (default on).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I looked for the "6 undeclared flags the registry test misses" from my own notes, expecting an env-flag registry with holes. There is none: the six were CORROBORATION flags (`tests/test_corroboration_registry.py:105`, `:210-216`), a different registry. So the env-flag gap is total, not partial — which is a stronger claim than I started with, and cheaper to fix.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a `_ENV_FLAGS` tuple in config.py naming every env var config.py reads plus the two channel lists, and a test that asserts (a) every `_env_bool("NAME", ...)` literal in the module is in it (source-scan, the shape `tests/test_corroboration_registry.py` already uses for corroborations) and (b) every name in it appears in DEPLOY.md. That turns the rollout doc into something a test keeps honest, which is what a release rollout needs most.

gaps.title: `Changeset.to_analyze()` — the patch chain — has no ORDER BY, the exact defect its sibling `UUID.to_analyze` documents as load-bearing at two channels
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Both ingestion chains are serial and self-re-enqueuing on the single `worker` dyno. The REPORT chain was explicitly fixed for multi-channel fairness (`ORDER BY uuids.id`, with a docstring at models.py:1642-1645 saying "whatever Postgres finds first ... stops being stable the moment there are two: a beta backlog could interleave arbitrarily with nightly's and starve it"). The PATCH chain emits `SELECT DISTINCT ON (nodes.id) ... LIMIT 1` with no ORDER BY at all, so which channel's changeset gets parsed next is planner-dependent.
gaps.evidence: Compiled both queries against the postgresql dialect: patch chain -> `SELECT DISTINCT ON (nodes.id) changesets.nodeid, nodes.node, nodes.channel FROM changesets JOIN nodes ... WHERE nodes.merge IS false AND changesets.analyzed IS false LIMIT 1` (no ORDER BY); report chain -> `... ORDER BY uuids.id LIMIT 1`. Prod node-id ranges show release rows currently hold the LOWEST ids (release 12,936-20,202; nightly 26,467-50,438; beta 40,316-50,441), so the two channels' rows genuinely interleave in this table.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to show this is a live starvation bug and could not. Postgres must scan `nodes_pkey` to satisfy `DISTINCT ON (nodes.id)`, so with `LIMIT 1` it stops at the lowest eligible node id — which is oldest-first, i.e. the fair order the report chain asks for explicitly. And the 793 release changesets still `analyzed=False` are NOT evidence of a stall: I queried them and all 793 sit on `merge=True` nodes, permanently excluded by the `Node.merge.is_(False)` filter (nightly has 338 of the same shape). So today's behaviour is correct by accident; the risk is a plan change, not a present defect. Downgraded to quality.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `.order_by(Node.id)` to `Changeset.to_analyze`'s no-channel branch — it is the ORDER BY `DISTINCT ON` needs anyway, it is free, and it makes the fairness property explicit rather than emergent. Copy the two-sentence rationale from `UUID.to_analyze`'s docstring so the next reader sees both chains state the same rule.

gaps.title: `buildhub_lookback_ndays` = 30 leaves the release selection window under-filled on 21% of days, against 1% for beta
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `config.get_buildhub_lookback_ndays`'s whole docstring is the measurement that this value must cover `Build.get_last_versions(n=3)` at the channel's build cadence — measured for BETA (2.00-day median gap) and never for release. Release's median gap is 7.07 days, so a 30-day window holds fewer than 3 builds far more often. And because `builds.nodeid` cascades from `nodes` (models.py:581) which `Node.clean` prunes at 30 days, this is a STEADY-STATE bound on the release selection window, not just a switch-on one.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED over Buildhub's full release history (`spike/_release_recon/config_buildhub_lookback.py`, 53 release builds 2025-08-04..2026-08-26, 388 covered days): release build gaps min 0.07 / p25 3.73 / **median 7.07** / p75 10.75 / max 20.89 days. Rolling-window occupancy — days holding <3 builds: 30d **80/388 = 21%** (release) vs 4/396 = 1% (beta) vs 1/400 = 0% (nightly). Span of the newest-3 builds as seen on a day: release median 14.0d, p90 28.1d, **max 31.2d** — i.e. the window itself can exceed the 30-day retention.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I expected this to also cause a `facets_limit` truncation, and MEASURED that it does not matter. Per-build release facets over 10 recent builds run 5,411-9,410 signatures with one at exactly 10,000 (152.0.6, 146,853 reports) — truncated. But the tail is entirely count-1 signatures and the WORST rank of any signature clearing release's `installs >= 50` gate is **230 of 10,000** (measured on three builds: worst ranks 230, 175, 155). So `facets_limit` is harmless at the shipped threshold. The window-depth finding survives; the truncation one does not.
gaps.proposed_fix: Raise `buildhub_lookback_ndays` to 45 (release drops to 7/388 = 2% under-filled; 60 buys nothing more) and say in the docstring that the binding channel is now release at a 7.07-day median cadence, not beta at 2.00. Note the coupling explicitly: at 45 the buildhub lookback exceeds `max_ndays` 30, so it no longer equals `Node.clean`'s retention — which the current docstring treats as a load-bearing identity. Either raise `max_ndays` with it or state that the identity is deliberately broken for release and why. This one belongs to the windows agent to price; I am flagging the measurement and the coupling.

gaps.title: `bin/predeploy.py` reports in-flight runs with no channel, so with three channels an operator cannot see whose spend a deploy would kill
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `in_flight_runs` builds `{uuid, status, age_s, signature}` and `_report` prints those four columns. With three channels at three different filing policies and (soon) three different cost profiles, "3 triage runs still running, ~$9 of work" does not say whether the release canary or nightly production is about to be thrown away. `tasks.html` gained a channel column for exactly this reason (`bee61c3`, templates/tasks.html:99-102).
gaps.evidence: Read bin/predeploy.py:86-91 (the dict has no channel key) and :103-104 (the format string has four fields). `models.Dossier.list_tasks` already returns channel — templates/tasks.html:102 renders `t.channel`, so the data is in hand and simply not printed.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether predeploy is even the right place: it is, because it is the ONLY pre-deploy gate and DEPLOY.md:100-114 makes it the documented step. I also confirmed the row objects carry channel (tasks.html reads the same `list_tasks` rows), so this is a two-line print change with no query change.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `"channel": row.channel` to the dict in `in_flight_runs` and one column to `_report`'s format string, plus a per-channel count in the cost line.
