kills.idea: Release needs a `CHANNEL_TYPE` enum migration, which needs `_ensure_enum_values`' broken ALTER fixed first (plan #18 §11 says this about ESR and it is tempting to assume it applies to release)
kills.why_dead: `release` has been in `config/global.json`'s `channels` list since commit `3695614` (2026-02-24 / "Add channels beta and release"), and `models.py:18` builds the enum from `config.get_channels()` at table-creation time. I read the prod enum directly: `SELECT enumlabel FROM pg_enum ... WHERE typname='CHANNEL_TYPE'` returns ('nightly',), ('beta',), ('release',). No migration, no `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` entry, nothing to fix. This is the one thing that genuinely separates release from ESR.

kills.idea: Raise `facets_limit` above 10,000 because release truncates the signature facet
kills.why_dead: Measured: one of ten recent release builds hits 10,000 (152.0.6, 146,853 lifetime reports) and the rest run 5,411-9,410. But I read the tail of the count-ordered facet and everything past rank ~1,000 has count 1: the WORST rank of a signature clearing release's `installs >= 50` gate is 230 of 10,000 (and 175 and 155 on two other builds). The truncation drops nothing the selector could ever select. Raising it only costs a bigger payload (already 1.6-1.9 MB/build). If `installs` is ever lowered below ~5, re-measure.

kills.idea: A third channel will OOM the 512 MB ingestion worker on the signature aggregation, so `worker` needs a bigger dyno
kills.why_dead: Measured with the real handler under tracemalloc: a release tick's `get_new_signatures` data dict retains 29.08 MB (peak 36.59 MB) against nightly's ALREADY-EXISTING 28.31 MB, because nightly loops 81 builds where release loops 3. Wall time: release 3.2s vs nightly 33.2s. Release is the cheaper tick on both axes. The only real memory event is the ONE-OFF 56-day `put_filelog` catch-up (peak maxrss 251.3 MB of 512 MB), which is a separate, self-healing item.

kills.idea: Redis Mini will run out of memory or connections with a third channel
kills.why_dead: Read prod Redis directly: 8.80 MB used of a 25 MB maxmemory (35%, peak 10.62 MB), 3,327 keys, 12 of 20 connections, all four queues empty. A third channel adds ONE `update` job per 20-minute tick (`update_all` enqueues per product x channel) with a two-string payload, and `result_ttl=0` means finished jobs do not linger. Adding a fourth agentworker dyno would take connections to ~14 of 20 — that is the number to watch, not memory. `Persistence: None` and `noeviction` remain true and remain unchanged by the channel count.

kills.idea: `compiled_out._CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]` was inferred from the beta reading of init.configure and must be verified against mozilla-release before release can be triaged
kills.why_dead: I verified it. Read `releases/mozilla-release`'s own `build/moz.configure/init.configure` (`is_early_beta_or_earlier=is_nightly` at :1140, `set_define("NIGHTLY_BUILD", milestone.is_nightly)` at :1166, `set_define("RELEASE_OR_BETA", milestone.is_release_or_beta)` at :1168) and `moz.configure` (`MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED ... when=moz_debug | milestone.is_nightly | moz_dev_edition` at :170) via `hgedge.raw_file(..., channel="release")`. All three ON macros and all five OFF macros in the release row are correct, as is `_CHANNEL_OFF_HOLLOW["release"]`. Nothing to change.

kills.idea: Release needs an aurora-style alias in `utils.get_search_channel`, the way beta needs `["beta", "aurora"]`
kills.why_dead: Facetted `release_channel` over Firefox with no channel filter: `release` is a single clean term at 601,089 reports and `esr` is a SEPARATE term at 453,746, so ESR does not leak into a release query and nothing leaks out. The junk tail (`release-localtest` 4, `releasexx` 1, `norelease` 1) is 6 reports out of 601,089. `get_search_channel("release")` returning the bare string is already right.

kills.idea: The stale 56-day release pushlog will repeat the beta merge's 3.3-4.5-hour patch-parse burst on the shared ingestion queue
kills.why_dead: Replayed the exact 56-day window with the repo's own `pushlog.pushlog()`: 20,094 changesets, but 19,727 of them arrive `via_merge` (two release cycle merges, 7,448 and 5,391 nodes) and `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction("release")` is True, so `collect` drops their files. Only 110 `changesets` rows / 34 nodes with an interesting file survive = ~2 minutes of `patch.parse`. The historical cost was real (prod holds 19,527 parsed release changesets from the June-July accidental ingest = 18.7-35.3 hours) but the mechanism that caused it shipped a fix in `4749e29` and that fix generalises to release for free.

kills.idea: The 793 unanalysed release `changesets` rows in prod prove the serial patch chain is stuck or livelocked
kills.why_dead: Queried them: all 793 sit on the 22 release nodes with `merge=True`, which `Changeset.to_analyze`'s `Node.merge.is_(False)` filter permanently excludes. Nightly has 338 rows of exactly the same shape. They are inert, they cost nothing, and the chain is not running because there is nothing eligible left. (The chain query DOES lack an ORDER BY, which is a separate quality item, but Postgres's `DISTINCT ON (nodes.id)` index scan makes it behave as id-order today.)

kills.idea: `tasks.html`'s channel column will collide or render "?" with three channels
kills.why_dead: templates/tasks.html:102 renders `(t.channel or '?')[:1]|upper` with the full channel and version in the cell title. Three channels give three distinct letters: N, B, R. No collision, and the `?` case is only for a NULL channel, which `bee61c3` already fixed. `templates/reports.html:41-50` builds its dropdown from the DB, so release appears automatically once release UUIDs exist, and `html.reports:100-105`'s fallbacks cannot IndexError on a channel key that exists (the key is only created by rows). `selection.html:86` prints the channel raw. Nothing in the UI needs a release change.

open_questions: Ship release as "triaged, filing HELD" (an explicit `agent.autofile.channels.release.enabled: false`, mirroring beta's Phase 4) or as ingest-only for a period first? RECOMMENDATION: ingest-only first, because it is free and because prod's stale `lastdate(release)` means the first tick is a 56-day / 251 MB event you want to watch in isolation. Then triaged-with-filing-held. Do not skip the held stage: config.py:595-613 makes the hold the only state that produces a log line, i.e. the only way to measure how much release WOULD file.

Flip release triage on via `config/global.json` `agent.channels` (needs a deploy, runs the 6 tests) or via `AGENT_CHANNELS` (no deploy, runs nothing)? RECOMMENDATION: land the JSON change and the three prerequisites (calibration `{}`, the two population rates, the autofile decision) in ONE deploy with `agent.channels` still `["nightly","beta"]`, then flip the env var for the canary, then make the JSON match before calling it shipped. That gets the test gate AND the no-deploy canary.

`buildhub_lookback_ndays`: leave at 30 and accept that release's 3-build selection window is under-filled on 21% of days, or raise to 45 and deliberately break its documented identity with `Node.clean`'s `max_ndays` retention? RECOMMENDATION: raise to 45 (release drops to 2%; 60 buys nothing) and state in the docstring that the identity is broken on purpose, with release's 7.07-day median cadence as the reason. The windows agent should price the retention side.

Sweep fairness at three channels: raise `max_per_run` from 3 to 4 (+~$12/day of ceiling, and the ceiling is rarely reached) or make `UUID.untriaged` fetch per channel so the over-fetch window cannot exclude a channel? RECOMMENDATION: the per-channel fetch, because it costs no money and fixes the actual mechanism; either way rewrite the config.py:484-490 comment, whose stated guarantee is false at three channels.

Does release get a trend statistic? RECOMMENDATION: no, and say so out loud. Release runs 6,194 distinct signatures over 3 days against `sigtrend.FACETS_SIZE` 2000, so the count-ordered page loses exactly the quiet rising signatures the module exists for. Add an INFO log to `backfill`'s unsupported-channel return so the absence is visible rather than silent.

Who fixes the docs, and in which change? RECOMMENDATION: fix them in the release diff, as plan #18 §12 intended for beta and the beta series did not do (only DEPLOY.md:15-18 was touched; DEPLOY.md:4 and docs/architecture.md:98-108 are untouched since 2026-07-06). The DEPLOY.md "do NOT set a Bugzilla token / strictly read-only" paragraph is the urgent one — it is flatly false in prod and it is the line someone rolling release out will read.
cross_dimension: SECURITY / COST, not my dimension but it is the hole in the release hold: `/api/tasks/retrigger` (POST, `@cross_origin()`, crashclouseau/__init__.py:260-265 -> crashclouseau/api.py:193-213) does NOT call `_require_write_token()` — only `/api/apply` does (api.py:173). `retrigger_agent` calls `enqueue_agent(..., force=True)`, which bypasses the `AGENT_CHANNELS` gate by design (orchestrator.py:4102). So an unauthenticated POST can force a ~$1-3 LLM run on any INGESTED crash regardless of channel. Filing is still contained (`autofile_channel_declared("release")` is False), but the claim "release ingest-only costs nothing" is false while this route is open. I did NOT POST to prod to confirm — this is a code read.

WINDOWS/PUSHLOG: `sigage.ORIGIN_CHANNEL = "nightly"` and `pushlog._ORIGIN_CHANNEL = "nightly"` are correct for beta (uplifts graft from central) but the release branch merges from mozilla-BETA, not central. `pushlog.collect`'s argument that a cycle merge's members are redundant rests on "1,932 of 1,932 merge-window candidates share a node hash with the m-c pushlog" — measured on BETA. For release the members' hashes live on beta, so release's merge suppression silently DEPENDS on beta being ingested. Turning beta ingestion off while release is on would leave release's merge members with no `changesets` rows anywhere. Worth measuring the release-merge hash overlap against both central and beta.

SELECTOR: release's staged rollout is a shape neither nightly nor beta has. Buildhub's newest release build (20260826195058 / 155.0) shows 2 reports and maxInstallCard 1 at FIVE days old, while 154.0 at 18 days shows 97,971 reports and 11,459 distinct install_times. So a release build sits near zero for days after ship, which is not the "0.2-2.7% on its own ship day" curve `get_no_user_build_floor` was measured on. `min_build_installs` = 15 and the "newest day is exempt" rule both need re-measuring against that.

SELECTOR: only 133-222 of 8,434-10,000 signatures per release build clear `installs >= 50` (1.6-2.6%), and `installs` is per BUILD-DAY not per lifetime, so the per-day figure is smaller still. That is the number that prices release volume, and `spike.floor` 50 EQUALS `thresholds.installs` 50 on release — so `tests/test_selection_log.py:42-46`'s tripwire premise (`floor(beta) > installs(beta)`) is equality on release, not inequality, and config.py:361-364's claim that the mature-installs half is "inert on beta/release, whose install thresholds (6/50) are already higher" is only marginally true there.

PROMPTS: `sigage.population_top_cpu_share_median` is None for both beta and release, but `POPULATION_LABEL` falls back to the bare string "Firefox" for release (sigage.py:455). A prompt that says "the median Firefox signature" next to a release number reads as a measured claim about a population nobody measured. Needs a "Firefox-release" label with the release rates, or an explicit refusal.

OPS: `heroku ps` contradicts two things I had as priors — agentworker is Standard-2X x3 (1 GB each, 3 concurrent runs), not one 512 MB dyno, so the "agent worker OOMs above 512 MB" note is stale for capacity purposes. And prod is at release v139 = `3a584d8a`, one commit BEHIND HEAD `4b7ceb7`, so the [refile] commit is undeployed.

reports.headline: The suite is green and the recipe works: 2,115 tests, 0 fail, 100 skip in 67s on `DATABASE_URL=sqlite://`, and 2,115 / 0 fail / 0 skip in 95s on a fresh Postgres — I verified all 11 Postgres-gated files individually with the documented docker recipe. `tests/test_shipped_channels.py` is exactly what its name says and it is the ONLY forcing function: I ran the suite from a symlinked scratch tree with `agent.channels = ["nightly","beta","release"]` and got 6 failures, all 6 in that one file; the other 2,109 tests do not notice. Add `autofile.channels.release` + `calibration.channels.release` and it drops to 7 across 2 files. So release can be plugged in with essentially no test in the diff — the same gap plan #18 §6.3 T10 wrote that file to close for beta, only half-closed. The dangerous silent passes concentrate in the selector: `test_selection_log.py:26` pins nightly's knobs and nothing anywhere pins release's `installs 50` / `protos 20` (untouched since 2018-02-24) or `min_build_installs 15` (copied from beta by the beta commit `4749e29`); `test_shipped_channels.py:435` asserts the buildhub lookback covers `3 × 2.0` days, beta's cadence, while release's 3-build window spans median 11.57d and max 30.15d against a 30-day lookback. Two real blockers outside the config: `tests/test_sigtrend.py:172` PINS release out of the trend collector (and the number behind it is real — release runs a measured median 3,125 distinct signatures/day against `FACETS_SIZE=2000`), and `tests/test_persistence.py:91` pins two enums but not `CHANNEL_TYPE`, which I demonstrated is the one value a long-lived DB could be missing.

gaps.title: The entire release forcing function is 6 assertions in one file; 2,109 of 2,115 tests do not notice release at all
gaps.where: tests/test_shipped_channels.py:87, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:115, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:155, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:156, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:226, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:306, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:489, tests/test_beta_autofile.py:351, tests/test_beta_autofile.py:363
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: A release rollout lands with 6 one-line edits to a single file and the suite goes green again. Every behaviour the beta series spent ~5,000 test lines pinning — the selector window, the sweep cap, the filing policy, the prompt's channel prose — is then unasserted on release, and the failure mode of every one of them is silence (a run that selects nothing, a prompt that quotes the wrong population, a filer that skips) rather than an exception.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED. I built a symlinked scratch tree (`spike/_release_recon/tree`, every path symlinked to the repo except `config/`, which holds a generated `global.json`) so I could flip config without touching the repo, since `config.py:19` opens `./config/global.json` relative to CWD. Variant A (`agent.channels = ["nightly","beta","release"]`, nothing else): `run 2115 fail 6 err 0 skip 100`, and all 6 failures are in tests/test_shipped_channels.py — :87 and :115 (`get_agent_channels() == ["nightly","beta"]`), :155 (`assertNotIn("release", ...)`), :226 (`assertFalse(autofile_channel_declared("release"))`), :306-311 (the calibration-must-be-named loop), :489-492 (the population-rates loop). Variant B (release also given `autofile.channels.release` and `calibration.channels.release: {}`): `fail 7`, now tests/test_shipped_channels.py plus tests/test_beta_autofile.py:351/:363, where `release` is merely the example of an *undeclared* channel. Full transcripts: spike/_release_recon/fail_A_agent_release.txt, fail_B_declared.txt; generator spike/_release_recon/tests_mkconfig.py, runner spike/_release_recon/failmap.py.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I first got 13 failures and suspected a much bigger forcing function. Four of those (test_prompt_budget, test_compiled_out_gate::test_empty_is_logged, test_autofile::test_a_systemic_second_rejection_is_logged_not_swallowed, two test_orchestrator retrigger tests) were artifacts of my own `logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)` in the runner — they assert on log records. Removing that line gave the true 6. I also re-ran the pristine tree twice (HEAD 4b7ceb7, clean `git status`) to confirm the baseline really is 0 failures, because a sibling recon agent edited `config/global.json` mid-run and briefly polluted one measurement.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not just edit the 6 assertions. Add a `tests/test_shipped_release_channel.py` (or extend test_shipped_channels.py) that pins, per shipped value with its measurement: `get_threshold("installs","Firefox","release")`, `get_spike("floor"|"ratio",...)`, `get_threshold("protos",...)`, `dc.get_no_user_build_floor("Firefox","release")`, `get_agent_autofile("release")["comment_on_existing"|"daily_cap"|"enabled"]`, `get_agent_calibration("release")`, `sigage.population_bit_flip_rate/broken_cpu_rate/top_cpu_share_median/population_label("release")`. Then generalise the three loops at :223, :306 and :489 by adding a fourth: every triaged channel must have a `POPULATION_LABEL` entry naming itself, not just two non-None rates — today `population_label("release")` returns the generic "Firefox" (measured) and nothing forces it to follow the rates.

gaps.title: `tests/test_sigtrend.py:172` pins release OUT of the trend collector, and nothing pins the consumer's behaviour on that channel
gaps.where: tests/test_sigtrend.py:172, crashclouseau/sigtrend.py:133, crashclouseau/sigtrend.py:123, crashclouseau/sigtrend.py:124, crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:859, crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:2630
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `test_release_is_skipped_without_a_single_query` asserts `sigtrend.backfill("Firefox","release") == 0` with SuperSearch never called. Whoever plugs release in must either delete that test (losing the arithmetic argument behind it) or leave release with no `chandaily`/`sigdaily` rows. In the second case `orchestrator.py:859` and `:2630` call `sigtrend.trend_facts(product, channel, signature)` with NO channel gate, so every release run silently gets `{}` — the rate paragraph vanishes from the prompt and `_record_signature_trend_facts` records nothing, with no log line saying the channel is unsupported. There is not one test in the file that calls `trend_facts` with a channel other than `"nightly"`.
gaps.evidence: Read: sigtrend.py:133 `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS = ("nightly", "beta")`; :123 `FACETS_SIZE = 2000`; :124 `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500`; :251 `if channel not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS: return 0`. The comment at :129 claims release runs ~3,200 distinct signatures/day. I MEASURED it with `_facets_size=4000` over 7 processed days 2026-08-24..30 (Firefox, `utils.get_search_channel`): release median 3,125 (min 2,457, max 3,218); beta median 401; nightly median 267 — the comment is right and both constants sit BELOW release's median, so the count would truncate silently (Socorro terms facets are count-ordered). Script: spike/_release_recon/tests_release_sigcount.py. Grep confirms `trend_facts` has no channel guard at either call site and every one of the 9 `trend_facts` assertions in tests/test_sigtrend.py (:253-:348) passes `"nightly"`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether Socorro would even accept a facets_size above release's signature count — `_facets_size=4000` returned 3,218 terms without error, so the cap is a repo choice, not a Socorro limit (config's own `facets_limit` is 10000). So "release is structurally uncoverable" is false; it is a cost/size decision. I also checked whether some other gate stops `trend_facts` on an unsupported channel: grep over crashclouseau/ found only the two orchestrator call sites and `corroborations.py:147/:204`, none channel-gated.
gaps.proposed_fix: Two tests, whichever way the decision goes. (1) `test_the_trend_consumer_says_nothing_on_an_uncollected_channel`: with an empty `chandaily`, assert `trend_facts("Firefox","release",sig) == {}` AND that the prompt/corroboration path omits the rate claim rather than printing a zero — this is the assertion that is missing today for beta too. (2) If `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` grows `release`, replace test_sigtrend.py:172 with `test_the_facet_page_covers_the_busiest_release_day`: assert `FACETS_SIZE > MAX_SIGNATURES > 3218` (the measured max) and keep a test that `collect_day` refuses rather than truncates when `len(rows) >= MAX_SIGNATURES` (sigtrend.py:226 already does; tests/test_sigtrend.py:152 covers it for nightly).

gaps.title: `test_enum_values` pins two enums and not `CHANNEL_TYPE` — the one value a long-lived DB could be missing
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: If prod's `CHANNEL_TYPE` lacks `release`, the first release ingest tick dies with `psycopg2.errors.InvalidTextRepresentation` on the `nodes` insert, and `_ensure_enum_values` can never fix it because `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` names only `VERDICT_TYPE`. Nothing in the suite would catch that before deploy, and nothing in `bin/predeploy.py` inspects enums.
gaps.evidence: DEMONSTRATED end to end on my own container. (a) Fresh DB from HEAD: `CHANNEL_TYPE = nightly,beta,release`, `PRODUCT_TYPE = Firefox`, `AGENT_STATUS_TYPE = pending,running,done,error`, `VERDICT_TYPE = culprit,lead,unrelated,abstain,error`. (b) Simulated a pre-2018 prod DB: built the schema from the scratch tree with `channels = ["nightly","beta"]` → `CHANNEL_TYPE = nightly,beta`; then ran `models.create()` against the REAL 3-channel config → enum still `nightly,beta` (create_all only runs when `lastdate` is absent, models.py:3721); then inserted `channel='release'` into `nodes` → `DataError ... invalid input value for enum "CHANNEL_TYPE": "release"`. (c) tests/test_persistence.py:91-94 asserts `VERDICT_TYPE.enums` and `AGENT_STATUS_TYPE.enums` and `DOSSIER_SCHEMA_VERSION`; grep for `CHANNEL_TYPE` across tests/ returns exactly one hit, a comment at tests/test_beta_compiled_out.py:390.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to prove prod is broken and could not — and the argument that it is FINE is reviewer-checkable without prod access, which is the answer to the question. `models.py:18` builds ONE named type from the whole list: `CHANNEL_TYPE = db.Enum(*config.get_channels(), name="CHANNEL_TYPE")`. `git log -S` shows `beta` and `release` were added to `config/global.json` in the SAME commit, `3695614` dated 2018-02-24 ("Add channels beta and release"). Postgres creates a named enum atomically in `create_all()`, and no other code path adds a single channel value (grep: `create_all` appears only at models.py:3722 and models.py:3941 `_ensure_tables`, and `create.py:15` wipes-and-recreates via `models.clear()`). So a prod DB that accepts `beta` — which it demonstrably does, beta is ingesting — cannot lack `release`. The only DB that lacks release is one created before 2018-02-24, which would also lack beta.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add to tests/test_persistence.py:91: `self.assertEqual(set(models.CHANNEL_TYPE.enums), set(config.get_channels()))` — one line, runs on sqlite, and it fails the moment somebody adds a channel to config without thinking about the enum. Then add a Postgres-gated round-trip: for each `config.get_channels()`, insert a `nodes` row with that channel and assert it reads back (that is the only test that can fail on a long-lived DB). Optionally add `CHANNEL_TYPE: tuple(config.get_channels())` to `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` so the ALTER path covers it — `_ensure_enum_values` does work now (it SELECTs `pg_enum` then `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` under AUTOCOMMIT, models.py:3680-3714), contrary to the older note in my memory.

gaps.title: sqlite accepts ANY channel string, so 2,015 of 2,115 tests cannot catch a channel-label typo
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: A release test written on the default sqlite backend will happily insert `channel="relase"`, `"RELEASE"` or `"esr140x"` and pass; Postgres rejects all three. So a release test file that looks thorough on a developer machine can be asserting nothing about the channel label at all, and the mismatch only shows up in a Postgres run — which CI does not reliably do (see the CI gap).
gaps.evidence: MEASURED. `db.Enum` renders as `VARCHAR(7)` on sqlite with NO check constraint (SQLAlchemy's `create_constraint` defaults to False since 1.4). I inserted four channel strings into `nodes` under `DATABASE_URL=sqlite://`: `'release'`, `'relase'`, `'RELEASE'` and `'esr140x'` — all four accepted, including the 8-character one that overflows VARCHAR(7). Column types confirmed: `chandaily.channel`, `sigdaily.channel`, `builds.channel`, `nodes.channel` are all `VARCHAR(7)`; `selection.channel` is a plain `VARCHAR(16)`. On Postgres the same inserts raise `InvalidTextRepresentation` (demonstrated in the enum gap above).
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the beta series avoided this by gating its build/node tests on Postgres — it deliberately did NOT: tests/test_beta_selection.py:42-53 argues at length that the file must run on sqlite because "the item-7 bug WAS the interaction between a database-side LIMIT and a Python-side loop". So the exposure is intentional and the fix cannot be "gate it on Postgres".
gaps.proposed_fix: In whatever `tests/test_release_selection.py` gets written, do NOT rely on the DB to validate the label: assert `channel in models.CHANNEL_TYPE.enums` on every value the fixture inserts (a one-line helper in the `_load()` equivalent), and keep the identity assertions on `revision`/`version` as tests/test_beta_selection.py:48-53 already does. Separately, make `_is_postgres()` check CONNECTIVITY, not just the URL scheme — today `db.engine.dialect.name` is derived from the URL, so a typo'd database name turns 100 skips into 114 errors instead of skipping.

gaps.title: CI's `DATABASE_URL` points at a Postgres the CI image does not provide: 114 errors, measured with the exact CI command
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The 100 Postgres-gated tests (soon more, since the release selector/sweep/filing tests belong behind the same gate) are in a state where a reviewer cannot tell from CI whether they ran, passed, or errored. Release work that only touches gated tests would show as a red-or-unknown CI either way, so the gate stops being a signal.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED. `.taskcluster.yml:48` sets `DATABASE_URL: postgres://clouseau2:passwd@localhost:5432/clouseau` on image `python:3.14` with no services block; `.taskcluster.yml:61` runs `uv run coverage run --source=crashclouseau -m unittest discover tests/ --verbose`. I ran exactly that DATABASE_URL with nothing listening on 5432: `Ran 2115 tests in 77.9s / FAILED (errors=114)`. The `postgres://` scheme itself is fine (something normalises it — `db.engine.dialect.name` reports `postgresql`), so `_is_postgres()` returns True and every gated test runs and then fails to connect. Breakdown of the 114 by module in spike/_release_recon/ci_errors.txt: test_reaper_recovery 15, test_beta_sweep_and_dedup 13, test_autofile 12, test_persistence 14, test_sweep_untriaged 14, test_beta_selection 10, test_sigtrend 9, test_beta_windows 7, test_beta_autofile 5, test_selection_log 5, test_beta_merge_push 4, test_clock_jobs 4, test_heartbeat 2. Of those, 14 are NOT skip-gated at all (the 10 `test_beta_selection.TestGetLastVersionsAcrossTheMerge` tests and 4 `test_clock_jobs` subtests) — they run on sqlite and error on an unreachable Postgres.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I assumed for a while that the 114 errors were a real suite defect. They are not: on a FRESH reachable Postgres the same discovery run is `Ran 2115 tests in 95.3s / OK` with 0 skips, and on a second run over the now-populated DB it is still OK — so the suite is clean and the 114 is purely "no database". I also considered that CI might get a Postgres from the taskcluster payload; the yml has no `services`, no `docker-compose`, and no `pg_ctl`/`initdb` in the command, so there is nowhere for one to come from.
gaps.proposed_fix: Pick one and state it in the yml. Either (a) set `DATABASE_URL: sqlite://` in `.taskcluster.yml:48` and accept the documented skips, adding a line to DEPLOY.md that the 100 gated tests are a manual pre-deploy step with the docker recipe; or (b) give CI a Postgres. Independently, make `_is_postgres()` in all 11 files try a real `SELECT 1` so an unreachable DB SKIPS (today's honest behaviour) rather than ERRORS — that single change turns the current ambiguous red into a clear 100-skip green and makes the release additions readable.

gaps.title: Release's six selector knobs are pinned nowhere, and two of them are untouched 2018 defaults while a third was copied from beta by the beta commit
gaps.where: config/global.json:25, config/global.json:32, config/global.json:41, config/global.json:69, tests/test_selection_log.py:26, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:340
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `test_the_shipped_beta_selection_knobs` (test_shipped_channels.py:340-386) pins beta's six values with the measurement that chose each one. There is no release equivalent, so `installs 50`, `protos 20`, `floor 50`, `ratio 3`, `min_build_installs 15` are live production spend decisions that no test names and no measurement backs. Whoever retunes them later — or "cleans up" the 2018 leftovers — moves the release budget with a green suite.
gaps.evidence: Read + `git log -S`. `thresholds.installs.Firefox.release = 50` and `thresholds.protos.Firefox.release = 20` both trace to commit `3695614`, 2018-02-24. `spike.floor.Firefox.release = 50` came from `9020f88` (2026-07-08, the spike detector). `spike.min_build_installs.Firefox.release = 15` came from `4749e29` (2026-08-26) — i.e. the BETA commit "[beta] the three windows and the selector" set release's value to beta's, and `dc.get_no_user_build_floor("Firefox","release")` returns 15 today (probed). Meanwhile tests/test_shipped_channels.py:412-415 asserts only beta=15 and nightly=0, and tests/test_selection_log.py:26-30 `test_shipped_values` pins only nightly's four. The one tripwire the file's own header calls out (`floor(beta) > installs(beta)`, test_selection_log.py:42-46) is beta-only; on release floor and installs are both 50, so the analogous relation is EQUAL and unasserted.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the copied 15 is actually WRONG for release, and on my instrument it is defensible: over 27 release builds 2026-04-01..09-01 (Buildhub build list × Socorro `build_id` facet with `_cardinality.install_time`, lifetime, all channels) the distinct-install counts are min 0, median 461, max 39,118, and the only builds under 100 are three at exactly 0/0 plus one at 98 and the brand-new 155.0 at 2. So any floor in [3, 97] is the same decision on this instrument and 15 sits inside it. Script: spike/_release_recon/tests_release_nouser.py.
gaps.proposed_fix: Write `tests/test_shipped_release_selection_knobs` mirroring test_shipped_channels.py:340, one assertion per knob with the measurement in the docstring, and add the shape claims rather than only literals: `installs(release) > installs(beta) > installs(nightly)`, `protos(release) >= protos(beta)`, and — for the no-user floor — `assertLessEqual(3, floor) ; assertLessEqual(floor, 97)` with the three measured 0/0 builds and the 98-install build named, so the interval is the assertion and not the literal.

gaps.title: `test_the_buildhub_lookback_is_the_retention_window` hardcodes beta's 2.00-day cadence; on release the same relation is violated by one real window
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The test asserts `get_buildhub_lookback_ndays() >= 3 * 2.0`, i.e. >= 6, where 2.0 is BETA's measured build gap. 30 satisfies that trivially, so the test passes on release and says nothing. The property it is actually protecting — that the FIRST tick after flipping `INGEST_CHANNELS` can see three builds — fails on release 24% of the time, which is exactly the switch-on hazard the beta work wrote this test for.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED from Buildhub via `crashclouseau.buildhub.get`, Firefox, 2026-02-01..08-31. Release: 32 builds, gap median 6.90d / mean 6.61 / max 20.89; 3-build span median 11.57d, p90 25.04d, MAX 30.15d — one window (2026-02-16 → 2026-03-18) exceeds the shipped 30-day lookback. Rolling 30-day window over 182 possible switch-on days: fewer than 3 builds on 44 of 182 = 24% (beta: 0 of 182, 0%; nightly: 0 of 182). Beta control on the same instrument: 82 builds, gap median 2.01d (reproducing plan #18's 2.00), 3-build span median 5.00d / p90 7.12 / max 12.23. Script: spike/_release_recon/tests_release_cadence.py and tests_release_window.py.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to make 30 sufficient by asking whether `Build.get_last_versions` needs three rows or just two: models.py:683 says `len(res) >= 1`, so a short window is degraded rather than broken, and models.py:666 measures the beta cost of a short window at 12 of 127 run-days. So the 24% is a degradation, not an outage — which is why I filed it as correctness rather than blocker. I also checked whether 30 is tunable in isolation: config.py:83 ties it to `max_ndays`, which is also `Node.clean`'s retention window, so raising it past 30 has a second consequence.
gaps.proposed_fix: Replace the beta-fitted literal with the property and a per-channel number: assert `get_buildhub_lookback_ndays() >= <measured p90 3-build span for the channel>` for every channel in `get_channels()`, with the measured spans in the docstring (nightly ~1.5d, beta 7.1d, release 25.0d). Then either raise the lookback above 30.2 or add an explicit test that a release window shorter than 3 is RECORDED (a `Selection` row with an untestable-prefix outcome) rather than silent — the 24% needs to be visible, not merely tolerated.

gaps.title: The two files most likely to be copied as release templates carry stale 'known defect / expectedFailure' prose describing code that has since been fixed
gaps.where: tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:28, tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:224, tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:308, tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:338, tests/test_beta_selection.py:35, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:124
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Whoever writes `tests/test_release_channel_wiring.py` will copy tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py, including a header that says "Three tests are `@unittest.expectedFailure`" and three multi-paragraph `# DEFECT: ... is not implemented` blocks that are now false. They will then either reproduce a wrong xfail on release or spend a session re-diagnosing three fixed bugs. The same file also contains the repo's canonical statement of what production runs, and that statement is wrong.
gaps.evidence: `grep -rn expectedFailure tests/*.py` returns only the two COMMENTS (test_beta_channel_wiring.py:28-30, test_beta_selection.py:35) — no decorator exists anywhere in the tree, and both files run fully green (71 tests, OK). The three described defects are all fixed: `utils.make_url_for_signature` now routes through `get_search_channel` (utils.py:398, and its docstring documents the fix that its test's DEFECT block says is missing); `orchestrator.py:819` now calls `_install_history(raw_crash, channel)` with the seed's channel; the twin-query date anchor passes. Separately, tests/test_shipped_channels.py:124 states "Prod has `INGEST_CHANNELS=nightly` today ... re-verified 2026-08-25", while the verified prod value is `INGEST_CHANNELS="nightly beta"` — and :144-147 pins `"nightly beta"` as the explicit example, which will silently keep passing when prod becomes `"nightly beta release"`.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the decorators might be applied dynamically (a loop, a metaclass, a helper) rather than as literal `@unittest.expectedFailure` — grep for `xfail`, `_KNOWN_DEFECT` and `expectedFailure` across both files found nothing but the prose, and `python -m unittest` reported no 'expected failure' lines at all, so the decorators are genuinely gone.
gaps.proposed_fix: Before copying either file, delete the two 'N tests are expectedFailure' header sentences and rewrite the three `# DEFECT` blocks in the past tense as `# WAS A DEFECT (fixed in <commit>)`, since the measurement in them is still worth keeping. Update tests/test_shipped_channels.py:118-130's prod statement to `"nightly beta"` and, when release is plugged in, change :144-147's explicit example to the new prod string — that line is the only thing tying the test to reality and it is not self-updating.

gaps.title: The sweep-cap tests are two-channel by construction and the one shape assertion cannot detect a missing per-channel multiplier
gaps.where: tests/test_beta_sweep_and_dedup.py:74, tests/test_beta_sweep_and_dedup.py:268, tests/test_beta_sweep_and_dedup.py:386, tests/test_sweep_untriaged.py:108, crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:4171, crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:4202
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: With three channels, `max_per_run=3` and `max_per_channel=2` mean at most two channels are served per tick and one is systematically starved — the exact failure item 28 was written to prevent, one channel further along. `_TwoChannelFixture` cannot express it, `_tick(channels=("nightly","beta"))` defaults to two, and `test_the_shipped_per_channel_cap_is_smaller_than_the_per_tick_total` asserts only `(3, 2)`, which is silent about the relation that matters at three channels.
gaps.evidence: Read: orchestrator.py:4171 over-fetches `cfg["max_per_run"] * max(1, len(channels or ()))`; :4202-4203 sets `per_channel = max_per_channel if len(present) > 1 else max_per_run`; :4215 caps the tick at `max_per_run`. So adding release does not increase spend (the tick stays 3) but does add a third competitor for it. tests/test_sweep_untriaged.py:107-109 deliberately asserts the SHAPE — `args[3] % 7 == 0` and `>= 7` — with a comment saying it does so precisely to avoid re-breaking when a channel is added; but `7*2 = 14` and `7*3 = 21` both satisfy it, so it would pass if the `len(channels)` multiplier were dropped. tests/test_beta_sweep_and_dedup.py:74-138 builds exactly one nightly and one beta build.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the two-channel fixture is merely convenient or actually load-bearing: the class comment at :246-249 says the fixture shape IS the starvation scenario (three beta candidates older than two nightly ones), so it is deliberate — and it is precisely why it cannot be reused: the third channel changes which of `max_per_run` and `max_per_channel` binds. I also confirmed the shipped cap does not need to change for containment (the per-tick total is unchanged at 3), so this is a coverage gap, not a live cost bug.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a `_ThreeChannelFixture` in a `tests/test_release_sweep.py` and assert: (a) with candidates waiting on all three channels, exactly `max_per_run` are enqueued and no channel takes more than `max_per_channel`; (b) the channel that gets nothing is DEFERRED and logged by uuid+channel (the mechanism tests/test_beta_sweep_and_dedup.py:303 pins for two channels) and is offered again on the next tick, i.e. starvation is bounded; (c) tighten tests/test_sweep_untriaged.py:108 to `args[3] == max_per_run * len(config.get_agent_channels())`; (d) in `TestTheShippedSweepCap`, add `assertGreaterEqual(max_per_channel * len(get_agent_channels()), max_per_run)` so a fourth channel cannot make the tick unfillable.

gaps.title: Release ships two builds on one calendar day three times in 27, which `find_no_user_days` cannot see and no test exercises
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `find_no_user_days` aggregates installs by build-DAY with `max`, so a zero-install respin that shares its calendar day with the shipped build is invisible — the day carries the twin's installs and the zero build silently becomes part of a real baseline. And the mirror: a 3-build window that collapses to 2 build-days gives `evaluate_days` one testable day instead of two at release's shift of 1, halving the selecting surface for that run-day with no record. `test_the_respin_window_of_two_identical_versions_survives` uses builds 4 days apart, so the same-day case is untested for beta as well as release.
gaps.evidence: MEASURED over 27 release builds 2026-04-01..09-01 (Buildhub × Socorro `build_id` facet with install cardinality). Three builds have exactly 0 reports / 0 installations: `20260506041011` (150.0.2), `20260513195118` (151.0), `20260727110312` (153.0.1). Two of the three share a calendar day with their shipped twin — 20260506041011 vs 20260506140522 (230 installs, ~10h later) and 20260727110312 vs 20260727124451 (2,343 installs, ~1.4h later) — so only 2026-05-13 is a lone quiet day the floor would drop. Read datacollector.py:189-197: `installs[day] = max(installs[day], seen)` keyed on `day`, newest day exempt. Script: spike/_release_recon/tests_release_nouser.py.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether release's quiet builds are the same phenomenon as beta's merge-day `N.0b1` and they are NOT — release has no merge-day build in the `builds` table sense; these are respins/never-shipped RCs. That matters because it means the release test cannot be a rename of `test_the_merge_day_build_is_still_selectable_while_it_is_the_newest_day`; the mechanism is different even though the zero-baseline consequence is identical. I also confirmed the beta→release merge push EXISTS and has the same shape as the central→beta one (hg push 5982 on releases/mozilla-release: 7,448 changesets, 34 merge members, desc "No Bug - Update configs after merge day operations a=release"), so the merge-push rule itself does generalize.
gaps.proposed_fix: In `tests/test_release_selection.py`, add (a) `test_two_builds_on_one_day_are_one_build_day`: load the real pair 20260506041011/20260506140522 and assert `get_last_versions(n=3)` returns 3 rows while the day series `evaluate_days` sees has 2 entries and only ONE testable index at shift 1 — and that the collapse is RECORDED, not silent; (b) `test_a_same_day_respin_with_no_users_is_not_a_baseline`, which is currently FALSE and should be an explicit known-defect test with the two measured pairs named; (c) `test_a_beta_build_never_leaks_into_the_release_window`, the missing mirror of tests/test_beta_selection.py:231 — the failure mode is different in that direction (a beta build in the release window is far QUIETER, so it reads as a spike from a low baseline).

gaps.title: `_provenance("release")` exists in code, is printed into every filed bug, and is asserted nowhere
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `_PROVENANCE_SCOPE["release"] = "release crashes"` is the last paragraph of every filed release bug — the one sentence whose job is to tell a human what wrote the analysis. `test_the_channel_is_the_only_thing_that_changes` loops `"release"` but asserts only the four channel-independent clauses, so deleting or misspelling the release key makes every release filing say "analyses Firefox crashes" (the generic fallback) with a green suite. The beta arm has a dedicated test (:562-569) asserting the phrase, its absence of "nightly", and "Developer Edition"; release has none.
gaps.evidence: Read report_bug.py:1020-1030 and probed all seven channel values: `release` maps to "release crashes", `beta` to "beta and Developer Edition crashes", and `aurora`/`esr`/`esr140`/`None` all fall through to "Firefox crashes". tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:591-596 loops `("nightly","beta","release",None)` asserting only `github.com/mozilla/crash-clouseau`, `INVALID`, `not an independent Mozilla discovery` and `resolve THIS bug as the duplicate`. No test anywhere asserts the string "release crashes".
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the release phrase is unreachable (in which case this would be dead config, not a gap): `report_bug.py:954` calls `_provenance(channel)` inside `build_bug_comment`, and tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:600-609 proves the channel comes straight from `uuid_info`, so a release filing does reach it. I also checked the aurora asymmetry — `_provenance("aurora")` returns the GENERIC text, not beta's, even though aurora IS beta everywhere else; that is a live beta defect, not a release one, so I left it out of this gap.
gaps.proposed_fix: Mirror tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:562 as `test_a_release_filing_says_release`: assert `"release"` in the note, `"nightly"` not in it, `"Developer Edition"` not in it (release is not DevEdition, so this is a DIFFERENT assertion from beta's, not a rename), and that the note does not fall back to the generic "Firefox crashes". Then generalise :591 into a loop over `config.get_agent_channels()` requiring each triaged channel's note to name a scope that is not the generic fallback — that is the version that catches the next channel.

gaps.title: 42 of 71 test files pin `channel="nightly"` as their fixture, so the release code paths are exercised by nothing outside test_beta_* and test_shipped_channels
gaps.where: tests/test_offstack.py:166, tests/test_signature_age_gate.py:35, tests/test_trend_window.py:36, tests/test_population.py:180, tests/test_stale_hg_identity.py:140, tests/test_signature_first_date.py:175
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Every gate the pipeline runs — the stale-signature gate, the bit-flip gate, the bad-machine gate, the off-stack window, the signature-first-date clock, the incomplete-fix detector, the prompt budget — is tested only on a nightly seed. On release each of these reads a different channel repo, a different population and a much larger shift between the origin and channel push dates, and the suite would report nothing if any of them silently degraded.
gaps.evidence: Counted: `grep -lE '"channel": *"nightly"|channel="nightly"' tests/*.py` → 42 files of 71; `grep -lE '"(beta|release|aurora)"' tests/*.py` → 22 files. Highest concentrations: test_offstack.py 25 occurrences, test_product_wiring.py 11, test_orchestrator.py 8, test_signature_first_date.py 5, test_patch_extract.py 5, test_compiled_out_gate.py 5. The measured consequence is the first gap in this list: release in `agent.channels` trips 6 tests, none of them in any of those 42 files.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether nightly-only fixtures are harmless because the channel is threaded through and therefore uniform — it is not: `sigage.landing_pair` (sigage.py:739-743) branches on `channel == ORIGIN_CHANNEL`, and on release the two clocks are median 47.6 DAYS apart (measured, see cross_dimension) against beta's 23.2, so the stale-signature gate's 7-day comparison sits on a different scale entirely. A nightly fixture takes the `own == origin` branch and never sees it.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not convert 42 files. Pick the gates whose input actually changes on a release branch and add a release arm to each, one test per gate, using the SAME fixture with `channel="release"`: the stale-signature gate (with the measured 47.6-day merge shift), `_install_history`/bad-machine (release population), the off-stack window (`releases/mozilla-release` pushlog), `sigage.pushdate_for_node`, and the prompt-budget/prompt-size guard on a release seed. Then add one enumerating guard in the release file, in the shape of tests/test_beta_channel_wiring.py:382 `_assert_all_channels`: build the MCP contexts for a release seed and assert every context carries `channel == "release"` and `SearchfoxCtx.repo == "mozilla-release"` — that one catches a sixth context added later.

open_questions: Does CI get a Postgres service, or does CI go sqlite-only? Measured: `.taskcluster.yml`'s exact command with its own DATABASE_URL and no server gives 114 errors; sqlite gives 2115/OK/100 skips; a real Postgres gives 2115/OK/0 skips. RECOMMENDATION: set `DATABASE_URL: sqlite://` in .taskcluster.yml:48 and change `_is_postgres()` in all 11 files to attempt `SELECT 1` so an unreachable DB SKIPS instead of ERRORS — then CI is unambiguously green, the 100 (soon ~120) gated tests are an explicit documented pre-deploy step, and release additions are readable in the diff. Adding a Postgres service is better but is a larger change to a taskcluster definition nobody has touched.

Do we lift `sigtrend.SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` to include release, or gate `trend_facts` at the consumer and keep the collector skip? Covering release needs `FACETS_SIZE`/`MAX_SIGNATURES` above the measured 3,218 max (median 3,125), which roughly doubles the per-day rollup rows. RECOMMENDATION: keep the collector skip AND gate the consumer — add a test that `trend_facts` on an uncollected channel returns `{}` and that the prompt omits the rate sentence rather than printing a zero, then rewrite tests/test_sigtrend.py:172 to pin the pair (collector refuses, consumer says nothing) instead of just the collector. That is one test, no cost, and it closes the same hole for beta.

Which release knobs are DECISIONS and which are 2018 leftovers to be re-derived? `installs 50` and `protos 20` date from commit 3695614 (2018-02-24) and have never been measured; `floor 50` from 9020f88 (2026-07-08); `min_build_installs 15` was set to beta's value by the beta commit 4749e29 (2026-08-26). RECOMMENDATION: treat all four as unmeasured, pin them in a `test_the_shipped_release_selection_knobs` with an explicit 'INHERITED, NOT MEASURED' note per value, and let the selector/cost agents replace the notes with numbers — a pinned unmeasured value is far safer than an unpinned one, because the next person cannot quietly clean it up.

Does `agent.autofile.channels.release` ship as `{"enabled": false, "comment_on_existing": "skip"}` (release triaged, filing HELD, mirroring beta's Phase 4) or is release ingest-and-triage-only with no autofile entry at all? These are different test shapes: the first needs tests/test_shipped_channels.py:230-236 and tests/test_beta_autofile.py:351 to drop 'release' from their undeclared-channel lists and gain a held-channel test; the second keeps those lists and needs a test that a release dossier reaching `autofile_bug` is refused on 'no autofile configuration' with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1` live. RECOMMENDATION: declare-and-hold, because tests/test_shipped_channels.py:238-264 argues (and pins) that 'undeclared' and 'declared and switched off' must stay different states, and a `tasks.html` retrigger with `force=True` bypasses the channel gate by design.

Should `test_shipped_channels.py` split into a per-channel file, or keep growing? It is 551 lines for two channels and is the ONLY forcing function; a third channel roughly doubles the per-channel assertion count in one file. RECOMMENDATION: keep the cross-channel INVARIANT loops (:223, :306, :489, plus a new label loop) in test_shipped_channels.py and move the per-channel literal pins into `tests/test_shipped_<channel>.py` — the invariants are what catch a fourth channel, the literals are what a reader looks up.

BUILDHUB LOOKBACK: release's 3-build window spans up to 30.15 days (2026-02-16 to 03-18) against the shipped `buildhub_lookback_ndays = 30`, and 44 of 182 possible switch-on days (24%) see fewer than 3 builds in a rolling 30-day window (beta: 0%). config.py:83 ties this value to `max_ndays`, which is also `Node.clean`'s retention window, so raising it has a second consequence.

SAME-DAY BUILDS: release shipped two builds on one calendar day three times in 27 builds (2026-05-06 ~10h apart, 2026-07-27 ~1.4h apart, plus 151.0 respun 3 days later). Every day-keyed structure in the selector — `find_no_user_days`, `evaluate_days`, the `Selection` day index — collapses those to one day, so a 3-build window becomes a 2-day series and at release's shift of 1 leaves ONE testable index instead of two.

reports.headline: Plugging release is a bad idea, and the measurement that kills it is a supply measurement, not a threshold one. Over 26 dot-release windows in 2026 (9 cycles), ZERO signatures were new on a dot-release build at the release install threshold of 50; and in a 31-run-day as-of replay of the production selector, 8 of 8 dot-release selections sat on signatures 33-553 days older than the uplift (median 146 d), which the stale-signature gate clamps from probable(70) to medium(50) — below `autofile.min_confidence` 70. The other 22 of 30 selections (73%) land on a version-bump build, where merge members get `files: []` so the on-stack candidate set is empty by construction and the off-stack enumerator fetches 8.0-11.9 MB / 5,405-7,464 changesets and keeps 150 (2.0-2.8%). Release also sees almost nothing new: 2 of the top 300 release signatures by installs (0.7%) have no nightly/beta/aurora report in 364 days and both are noise, while 16 of the 30 release-selected signatures were already ingested AND analysed by the nightly/beta pipeline inside one 30-day prod window. Against that, the human baseline is hours: 91 release-tracked crash bugs in 2026, 65% already carrying `regressed_by`, median 21.7 h from filing to the regression range being set — versus our median 11.1-day lag from the release build shipping to a first selection. Two of plan #18 §11's four stated reasons are now dead (the `get_last_versions` blackout was fixed by the beta work; `spike.floor.release` is dominated by the install threshold), so the honest answer is not "the reasons were wrong" but "the reasons were the wrong reasons and the real one is that there is no addressable set".

gaps.title: The addressable set on release is empty: 0 new-on-a-dot-release signatures at >=50 installs over 26 dot-release windows, and 8/8 dot-release selections are stale by a median 146 days
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Nothing breaks; the feature produces zero filings and zero leads worth reading, while spending $207-740/month. The only builds on release with a usable candidate window are the dot releases (median 52 changesets, median 6 touching a C/C++/Rust file). Every crash the selector picks on such a build is on a signature that already existed long before the uplift, so `_apply_signature_age_gate` clamps `probable`->`medium` and the filer's `min_confidence: 70` refuses it. Release would therefore be a triage-only channel forever, by arithmetic rather than by policy.
gaps.evidence: (1) For every dot-release window of 2026 I compared the lifetime signature set of build N against build N-1 on `release_channel=release`: 26 windows, 8 signatures new at >=50 installs, ALL 8 from the single 153.0.1 respin pair (the superseded buildid has 0 reports so everything looks new) and all 8 boilerplate (`OOM | small` 413 installs, `EMPTY: no frame data` 273, `OOM | js::gc::FreeSpan::allocate` 136, `IPCError-browser | GPUProcessKill` 122, `shutdownhang | RtlWaitOnAddress` 76). Genuine count: 0. (2) As-of replay of `datacollector.get_new_signatures` + `utils.evaluate_days` + `datacollector.find_no_user_days` at production config over 2026-07-27..08-26: 30 distinct (signature, buildid) pairs, 8 on dot-release builds. Their (build date - `sigage.signature_history(...)['first_seen_any']` build date) gaps: 33.2, 58.1, 103.1, 117.2, 175.0, 347.0, 348.7, 552.8 days. (3) 12 of 12 sampled dot-release uplift changesets 404 on mozilla-central json-rev (`sigage.landing_pair` origin=None), so `pushdate_for_node` falls back to the release-branch pushdate == the dot-release build date; the gate therefore compares those exact gaps against `min_age_days: 7`.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not plug release. If the user wants the dot-release class covered at all, the deliverable is NOT an LLM channel: it is a free, zero-spend watch that (a) records a `Selection` row per release build-day and (b) when a signature is new on a dot-release build OR triples on it, emits the ~6-changeset uplift window as a link. Ship that only after the supply test above returns non-zero: re-run `v26_addressable.py` monthly and require >=3 windows in 6 months producing a signature whose `first_seen_any` is within 7 days of the uplift pushdate.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried three ways to make the class exist. (a) I widened from "new signature" to "any selection" — the selector found 8 dot-release selections, and all 8 failed the same age test. (b) I checked whether my age proxy was the wrong clock: for a version-bump candidate it IS wrong (the merge member's central pushdate can predate first_seen, so the gate need not fire), which is why I restricted the claim to dot releases, where `landing_pair` returns origin=None on 12/12 sampled nodes and the release-branch date is the only clock. (c) I checked whether the retrospective "new" test was confounded by exposure — it is, in the direction that would INFLATE the count (the newer dot release supersedes the older build and gets more exposure), so 0 is not an artefact of a conservative test.

gaps.title: 73% of release's selection supply lands on a version-bump build, where the on-stack candidate set is empty by construction and off-stack keeps 150 of 5,405-7,464 changesets
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The pipeline spends ~$1.12-4.00 per dossier on a question it cannot answer. `suppresses_merge_extraction(channel)` is true for release (`channel.lower() != 'nightly'`), so a cycle merge's 5,405-7,464 members get `files: []`, no `changesets` rows, and `Changeset.find` returns nothing — correct, and it means every bump-build crash falls to the off-stack path, whose window IS the whole merge. Plan #18 kill #13 treated the 5,000-changeset window as an edge case reachable only if the merge-day `builds` row goes missing; on release it is the DEFAULT for 73% of the supply, because there is no merge-day build to bound it.
gaps.evidence: 22 of 30 replayed selections are on a build that is the first of its major (153.0, 154.0). Measured live through `crashclouseau.net`: json-pushes?full=1 for 153.0.4->154.0 = 7,464 changesets / 11.9 MB / 4.0 s, and 154.0.1->155.0 = 5,405 / 8.0 MB / 3.6 s, against `max_candidates` 150 (2.0-2.8% kept). Whole-window shape over 8 version bumps in 2026: median 6,952 changesets, median 2,632 touching an interesting file, median 3,470 distinct bugs. In-cycle (dot-release) windows, n=26: median 52 changesets, median 6 interesting, median 26 bugs.
gaps.proposed_fix: If any release ingestion happens, gate the agent on the build being a dot release: refuse to enqueue when `Build.get_two_last` spans a major-version change on a release branch, and record the refusal in `Selection` rather than spending. That is a two-line predicate and it removes 73% of the projected spend without touching nightly or beta. But note this leaves the dot-release 27%, which gap #1 shows is empty — so the correct action remains not to ingest release for the agent at all.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the bump window is reasoning-hostile or merely large: plan #18 measured that file intersection narrows a beta merge to a median 28.5 candidates and line-proximity to a median 3.0 scoring >=5, so the window is not intrinsically unusable. It is unusable HERE because `suppresses_merge_extraction` deliberately writes no `changesets` rows for merge members, so the file-intersection step that would narrow it never runs; the off-stack path that does read the files ranks them and then truncates to 150 with a recency tiebreak over a 4-week cycle. Both halves verified in the tree, not inferred.

gaps.title: Release sees essentially nothing nightly and beta cannot: 0.7% of the top-300 release signatures are release-only, and 53% of release's selections were already analysed by the live pipeline inside one month
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The stated case for release — the real user population, PGO/no-DEBUG builds, release scale — does not survive its own measurement. Adding release re-buys analyses we already paid for on nightly, and the residue it adds is population noise rather than regressions.
gaps.evidence: (1) Top 300 release signatures by distinct `install_time` over 2026-07-27..08-27: 2 (0.7%) have no `nightly`/`beta`/`aurora` report in 364 days — `@0x0 | neqo_udp::recv_inner` (274 installs, esr+release) and `arise_dri.so` (166, a third-party driver). (2) Prod DB, read-only: of the 30 signatures the release selector would pick, 16 already have ingested uuids AND completed dossiers on nightly or beta (34 dossiers, ~$58 at the measured $1.71/dossier) inside a `uuids` table that only reaches back to 2026-08-01; 24 of 30 appear in the `selection` table, whose nightly history is only 2026-08-11..08-31. (3) Composition: 63.9% of release reports and 66.8% of the summed per-signature install cardinality sit in classes with no in-tree regressor to name — OOM 32.9%, shutdownhang/hang 13.6%, AsyncShutdownTimeout 9.1%, stackoverflow 3.3%, EMPTY/EmptyMinidump 2.2%, third-party dll/so 2.0%, IPCError 0.6% (n=2,000 signatures, 566,718 reports).
gaps.proposed_fix: Record this as the answer to "what can release see": nothing, at 0.7%. Do not build a release arm on a scale argument. If the population argument is wanted, the honest version is the one plan #18 §2.2 already used for beta — a specific hardware/32-bit/AV class with a named gate — and on release that class is `arise_dri.so`-shaped, i.e. exactly what `sigage.hardware_noise` exists to suppress.
gaps.falsification_attempt: The obvious objection is that "seen on nightly" is not "actionable on nightly": a signature at 1-2 nightly reports/day never clears the spike rule. That is why I did not stop at the Socorro comparison and went to the prod DB instead — the question there is not whether the signature exists on nightly but whether OUR pipeline already selected and analysed it, and 24 of 30 appear in the `selection` record within a 21-day nightly window, 16 of 30 with a finished dossier. The 6 that never appear are `(anonymous namespace)::ChildImpl::ThreadInfoWrapper::InitStarter`, `AsyncShutdownTimeout | quit-application | newtabTrainhopAddon`, `RtlWakeAllConditionVariable | js::ConditionVariable::notify_all`, `mozilla::dom::OptionalServiceWorkerData::AssertSanity`, `mozilla::dom::cache::ReadStream::Inner::Read`, `stackoverflow | style::values::specified::calc::impl$10` — and all six are stale by 5-140 days, so none is attributable.

gaps.title: The human baseline on release is 21.7 hours to a regression range; our first selection arrives a median 11.1 days after the build ships
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Even if a release lead were correct, it arrives after the decision it would inform. Release crash triage is a staffed process with tracking flags; our contribution has to be earlier or better-attributed than theirs, and it is neither.
gaps.evidence: 91 crash-signature bugs with `cf_tracking_firefox150..155` in (+, blocking) created in 2026 = 11.4/month; 59 of 91 (65%) already carry `regressed_by`. From BMO `/history`, time from bug creation to `regressed_by` first being SET, n=43: median 21.7 h, p25 1.8 h, 23/43 (53%) within 24 h, 31/43 (72%) within 72 h; median time to resolution 5.3 d (n=87). Our lag, from the same replay, build date -> first selection day: n=30, median 11.1 d (bump builds 11.1 d, dot releases 7.9 d), min 4.3, max 13.3. The canonical dot-release regression, bug 2049845 ("Firefox 152.0.2 extreme memory usage and complete freeze on startup (regression from 152.0.1)"), got its regression range in 21.7 h.
gaps.proposed_fix: State the latency requirement explicitly before any release work: a release lead is worth something only if it lands inside ~24 h of the build. On a 3-build window with median 7.07-day gaps and 10% sampling, it cannot. If earlier release detection is genuinely wanted, that is a different product (a per-build rate test on the release build's first day), not this pipeline.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to argue our lag is an artefact of the 3-build window rather than of arrival: it is not, because the 11.1-day median is dominated by how long it takes a release build to accumulate enough crashes to clear installs>=50 against the previous build (the selections on 154.0, shipped 08-12, start on 08-19 and keep arriving through 08-26). Lowering the threshold shortens the lag but multiplies volume 10-15x (see the cost gap). I also checked the human number is not survivorship: it is measured over release-TRACKED bugs, i.e. the ones release management actually cares about, which is exactly the population our filings would land next to.

gaps.title: Cost: $207-740/month for zero expected filings, and $1,050-3,740/month if the thresholds are lowered to beta's to buy supply
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Release is affordable at today's thresholds and worthless; it is unaffordable at the thresholds that would give it supply. Either way the unit economics are 26-94x worse than nightly's.
gaps.evidence: Real prod spend, read-only from the production Postgres, last 30 days: nightly 2,664 dossiers / $4,552.95 = $1.71/dossier = $151.76/day; beta 38 dossiers / $42.68 over 2026-08-27..08-31 = $1.12/dossier = $8.54/day. Release projection from the replay: 30 distinct pairs / 31 run-days = 0.97/day; measured distinct `proto_signature` cardinality per selected pair (median 3, mean 11.0, max 75) capped by `thresholds.protos.release: 20` gives 191 uuids / 31 d = 6.2 uuids/run-day -> $6.90-24.65/day = $207-740/month (upper bound uses `max_cost_usd_per_crash_offstack` 4.0, which 73% of release runs would sit against). Re-priced off the same cached facets: installs 50/floor 10 = 30 pairs (identical); installs 20 = 59 pairs, 8.9 uuids/day, $10-36/day; installs 6 (beta's value) = 290 pairs, 31.2 uuids/day, $35-125/day = $1,050-3,740/month; installs 1 (nightly's value) = 29,412 pairs, 949/day, $3,191-11,396/day. Unit economics: nightly $4,553/month / (2.86 filings/day x 30 x 0.28 naming accuracy = 24 correct) = ~$190 per correct attribution ($276 per FIXED at 14/73 = 19%); release, generously ignoring the stale clamp, 3 desktop-native uplift-caused crash bugs / 20 months x 0.28 = one correct attribution per ~24 months at $207-740/month = $5,000-17,800 each.
gaps.proposed_fix: If a decision is wanted on cost alone: release at today's thresholds is 4.3-15.4% of the measured $4,809/month nightly+beta spend, which is affordable but buys nothing; at installs=6 it is 22-78% of total spend. Recommend spending the same money on plan #19's 24 h build-axis attribution window on nightly, which is already measured to name a regressor nobody set (`3bb594db2dda` / bug 1158387) at 12/20 vs production's 5/20.
gaps.falsification_attempt: The uuid count is the number I distrusted most, so I measured it two ways: the per-pair `_cardinality.proto_signature` (median 3, and only 4 of 30 pairs hit the cap of 20) and the deployed beta comparison (beta's live prod rate is 7.6 dossiers/day against my 6.2/day release projection — the same order, from an independent instrument). The lower-threshold rows use the median 3 for pairs whose proto count I did not measure, which if anything under-counts; the $/day range therefore has a soft upper bound and a hard lower one.

gaps.title: The one detector that fits release's actual crash population refuses release by design
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Release's population is old signatures at steady rate (median first_seen_any age of a selection: 118 days, max 860). The statistic built for exactly that shape — plan #19's trend-change detector — returns 0 immediately for release, so "plug release" cannot include the one thing that would justify it.
gaps.evidence: `sigtrend.backfill` opens with `if channel not in SUPPORTED_CHANNELS: return 0` and `SUPPORTED_CHANNELS = ("nightly", "beta")`, with the reason stated in the tree and re-measured here: release runs ~3,200 distinct signatures/day (my 30-day facet hit the 2,000 cap exactly) against `FACETS_SIZE` 2000 and `MAX_SIGNATURES` 1500, and Socorro's terms facets are count-ordered so an over-full day silently drops its quietest signatures — which are the only ones the module is for. Independently: release is 10% sampled, so the install counts the negative-binomial test consumes are not comparable with nightly's or beta's. My staleness measurement is the confirmation that this is the right detector for release: 29 of 30 selections are on signatures >7 days old, median 118 d, p25 42 d.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do not extend `sigtrend` to release by raising `FACETS_SIZE`: the fix is a per-signature query shape (plan #19 already says release "is queried per-signature as an environmental control"), which is ~3,200 queries/day, not one. Keep release as plan #19 already uses it — a cross-channel environmental control (family F8) read on demand, never ingested.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I checked whether the guard is a stale comment rather than live code: it is line 251 of the function `put_crashes` calls, so on release it is a silent per-run no-op, not a warning. I also checked whether the 3,200-signature figure holds today rather than only in plan #19's 206-day window — my own `_aggs.signature` request with `_facets_size: 2000` returned exactly 2,000 terms over 30 days, i.e. truncated, which is the same finding from a different query.

gaps.title: Redundancy: 70% of top release signatures already have an open bug, and 11 of 13 release selections with a full 30-day look-ahead were already covered
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: If release filing were ever armed, most of it would be comments on somebody else's open bug — and `agent.autofile.comment_on_existing` defaults to `comment`, which is the mode :apehrson already objected to on nightly. The one class where we WOULD be first is a reporting gap, not an attribution gap, and BugBot's crash filer plus aryx already cover reporting.
gaps.evidence: Top 100 release signatures by installs, through the repo's own `_open_bugs_for_signature` plus a raw `cf_crash_signature` search: 70 have an OPEN bug (70%), 84 have ANY bug (84%) — against beta's measured 58-59% and nightly's 23%. Per selection: 21 of 30 already had a bug at selection time (70%); restricted to the 13 selections with a full 30-day look-ahead (day <= 2026-08-01), 10 already had a bug, 1 got one within 3 days, and only 2 never did (`mozilla::dom::cache::ReadStream::Inner::Read` 199 reports, `(anonymous namespace)::ChildImpl::ThreadInfoWrapper::InitStarter` 121) — and both of those are stale by 33 and 44 days, so neither is attributable. The existing reporting machinery: 97 bugs with keyword `topcrash` created in 2026 (12.1/month, 76% FIXED/VERIFIED, 59% with `regressed_by`), and `release-mgmt-account-bot@mozilla.tld` filed 59 `Crash in [@ ...]` bugs since 2026-06 (~20/month) — its comment 0 says "By querying Nightly crashes reported within the last 2 months", so it is a nightly filer, not a release one.
gaps.proposed_fix: Leave `agent.autofile.channels.release` absent. `autofile_channel_declared` (bugzilla_apply.py:1059) already refuses an undeclared channel, so release filing is fail-safe today and should stay that way; adding a `release: {enabled: false}` entry would be worse than nothing, because `autofile_channel_declared` returns True for any channel with an entry and only `enabled` then holds it.
gaps.falsification_attempt: I tried to make the reporting gap into the case for release: if 15% of release selections are genuinely unreported crashes at 121-199 reports, maybe filing them is the value. Two things kill it. Both unreported cases are stale by 33-44 days, so we would file a bug with no regressor and no regression range — i.e. exactly what the release-mgmt bot already produces 20 times a month, and only 7 of its 59 bugs carry `regressed_by`. And our own record says the marginal filing is not free: of 73 pipeline filings ever, 11 (15%) are INVALID-class and 7 (10%) DUPLICATE.

measurements.claim: Over 26 dot-release windows in 2026, 0 signatures were genuinely new on the dot-release build at the release install threshold of 50
measurements.method: For each consecutive pair of `target.channel=release` Buildhub builds within a major (dot releases only), one SuperSearch per buildid with `_aggs.signature: [_cardinality.install_time]`, `_facets_size: 10000`, no date bound (lifetime). "New" = present on build N, absent on build N-1, installs >= `config.get_threshold('installs','Firefox','release')`.
measurements.numbers: 26 windows; 8 hits, all 8 from the single 153.0.1 respin pair (superseded buildid has 0 reports so its whole signature set reads as new) and all 8 boilerplate (OOM|small 413 installs, EMPTY 273, OOM|FreeSpan::allocate 136, IPCError|GPUProcessKill 122, OOM|crash 100, shutdownhang 76, +2). Genuine: 0. Sanity point: 154.0 has 5,032 signatures and 154.0.1 has 5,444, and 0 new at >=50 installs.

Window from the Buildhub release build list (`Build.get_last_versions` semantics, n=3, buildid <= D); per-buildid SuperSearch with the exact params of `datacollector.get_new_signatures` bounded `< D+1`; then `datacollector.find_no_user_days` and `utils.evaluate_days(numbers, ndays=1, threshold, floor, ratio)` with `get_maturity_bar` returning (None, 1) off nightly.
