kills.idea: Plan #18 §11 reason (c): "the same `get_last_versions` blackout applies" to release
kills.why_dead: The beta work removed the major-version break. `models.py:658` states "THE MAJOR-VERSION BREAK IS GONE" and the code at `models.py:688-708` has no break, only `.limit(n)`. My 31-run-day release replay had ZERO blackout days and the window correctly straddles a version bump (2026-07-27 window = ['152.0.5','152.0.6','153.0'], 13 selections). This reason for scoping release out is no longer true, and the plan paragraph should not be cited as if it were.

kills.idea: Plan #18 §11 reason (a) read as "release needs its spike floor tuned"
kills.why_dead: Measured on the cached as-of facets: `spike.floor.release` 50 -> 10 changes 0 of 30 selections, because `thresholds.installs.release: 50` dominates it (a build-day that clears 50 installs and 3x the previous build almost always carries >=50 crashes). The install threshold is the whole gate, exactly as on beta — but for the opposite reason (there, 78-89% came through the ungated from-zero branch; here the split is 16 from-zero / 14 floor+ratio and the floor still never binds). Tuning the floor is dead work in either direction.

kills.idea: "Release has an `aurora`-style alias problem like beta's, so `utils.get_search_channel` needs a release arm"
kills.why_dead: No. `release` is a single string carrying 52.03% of Firefox crash reports; `esr` is its own separate string at 39.60% and is scoped out by plan #18 §11 for the CHANNEL_TYPE-enum reason; `default` (unbranded/self-built) is 1.45%; every other term including `Bosch`, `no`, `r`, `nighwtly` totals under 0.3%. `utils.get_search_channel('release')` returning `'release'` is correct as written and needs no change. (The real omission is ESR, which is a 40%-of-reports channel we do not read at all — a scope question, not an alias bug.)

kills.idea: "The day INGEST_CHANNELS gains release, one tasks.html retrigger files a release bug under nightly's rules"
kills.why_dead: Closed by plan #18's own item 18. `bugzilla_apply.py:1059` calls `config.autofile_channel_declared(channel)` and returns `{"filed": False, "skipped": "channel 'release' has no autofile configuration"}` for any channel with neither an `agent.autofile.channels.<ch>` entry nor equality with `default_channel`. `config/global.json` has only a `beta` entry, so release filing is fail-safe today even with `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1` and even through `retrigger_agent(force=True)`. The residual hazard is SPEND, not writes: `get_agent_channels()` returns `env.split()`, so an explicitly empty `AGENT_CHANNELS` means every channel.

kills.idea: "Ingest release read-only so the stale-signature gate and `signature_age.other_channel_floor` get a real release clock"
kills.why_dead: They already have one, and it costs nothing. `sigage.signature_history` builds `any_params = {**base, "_facets": "release_channel"}` (sigage.py:160) with NO `release_channel` filter, so `first_seen_any` and `total_other_channels` already read release and esr today; the docstring even reasons about release's 10% sampling. Ingesting release adds `builds`/`nodes`/`changesets`/`selection` rows and release UI pages, and adds exactly nothing to the age clock.

kills.idea: "Release scale (39x nightly's crashing installations per day) makes even a low-precision lead worth more"
kills.why_dead: Two measurements. Composition: 63.9% of release reports and 66.8% of its install weight sit in classes with no in-tree regressor (OOM 32.9%, shutdownhang 13.6%, AsyncShutdownTimeout 9.1%, stackoverflow 3.3%, EMPTY 2.2%, third-party dll/so 2.0%). Uniqueness: 2 of the top 300 signatures (0.7%) are invisible on nightly/beta over 364 days, and both are noise. Release has 39x the population and 0.9% of the selection supply (0.97 pairs/day vs nightly's 102-145) because the selector asks "is this build crashier than the last" and release's population is old signatures at a steady rate.

kills.idea: "Extend plan #19's trend detector to release, since release's population is exactly the class it was built for"
kills.why_dead: `sigtrend.backfill` returns 0 for release at line 251, and the reason is arithmetic, not policy: release runs ~3,200 distinct signatures/day (my own `_facets_size: 2000` request truncated at exactly 2,000) against `FACETS_SIZE` 2000 and `MAX_SIGNATURES` 1500, and Socorro's terms facets are count-ordered, so an over-full day silently drops the quietest signatures — the only ones the module exists for. Raising the cap does not fix it; covering release needs ~3,200 per-signature queries a day. Plan #19 already reaches the same conclusion and keeps release as a per-signature environmental control (family F8).

kills.idea: "Even one dot-release regression a cycle would pay for release, because the dot-release window is 6 native changesets and precision would be far above nightly's 28%"
kills.why_dead: The precision premise is probably true and irrelevant: there is nothing in the window to attribute. 0 new-on-a-dot-release signatures at >=50 installs over 26 windows; 8/8 dot-release selections stale by 33-553 days (median 146 d), so `_apply_signature_age_gate` clamps them to `medium(50)`, below `min_confidence: 70`. Even granting a bypass, the rate is 3 desktop-native uplift-caused crash bugs in 20 months x our 28% naming accuracy = one correct attribution per ~24 months at $207-740/month = $5,000-17,800 each, against a measured ~$190 per correct nightly attribution.

open_questions: Which goal is actually being asked for: (A) attribute release regressions, or (B) cover release crash REPORTING? My recommendation: neither on release. (A) has 0 measured supply (0 new-on-a-dot-release signatures at >=50 installs over 26 windows) and (B) is already done by others (97 `topcrash` bugs in 2026 = 12.1/month, `release-mgmt-account-bot` 20 crash bugs/month, aryx 109 crash-signature bugs in 2026). If the underlying wish is "catch more real regressions for the same money", the measured answer is plan #19's 24 h build-axis attribution window on NIGHTLY (12/20 vs production's 5/20), not a new channel.

Do we ship an ingest-only release phase as a measurement, or nothing at all? Recommendation: nothing. The usual argument for ingest-only — it is free and it builds the record — is weaker here than it was for beta, because (i) the age clock already reads release without ingestion (`sigage.py:160`), (ii) the trend statistic refuses release (`sigtrend.py:251`), and (iii) each cycle merge writes ~5,400-7,500 `nodes` rows plus author round-trips into a Postgres whose `builds`/`uuids` tables are already pruned to 30 days. The only thing it buys is `selection` rows for release, and the replay in `spike/_release_recon/v11_selector.py` already produces them offline for free.

If release is refused, should ESR be reconsidered instead of quietly inheriting the same "out of scope" line? ESR is 39.60% of Firefox crash reports and 12,084 crashing installations/day — a bigger slice than release-channel-only reasoning suggests. Recommendation: no, and for a stronger reason than plan #18 §11 gives (the CHANNEL_TYPE enum): ESR code is older still, so every argument above gets worse, and ESR's uplift windows are the same dot-release shape. Record it as measured-dead rather than deferred, so it is not re-litigated.

What is the tripwire that would reopen this? Recommendation: re-run `spike/_release_recon/v26_addressable.py` once a month (26 Socorro queries, ~2 minutes) and reopen only if >=3 dot-release windows in any 6-month period produce a signature that is new on release AND whose `first_seen_any` is within 7 days of the uplift's release-branch pushdate. That is a supply test, it costs nothing, and it is the number that would change my recommendation.
cross_dimension: FILING, possible duplicate on a FIXED bug's signature: `clouseau-bot@mozilla.tld` filed bug 2067456 on 2026-08-28 for `AsyncShutdownTimeout | profile-before-change | CookiePersistentStora...` — the exact signature of plan #19's motivating bug 2063336, which aryx filed 2026-08-13 and baku RESOLVED FIXED 2026-08-19. `bugzilla_apply._open_bugs_for_signature` passes `resolution: "---"`, so a FIXED bug is invisible to it and cannot be a venue nor a duplicate check. Memory already records the mirror case ([[dup-across-signatures]]); this looks like the same hole from the other side. Worth the filing dimension checking whether 2067456 should have been a comment on 2063336.

FILING / feedback: the filing account moved from `cdenizet@mozilla.com` to `clouseau-bot@mozilla.tld` on 2026-08-27 (10 bugs, 1 already RESOLVED INVALID, 5 still UNCONFIRMED). `feedback._filed_bugs` sources bug ids from `Dossier.payload['filed_bug']` so it is unaffected, but `_COMMENT_MARK`/`creator`-based reasoning and any hand query that assumes cdenizet will now split the corpus in two. Any "how often are we right" number computed after 08-27 needs both accounts.

OPS: on a release version-bump build the off-stack enumerator would fetch a live `json-pushes?version=2&full=1` of 8.0-11.9 MB in 3.6-4.0 s, and 22 of 30 release selections are bump-build, so that is ~6 such fetches per run-day, uncached, on the one serial analysis chain. Plan #18 §12 already notes beta roughly doubles that chain's traffic; release's per-fetch payload is 1.6-2.3x beta's measured 7.5 MB.

INGESTION: prod's `builds` table holds 61 nightly and 12 beta rows and `uuids`/`dossiers` begin 2026-08-01, so ANY retrospective claim taken from the production DB has a <=30-day window (and `selection`'s nightly history is only 2026-08-11..08-31, beta's 08-26..08-31). I used it for a 30-day overlap claim only; anyone reaching further back will silently get a truncated denominator.

POPULATION / SCOPE: `esr` is 39.60% of all Firefox crash reports (476,584 in 30 days, 12,084 distinct installs/day) and there is no `esr` value in `CHANNEL_TYPE`. That is by far the largest crash population the product cannot represent at all, larger than release-minus-esr reasoning implies, and it interacts with `sigage.signature_history`, which already counts esr reports toward `other_channel_floor: 20` without anyone having decided that it should.

reports.headline: ESR is a non-problem where plan #18 said it might be one, and a real problem where nobody looked. No enum work exists for release: I built a fresh Postgres from `models.create()` AND read production's `pg_enum` — `CHANNEL_TYPE` is already `nightly|beta|release` in both, so `_ENUM_ADDITIONS`/`_ADDED_TABLES` need nothing, and ESR is a genuinely separate Socorro label (`esr`/`esr115`/`esr128`/`esr140`) and a separate buildhub `target.channel`, so no release query picks it up. What ESR *does* break is the stale-signature gate: on release the `other_channel_floor` of 20 is inert (30/30 and 25/25 cleared, 93%/80% on `esr*` labels alone), so `first_seen` is always the unfloored all-channel value the config itself calls "not usable as-is", and 25/25 of the near-threshold population sits 43-894 days before the build. Three adjacent things will actually bite on day one: production still holds 7,267 stale `release` nodes and a `lastdate.release` of 2026-07-06, so the first tick fetches 8 weeks (29.9 MB in one unbounded request, measured 335 s end-to-end); buildhub's release channel carries the *next* release's RC (155.0, 2 installations) and it takes one of the three window slots, on which the real selector selects 0 signatures; and six shipped tests fail the moment release joins `agent.channels`, naming the three missing config entries (population rates, calibration, autofile declaration). Separately, `/api/selection` validates `channel` and then ignores it, and its 500-row feed is already saturated at two channels while release would add 3,310 rows per tick.

gaps.title: Production holds 8 weeks of stale release ingestion state, so the first release tick fetches 20,094 changesets / 29.9 MB in one unbounded request (measured 335 s)
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The first `update(None, "release", "Firefox")` job is not a 20-second delta, it is a 5.6-minute job holding one unbounded 29.9 MB HTTP response plus 20,094 ORM inserts in a single transaction, on the shared `low` queue that also carries nightly/beta report scoring, on a 512 MB dyno. It will not be killed (I checked: `worker.get_queue` sets `default_timeout=6000`), but it stalls nightly+beta scoring for its duration and peaks memory near the OOM band that has already killed the agentworker twice.
gaps.evidence: Read-only `heroku pg:psql -a crash-clouseau-augmented`: `nodes` holds channel=release 7,267 rows with pushdate 2026-06-07 18:10:51 .. 2026-07-06 12:00:35; `lastdate` has a release row mindate 2026-06-07 18:10:51 / maxdate 2026-07-06 12:36:38; `builds` has ZERO release rows (nightly 61, beta 12). So release ingestion ran in prod for a month and was switched off, leaving the resume point 8 weeks in the past. `put_filelog` (update.py:29-40) resumes from `Node.get_max_date(channel)` + 1 s, else `LastDate` + 1 s. Measured on hg: releases/mozilla-release 2026-07-06..08-31 = 323 pushes / 20,094 changesets / 29,889,956 bytes of json-pushes, against a steady-state day of 2 pushes / 3 changesets / 24,194 bytes. End-to-end against a throwaway Postgres seeded with prod's exact stale lastdate: `put_filelog("release")` 335.5 s, peak RSS 234 MB, 13,041 nodes retained after `Node.clean`, 26 `changesets` rows owing a `patch.parse`.
gaps.proposed_fix: Before flipping `INGEST_CHANNELS`, reset the release resume point: delete the 7,267 stale `nodes` rows for channel='release' and set `lastdate.release.maxdate` to now-3d (or drop the lastdate row so `put_filelog` falls to `now - max_ndays`, which is 30 days and still ~2 merges). Alternatively, bound `pushlog.pushlog` to a max window (e.g. chunk into 7-day json-pushes requests) so a cold or long-stalled channel can never issue an unbounded fetch — that also fixes nightly and beta after any ingestion stall.

gaps.title: `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` has no release entry, and a shipped test makes that a hard prerequisite — measured: release bit_flip 8.91%, broken_cpu 5.79%
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `test_every_triaged_channel_has_its_own_two_rates` iterates `config.get_agent_channels()` and asserts both rates are not None, so adding release to `agent.channels` fails the suite (verified). If someone deletes that assertion instead of measuring, every release crash brief prints the signature's own bit-flip share with no population claim beside it, against a population whose base flip rate is 3.6x nightly's shipped 2.5% — the exact `hardware-noise-denominator` mistake, one level up.
gaps.evidence: `_population("release")` returns `{}` (sigage.py:424-426), so all three accessors return None and `population_label("release")` returns the bare "Firefox". Re-measured with the shipped instrument (Firefox, `get_search_channel(channel)`, 364 days, the two facets `hardware_noise` reads): nightly bit_flip 0.0375 / broken_cpu 0.0447 (n=533,914); beta 0.0672 / 0.0585 (n=267,917) — which reproduces the shipped beta values 0.0675 / 0.0582 to 3 decimal places and so validates the instrument; release 0.0891 / 0.0579 (n=3,759,235), top cpu model share 0.060. Simulating release in `agent.channels` in memory (no file edit) fails exactly 6 shipped tests, one of them this one with "AssertionError: unexpectedly None (channel='release')".
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `_POPULATION_RATES["release"] = {"bit_flip": 0.0891, "broken_cpu": 0.0579, "top_cpu_share": None}` and `POPULATION_LABEL["release"] = "Firefox-release"`, citing n=3,759,235 / 364 d / 2026-08-31; leave `top_cpu_share` None (nobody has drawn the 200-signature sample on release, and the beta precedent is to say nothing). Then rewrite tests/test_shipped_channels.py:519-525, which currently pins the ABSENCE of all three release rates and the "Firefox" label as correct behaviour.

gaps.title: ESR history clears `other_channel_floor` on 100% of release signatures, so the stale-signature gate degenerates to the all-channel rule the config itself calls unusable
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The floor exists to be a discriminator: below 20 off-channel reports the answer is the channel's own first-seen, above it the all-channel one. On release it never binds, so `first_seen` is always `first_seen_any` — and `sigage.signature_history`'s own docstring says the unfloored all-channel rule, replayed on 35 filings, "split roughly evenly into filings a human refuted and filings a human FIXED. It is not usable as-is." Downstream, 25/25 of the population have `first_seen` 43-894 days before the build, so `days_landed_after_first_seen > 7` for any candidate drawn from the build's own pushlog window and `_STALE_SIGNATURE_CLAMP` fires on essentially every release lead (probable->medium, medium->low), i.e. under the 70 filing floor unless the blind second opinion undoes it.
gaps.evidence: Two samples, both through the repo's own `sigage.signature_history(sig, product="Firefox", channel="release")` plus one extra per-signature `release_channel` facet over the same 364 days to attribute `other`. (a) Top 30 release signatures by distinct installations, last 3 processed days: floor cleared 30/30 = 100%, clearable by `esr*` labels ALONE 28/30 = 93.3%, `first_seen` moved off the channel value on 18/30. (b) Falsification pass, deliberately drawn to defeat the ancient-loud bias: the 25 QUIETEST signatures above the 50-install threshold on the newest real release build 20260824154132 (78 qualified): floor cleared 25/25, ESR alone 20/25 = 80%, first_seen moved 15/25, and `first_seen` more than 7 days older than the build 25/25 (min 43 d, most 750-894 d). The volume that makes it inevitable: `esr` is 116,608 reports / 58,877 installations per 7 days against release's 144,236 / 106,426, and ESR branches run back to 115.
gaps.proposed_fix: Make the floor scale with the channel's own volume rather than being an absolute 20 (e.g. require the off-channel history to be a share of the signature's own channel count), or scope the admitted off-channel set: exclude `esr*` from `other`/`first_seen_any` for a release crash, because an ESR-140 report proves the code is old on a branch that is by construction old, which is not evidence about whether this release build introduced the crash. Whichever is chosen, re-back-test it — the current 20 was calibrated on 10 nightly points and this measurement shows it transfers to release as a constant-true predicate.

gaps.title: Buildhub's release channel carries the NEXT release's candidate build, it takes one of the three window slots, and the no-user floor cannot remove it because the newest day is exempt
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `update_builds` inserts the RC as an ordinary release build, `Build.get_last_versions(n=3)` returns it as the newest, and the selection window becomes [RC with 2 installations, 154.0.1, 154.0] instead of three builds people run. `find_no_user_days` exempts the newest build-day unconditionally (by design, because a fresh build holds 0.2-2.7% of its crashes on ship day), so the release `min_build_installs` floor of 15 cannot drop it. The window that beta's `VERSION_PATS["beta"]` regexp exists to protect has no equivalent protection on release, and `models.py:676-681` says so in as many words — "do NOT 'fix' that regexp either; it is what protects this window" — for beta only.
gaps.evidence: Buildhub, `target.channel=release`, source.product=firefox: 155.0 at build.id 20260826195058 (revision 21a096119103, a "Promote beta to release" merge head), 5 days before it ships, while the shipped release is 154.0.1. Socorro for that build_id: 2 reports / 2 distinct install_time, all `release_channel=release`, version 155.0 — against 48,890 reports / 36,417 installations for 20260824154132. `VERSION_PATS["release"]` = `[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` drops 0 of the 32 release versions in buildhub since 2026-01-01, i.e. it admits every RC and dot release. End-to-end on a throwaway Postgres: `dc.get_builds("Firefox", "release", now)` -> `['20260826195058', '20260824154132', '20260812182057']`, search_date `>=2026-08-12`; `dc.get_no_user_build_floor("Firefox","release")` = 15; `dc.get_maturity_bar("Firefox","release")` = (None, 1). Running the REAL selector on that window: 0 signatures selected, outcomes {below_install_threshold: 3056, untestable_prefix: 159, not_spiking: 95}, and the RC's build-day rows read `bids={2026-08-26: 1}`.
gaps.proposed_fix: Either exclude not-yet-shipped candidate builds from the release window (there is no `target.channel` marker for an RC, so the usable discriminator is a Socorro installation count below `min_build_installs` — a lookup `update_builds` does not currently do), or lift the newest-day exemption in `find_no_user_days` for a build older than ~1 day whose installations are below the floor, or widen release's window (`get_last_versions(n=)`) so an RC slot does not cost a third of it. Do not "fix" `VERSION_PATS["release"]`: dot releases ARE release's builds, and the regexp is what keeps ESR out (verified below).

gaps.title: `/api/selection` and `selection.html` validate `channel` and then ignore it, and the 500-row feed is already saturated at two channels while release adds 3,310 rows per tick
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: The one surface built to answer "why was signature X not analysed" will be dominated by release `below_install_threshold` rows and offers no way to filter them out. `api.selection()` aborts 400 on a channel outside the enum, then passes `channel` only on the `?signature=` branch; the feed branch calls `Selection.summary(days)` and `Selection.recent(outcome, days)`, neither of which takes a channel. `html.selection()` never reads the parameter at all, though the template renders a channel column.
gaps.evidence: Live, read-only, against the deployed app: `GET /api/selection?channel=release` -> 200 with 500 rows whose channels are Counter({'nightly': 448, 'beta': 52}) — the filter is silently dropped, and the row count is exactly `Selection.recent`'s `limit=500`, i.e. already truncating. Prod DB, read-only: `selection` holds 1,890 nightly + 1,021 beta = 2,911 rows for the last 14 days, so the feed shows 17% of what exists. `GET /api/selection?channel=esr` -> 400 "The channel must be one of: ['nightly', 'beta', 'release']". One real release selector run against the real window produced 3,310 records (3,056 + 159 + 95), and `Selection.prune` retains 60 days.
gaps.proposed_fix: Thread `channel` (and `product`) into `Selection.recent` and `Selection.summary` as filter arguments, pass them from `api.selection()`'s feed branch and from `html.selection()` (add the query arg + a channel selector to selection.html), and raise or paginate the 500-row `limit` — it is already truncating at two channels. If release ingestion lands before this, the release rows should default to hidden on selection.html rather than merged in.

gaps.title: An undeclared release channel inherits NIGHTLY's calibration table, so a release lead would publish nightly's calibrated probability to Bugzilla
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: `get_agent_calibration("release")` returns `{25: 0.5, 50: 0.5714, 70: 0.7234, 85: 0.7234}` — nightly's fit, measured against nightly filings — because the per-channel overlay only special-cases channels that are named. Beta gets `{}` precisely because someone declared it empty. A release bug comment would therefore state a "% worth investigating" number derived from a different channel's outcome distribution.
gaps.evidence: Measured in-process: `config.get_agent_calibration('nightly')` = {25: 0.5, 50: 0.5714, 70: 0.7234, 85: 0.7234}; `('beta')` = {}; `('release')` = the nightly table; `(None)` = the nightly table. Simulating release in `agent.channels` fails `test_beta_publishes_no_calibrated_probability` with "'release' not found in {'beta'} : a triaged channel with no calibration entry silently publishes nightly's fit to Bugzilla". Also measured: `config.autofile_channel_declared('release')` is False and `get_agent_autofile('release')` returns the GLOBAL defaults (`comment_on_existing: 'comment'`, `daily_cap: 10`) rather than beta's held policy — filing is contained today only because `autofile_bug` fails closed with "no autofile configuration" (pinned at tests/test_shipped_channels.py:230-236).
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `agent.calibration.channels.release: {}` and `agent.autofile.channels.release: {"enabled": false, ...}` in the same commit that adds release to `agent.channels`, so the two invariant tests pass for the right reason. Note the asymmetry to avoid: the autofile fallback hands release nightly's `comment_on_existing: comment` / `daily_cap: 10` on a population 37.7x larger by installations, so if release filing is ever armed it must be armed with its own explicit numbers, not by inheritance.

gaps.title: `/pushlog.html` 500s on any channel outside the enum, and `/diff.html` renders an unvalidated channel into the hg URL
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: Adding a third valid channel value invites people (and links) to type a fourth. `html.pushlog()` has no try/except — unlike `reports()`, `tasks()` and `selection()`, which all catch and 404 — so an out-of-enum channel reaches a Postgres CHANNEL_TYPE comparison and 500s. `html.diff()` builds `Mercurial.get_repo_url(channel)` from raw input; the host is fixed but the path is not, so the page renders links into arbitrary `hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-<input>/` paths.
gaps.evidence: Live, read-only: `/pushlog.html?buildid=20260824154132&channel=release` -> 302 to `https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-release/pushloghtml?fromchange=9ce1ee6baeb9&tochange=8b532c2140db` (so the route is already release-correct, resolved via buildhub even with zero release rows in prod). `...&channel=esr` -> 500. `...&channel=bogus'` -> 500. `/diff.html?channel=..%2f..%2fevil&node=abc&filename=a.cpp&changeset=abc` -> 200 rendering `hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-../../evil/file/abc/a.cpp` and `.../diff/abc/a.cpp` in hrefs. `Mercurial.get_repo_url('')` returns `https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-`.
gaps.proposed_fix: Validate `channel` against `models.CHANNEL_TYPE.enums` in `html.pushlog()`, `html.diff()` and `html.codeview()` the way `api.reports()`/`api.selection()` already do (abort 400), or at minimum wrap `pushlog()` in the same try/except-404 the other three views use. Cheap, and it is the one place a release rollout adds a value to a list users hand-edit.

gaps.title: `reports.html` silently substitutes another channel for an unknown or empty one, so `?channel=release` looks like it worked
gaps.what_breaks_on_release: During the switch-on window (release ingested but no scored reports yet) `reports.html?channel=release` will render nightly's build list with no indication that the requested channel was dropped, so the operator watching for the first release build cannot tell "not yet" from "broken". The dropdown is data-driven off `UUID.get_buildids()`, so it will grow a release entry on its own once rows exist — no template change needed.
gaps.evidence: `reports()`/`reports_no_score()` default `channel` to "nightly" then do `if channel not in products[prod]: channel = next(iter(products[prod]))` — no validation, no message. Live: `/reports.html?channel=release`, `?channel=esr` and `?channel=%3Cscript%3E` all return HTTP 200 with byte-identical length 21,771, and the rendered dropdown contains only `option value="nightly" selected` and `option value="beta"`. `?channel=beta` returns a different page (13,448 bytes), so the parameter does work for a channel with data.
gaps.proposed_fix: Leave the fallback (a silent switch-off would be worse) but render the substitution: if the requested channel is not in `products[prod]`, show "no scored reports on <channel> yet — showing <fallback>". One line in the template.

measurements.claim: `release` is already a value of the `CHANNEL_TYPE` Postgres enum, both in a fresh schema and in production, so a release rollout needs no enum migration and no `_ENUM_ADDITIONS`/`_ADDED_TABLES` entry
measurements.method: Built a fresh schema with the repo's own `models.create()` against a throwaway `postgres:16` container and dumped `pg_enum`; then read production's enum with a single read-only SELECT via `heroku pg:psql -a crash-clouseau-augmented`.
measurements.numbers: Fresh DB: CHANNEL_TYPE = nightly(1), beta(2), release(3); PRODUCT_TYPE = Firefox; VERDICT_TYPE = culprit, lead, unrelated, abstain, error; AGENT_STATUS_TYPE = pending, running, done, error. 20 tables created, `set(_ADDED_TABLES) - tables` = empty. Columns typed CHANNEL_TYPE: builds, chandaily, lastdate, nodes, sigdaily (`selection.channel` is `db.String(16)`, models.py:1056, so it is already permissive). Production: CHANNEL_TYPE = nightly(1), beta(2), release(3).

measurements.claim: ESR is a separate Socorro `release_channel` label, so `release_channel=release` cannot pick up ESR crashes; release is 37.7x nightly by distinct installations
measurements.method: One SuperSearch facet on `release_channel` with `_cardinality.install_time`, Firefox, date >=2026-08-24 <2026-08-31, plus a per-channel `version` facet.

kills.idea: Release needs a `CHANNEL_TYPE` enum addition, or an `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` / `_ADDED_TABLES` entry, and therefore needs `_ensure_enum_values`' ALTER defect fixed first (plan #18 §11's ESR framing invites this)
kills.why_dead: Proven twice. A fresh Postgres built by `models.create()` reports CHANNEL_TYPE = nightly/beta/release, and production's own `pg_enum` reports the same three labels with sortorder 1/2/3 (read-only `heroku pg:psql`). `_ENUM_ADDITIONS` is `{"VERDICT_TYPE": ("lead",)}` and needs nothing; `_ADDED_TABLES`' seven tables all exist in the fresh schema and release introduces no new table or column. The `_ensure_enum_values` ALTER defect is only reachable for a channel added AFTER a DB was created — i.e. `esr`, which is out of scope.

kills.idea: A release query will accidentally sweep in ESR crashes, the way beta needed `aurora` added
kills.why_dead: Measured the opposite in both data sources. Socorro's `release_channel` facet gives `release` and `esr`/`esr115`/`esr128`/`esr140` as distinct labels (release 144,236 reports; esr 116,608), and `utils.get_search_channel("release")` returns the bare string with no twin, so every `release_channel=release` query in the repo already excludes ESR. Buildhub separates them by `target.channel`, and asking buildhub for channel=esr with `VERSION_PATS["release"]` returns [] because Elasticsearch anchors `regexp` — `140.8.0esr` does not fullmatch the pattern. `orchestrator._DB_CHANNEL` maps only aurora->beta, so there is no reverse aurora/beta bleed into release either.

kills.idea: Release signatures share more BMO history with Thunderbird/ESR, so `_OTHER_APP_PRODUCTS` needs release-specific entries
kills.why_dead: 78 release signatures above the 50-install threshold, run through the real `_open_bugs_for_signature` + `_split_by_application`: 5 carry a Thunderbird-family bug but **0** where a Thunderbird bug is the only candidate, so the venue chooser never has to drop to one. The [meta] rate (5/78 = 6.4%) is within noise of the config's nightly baseline (9/200 = 4.5%). The exclusion list as shipped is sufficient for release; the named collisions (1895101, 1928888, 1882757, 1813973) are all already handled by it.

kills.idea: Release's cycle merges will flood the queue with thousands of `patch.parse` calls, so release needs its own merge-push rule
kills.why_dead: `pushlog.suppresses_merge_extraction` is already `bool(channel) and channel.lower() != "nightly"`, so release gets beta's rule for free. Measured on the full 8-week release backlog: 19,727 of 20,094 changesets (98.2%) are `via_merge` and carried by 3 "Promote beta to release" pushes; after the rule and `Node.clean` only 26 `changesets` rows owe a patch parse. The cost of a release switch-on is the pushlog FETCH and the node INSERTs, not patch extraction.

kills.idea: RQ will kill the 5.6-minute first release ingestion job and the retry will loop forever without ever advancing the resume point
kills.why_dead: `worker.get_queue` sets `default_timeout=6000` (100 minutes), so a 335-second `put_filelog` finishes comfortably. I looked specifically because the failure mode would have been severe (no commit until `Changeset.add`, so a kill loses all progress) and it is not reachable at these numbers.

kills.idea: A third channel re-breaks `_chain_is_running`, so `analyze_reports` becomes a silent no-op every tick
kills.why_dead: That was the OLD `len(queue) <= 1` heuristic, and update.py:139-160 documents it while naming "three channels or two products" as the exact breaking point. The shipped version counts only jobs whose `func_name` is the chain's own, so the clock's per-channel `update` jobs no longer suppress the chain. Release adds one more `update` job per tick and nothing else.

kills.idea: Release needs its own `mature_after_days` / `mature_installs` values tuned
kills.why_dead: `datacollector.get_maturity_bar` returns `(None, 1)` for any channel other than nightly — measured live for release — so the release entries in `config/global.json` (`mature_after_days: 5`, `mature_installs: 4`) are dead config exactly as beta's are. Tuning them changes nothing; the levers that bind on release are `installs`, `spike.floor`, `spike.ratio` and `min_build_installs`.

kills.idea: Release needs a searchfox tree mapping and a compiled-out macro partition
kills.why_dead: Both already exist and resolve: `searchfox._CHANNEL_REPO["release"] = Repo.RELEASE` -> tree `firefox-release`, which answers HTTP 200 and is pinned by tests/test_product_wiring.py:1160; `compiled_out._CHANNEL_MACROS["release"]` is a complete on/off partition. `Mercurial.get_repo_url("release")` resolves to releases/mozilla-release, whose pushlog I fetched successfully.

open_questions: Reset the release resume point before switch-on, or bound the fetch in code? I recommend BOTH but in that order: delete the 7,267 stale prod `nodes` rows for channel='release' and set `lastdate.release.maxdate` to now-3d as a one-off operational step (5 minutes, no deploy), and file the chunked-json-pushes change separately — it also protects nightly/beta after any future ingestion stall, which is a known recurring failure here.

For the stale-signature gate on release, exclude `esr*` from the off-channel history, or make the floor proportional to the channel's volume? I recommend excluding `esr*` for a release crash: it is the smaller, more explainable change, and the measurement says an ESR-140 report is what clears the floor 80-93% of the time while proving nothing about whether THIS release build introduced the crash. Either way it needs a back-test before release triage is armed, because today the gate would clamp every release lead.

Do we keep release's RC build in the selection window, or filter it? I recommend filtering: require a buildhub-derived build to have >= `min_build_installs` distinct installations before it enters the window (one Socorro lookup per new build in `update_builds`), because the alternative — lifting the newest-day exemption in `find_no_user_days` — was itself measured into existence for beta and I would not disturb it.

Ship release with `agent.calibration.channels.release: {}` (publish no probability, beta's precedent) or measure a release calibration first? I recommend `{}`: beta ships that way, the nightly table would otherwise leak silently, and a release calibration cannot be measured until release filings exist.

Add `_POPULATION_RATES["release"]` with my measured 0.0891 / 0.0579, or re-measure at switch-on time? I recommend adding mine now with the n and date in the comment — the same query reproduces the shipped beta values to three decimals, so the instrument is validated — and flagging that nightly's shipped 0.025 now reads 0.0375 on the same instrument, which is a separate drift somebody should look at.

Does release triage go live with `SHOW_ABSTAIN`/selection.html unfiltered, or does the channel filter land first? I recommend the filter lands first: release writes 3,310 selection rows per tick against a feed that already truncates at 500, so without it the one page that explains the selector becomes unreadable on day one.
cross_dimension: GATES: on release the stale-signature clamp fires on essentially every lead (25/25 of the near-threshold population on build 20260824154132 has `first_seen` 43-894 days before the build), so `_STALE_SIGNATURE_CLAMP` moves probable->medium / medium->low below the 70 filing floor unless the blind second opinion undoes it. Somebody needs to price whether release triage produces any filable lead at all under the current gate, or whether the gate's premise ("the regressor is in this build's pushlog window") simply does not hold on a branch that receives a whole cycle at once.

GATES: the hardware-noise suppression thresholds are ABSOLUTE and nightly-fitted (`max_bit_flip_rate` 0.2, `max_broken_cpu_rate` 0.7, orchestrator.py:2671-2675) but release's base bit-flip rate is 8.91% against nightly's shipped 2.5% — 3.6x. More release signatures will sit near 0.2 for population reasons rather than signature reasons. That firing-rate change should be measured before release triage is armed.

REPORT_BUG / FILING: 19,727 of 20,094 release pushlog changesets (98.2%) are `via_merge`, so `report_bug.is_suspected_regression` will refuse the `regression` keyword on nearly every release candidate, and the off-stack window between two consecutive release builds straddles a "Promote beta to release" merge carrying 5,391-7,448 changesets against `agent.offstack.max_candidates` = 150. Whoever owns off-stack should check what the truncation selects.

SECURITY: the anonymous exposure surface scales with the population, not the code. Release is 106,426 distinct installations per 7 days against nightly's 2,825 (37.7x) and 144,236 reports against 9,596 (15x). `API_WRITE_TOKEN` IS set in prod (confirmed by `heroku config`), so `sensitive.py` withholding is live and `viewer_authorized()` returns False for anonymous requests — the mechanism works; it is the blast radius of a withholding MISS that grows 37.7x.

SELECTOR: `release_channel=release` includes Linux-distro/repackaged rebuilds whose buildids are not in buildhub — 6 of the 20 buildids answering the release label have 2-16 installations against 200-800 reports (e.g. 20260825051950 = 154.0.1, 788 reports / 16 installs). Harmless for the pipeline because release's build axis comes from `Build.get_last_versions`, but any hand-rolled "newest release build" query off Socorro picks one of these — mine did, on the first attempt, and it returned 0 signatures above threshold.

PROCESS: `config/global.json` changed on disk mid-session (release was added to `agent.channels`) and was reverted before I re-read it; `git status` is clean and `spike/_release_recon/` shows nine other agents' scratch files. Any config-derived number in these reports should be re-checked against HEAD rather than trusted from a sibling agent's transcript.

DEAD CODE: `crashclouseau/single.py` is orphaned (nothing imports it) and calls `pushlog.puhslog`, which does not exist. It is the only place our channel label would come straight from Socorro's raw `release_channel` (`inspector.get_crash_by_uuid`, inspector.py:79), i.e. the only path where `aurora`/`esr`/`default`/`Bosch` could reach a CHANNEL_TYPE column. Unreachable today; worth deleting rather than leaving as a trap for the next channel.

contradictions.topic: Does the 30-day node retention shorten the release selection window? (ingestion 19.1% vs selection's KILL "not at n=3")
contradictions.positions: ingestion [blocker/measured]: replayed the real `datacollector.get_builds`/`Build.get_last_versions` over 549 run-days with `Node.clean` emulated -> build ROWS {1:1, 2:83, 3:465}, distinct build-DAYS 3 on 444 (80.9%), 2 on 104 (18.9%), 1 on 1 (0.2%); short <3 on 105/549 = 19.1%. selection KILL: "Not at n=3 -- the widest 3-build release window in the whole Buildhub history spans exactly 30 buildid-days (148.0 -> 149.0) and 0 of 33 exceed 30 days." config: 21% of days under-filled, max 3-build span 31.2 d. tests: 24% of switch-on days see <3 builds, max span 30.15 d. windows: "in the cycles measured every dot release ships before that, so no window actually jumps."
contradictions.resolution: ingestion WINS, exactly. I re-derived it from the same 83-build Buildhub list (spike/_release_recon/resolve_01_retention.py) and reproduced every number to the unit: 19.1% short, 0.2% one-build-day, no-pruning control 3.8%, retention sweep 30->80.9% / 35->90.2% / 40->94.7% / 45->96.0% / 50-90->96.2%. selection's kill uses the WRONG STATISTIC: the retention clock runs from the RUN DAY, not from the newest build, and the newest release build is itself a median 4.20 / p90 10.47 / max 20.35 days old at a run-day, so the retention must cover (age of newest) + (3-build span) = up to 51.6 d, not 31.2 d. selection's own statistic is also mis-stated twice: over all 83 builds 2 of 81 triples exceed 30 d (max 31.24), and its "n=33, max 30, 0 exceed 30" is the 2026-01+ slice where the max is 30.1 d, i.e. 1 of 33 exceeds 30 (rounded down). population and selection both restricted to 2026-04+ (26 gaps, median 5.25 d, max 12.2 d), a 5-month slice that EXCLUDES the largest gap in the data (20.89 d). config's 21% and tests' 24% are the same finding measured as a Buildhub-lookback question rather than a retention one and are compatible.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:// uv run python spike/_release_recon/resolve_01_retention.py`, which computes selection's span statistic and ingestion's run-day statistic side by side off `spike/_release_recon/v06_builds.json` (83 real builds 2025-01-13..2026-08-26). Any future re-measurement must span >= 12 months, because the 20.89-day gap that drives the result is outside every 2026-04+ window.

contradictions.topic: Release selection volume: 2.47 pairs/run-day (selection) or 0.97 (value) or ~1/day (population) or 0 (esr)?
contradictions.positions: selection: 329 distinct (signature, buildid) pairs over 133 run-days 2026-04-20..08-30 = 2.47/day, reproduced twice (two independent reimplementations both gave 329/2.47/max 35). value: 30 pairs over 31 run-days 2026-07-27..08-26 = 0.97/day. population: 220 pairs over the two builds of one cycle = ~110/build = ~1/day. esr: the real selector on the real window today selected 0 signatures.
contradictions.resolution: THEY AGREE; the headline difference is entirely the window. selection's own sub-window figure is 27 pairs over 36 run-days 07-26..08-30 = 0.75/day, and value's 30 pairs over 31 days 07-27..08-26 = 0.97/day — the same measurement, and the two also agree on the BRANCH split (selection 55.6% from-zero in that sub-window; value 16 from-zero / 14 floor+ratio). selection's 2.47/day is higher because its 133-day window contains four ratio-branch bursts (05-25..31, 06-23, 06-30..07-05, 07-22..26) and value's 31-day window contains none. The bursts are REAL, not an artefact: I confirmed the mechanism (spike/_release_recon/resolve_09_burst_vs_handicap.py) — every burst has a baseline build that was current for only 3-4 days and therefore has a permanently small lifetime install base (151.0 21,850 vs 151.0.1 71,392 = 3.27x; 152.0.2 25,584 vs 152.0.3 70,747 = 2.76x; 152.0 29,264 vs 152.0.1 83,575 = 2.86x — all three of selection's figures reproduced). The burst-generating configuration (a DOT release arriving <=4 days after the previous build) occurs on 8 of 82 builds overall, 3 of 18 in selection's window, 1 of 7 in value's. USE 2.47/day for a cost ceiling and 0.75-0.97/day for the quiet steady state; esr's 0 is one run-day and is consistent with selection's 52.6% zero-selection days.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled from the two replays' own outputs plus spike/_release_recon/resolve_09_burst_vs_handicap.py, which fetches the per-build arrival histograms and reproduces all three burst ratios. Any single-cycle replay of release must state whether its window contains a <=4-day dot-to-dot gap; if it does not, its rate is a lower bound.

contradictions.topic: Proto fan-out per selected pair, and therefore the whole release cost model: 12.3 kept/pair and $960-4,050/month (selection) or 6.4 kept/pair and $207-740/month (value) or 8.2 runs/selection (llm)?
contradictions.positions: selection sel_18_protos.py: 27 pairs, distinct protos median 11, mean 50.7, max 250, 11/27 capped, 332 kept = 12.3/pair -> 58.4 UUIDs/day -> $32-135/day. value v19_protos.py: 30 pairs, median 3, mean 11.0, max 75, 191 kept = 6.4/pair -> 6.2 UUIDs/day -> $6.90-24.65/day. llm llm_23_protos_random.py: 20 RANDOM signatures on one build, median 6, p75 13, max 178, cap 20 -> 8.2 runs/selection.
contradictions.resolution: BOTH ARE WRONG-DENOMINATOR, and the production number is 11.7 kept/pair — close to selection, 1.9x above value. Production (`datacollector.get_proto_small`/`get_proto_big`) passes `search_date` = '>=' + the oldest build-DAY of the 3-build window, evaluated AT the run-day. selection's script passed `date='>=2026-07-01'` (up to 61 days, well past the run-day); value's script passed NO `date` key at all, and SuperSearch silently substitutes a 7-DAY window. Measured on the SAME 30 pairs with all three shapes (spike/_release_recon/resolve_03_protos.py): production median 10, mean 25.8, max 140, 350 kept = 11.7/pair, 10/30 capped; selection's shape median 16, mean 47.8, max 250, 13.0/pair; value's shape median 3, mean 10.9, max 73, 6.3/pair — reproducing value's published median 3 / mean 11.0 / max 75 exactly and confirming it as the 7-day-default artefact. So value's cost projection is understated ~1.9x on the proto axis alone, and ~2.5x more on the pair-rate axis (see the volume row). At production's 11.7/pair: 11.29 UUIDs/day over value's quiet window and ~29/day at selection's 2.47 pairs/day. llm's draw is over random signatures, not selections, and llm flags this itself. Note also `date=""` is a hard 400 while an ABSENT `date` is a silent 7-day default.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_03_protos.py` prints all three window shapes per pair. Any cost figure for release must state the proto query's date bound; the only defensible one is `>= oldest build-day of the window, < run-day + 1`.

contradictions.topic: How much does the 10% release sample understate machines? 7.80x (selection) or 4.1x (population), and what is the effective accept rate — 10%, 10.72% or 6.2%?
contradictions.positions: selection: fitted a shifted-geometric true-crash-count under p=0.1 to the observed per-pair reports/install of 1.036 -> 7.80 true machines per observed install, so installs=50 ~ 390 machines. population: applied antenna's 10% rule to the unsampled esr153 CHANNEL-WIDE k-histogram (4,182 installs, mean k=2.314) -> 18.4% of installs visible = 5.4x, 4.1x once the 7.4% unsampled slice is mixed in, so installs=50 ~ 205 machines; also derives an effective observed rate of 10.72%. trend: solved `observed = s/(s+r(1-s))` on the gpu share and on the throttleable F-share against esr and got a non-background accept rate r = 6.2% / 6.22%.
contradictions.resolution: selection is right for the gate that matters; population applied a CHANNEL-WIDE factor to a PER-SIGNATURE threshold. `thresholds.installs` is a per-(signature, build-day) gate, so the relevant k is the per-(signature, build) reports-per-install. Measured directly on the unsampled esr153 population (spike/_release_recon/resolve_04_thinning.py, 14 signatures on build 20260716160951): per-(signature,build) mean k median 1.150, so a 10% per-report Bernoulli leaves a median 11.33% of installs visible -> understatement median 8.83x, range 4.27-9.67x. selection's 7.80x is within 12% of that; population's 4.1x is 2.2x too small for this axis. population's 4.1x IS the right order for a CHANNEL-WIDE install count (a machine crashing on many signatures over a month has large k and almost always survives the sample) — my truncated channel-wide facet gives mean k 20.7 and only 1.25x, so the channel-wide factor is somewhere in 1.25-4.1x depending on tail coverage. trend's r=6.2% is a model inversion assuming esr and release have identical process-type composition, which is not established; treat 10% as the nominal and 6-11% as the uncertainty band. All three are models, not measurements — only the esr k-distribution is measured.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled for the per-signature axis: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_04_thinning.py`. To close the residual, facet `install_time` per (signature, buildid) on an unsampled channel for ~100 signatures across the install range and report the visible-fraction distribution rather than a single multiplier.

contradictions.topic: Is the 100%-accepted (unsampled) slice 0.00% of what release SELECTION sees (selection) or 7.4% of the channel (population) or 6.63% (trend)?
contradictions.positions: selection KILL: "exempt-process reports across all 27 selections = 0 of 22,784 (0.00%)... A flat 10% is the correct model for everything release selection ever sees." population: throttleable=F 6.7% + background process 1.9%, measurable union 7.4% of release reports. trend: throttleable F-share 6.63% over August, gpu enrichment 15.8x vs esr.
contradictions.resolution: ALL THREE MEASURED DIFFERENT THINGS, and the number selection needed is 1.86% with a 43% tail. On the 30 real selected pairs (spike/_release_recon/resolve_05_unsampled_slice.py, 23,094 reports): background-process reports 0 (0.00%) — selection's process-type arm is exactly right — but `throttleable=F` (antenna's `throttleable_0` / about:crashes rule, 100% accepted) is 429/23,094 = 1.86%, and it ranges 0.00% to 43.42% ACROSS pairs: `std::_Reverse_vectorized` 43.4%, `mozilla::dom::OptionalServiceWorkerData::AssertSanity` 23.9%, `recvfrom | std::sys::net...` 20.0%, `nsBlockFrame::RemoveFrame` 19.7% — 4 of 30 pairs (13%) at 2-5x the nominal rate. Channel-wide I reproduce population and trend: release throttleable=F 6.60%, background 1.85% (esr 0.44%/0.25%, nightly 2.96%/40.70%, beta 1.39%/0.81%). So selection's conclusion is 98% right on average and materially wrong per signature, and its "has_comments/has_phc are 100% ACCEPT" premise is UNMEASURABLE: I confirmed that a FILTER on `user_comments` or `phc_kind` is silently ignored (returns the full unfiltered total with `errors: []`), so nobody can measure those two slices at all. nightly's 40.70% background share also confirms trend's kill of nightly-as-reference.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_05_unsampled_slice.py`. Any per-signature rate on release must report the pair's own `throttleable` split, because the effective accept rate is a per-signature quantity, not a channel constant.

contradictions.topic: Is there a release-only crash class in the head of the distribution? 0 of top 200 (population) vs 2 of top 300 = 0.7% (value) vs 4 of 350 = 1.1% (filing)
contradictions.positions: population: 0 of the top 200 release signatures by installs (92.6% of channel install-hits) has zero nightly+beta reports over 2026-01-01..08-27; 14.2% of a ranks-200-2000 sample IS release-only at median 4 installs. value: 2 of the top 300 (0.7%) have no nightly/beta/aurora report in 364 days — `@0x0 | neqo_udp::recv_inner` (274 installs) and `arise_dri.so` (166). filing: top 100 -> 0 never on nightly OR beta; ranks 101-350 -> 5/250 release-only, 3 un-bugged (`@0x0 | neqo_udp::recv_inner` 103 installs, `arise_dri.so` 83, `cx4_dri.so` 80); net 4/350 = 1.1%.
contradictions.resolution: ALL THREE AGREE once the rank is fixed; the apparent conflict is that value presented rank-202 and rank-235 signatures as a top-300 finding. I rebuilt one ranking (14-day install cardinality, 400-signature facet) and tested the same 300 signatures against three upstream windows (spike/_release_recon/resolve_06_release_only.py): every window gives 0 in the top 100, 0 in the top 200, 4 in the top 300 — at ranks 202 (`@0x0 | neqo_udp::recv_inner`, 102 installs), 235 (`arise_dri.so`, 80), 236 (`cx4_dri.so`, 79), 264 (`astmcwebextension3.dll | RtlAllocateHeap...`, 68). filing's ranks and installs match mine to within 1. So population is right that the top 200 is empty, filing is the most precise, and value's two signatures are the same ones filing found in the tail — its install figures (274, 166) are a 31-day cardinality while filing's (103, 83) are 14-day, and neither is a machine count. The upstream window is irrelevant: 90 d, 2026-01+, and 364 d give identical answers.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_06_release_only.py` prints rank, installs and the upstream total per candidate under all three windows. Any release-only claim must state the rank and the ranking window.

contradictions.topic: Is the merge-suppression docstring's justification true on release? (ingestion "FALSE there" vs trend "which is right")
contradictions.positions: ingestion: the docstring's reason ("its members are a whole development cycle of work that already has `changesets` rows under nightly") is FALSE on release — 4.9-10.2% of a beta->release merge push's members exist on mozilla-beta and NOT on mozilla-central (155.0: 263/5,391 = 4.9%; 154.0: 533/7,448 = 7.2%; 153.0: 705/6,888 = 10.2%) — and `Changeset.find` is channel-filtered anyway. trend: "which is right (a release merge push's members already have `changesets` rows under nightly)". windows: 92.8-95.1% on m-c, 99.9-100% on beta. config cross-dimension: release's merge suppression "silently DEPENDS on beta being ingested".
contradictions.resolution: ingestion WINS on both halves and trend restates the docstring without testing it. I confirmed in the tree that `Changeset.find` (crashclouseau/models.py:502-524) filters `Node.channel == channel`, so a release crash can only ever score against release `changesets` rows and an m-c row is unreachable no matter how many hashes overlap — the docstring's premise is not a reachability argument for release at all. And the docstring's own measurement ("1,932 of 1,932 merge-window candidates share a node hash with the m-c pushlog") was taken on the central->beta merge, not the beta->release one. windows' 4.9%/7.2% agrees with ingestion's for the two majors windows measured cleanly; windows disclaimed only 152.0 as fetch-window-contaminated, so ingestion's 10.2% for 153.0 stands (its m-c universe, 39,462 hashes over 2026-03..08, covers the whole 153 cycle). config's inference is a corollary of the same fact and is correct.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled by reading crashclouseau/models.py:516 (`Node.channel == channel`) plus crashclouseau/pushlog.py:39-68. The remaining open number — the beta-only graft count per merge — should be re-run with an m-c universe that provably spans the whole preceding cycle for each major, which ingestion's does and windows' does not for 152.0.

contradictions.topic: `spike.min_build_installs` = 15: safe range [2, 833] (selection) vs [2, 6000] (population) vs [3, 97] (tests), and does the floor catch the unshipped RC? (population "nothing to tune" vs esr "the exemption cannot catch it")
contradictions.positions: selection: over 245 non-newest build-day observations, respin-only days sit at 1 (9/9) and the quietest LEGITIMATE day at 833 -> safe [2, 833], 55x margin. population: no-user builds 0-1, real builds 6,859-12,980 -> defensible over [2, 6000], 6,859x margin, "nothing to tune". tests: 27 builds, lifetime installs min 0 median 461 max 39,118, only builds under 100 are three at 0/0 plus one at 98 -> any floor in [3, 97]. population KILL: min_build_installs already catches the one real case. esr: the RC takes the newest window slot and `find_no_user_days` exempts the newest day unconditionally, so the floor CANNOT drop it.
contradictions.resolution: selection has the right statistic and the tightest bound; tests has the wrong statistic; population and esr are describing two different builds and both are right. `find_no_user_days` (crashclouseau/datacollector.py:170-198) computes the MAX per-signature install cardinality per build-DAY as seen at the run-day, and exempts `newest = max(installs)` unconditionally. selection measured exactly that at the run-day (833). population measured the same statistic at a different instant/build set (6,859). tests measured the BUILD's lifetime total install cardinality (98) — a different and larger quantity than the max-per-signature, so its [3, 97] is the wrong interval. On the RC: population's "one real case" is the SUPERSEDED 151.0 build 20260513195118 which becomes a non-newest baseline and IS caught; esr's case is the unshipped 155.0 RC which is the NEWEST day and is exempt by design. Both true, different builds — but the harm differs: a superseded build is a bad baseline (real harm, caught), while the RC is only a wasted window slot (it sits at index 2 where nothing follows it, so it is never a baseline). I confirmed 155.0 is 2 reports / 2 install_time / max 1 per day. 15 is safe; population's KILL is too broad because it does not dispose of the RC slot, and esr's gap overstates the harm.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled by reading crashclouseau/datacollector.py:170-198 and by spike/_release_recon/resolve_12_install_denominator.py for the RC. To pin the floor properly, re-run selection's 245-observation instrument (max per-signature install cardinality per non-newest build-day AT the run-day) over 12 months rather than 4.5, since the tightest bound is the one that matters.

contradictions.topic: Does declaring release with `enabled: false` hold filing, or arm it? (value "worse than nothing" vs filing/config/tests/esr "declare and hold")
contradictions.positions: value KILL: "adding a `release: {enabled: false}` entry would be worse than nothing, because `autofile_channel_declared` returns True for any channel with an entry and only `enabled` then holds it." filing [blocker/measured]: overlay `{enabled: false}` -> declared=True, held=True, tripwires silent; overlay `{}` -> declared=True, held=False, armed at cap 10 / mode comment. config, tests, esr: declare-and-hold.
contradictions.resolution: value is REFUTED by the code and by a live probe. `config.get_agent_autofile` computes `channel_veto = over.get("enabled") is False` and returns `"enabled": _env_bool("AUTOFILE_BUGS", ...) and not channel_veto` (crashclouseau/config.py:638-651), and the docstring states the asymmetry deliberately. Probed under prod's live AUTOFILE_BUGS=1 (spike/_release_recon/resolve_07_autofile.py): no overlay -> declared=False held=False; `{}` -> declared=True held=False enabled=True cap=10 mode=comment (ARMED, exactly filing's blocker); `{'enabled': false}` -> declared=True held=True enabled=False; `{'comment_on_existing':'skip','daily_cap':3}` with no `enabled` key -> ARMED; AUTOFILE_BUGS=0 beats an armed overlay. beta ships as `{'enabled': False, 'comment_on_existing': 'skip', 'daily_cap': 3}`. So declare-and-hold works, is the only state that produces a log line, and the ONLY dangerous shape is an overlay without an explicit `enabled` key.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_07_autofile.py` patches the overlay in memory (no file edit) and prints declared/held/enabled/cap/mode for five shapes under both AUTOFILE_BUGS values.

contradictions.topic: `skip` vs `file_new` for release, and the venue share the choice rests on: 64% (filing) / 70% (value) / 72.5% (tests) / 69.2% (esr)
contradictions.positions: filing: release venue 64/100 = 64.0%, nightly 64.0%, beta 60.0% on top-100-by-installs -> "the panel, not the channel, produced the 58-59%-vs-23% contrast"; recommends `file_new` because "`skip` additionally discards the 36% of release selections that have NO venue at all". value: 70% open / 84% any bug on the top 100, quoted against plan #18's beta 58-59% and nightly 23%. tests: release 72.5% vs beta 70.0% on top-40 -> "+2.5pp", and flags the denominator caveat itself. esr: 54/78 = 69.2% on the >=50-install population of one build.
contradictions.resolution: EVERY published figure is a top-by-volume panel; nobody measured release at the SELECTION level, which is the population the filer sees. I did (spike/_release_recon/resolve_10_venue.py, the repo's own `_open_bugs_for_signature` -> `_split_by_application` -> `_split_out_metas` over the 30 real selected signatures): venue = 14/30 = 46.7% (Wilson 30.2-63.9%), no open bug at all 16/30 = 53.3%, other-app-only 0, meta-only 0. So the top-by-volume panel OVERSTATES release's selection-level venue rate by ~20 points, and filing's "36% with no venue" is really 53.3%. filing and tests are right that the channels are indistinguishable on a shared panel; value's comparison mixes panels (plan #18's own nightly control is 28/120 = 23% on a "matched sample" AND 102/200 = 51% "on the repo's own panel", so even its baseline is two numbers). Separately, filing's RATIONALE for `file_new` is INVERTED: crashclouseau/bugzilla_apply.py contains `if existing and mode == "skip" and not withheld: return {"filed": False, "skipped": "open bug N exists"}` — `skip` discards the selections that HAVE a venue (46.7%) and FILES the ones that do not (53.3%). So `file_new` roughly doubles release filings relative to `skip`; it does not "restore the no-venue selections".
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_10_venue.py` (n=30, the whole selected population of the 07-27..08-26 replay). To narrow the CI, run the same chain over selection's full 203 selected signatures; and re-state the `skip`/`file_new` trade against bugzilla_apply.py's actual branch rather than against the venue rate's complement.

contradictions.topic: Does the stale-signature gate fire more on release than on nightly, or is that a panel artefact? (selection 98.0% vs filing's KILL)
contradictions.positions: selection [blocker/measured]: 199/203 = 98.0% of release SELECTED signatures clear `min_age_days`=7 on the gate's own windowed clock (99.0% all-time), against "beta 88%, nightly control 71%". population: ~95%. esr: 25/25 = 100% of the near-threshold population, ages 43-894 d. value: 29 of 30 selections >7 d old, median 118 d. filing KILL: "I measured 25/25 clamps on release's top-25 — and then 25/25 on nightly's and 25/25 on beta's... the measurement is a panel artefact and says nothing channel-specific."
contradictions.resolution: BOTH RIGHT ON THEIR OWN PANELS, and the panel that decides is the SELECTED one, where a nightly control already exists. selection's "beta 88% / nightly 71%" are plan #18's own selection-level figures (plans/18-beta-channel-support.md:215-216, 68/77 beta and 85/120 nightly), so release 98% vs nightly 71% is a legitimate three-channel comparison on the selected population. filing's kill is a valid caution against the top-by-volume instrument (which saturates at 100% everywhere) but does not refute it. HOWEVER both overstate the consequence: `_apply_signature_age_gate` returns early for `v.decision != Decision.lead` (crashclouseau/agent/orchestrator.py:2055-2062), and `_STALE_SIGNATURE_CLAMP` has no `high` key — so the gate blocks every release LEAD (a lead's `high` is itself clamped to `probable` by `_consistency_rule`, so probable/medium/low is all a lead can be) but does NOT touch a `culprit`/strong-evidence verdict, which is in `autofile.verdicts` and files at >= 70 regardless of staleness. "Filing is structurally blocked" should read "every release LEAD is blocked; a culprit is not", and on nightly's measured mix a culprit is ~0.2% of runs.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled by reading orchestrator.py:1972-1975 and 2050-2071 plus plans/18-beta-channel-support.md:215. The open number is the release CULPRIT rate: count `verdict='culprit'` per channel over a held release cycle, which is exactly what `autofile_channel_held`'s log line was built to produce.

contradictions.topic: Is `spike.floor.Firefox.release` = 50 inert? (selection "provably inert" vs population "roughly the same percentile" vs config "only marginally true")
contradictions.positions: selection: structurally inert for selection because `count >= installs` by construction, and measured — floor 1/3/10/20/50 all give exactly 329 pairs; it first binds at 100. population: "5x beta's 10 on a distribution whose p99 is 93 vs beta's 48, so roughly the same percentile — say so rather than leaving it unexplained". config: floor 50 EQUALS installs 50 on release, so `tests/test_selection_log.py`'s tripwire premise (floor(beta) > installs(beta)) is equality on release, and config.py:361-364's claim that the mature-installs half is inert "is only marginally true there". value: floor 50 -> 10 changes 0 of 30 selections.
contradictions.resolution: selection's structural claim is CORRECT and I verified it in the tree. `evaluate_days` computes `spiked` first and `if not spiked: continue` before the install test, so the floor gates entry — but `numbers[day]["count"]` is the SUM over that day's buildids of each buildid's report count (crashclouseau/datacollector.py:277-279), and for a given buildid reports >= `cardinality_install_time` by construction (with 0 coerced to 1). Therefore day count >= max per-bid installs, so a day failing floor=50 could never have passed installs>=50: any floor <= the install threshold cannot exclude a selectable day. value's empirical result confirms it. config conflated two different knobs: the `mature_installs` half is inert for a stronger reason than it gives — `get_maturity_bar("Firefox", "release")` returns `(None, 1)` (verified live), so `mature` is always False off nightly and the whole maturity bar, not just its install half, is unreachable on release; `mature_after_days`/`mature_installs` release entries in config/global.json are dead config. population's percentile framing is a defensible way to document the value but is not a refutation.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled by reading crashclouseau/utils.py:299-347 + crashclouseau/datacollector.py:264-282 and by probing `dc.get_maturity_bar('Firefox','release')` -> (None, 1). The live effects of the floor on release are only the `UNTESTABLE_PREFIX` record and the `Selection` write-volume filter; document that rather than the percentile.

contradictions.topic: Should release join `sigtrend.SUPPORTED_CHANNELS`? trend says ADMIT (105.7 MB), population says STAY OUT (1.13M rows/year, 4.7x)
contradictions.positions: trend: the complete release facet closes at 3,218 terms / 0.59 s / 410 KB per day, 91/91 days complete at `_facets_size=4000`; +271,538 rows and +105.7 MB in real Postgres on a 204 MB / 10 GB plan; per-run write 0.21 s, prune 19.5 ms; ADMIT (three constants + one test). population: 216,720 backfill rows at BACKFILL_DAYS=70 and "steady state 1,130,040 rows/year vs 93,440 + 144,540 = 4.7x the two supported channels combined"; STAY OUT. config: stay out ("release runs 6,194 distinct signatures/day" vs FACETS_SIZE 2000). tests: keep the collector skip, gate the consumer. value: don't extend.
contradictions.resolution: trend's cost figures are right and population's headline storage number is a THROUGHPUT figure mislabelled as storage. `SignatureDaily.prune(days=90)` runs every tick from `update.put_crashes` (crashclouseau/models.py:3900, crashclouseau/update.py:250), so the table is a rolling 90-day window: steady state is ~90 x 2,984 = ~268k release rows, which is exactly trend's measured 271,538 / 105.7 MB, not 1.13M rows. population's 4.7x RATIO survives (release ~268k vs nightly+beta ~59k). config's "6,194 distinct signatures/day" is a 3-DAY cardinality compared against a per-day constant — I measure 5,765 over 3 days and 2,457-3,218 per day. trend also finds the decisive blocker nobody else did and I confirmed it by reading: `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` < `FACETS_SIZE = 2000`, so `collect_day` refuses 500 terms before truncation can begin and raising `FACETS_SIZE` alone still writes zero release rows on every day (all 10 days I measured have `refused_by_MAX=True`). The DECISION is still open on value, but the cost case is trend's.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_08_facets_size.py` (per-day counts, coverage, and the refusal) plus reading crashclouseau/models.py:3900. Whoever decides should price it against the 90-day pruned steady state, never against a rows-per-year figure.

contradictions.topic: Is `_facets_size=10000` rejected by Socorro? (crashclouseau/sigage.py:22 says HTTP 400; trend and population say it is accepted)
contradictions.positions: sigage.py:22, in the tree: "`_facets_size=10000` is rejected outright (HTTP 400)". trend: 10000 is accepted for `collect_day`'s shape and returns byte-identical results to 4000/5000. population: "Socorro accepted `_facets_size=10000` in my probes". config: measured a per-build facet returning exactly 10,000 (i.e. accepted and truncating).
contradictions.resolution: The tree's docstring is WRONG as written. Measured (spike/_release_recon/resolve_08_facets_size.py): on `collect_day`'s shape, 2000/3000/4000/5000/10000 all succeed and 10001 is the first 400 — so 10000 is the MAXIMUM ACCEPTED value, not a rejected one. On the sigage shape itself (a `build_id` facet over a 364-day window) 200/2000/10000 all succeed too. `config.facets_limit` is already 10000 and is used in production, which is independent corroboration. trend and population are right; the sigage docstring needs correcting, and any future "we cannot raise the facet" argument must not cite it.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_08_facets_size.py` prints the acceptance boundary. Whatever 400 was originally hit was either >10000 or a different constraint (e.g. the 365-day range rule two lines below); the docstring should say which.

contradictions.topic: Which dyno pays the off-stack cost, and is it a 512 MB OOM risk? (windows "+54 MB RSS per run, on a 512 MB dyno" vs config "agentworker is 3 x Standard-2X")
contradictions.positions: windows [cost/measured]: `_offstack_candidates` fetches 8.0-17.1 MB live per analysis, measured +54 MB resident (95 -> 149 MB), "on a 512 MB dyno with a known OOM history". config: `heroku ps` shows agentworker = Standard-2X x3, "so the 'agent worker OOMs above 512 MB' note is stale for capacity purposes". ingestion and esr: the switch-on pushlog fetch peaks at 215/234/251 MB on "a 512 MB dyno".
contradictions.resolution: config is right and windows names the wrong dyno. `heroku ps -a crash-clouseau-augmented` today: agentworker Standard-2X x3 running `QUEUES="agent"` (1 GB each, 3 concurrent runs); worker Standard-1X x1 running `QUEUES="high default low"` (512 MB); clock Standard-1X x1; web Standard-1X x1 with gunicorn and no `-w`. So the off-stack fetch and the LLM run are on 1 GB dynos and windows' 512 MB framing is wrong; the INGESTION memory claims (ingestion, esr) are on the right dyno and all three of their peak figures (215.0 / 234 / 251.3 MB, three different instruments) sit comfortably under 512 MB today. ingestion's OOM claim survives only as a GROWTH claim at ~183 days, which ingestion states correctly and falsifies itself on.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled by `heroku ps -a crash-clouseau-augmented` (read-only). Every memory claim in this set should name the dyno and its size; the two that matter are worker=512 MB (ingestion) and agentworker=1 GB (analysis).

contradictions.topic: Are selection's ratio-branch BURSTS and population's 0.51x maturity HANDICAP the same thing?
contradictions.positions: selection: the ratio branch is an install-base-ratio detector — run-days with >=5 selections have a median evaluated/baseline install-base ratio of 2.71 vs 0.40 on zero-selection days; four bursts of 90-110 pairs. population: the evaluated build is judged at 41.3% arrival against an 80.7% baseline — a 0.51x handicap that turns ratio=3 into an effective 5.9x — and proposes fixing it by restricting both sides to equal days-since-ship.
contradictions.resolution: They are TWO DIFFERENT mechanisms acting on the same numbers with opposite signs, and neither report noticed the other. Measured the actual arrival curves (spike/_release_recon/resolve_09_burst_vs_handicap.py): in the 2026-05-26 burst window the evaluated build 151.0.1 is 6 days old at 54.4% arrival while its baseline 151.0 is 10 days old at 79.1% — so on the ARRIVAL axis the evaluated build is still handicapped (0.69x), exactly population's effect. The burst comes from a different axis: 151.0's LIFETIME install base is permanently small (21,850 vs 71,392 = 3.27x) because it was current for only 4 days before being superseded. Consequence for the plan: population's recommended fix (a) — compare equal days-since-ship — removes the HANDICAP but NOT the bursts, because at equal day-6 the superseded baseline had already stopped acquiring users. Removing the bursts needs a rate normalisation by the build's own install base (selection's option (b)) or the ratio raised to 5. population's "RECOMMEND (a)" is therefore incomplete.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_09_burst_vs_handicap.py` prints per-build arrival curves and the burst ratios. To decide the fix, replay both counterfactuals over selection's full 133 run-days and report the burst worst-run under each; selection has the harness.

contradictions.topic: Novelty: 9 of 188 new-on-release (population) vs 0 over 26 dot-release windows (value) vs 2 of 329 pairs (selection)
contradictions.positions: population: 9 of 188 above-threshold signatures (4.8%) have zero release reports in the previous 120 days; 6 of the 9 were already visible upstream; 1 of 188 is new-on-release AND unseen upstream. value [blocker/measured]: 0 signatures genuinely new on a dot-release build at >=50 installs over 26 dot-release windows (8 apparent hits, all from the 153.0.1 respin pair). selection: exactly 2 of 329 pairs sit on a signature first seen on the selected build. llm: 0 of 60 sampled release signatures are <= 7 days old.
contradictions.resolution: THEY COMPOSE and the resolution is the interesting finding: new signatures reach release at the MAJOR (a beta escape), never at a dot release. population's 188 come from the two builds of one cycle — 20260812182057 (154.0, the merge-day MAJOR) and 20260824154132 (154.0.1, a dot) — and 8 of population's 9 named new signatures are also in value's own selected set, all 8 on buildid 20260812182057, the MAJOR. value restricted to DOT windows and correctly got 0. So: 4.8% novelty at the major, 0% at the dots, and 22 of value's 30 selections (73%) are on a major where the on-stack candidate set is empty by construction. The second half also composes: population's "new on release" signatures are still OLD to the stale gate, because release clears `other_channel_floor`=20 on ~100% of signatures (esr: 25/25, 30/30) so `first_seen` is always the all-channel value. New on release does not mean new anywhere.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Settled by cross-tabulating population's nine named signatures against value's v12_pairs.json buildids (all on 20260812182057). Any release novelty figure must be split MAJOR vs DOT, because the two populations differ by 4.8 points and only the dot windows have a usable candidate window.

contradictions.topic: How many bugs has the pipeline filed: 72 (filing) or 73 (value)?
contradictions.positions: filing: 72 bugs / 71 parseable signatures, from `depends_on` of the clouseau meta bug 1396527 with id >= 2060000, creators cdenizet@mozilla.com + clouseau-bot@mozilla.tld, since 2026-08-05; status NEW 28 / FIXED 14 / INVALID 10 / DUPLICATE 7 / ASSIGNED 6 / UNCONFIRMED 5 / REOPENED 1 / WORKSFORME 1. value: 73 = 63 (cdenizet, summary `Crash in [@`, since 2026-08-05) + 10 (all clouseau-bot); NEW 29 and otherwise identical.
contradictions.resolution: The two instruments differ by exactly ONE bug — 2061691 — which value's creator+summary query finds and filing's `depends_on(1396527)` list does not (spike/_release_recon/resolve_11_filings.py). filing's list is 62 cdenizet + 10 bot = 72; value's is 63 + 10 = 73. Both are defensible; the honest phrasing is "72 filings linked to the clouseau meta bug, 73 by creator+summary". filing's warning is confirmed and important: a cdenizet-only filter under-counts by 10 because the account moved to clouseau-bot@mozilla.tld on 2026-08-27, so every docstring in bugzilla_apply.py and models.py that identifies our filings by creator is now one account out of date.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_11_filings.py` prints both instruments and their set difference. Decide whether 2061691 is a pipeline filing that is simply not blocked on the meta bug, and if so fix the meta link so one query answers it.

contradictions.topic: Release build cadence: median gap 4.96/5.0/5.25 d or 6.90/7.02/7.07 d?
contradictions.positions: population: 27 builds / 145.2 d since 2026-04-01, median gap 4.96 d, 1.25 builds/week. selection: n=26 since 2026-04, median 5.0, max 12. trend: 27 builds, median 112 h = 4.67 d, one per 5.4 days. tests: 32 builds since 2026-02-01, median 6.90, max 20.89. ingestion: 45 gaps since 2025-10-01, median 7.02, max 20.89. config: 53 builds since 2025-08-04, median 7.07. value: 83 builds since 2025-01-01, median 7.07, max 20.89.
contradictions.resolution: No conflict — every figure is right for its window, and I reproduced all of them off one build list (spike/_release_recon/resolve_02_span_window.py): 2026-04+ gives 26 gaps / median 5.25 / max 12.22; 2026-02+ gives median 6.90 / max 20.89; 2025-10+ gives median 7.02; 2025-08+ and 2025-01+ give median 7.07 / max 20.89. But the choice of window is NOT neutral: the 20.89-day maximum gap falls entirely outside 2026-04+, and that gap is what drives the retention and lookback findings. So the three reports that recommend against a retention/lookback change (selection, population, and by extension the 2026-04+ replays) are reasoning from a 5-month slice that excludes the worst case. Use 7.02-7.07 d as the cadence and 20.89 d as the maximum for any threshold decision.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Already settled: `spike/_release_recon/resolve_02_span_window.py` prints gaps and 3-build spans per candidate window. Any release cadence figure must state its window and its maximum gap, not just its median.

unsupported_claims: selection: "a flat 10% is the correct model for everything release selection ever sees" — labelled measured, but only the PROCESS-TYPE arm was measured (0 of 22,784 background-process reports, which I confirm). The other three 100%-accept rules (`throttleable_0`, `has_comments`, `has_phc`) were asserted from antenna's source, not measured on the selected population. Measured: `throttleable=F` is 1.86% of the 30 selected pairs' 23,094 reports and ranges 0.00%-43.42% per signature (4 of 30 pairs above 19%). And `has_comments`/`has_phc` are UNMEASURABLE: `user_comments` and `phc_kind` are protected fields and a FILTER on them is silently ignored — `user_comments=!__null__` returned the full unfiltered 602,701 with `errors: []`.

selection: "50 observed installs ~ 390 real machines" via a shifted-geometric FIT — selection labels this a fit and bounds it, which is honest, but the report's own MEASUREMENTS block then states it as "~390 real machines" without the caveat. The direct measurement (per-(signature,build) k on unsampled esr153) gives 8.83x median, range 4.27-9.67x, so ~440 machines with a wide band.
