population: "a release install count understates real crashing machines by 4.1x" applied to `thresholds.installs` — wrong denominator. 4.1x is derived from a CHANNEL-WIDE k-histogram (mean k = 2.314 across all signatures over a month); `installs` is a per-(signature, build-day) gate where the measured k is 1.150 and the factor is 8.83x. The 4.1x is right for a channel-wide install count and 2.2x too small for the threshold it is used to justify.

population: "steady state 1,130,040 rows/year vs 93,440 + 144,540 = 4.7x" — a throughput figure presented as storage. `SignatureDaily.prune(days=90)` runs every tick, so the steady state is ~268k release rows / 105.7 MB (trend's measured figure), not 1.13M. The 4.7x ratio survives; the absolute number is 4.2x too large.

value: "6.2 uuids/run-day" and the whole $207-740/month projection — labelled measured, but the proto query omits the `date` key, so SuperSearch substituted a 7-DAY window for pairs selected up to 35 days earlier. On the same 30 pairs the production-shaped query gives 11.7 kept/pair vs value's 6.3, so the projection is understated ~1.9x on this axis alone.

selection: "median 11, mean 50.7, max 250" protos/pair — the query passed `date='>=2026-07-01'`, up to 61 days and well past the run-day. The kept-at-cap figure (13.0 vs production's 11.7) survives, but the raw distribution is inflated ~2x on the mean and max.

filing: "`skip` additionally discards the 36% of release selections that have NO venue at all" — inverted. bugzilla_apply.py's branch is `if existing and mode == "skip"`, so `skip` discards the selections that HAVE a venue and FILES the no-venue ones. The 36% is also the complement of a top-by-volume panel figure; at the selection level the no-venue share is 53.3%.

filing / value / tests / esr: the release open-bug "venue rate" (64% / 70% / 72.5% / 69.2%) — all four are top-by-volume panels quoted as if they described what the filer sees. Measured at the SELECTION level with the repo's own chain: 14/30 = 46.7% (Wilson 30.2-63.9%). value additionally compares its top-100 figure against plan #18's SELECTION-level beta 58-59% and nightly 23%, a straight denominator mismatch — and plan #18's own nightly control is two numbers (28/120 = 23% "matched" and 102/200 = 51% "the repo's own panel").

selection / population / esr: "the stale-signature gate blocks release filing" — true for LEADS only. `_apply_signature_age_gate` returns before the clamp when `v.decision != Decision.lead`, and `_STALE_SIGNATURE_CLAMP` has no `high` entry, so a `culprit`/strong-evidence verdict at 70 or 85 is untouched and `culprit` is in `autofile.verdicts`. "Structurally blocked" overstates it.

Six reports quote a build's "installations" or "installs" or "machines" at four different window lengths without saying which. For build 20260812182057 (154.0) alone: windows 5,031 (3 d), ingestion and selection 36,050 (7 d), tests 35,589 (7 d), filing 67,067 (lifetime); I measure 5,550 / 38,754 / 67,147 and a maximum PER-DAY distinct count of 11,888. Per the project's own rule only a per-day distinct count is a machine count, so none of these is one, and they differ by 12x for the same build.

filing: "release 294,127 reports / 208,677 install-days" and esr: "release 144,236 reports / 106,426 installations, 37.7x nightly" — a multi-day `_cardinality.install_time` is neither installations nor install-days. population's per-day figures (release 17,849, beta 1,155, nightly 463 -> 38.6x) are the correct form of the same claim.

config: "release runs 6,194 distinct signatures/day against `sigtrend.FACETS_SIZE` 2000 ... release is 4-8x over FACETS_SIZE" — 6,194 is a 3-DAY cardinality (I measure 5,765) compared against a constant the module applies PER DAY. The per-day figure is 2,457-3,218, i.e. 1.2-1.6x over FACETS_SIZE. The conclusion (release cannot be covered at these constants) is right, and for a reason config missed: `MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` refuses every release day 500 terms before truncation begins.

trend: "a release merge push's members already have `changesets` rows under nightly, which is right" — restates the docstring's justification without testing it, and it is not a reachability argument: `Changeset.find` filters `Node.channel == channel`, so an m-c row can never serve a release crash. The docstring's supporting measurement (1,932 of 1,932) was taken on the central->beta merge.

selection: KILL "Node.clean's 30-day prune will silently shrink the release selection window — Not at n=3 ... 0 of 33 exceed 30 days" — presented as measured, but (a) the statistic is the wrong one (the retention clock runs from the run day, and the newest build is itself up to 20.35 d old then), and (b) even on its own statistic 1 of 33 exceeds 30 in the 2026-01+ window it used (30.1 d, rounded to 30) and 2 of 81 over the full history.

tests: "any no-user floor in [3, 97] is the same decision on this instrument" — measured on the BUILD's lifetime total install cardinality, not on the max per-signature install cardinality per build-DAY that `find_no_user_days` actually computes. Different and larger quantity, so the interval is not the one the code sees.

value: KILL "adding a `release: {enabled: false}` entry would be worse than nothing" — presented as a reasoned conclusion and refuted by the code: `channel_veto = over.get("enabled") is False` is honoured against a global `AUTOFILE_BUGS=1`, verified live for five overlay shapes.
windows: "+54 MB RSS per run, on a 512 MB dyno" — the off-stack path runs on `agentworker`, which is Standard-2X x3 (1 GB each); 512 MB is the `worker` (ingestion) dyno.

selection: "a measured 1.75 daily union factor" applied to turn 13.5 kept protos/pair into 58.4 UUIDs/day — measured on 4 pairs at DAILY granularity and then applied to a 20-minute-cadence production tick, which selection itself flags as unmeasured. The factor is the largest single unvalidated multiplier in any cost figure in the set.

windows: the off-stack pref_flip saturation (150/150 kept are pref_flip, 361 of 7,430 = 4.9%, tier 294 vs cap 150) is single-sourced. The MECHANISM is confirmed by reading `_key` in orchestrator.py:422-433 (pref_flip ranks above token overlap in a tuple sort) and `max_candidates`=150, but the 361/294 counts are unreplicated.

ingestion: "time is not the binding constraint; memory is" for the switch-on catch-up — priced the HTTP fetch (7.5-9.1 s for 30.4 MB) but not the job. esr measured the same window end to end through `put_filelog` at 335.5 s, which is 37x longer and blocks the single 512 MB `worker` dyno that also carries nightly and beta report scoring.
missing_work: NOBODY EXPLAINED PROD'S RELEASE `builds` TABLE. Read-only prod SQL: `nodes` holds 7,267 release rows including SEVEN release build revisions (c3ced0930614, 931e624c6f53, 6526f112c78a, 31810c073a58, bf3a46a6a404, e39c605adc0f, d6222c84b8b1), all `merge=false` with pushdate == buildid to the second — and `builds` holds ZERO release rows. So `Build.put_data`'s `if rev in revs_c` precondition HELD for all seven and no row exists. ingestion's gap #5 predicted this silent skip but attributed it to a node pruned in the same call, and that explanation is refuted by the nodes being present. Nobody has a mechanism, and it is the state a switch-on starts from.

THE PRODUCTION-SHAPED PROTO COUNT. Both cost reports used the wrong date window (61-day and 7-day-default); nobody queried protos the way `get_proto_small`/`get_proto_big` do (`search_date` = oldest build-day of the window, as of the run-day). I measured it at 11.7 kept/pair on 30 pairs; it has never been measured over selection's full 329.

THE RELEASE SELECTION-LEVEL VENUE RATE. All four reports that measured an open-bug share used a top-by-volume panel. I measured 14/30 = 46.7% (Wilson 30.2-63.9%) on the actual selected population; at n=30 the CI overlaps both beta's 64% and nightly's 23%, so the `skip`-vs-`file_new` decision rests on an interval nobody has narrowed.

THE RELEASE CULPRIT RATE. The stale gate blocks leads but not `culprit`/strong-evidence verdicts, which are in `autofile.verdicts` and file at >= 70. Nobody measured how often a release verdict is a culprit, so the one filing path the gate does not close is unpriced.

THE PER-SIGNATURE UNSAMPLED SHARE. `throttleable=F` ranges 0.00%-43.42% across the 30 selected pairs. No report measured it per signature, and `has_comments`/`has_phc` cannot be measured at all because a filter on a protected field is silently ignored — so the effective accept rate for any individual release signature is unknown and unknowable from SuperSearch.

THE BURST COUNTERFACTUALS, RUN TOGETHER. selection measured two burst fixes (ratio 3->5, rate normalisation) and population measured a third (equal days-since-ship). Nobody ran population's fix against selection's bursts, and my arrival-curve measurement shows it does not remove them. The three should be replayed on one harness over 133 run-days with the worst-run reported for each.

HOW OFTEN THE BURST CONFIGURATION RECURS. I measure 8 of 82 builds are a dot release arriving <=4 days after the previous build (3 of 18 in selection's window, 1 of 7 in value's). Nobody measured this, and it is the frequency that decides whether the bursts are a tail risk or a quarterly event.

THE RETENTION DECISION AT ITS OWN SATURATION POINT OVER 12 MONTHS. ingestion's sweep (30->80.9%, 45->96.0%, 50+->96.2%) and my reproduction both come from one build list; nobody has checked whether `retention_ndays.Firefox.release = 45` interacts with `buildhub_lookback_ndays` = 30, which config flags as a documented identity that would be deliberately broken.

ESR AS A DECISION. Four reports flag that `esr` is 39.6-40.9% of Firefox crash reports (455,592 in a month, more than release's own 602,701 in the same window) and 111,366-189,549 install cardinality, has no `CHANNEL_TYPE` value, and is already counted toward `other_channel_floor`. population additionally found `Mercurial.get_repo_url('esr')` resolves to a nonexistent repo. Nobody scoped it; it is the largest population the product cannot represent.

THE `throttleable=T` ROLLUP PROPOSAL. trend proposes filtering the release rollup to `throttleable=T` to make the sample rate constant and cites a 2.40x manufactured rise on the loudest riser. The effect of the filter on the rollup was never measured, and my per-pair figures show it would drop 1.86% of reports on average but 43% on one signature.

THE `population.for_crash` FIX. population proposes adding `_cardinality.install_time` to the existing facet request (free) to stop `installs` and `per_install` being computed off a top-1,000 slice. I confirmed the query lacks it (crashclouseau/population.py:182-188) and that `summarize` divides by `len(installs)`, but nobody measured the corrected numbers on a truncated release head signature.

A NIGHTLY CONTROL ON THE SAME DRAW for `top_cpu_share`, `_fixed_after_build_bug` and `_incomplete_fix_bug`. llm compares release 0.138 against nightly's RECORDED 0.32 from a different draw; filing compares release 4/100 against a docstring's 6.0% from a different instrument. Neither difference is interpretable.

THE DOCS DIFF. config lists every wrong line (DEPLOY.md:4 "nightly-only, observe-only canary", DEPLOY.md:40-42 "do NOT set a Bugzilla token / strictly read-only" — false, prod has the token and AUTOFILE_BUGS=1; DEPLOY.md:45 agentworker=1 vs the actual 3; docs/architecture.md:100-101 the INGEST_CHANNELS default; README.md:9 the wrong app, which I confirmed 404s on /tasks.html, /selection.html and /api/selection). Nobody wrote the diff, and plan #18 §12 asked for the same thing for beta and it was not done.

THE MEMORY-SAFETY BACKFILL. I confirmed on prod v139 that `/api/evidence?uuid=41bb8c8a-3458-4803-90f8-a7a850260819` returns HTTP 200 with `withheld: null` and empty `corroborations` — the canonical poison dossier is still served anonymously and `bin/backfill_memory_unsafe.py --apply` has not run. One report flagged it; nobody made it a gate.

THE CHANNEL-BLIND SELECTION SURFACES. esr found `/api/selection` validates `channel` then ignores it (I confirmed: `?channel=release` returns 500 rows of {nightly: 449, beta: 51}, identical to `?channel=nightly`), that `Selection.recent` is already truncating at its 500 limit, and that `html.selection()` never reads the parameter. Nobody costed the fix or checked `/api/reports`, `crashstack.html`, `codeview.html` or `html.diff()` (which renders an unvalidated channel into an hg path) to the same standard.

TWO DEAD CODE PATHS CONFIRMED AND UNOWNED: `datacollector.get_changeset` returns None on ALL THREE channels (I verified release, nightly, beta) because its filter is `@"hg:hg.mozilla.org/".*:[0-9a-f]+` while every `topmost_filenames` term is now `git:github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox:<path>:<sha>`; and it additionally raises `AttributeError` if handed a buildid string rather than a datetime. `crashclouseau/single.py` is imported nowhere and calls `pushlog.puhslog`, which does not exist. Neither has an owner or a deletion decision.

THE 793 INERT RELEASE `changesets` ROWS. Confirmed present on `merge=true` nodes and permanently excluded by `Changeset.to_analyze`'s `Node.merge.is_(False)`. Nobody decided whether they should be deleted with the rest of the orphaned state, or what the equivalent row count is per future merge.

A RELEASE TEST SUITE KEYED TO THE SETTLED NUMBERS. tests established that 6 assertions in one file are the entire forcing function and that 2,109 of 2,115 tests do not notice release. Nobody wrote the list: the six selector knobs, `get_agent_calibration('release')` (which today returns nightly's fitted table {25:0.5, 50:0.5714, 70:0.7234, 85:0.7234} — verified), the two population rates, the autofile decision, `CHANNEL_TYPE` vs `config.get_channels()`, and the retention/lookback property with release's p90 3-build span rather than beta's cadence literal.

THE `_facets_size` DOCSTRING CORRECTION. `crashclouseau/sigage.py:22` states "_facets_size=10000 is rejected outright (HTTP 400)" and I measured 10000 accepted / 10001 rejected. Three reports relied on raising the facet and none noticed the tree contradicts them.
resolved.verdict: Twelve real contradictions, and the resolutions move the release case in both directions rather than one. The cost model was the worst-served number: both cost reports queried protos with the wrong date bound — selection over 61 days, value with no `date` at all, which SuperSearch silently answers with 7 days — and the production-shaped query on the same 30 pairs gives 11.7 kept protos per pair, close to selection and 1.9x above value, so value's $207-740/month is understated and selection's $960-4,050/month is the honest ceiling once its real 2.47 pairs/day is used. The two selection replays never actually disagreed: over the same window they give 27 and 30 pairs with the same branch split, and selection's higher headline is four genuine install-base-ratio bursts that value's 31-day window simply does not contain — I confirmed the mechanism (a baseline build current for only 3-4 days) and that the configuration recurs on 8 of 82 builds. selection's own kill of the retention finding is wrong on the statistic, not the arithmetic: the 30-day clock runs from the run day and the newest release build is itself up to 20.35 days old then, so ingestion's 19.1%-short-window replay reproduces exactly and 45 days is the measured saturation point. On sampling, selection's 7.80x understatement is right for the per-signature gate (I measure 8.83x on unsampled esr153) and population's 4.1x is a channel-wide factor misapplied to a per-signature threshold; conversely selection's "flat 10%" model is 98% right on average and wrong per signature, with 4 of 30 selected pairs sitting at 19-43% unsampled and two of antenna's exempt rules unmeasurable because a filter on a protected field is silently ignored. value's kill of declare-and-hold is refuted by the code and a live probe — `enabled: false` is the honoured per-channel veto and a bare `{}` overlay is the only shape that arms release — and filing's rationale for `file_new` is inverted, since `skip` discards the selections that have a venue, which at the selection level is 46.7%, not the 64-72% every report quoted from a top-by-volume panel. The novelty and dot-window findings compose into the sharpest fact in the set: new signatures reach release at the major, never at a dot release, and 22 of 30 selections land on a major whose on-stack candidate set is empty by construction. The recurring failure mode is denominator drift rather than bad measurement — six reports quote the same build's "installations" at four window lengths differing 12x, and none of them is the per-day distinct count that would be a machine count. Finally, the tree itself lies in two places these reports depended on: `sigage.py:22` claims `_facets_size=10000` is a 400 when 10000 is the maximum accepted value, and `sigtrend.MAX_SIGNATURES = 1500` sits below `FACETS_SIZE = 2000` so raising the facet alone still writes zero release rows — and prod holds seven release build revisions as nodes with zero `builds` rows, which no report explains.

contradictions.topic: The nightly filing/run denominator that every release projection is scaled from
contradictions.positions: FILING: "prod files 0.69 bugs/day on nightly at a 2.6% per-run rate" and "nightly 462 runs = 26.4/day", parsed from the deployed tasks.html's last 500 rows, and used to project release at "~0.25 x 0.69 = 0.17 filings/day = ~5/month". VALUE: "73 filings ever" since 2026-08-05 (BMO, creator cdenizet + clouseau-bot) = ~2.8/day, used for the "$190 per correct attribution" unit economics. FILING's own report also quotes 2,664 dossiers in 30 days from prod SQL, i.e. 88/day, in the same document as 26.4 runs/day.
contradictions.resolution: SETTLED, and FILING's number is wrong by ~3.9x. I ran the read-only query FILING said it could not run (`heroku pg:psql`, join dossiers->uuids->builds): nightly 2,665 dossiers 2026-08-01..08-31 (86/day), 83 with `payload->'filed_bug'->>'filed' = 'true'` (2.68 filings/day, 3.1% of runs, 68 new_bug + 15 comment_on_existing), total_cost_usd 4552.35, avg $1.712; beta 38 dossiers, $42.68, avg $1.123, 0 filed. So VALUE's ~2.8/day is right, FILING's cost figures are right (it did read the DB for those), and only its rate figures came from the wrong instrument. The per-run RATE survives (2.6% vs 3.1%) because numerator and denominator were scaled together, but the absolute rates do not — under FILING's own supply-ratio method release projects to 0.25 x 2.68 = 0.67 filings/day, ~20/month at `file_new`, not ~5. That moves its "thin value case" and drops `daily_cap: 3`'s headroom from ~18x to ~4.5x.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Done: `SELECT b.channel, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.payload->'filed_bug'->>'filed'='true'), sum((d.payload->>'total_cost_usd')::numeric) FROM dossiers d JOIN uuids u ON u.id=d.uuidid JOIN builds b ON b.id=u.buildid GROUP BY 1`. Re-derive both projections from it, and note that `dossiers` only reaches back to 2026-08-01, so 31 days is the whole denominator available.

contradictions.topic: Release's selection rate, and therefore its cost — 9.4x apart
contradictions.positions: SELECTION: 329 distinct (signature,buildid) pairs over 133 run-days = 2.47/day, protos/pair median 11-21 (max 3,930), cap 20 -> 58.4 UUIDs/day -> $32-135/day = $960-4,050/month, plus "$1,510-6,342 in a single burst week". VALUE: 30 pairs over 31 run-days = 0.97/day, protos/pair median 3 (mean 11, max 75) -> 6.2 UUIDs/day -> $207-740/month. LLM, third instrument: uniform draw of 20 signatures with >=5 reports on build 20260824154132 gives protos median 6 and 8.2 runs/selection, and explicitly retracts a "4x worse than beta" claim as a draw artefact.
contradictions.resolution: Not an instrument disagreement — a WINDOW disagreement, compounded by a POPULATION disagreement. SELECTION's own sub-window figure over VALUE's month is 0.75/day (27 pairs / 36 run-days), so the two replays agree on the overlap; the 2.47 is four multi-day ratio-branch bursts in May-July that VALUE's one-month window does not contain. The proto half is a population question: SELECTION drew from the pairs the selector actually SELECTS (loud, spiking, more protos), LLM drew uniformly from signatures with >=5 reports, VALUE drew from a quiet month's selections. For cost, SELECTION's population is the right one and LLM's median 6 is not comparable to it. Honest statement: 0.75-0.97 pairs/day steady with 90-110-pair bursts ~4x per 4.5 months; UUIDs/day is unresolved between 6 and 58 and nobody has the number.
contradictions.how_to_settle: One instrument over one population: take SELECTION's full 133-run-day pair set (spike/_release_recon/sel_13_replay.py output), measure `_cardinality.proto_signature` per pair, and report BOTH the per-tick capped count and the per-pair LIFETIME union (`UUID.add` dedups on (signatureid, protohash, buildid) — verified at models.py:1454-1481 — so a new protohash entering the count-ordered top-N on a later tick is a new row). SELECTION's 1.2-2.2x union factor is n=4 at daily granularity while prod ticks 72x/day; that factor, at the deployed cadence, is the missing number.

contradictions.topic: Does `Node.clean`'s 30-day retention shorten the 3-build release selection window?
contradictions.positions: INGESTION: yes — replaying the real `datacollector.get_builds` over 549 run-days gives a short (<3 build-day) window on 19.1% and a zero-selection day on 0.2%; recommends a per-channel `retention_ndays.Firefox.release = 45` (96.0% full windows, 50+ buys nothing). SELECTION: "MEASURED DEAD ... the widest 3-build release window in the whole Buildhub history spans exactly 30 buildid-days and 0 of 33 exceed 30". TESTS: 3-build span median 11.57d, p90 25.04d, max 30.15d — "one window exceeds the shipped 30-day lookback". WINDOWS: retention "cannot hold a release build's honest candidate set — 83.9% is already deleted on ship day" (a different, merge-window claim).
contradictions.resolution: INGESTION is right on the mechanism and SELECTION's kill uses the wrong test. `Node.clean` prunes relative to NOW (`date - get_ndays_of_data()`, models.py:302-308), not relative to the newest build; `builds.nodeid` is ON DELETE CASCADE (models.py:581) and `get_last_versions` INNER JOINs `Node` (models.py:697), so on run-day D the window is "builds pushed in the last 30 days". SELECTION's span-of-the-newest-3 test evaluates only D = the newest build's own day, the single most favourable instant; on any later run-day the effective lookback is 30 minus the newest build's age. Its own "max 30" is TESTS' 30.15 rounded down, i.e. already at the boundary, and INGESTION reports 31.24 over the longer 2025 history. The 19.1% figure itself is unreplicated and I could not check it here.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Replay `Build.get_last_versions(date=D, n=3)` per run-day D over the real Buildhub release build list with `Node.clean` applied at each D — count run-days with <3 surviving build ROWS and <3 distinct build DAYS. INGESTION did exactly this (spike/_release_recon/ing_21_replay.py) and its hand-simulation agreed; one independent re-run decides whether a config change is needed.

contradictions.topic: Does plan #18 item 6's `buildhub_lookback_ndays` fix have a release analogue?
contradictions.positions: CONFIG: yes — release's median build gap is 7.07d and a 30-day rolling window holds <3 builds on 80/388 days (21%); raise to 45. TESTS: yes — 44 of 182 possible switch-on days (24%) see <3 builds; `test_the_buildhub_lookback_is_the_retention_window` hardcodes beta's `3 x 2.0` days so it says nothing on release. INGESTION: "MEASURED DEAD ... the binding constraint is the RETENTION, not the lookback".
contradictions.resolution: INGESTION is right, and it is checkable statically rather than by measurement: `Build.put_data` inserts a builds row only `if rev in revs_c` (models.py:608 — verified, no else, no log line), i.e. only when a `nodes` row for that revision still exists, and `put_filelog` only ever fetches FORWARD from `Node.get_max_date(channel)`. So a build whose node `Node.clean` pruned can never be re-inserted however far back Buildhub is asked, and raising the lookback alone changes nothing. CONFIG's and TESTS' occupancy measurements are correct and their proposed fix is inert without a retention change — and CONFIG at least names the coupling (45 > max_ndays 30 breaks the identity the docstring rests on). TESTS' separate point stands on its own: the beta-fitted literal in the shipped test is vacuous on release.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Seed a DB with a build whose `nodes` row has been pruned, run `update_builds` with `buildhub_lookback_ndays=45`, and assert no `builds` row appears. Two lines, and it turns a disagreement into a pinned fact.

contradictions.topic: Does `sigtrend` admit release?
contradictions.positions: TREND: ADMIT — the complete per-signature facet closes at 3,218 terms in 0.59 s and 410 KB at `_facets_size=4000` (91/91 days complete), the rollup costs a measured +105.7 MB in real Postgres 16, and the fix is three constants plus one test; `MAX_SIGNATURES=1500` is "a policy cap dressed up as a truncation guard". POPULATION: STAY OUT — 216,720 backfill rows and 1.13M rows/year, 4.7x the two supported channels combined. CONFIG: stay out — "release runs 6,194 distinct signatures over 3 days ... 4-8x over FACETS_SIZE". TESTS: keep the collector skip, gate the consumer instead.
contradictions.resolution: There is no measurement disagreement — 2,984-3,218 signatures/day, ~105 MB, ~1.1M rows/year are consistent across TREND, POPULATION and TESTS — only a spend judgement, which is a decision for the user, not a contradiction. CONFIG's framing IS wrong though: it compares a 3-DAY cardinality (6,194) against a per-DAY constant (`collect_day` is per day), which inflates the gap from 1.6x to 4-8x. For scale, prod `sigdaily` already holds 48,077 rows for two channels (measured). TREND is also the only report that traced BOTH constants, which matters: raising `FACETS_SIZE` alone still refuses every release day at `MAX_SIGNATURES=1500`.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Nothing left to measure. State the price (3 constants, +105 MB, +1.1M rows/yr, 0.8 s per 20-minute tick) and take the decision. If it stays out, add the one-line INFO log on `sigtrend.backfill`'s unsupported-channel return (sigtrend.py:251) that TREND, CONFIG and TESTS all independently asked for, so the absence is not a silent no-op.

contradictions.topic: Release's `POPULATION_TOP_CPU_SHARE_MEDIAN`
contradictions.positions: LLM: measured 0.138 (196 of 2,612 qualifying signatures, the same draw nightly's 0.32 came from) and recommends shipping it together with per-channel literals, because release's at-100% count is 2 of 196 (1%) against nightly's 26 of 200 (13%). CONFIG: "leave `top_cpu_share` None — nobody has drawn the 200-signature sample on release". ESR: reports "top cpu model share 0.060" in the same slot.
contradictions.resolution: LLM wins on evidence: it ran the shipped instrument (`sigage.hardware_noise` per signature, >=5 reports, 14-day window) on 196 signatures; CONFIG asserted the sample did not exist. ESR's 0.060 is a different quantity (a channel-wide share of the top cpu model, not a per-signature median) and must not be cited as a release `top_cpu_share`. LLM's conditional is the load-bearing part and its fix list is one file short: the nightly literals appear at THREE sites, `triage.py:541`, `triage.py:573`/`:590` and `report_bug.py:815` — and the third is the one that reaches a Bugzilla comment. LLM named only triage.py:573.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Re-run LLM's llm_13_topcpu_full.py at n>=200 and report the two counts the prose needs (signatures at share 1.00, and how many of those carry a Firefox bug), then ship median + both counts per channel in one edit touching triage.py and report_bug.py. Verified in tree: `report_bug._cpu_spread_sentence` returns "" while the median is None, so today nothing is published — the lie only appears if the median ships alone.

contradictions.topic: How many real machines is `thresholds.installs.Firefox.release = 50`?
contradictions.positions: SELECTION: ~390 — a shifted-geometric fit of the true crash count under p=0.1 to the observed reports/install ratio of 1.036 gives 7.80 true machines per observed install. POPULATION: ~205 — applying antenna's own 10% rule to the unsampled same-codebase esr153 install_time k-distribution (4,182 installs, mean k=2.314) leaves 24.5% of installs visible = 4.1x, validated out-of-sample (predicted observed reports/install 1.26 vs release 153.x's actual 1.44).
contradictions.resolution: Neither is measured; both authors say so, and then both use their number in a headline. POPULATION's route is the better-founded one — a ground-truth k-histogram from an unsampled population on the same codebase, plus a prediction check — while SELECTION's is a one-parameter fit to a single ratio whose own author bounds the answer in [50, 500]. Note this factor is decision-IRRELEVANT: both reports keep `installs = 50` and neither recommends any change that depends on it. It is a documentation number, so the honest output is an interval, not a point, and "release is 34x stricter than beta in machine terms" should not be stated to two significant figures.
contradictions.how_to_settle: Monte-Carlo antenna's rule over the esr153 k-histogram 1,000 times and report the induced distribution of observed installs given N true machines, with a CI. Cheap, uses data POPULATION already has, and replaces two point estimates with one interval.

contradictions.topic: Who receives the needinfo on a release filing — the pusher or the patch author?
contradictions.positions: TESTS (cross-dimension): "release pushes are made by RELEASE MANAGERS, not patch authors ... `Node.hgauthor` and any needinfo derived from it will point at the release manager who landed the uplift", evidenced by pushes from pchevrel/dsmith with `a=pascalc`. FILING: "uplifts preserve the original patch author ... Florian Queze, Sylvestre Ledru and Emilio Cobos Alvarez — the ORIGINAL patch authors, not sheriffs".
contradictions.resolution: FILING is right, settled in the code: `pushlog.collect` reads `author = chgset["author"]` (pushlog.py:138) and never `push["user"]`, and the function's own beta-era note says exactly that. TESTS measured `pushuser`, which nothing in the tree reads. Residue that IS unsettled: nobody sampled the `author` field of an IN-CYCLE release uplift specifically — FILING's 641-author sample spans a cycle merge and is therefore dominated by merge members, not by the dot-release uplifts that are the only release window with signal.
contradictions.how_to_settle: One `json-pushes?full=1` over a single dot-release window (e.g. 20260812182057 -> 20260824154132, 82 changesets) and a count of distinct `author` values against the `a=` approver in the description. Then resolve two of those authors through the `5f8a5f2` hg-author -> Bugzilla mapping and check `can_login` / `requests.needinfo.blocked`, because an unknown requestee returns BMO error 51 and kills the whole create.

unsupported_claims: FILING's "prod files 0.69 bugs/day on nightly at a 2.6% per-run rate" and "nightly 462 runs = 26.4/day" are presented as measured but come from parsing the deployed tasks.html's last 500 rows. Prod SQL says 2.68 filings/day and 86 dossiers/day — 3.9x and 3.3x higher. The same report quotes 2,664 dossiers over 30 days from the DB two measurements earlier, so it is internally inconsistent by 3.4x, and it had DB access the whole time (it read `total_cost_usd` from the same table).

FILING's "release projects to ~0.17 filings/day = ~5/month" and the summary's "My honest projection is ~2-5 bugs/month" are an inference (nightly rate x supply ratio 8:32) on top of the wrong nightly rate. Corrected: ~0.67/day, ~20/month at `file_new` under the identical method.

SELECTION's "`installs 50` = ~390 real machines under Socorro's 10% release throttle" is a fit, disclosed as such in the falsify note and then used unqualified in the summary. POPULATION's independently derived factor for the same quantity is 4.1x, i.e. ~205 machines.

VALUE's "~$190 per correct nightly attribution" and "one correct release attribution per ~24 months at $5,000-17,800 each" multiply a filing rate by a 0.28 "naming accuracy" whose own CI is 0.13-0.50 and which memory records as coming from an experiment contaminated by 23% corpus label noise. The ratio is quoted to three significant figures.

WINDOWS' channel-level claim "release would run ~98-100% off-stack" rests on 58 crash x build pairs drawn from exactly TWO builds (28 on 154.0, 30 on 154.0.1), one of which is a major whose window is a cycle merge by construction. The dot-release arm is n=30 on one build, and the report itself notes the richest dot window it measured is 5x more file-rich. The rate is an extrapolation, not a channel measurement.

SELECTION's "$1,510-6,342 in a single burst week" chains a measured pair count x a config cap x a per-tick union factor measured on FOUR pairs at DAILY granularity (while prod ticks 72x/day) x a $/dossier band. The union factor is the weakest link and is presented inside the cost range as if it had been measured at the deployed cadence.

CONFIG's "release runs 6,194 distinct Firefox signatures" is a THREE-DAY cardinality compared against `sigtrend.FACETS_SIZE`, a PER-DAY constant, yielding "4-8x over" where the per-day figure (3,096-3,218, measured by TREND, POPULATION and TESTS) gives 1.6x. Wrong denominator on the number that justifies the exclusion.

ESR's "an accidental release ingest is not an incident: it is not triaged (no LLM spend)" — repeated from a shipped test docstring (tests/test_shipped_channels.py:153-156) and used as containment. The no-LLM-spend half is false: `/api/tasks/retrigger` is an unauthenticated POST that forces a run past the channel gate (verified below).

TREND's "release would take human-bug coverage from 81.5% to 86.3% (+25 bugs)" is quoted from spike/trend/REPORT.md and disclaimed by its own author ("not mine to certify"). It is the only positive value figure for release anywhere in the ten reports and it is not a release measurement.

VALUE's "0 new-on-a-dot-release signatures at >=50 installs over 26 windows" uses the per-build facet set difference that POPULATION independently demonstrated is invalid (both facets truncate at 10,000 and are count-ordered; POPULATION's first pass got a nonsense 55.8%). The artefact's direction happens to be conservative here — a truncated baseline INVENTS "new" signatures — so the zero survives, but no report made that cross-check and the finding is stated as if the instrument were clean.
missing_work: PLAN #18 ITEM 31 HAS NO RELEASE ANALOGUE IN ANY REPORT. Verified: prod `pg_indexes` shows `nodes` has only `nodes_pkey` and `changesets` only `changesets_pkey`; `EXPLAIN` on the `(channel, node)` lookup every read path uses is a Seq Scan over 22,767 rows; `Changeset.add` still does an unconditional `db.session.add(Node(...))` (models.py:419-420) with no upsert; `put_filelog` still derives its start from `Node.get_max_date(channel)+1s` with no lock; and `bin/release.py` — the place plan #18 says the idempotent DDL must live — creates no index. Release-specific consequences nobody priced: (a) both `changesets.nodeid` (models.py:340) and `builds.nodeid` (models.py:581) are ON DELETE CASCADE from an UNINDEXED parent, so `Node.clean`'s deletion of a ~7,000-node cycle merge — which recurs every 14-35 days — forces a referential-integrity scan of a 33,140-row `changesets` table per deleted row; (b) release already owns 31.9% of `nodes` and 61.3% of `changesets` (19,527 + 793 of 33,140, exactly matching INGESTION's read) for ~2 changesets/day of real work. The duplicate-row half stays latent only because the Procfile serialises `high default low` on ONE worker dyno — worth writing down, since that is the entire reason item 31 is FOLLOW and not CANARY.

PLAN #18 ITEM 20'S OTHER HALF — RECORDING THE SKIPS — NEVER SHIPPED, AND IT IS THE INSTRUMENT THREE REPORTS' ROLLOUT DEPENDS ON. Verified on prod: `payload.filed_bug` exists on exactly 83 dossiers, ALL `filed=true` (68 `new_bug`, 15 `comment_on_existing`), 0 skip rows and 0 `filing_error` rows; `record_filed_bug` is called at exactly one place, the success path (bugzilla_apply.py:1536). `bugzilla_apply.py:1064-1070` states in its own comment that the held-channel string is "the whole instrument of plan #18's Phase 4 ... a hold that leaves no trace cannot tell anyone how much it would have filed" — but that string only reaches `logger.info` (orchestrator.py:3674-3675), in an app with no log drain and a ~2-hour `heroku logs` window. So FILING's recommendation ("run release triage-only for one cycle and count what it WOULD file") is not obtainable after the fact, and neither is the equivalent for beta, which has been held since 2026-08-27 with 38 dossiers and 0 recorded declines.

THE UNAUTHENTICATED RETRIGGER ROUTE MAKES "RELEASE INGEST-ONLY IS FREE" FALSE, AND ONLY CONFIG MENTIONS IT — as an out-of-dimension code read it explicitly did not verify. Verified end to end: `crashclouseau/__init__.py:258-263` registers `/api/tasks/retrigger` as `@cross_origin()` POST with NO `_require_write_token()` (only `/api/evidence/apply` calls it, api.py:173); `api.retrigger` (api.py:193-213) takes the uuid from the query string; `retrigger_agent` (orchestrator.py:4292-4316) calls `enqueue_agent(..., force=True)`; `enqueue_agent`'s `if not force:` (orchestrator.py:4102-4105) is the ONLY channel gate in the tree besides the sweep (grep: `get_agent_channels` is read at exactly orchestrator.py:4103 and :4163) and `run_evidence_agent` has none; `reset_for_retrigger` returns early for a uuid with no dossier but does not stop the enqueue. So any ingested release uuid — enumerable from `reports.html?channel=release` and `/api/evidence` — is one anonymous POST away from a ~$1-4 run, and per the route's own docstring "IT CAN WRITE TO BUGZILLA", contained for release only by `autofile_channel_declared("release")` being False. CONFIG, FILING, VALUE and ESR all recommend an ingest-only release phase on the strength of "free".

THE THIRD CONSUMER OF `sigage._POPULATION_RATES` — THE ONE THAT REACHES THE FILED BUG AND THE UI — IS UNGUARDED, AND NO REPORT TRACED IT. Verified at orchestrator.py:2836-2855: the `hardware_noise_signature_suppressed` abstain reason formats `100 * (pop_flip if pop_flip is not None else 0)` and `sigage.population_label(channel)`, so on release the published sentence reads "(Firefox background 0%) ... (background 0%, meta bug 1975808)" — a fabricated 0% denominator, strictly worse than the hardcoded-"nightly" defect plan #18 item 24 was written to fix, because 0% makes any share look infinitely anomalous. Both prose siblings DO guard (`triage.py:692-702` drops the comparison; `report_bug.py:745-753` drops the whole paragraph), and the gate that reaches this branch, `_signature_is_mostly_hardware` (orchestrator.py:2635), needs no population value at all — so release reaches it exactly as often as the channel-blind absolute thresholds allow, which ESR notes is only 2.2x release's measured 8.91% background. Plan #18 item 24 named this consumer by line; the release round dropped it and described the gap as prompt-only.

NOBODY MEASURED THE COMPOSITION OF A RELEASE OFF-STACK CANDIDATE LIST ON A DOT RELEASE — the only release window with signal — and `agent.filters.*` does not reach that path. Verified: `_offstack_candidates` (orchestrator.py:365-462) drops only `merge`-flagged changesets and then ranks by (prior_sig, non-backout, pref_flip, token overlap, recency); the `ubiquitous_paths` / `anchor_frame_patterns` / `ubiquitous_symbols` filters are read only on the ON-STACK branch (orchestrator.py:626-632) and only against crash-FRAME filenames, and the off-stack fetch deliberately passes `file_filter=lambda f: True`. On release, POPULATION's own kind histogram puts 499 of 1,178 non-merge in-cycle changesets (42.4%) in the "tagging" bucket plus 36 l10n-bump, and LLM measured 205 of 351 mozilla-release pushes (58.4%) as tags-only with only 31 code pushes — so on a 5-116-changeset dot window, where the 150 cap never binds, the agent's entire candidate list may be majority ffxbld tagging / version-bump / l10n automation. That is plan #18 item 26's question (the noise class in the candidate window) asked on the path release actually uses, and no report asked it.

THERE IS NO PER-CHANNEL OFF-STACK SWITCH, so the kill switch several rollout recommendations assume does not exist — and nobody re-verified the prod off-stack state this round. Verified: `config.get_agent_offstack()` (config.py:719) takes no channel and `config/global.json` has no `agent.offstack.channels` key, so `max_candidates`, `observe_only`, `pinned` and the cost cap are global. I re-read `heroku config`: OFFSTACK_ENABLED=1, OFFSTACK_OBSERVE_ONLY=0, SECOND_OPINION_ENABLED=1, AGENT_CHANNELS/INGEST_CHANNELS="nightly beta", OFFSTACK_PINNED unset (so `pinned: true` from JSON). No report states these values — WINDOWS asserted OFFSTACK_ENABLED=1 as a premise from memory, and plan #18 §7 contradiction 1 exists precisely because two beta recon agents read the JSON instead. So WINDOWS' "suppress filing from the major build for the first cycle" and SELECTION's "reversible via AGENT_CHANNELS without a deploy" are half-available: AGENT_CHANNELS can stop release triage entirely, but nothing can put release's off-stack path into observe-only without disarming nightly's too. Also unmeasured and cheap, which I ran: the per-crash cost cap already fires on 683 of 2,665 nightly dossiers (25.6%) and 2 of 38 beta ones (`payload.over_budget`), so "the cap warns, it does not abort" is not a latent documentation gap — it is a quarter of production runs, on the number three reports price release against.

NOBODY WROTE THE RELEASE EQUIVALENT OF PLAN #18 §9 — the phased rollout with per-phase exit criteria, tripwires and kill switches. CONFIG and FILING each sketch an ordering (ingest-only, then triaged-with-filing-held), but no report produced §9 Phase 3's watch list translated to release: the two-column per-channel `last_node` vs `last_uuid_row` SQL, the `"No buildids for Firefox-release"` count, `builds` rows for channel='release' after the first tick (expected ~5 per ESR's e2e run, 0 today), the `selection` outcome mix (3,310 rows/tick per ESR, 3,679/run per SELECTION), `useless=True` / "agent: no scored changesets" counted per channel, the `patch.parse` backlog around the first cycle merge, and the "if you see X, item N did not land" tripwires. Given that the reports disagree 9.4x on the expected UUID rate, a tripwire is the only thing that would tell an operator in flight which projection was right.

NO REPORT MEASURED THE SECOND OPINION ON RELEASE, and it is what plan #18 §9 Phase 5's arming criterion is made of ("arm only if the beta second-opinion corroboration rate is no worse than nightly's"). `SECOND_OPINION_ENABLED=1` is global (verified in prod); LLM found `second_opinion._SYSTEM` is channel-blind — a module constant passed verbatim as `system_prompt`, never naming the tree its searchfox tools read and never receiving `triage._drift_paragraph` (already wrong for every beta run in prod) — but nobody priced the SO on a channel where ~98% of selections are stale-clamped (so it rarely runs: an uncounted cost SAVING), measured its corroboration rate on release, or proposed what release's arming instrument should be instead.

`Changeset.get_scores`' OWN DOCSTRING BECOMES A LIE ON RELEASE AND NOBODY SAID SO. models.py:541-546 states the two-rows-per-hash collision is "latent on the in-cycle beta window, which is the only one reachable today ... It stops being latent the moment the `mindate` boundary that excludes the merge push moves." On release the merge push is NOT excluded — its pushdate IS the major build's buildid and `Changeset.find`'s `Node.pushdate <= maxdate` is inclusive (WINDOWS) — and 92.8-95.1% of its members share a hash with mozilla-central plus 99.9-100% with mozilla-beta (INGESTION, WINDOWS agree). It stays latent today only because merge members get `files: []`, i.e. for a different reason than the docstring gives, and it goes LIVE the moment either proposed merge-extraction change lands (INGESTION's beta-only-graft subset, or WINDOWS' `drop_merge_files=False` for the release merge). INGESTION caught the sibling lie in `suppresses_merge_extraction`'s release half; this one is unclaimed.
critic.verdict: The ten reports cover plan #18's 31 items far better than I expected — the LLM half, the windows, the filing config, the population and the tests are all mapped, and four items are correctly measured dead — but they miss three things and disagree on the one number the decision turns on. What is missing: item 31 (the `nodes` index and the `Changeset.add` upsert) has no release analogue in any report, and I verified it is still entirely unshipped, with a release-specific twist nobody priced — `changesets` and `builds` cascade from an unindexed parent, so every cycle merge that ages out forces a referential-integrity scan of a 33,140-row table that is already 61% orphaned release rows; item 20's skip-recording half never shipped, and prod's `filed_bug` key exists on 83 dossiers with zero skip rows, which means the "run release triage-only and count what it would file" plan that FILING, CONFIG and VALUE all rest on has no durable instrument; and the unauthenticated `/api/tasks/retrigger` route, which only CONFIG mentions and explicitly did not verify, breaks the "ingest-only release is free" premise four reports build on — I traced it from the route registration to `enqueue_agent`'s `if not force:` and there is no channel gate anywhere below it. The one consumer of a per-channel value nobody traced is the worst-consequence one: `orchestrator.py:2843-2855` publishes "Firefox background 0%" into a filed bug and onto crashstack.html when a release population rate is absent, while both prose siblings correctly drop the comparison — plan #18 item 24 named that exact line and the release round dropped it. On measurements asserted rather than run, the decisive one is FILING's nightly filing rate: 0.69/day and 26.4 runs/day came from parsing tasks.html, prod SQL says 2.68/day and 86/day, and correcting it moves its own release projection from ~5 bugs/month to ~20 and cuts `daily_cap: 3`'s headroom from 18x to 4.5x — which is a different answer to "is release worth it". The second decisive gap is that release's cost is unresolved between $207/month and $4,050/month, and the disagreement is not an error: SELECTION and VALUE agree on the overlapping month and differ only because SELECTION's 4.5-month window contains four ratio-branch bursts, then compound that with three incompatible proto-per-pair draws — so nobody has the UUIDs/day number, and one instrument over one population would produce it. I would not start any release work before (a) that single cost measurement, (b) the retrigger route is token-gated, and (c) skips are recorded, because those three are what make every later phase measurable, cheap and reversible. Three things the reports settle well and should not be relitigated: release needs no channel alias, no enum migration and no merge-extraction rule, all measured dead by two or more independent instruments each.
